CAPTION_ENDORSE: Political protest blocks area in front of Parliament of Georgia on Rustaveli Avenue in Tbilisi
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Opponents of the "Georgian Dream" have been protesting in Tbilisi for 583 days.
On the 583rd day of continuous protests, participants gathered outside the Parliament of Georgia demanded the release of women political prisoners, including Nanu Sander, who was convicted in the case of the attempted storming of the presidential residence. The activist again reported inhumane treatment in prison.
As reported by "Caucasian Knot", on July 2, on the 582nd day of continuous actions, participants gathered in front of the Parliament of Georgia demanded open elections and the release of prisoners of conscience, as well as opposed politically motivated dismissals.
Supporters of Georgia's Eurointegration with national flags and EU flags gathered in front of the Parliament building in Tbilisi for the 583rd evening in a row. Activists with flags stood at the edge of the sidewalk near the roadway of Rustaveli Avenue, while others were on the sidewalk and square in front of the Parliament, communicating with each other. At least 100 people participated in the gathering, according to a video published by Mtavari.
The protesters held banners: "Fire to Putin and the Kremlin, glory to the heroes", "Don't get used to the occupation", "Women in Ivanishvili's captivity" and "Freedom for Nanu Sander", according to photos published by photographer Georgy Mosiashvili (Mo Se) and Netgazeti on Facebook*.
37-year-old Nanu Sander, sentenced to seven years, again complained about the conditions in women's colony No. 5 in Gardabani. According to the activist, for nine months she has faced pressure and violations of her rights, as well as being deprived of medical assistance and proper nutrition.
Sander was subjected to humiliating treatment immediately after being transferred to this prison. "The activist claims that the prison guards insulted her for about 40 minutes, refused to give her water despite her deteriorating condition, and demanded she undergo a strip search in a gynecological chair," writes "News-Georgia".
Nanu Sander also stated that the administration of the facility isolates her from other prisoners for long periods and restricts her correspondence. She added that psychological pressure in the colony pushed her to attempt suicide. The Special Penitentiary Service of Georgia rejected all accusations, stating that the convict is provided with all necessary medical services.
Protest participants in Georgia have been demanding new parliamentary elections and the release of political prisoners since November 28, 2024. Security forces have conducted harsh dispersals of protests, using tear gas and water cannons, and detained protesters. During the protests, thousands of people have faced administrative prosecution. CAPTION_ENDORSE: Protest blocks Periferico in Gomez Palacio, Durango, Mexico
MESSAGE_TEXT:
AMOTAC Durango se une a marcha nacional para exigir mayor seguridad
Integrantes de la Alianza Mexicana de Organizaciones de Transportistas A.C. (AMOTAC) se unieron a la manifestación nacional en la Laguna de Durango
Alma Gudiño
Para demandar mejores condiciones de seguridad y denunciar presuntamente abusos por parte de autoridades federales, integrantes de la Alianza Mexicana de Organizaciones de Transportistas A.C. (AMOTAC) se unieron a la manifestación nacional en la Laguna de Durango.
César Quiñones Loredo, delegado estatal de AMOTAC en Coahuila y Durango, sostuvo que la inconformidad es para respaldar a sus dirigentes nacionales quienes se encuentran dialogando con las autoridades.
Los manifestantes recorrieron el Periférico de Gómez Palacio, para salir por la carretera a Chihuahua y terminar en El Vergel.
Se realizaron bloqueos de 30 minutos, para posteriormente dar paso al tráfico vehicular.
En la movilización participaron 150 agremiados de la región norte.
Recordó que los transportistas enfrentan la inseguridad en las carreteras del país, así como las revisiones que realizan las autoridades federales, lo cuales son muy estrictos en los retenes que realiza la Fiscalía General de la República (FGR).

AMOTAC Durango Joins National March to Demand Greater Security
Members of the Mexican Alliance of Transportation Organizations (AMOTAC) joined the national demonstration in the Laguna region of Durango
Alma Gudiño

César Quiñones Loredo, AMOTAC's state delegate for Coahuila and Durango, stated that the protest was to support their national leaders who are currently in dialogue with the authorities.

The demonstrators marched along the Gómez Palacio ring road, exiting onto the highway to Chihuahua and ending in El Vergel.
They held 30-minute blockades, after which they allowed traffic to flow again.
150 members from the northern region participated in the demonstration. He noted that truckers face insecurity on the country's highways, as well as strict inspections by federal authorities, particularly at checkpoints operated by the Attorney General's Office (FGR).

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Protest blocks area at Plaza de Armas in Arequipa, Peru
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Los trabajadores bajo el régimen CAS del Instituto Nacional de Estadística e Informática (INEI) realizaron una protesta en la Plaza de Armas de Arequipa para exigir el cumplimiento de la Ley N.° 32563. Esta ley reconoce el pago del 100 % de las gratificaciones y la Compensación por Tiempo de Servicios (CTS). Los manifestantes rechazaron la propuesta del Ejecutivo de aplicar estos beneficios de manera progresiva y solicitaron que se respeten las condiciones aprobadas por el Congreso.
Rodolfo Álvarez, representante de los trabajadores CAS del INEI, explicó que la ley fue aprobada este año y establece el pago íntegro de ambos beneficios. Sin embargo, señaló que el Ministerio de Economía plantea entregar únicamente el 10 % durante 2026 y aumentar el porcentaje de forma gradual hasta alcanzar el total en 2030. “Esta ley que salió este año y aprobada por el presidente del Congreso establece que se nos debe pagar la gratificación y el CTS al 100 %, pero el Ejecutivo está proponiendo que solo nos paguen este año el 10 %”, manifestó.
Según indicó, en el INEI laboran más de 500 trabajadores CAS a nivel nacional y alrededor de 18 pertenecen a la sede de Arequipa. Precisó que el monto a recibir dependerá de la remuneración de cada servidor, por lo que el 10 % representaría apenas entre 180 y 200 soles para quienes perciben un sueldo cercano a los 1,800 soles.
Antes recibían 300 soles
Álvarez recordó que anteriormente los trabajadores CAS solo recibían una gratificación fija de 300 soles y no contaban con CTS. Por ello, sostuvo que la aprobación de la Ley N.° 32563 representó un avance importante en el reconocimiento de sus derechos laborales. No obstante, advirtió que el argumento de falta de presupuesto no debería impedir su aplicación.
El dirigente cuestionó que existan recursos para otros sectores del Estado mientras se pretende postergar el pago de beneficios laborales. “Nuestra lucha es por el respeto a esta ley, que se nos debe pagar nuestro beneficio”, afirmó. Asimismo, señaló que la principal demanda del gremio es el cumplimiento de la norma sin fraccionamientos.
Asimismo, informó que los sindicatos del INEI mantienen reuniones con organizaciones de otras entidades públicas para evaluar nuevas medidas de protesta. Agregó que trabajadores de los regímenes 276 y otras instituciones también respaldan este reclamo, por considerar que fortalece los derechos laborales en el sector público.
Los manifestantes advirtieron que continuarán realizando movilizaciones mientras no exista un compromiso del Ejecutivo para ejecutar el pago completo de las gratificaciones y la CTS conforme a lo establecido en la ley vigente.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Workers under the CAS (Special Administrative Contract) regime at the National Institute of Statistics and Informatics (INEI) held a protest in Arequipa's Plaza de Armas to demand compliance with Law No. 32563. This law guarantees the payment of 100% of bonuses and the Compensation for Length of Service (CTS). The protesters rejected the Executive's proposal to implement these benefits gradually and demanded that the conditions approved by Congress be respected.

Rodolfo Álvarez, a representative of the INEI's CAS workers, explained that the law was passed this year and mandates the full payment of both benefits. However, he pointed out that the Ministry of Economy is proposing to pay only 10% during 2026 and gradually increase the percentage until reaching the full amount in 2030. “This law, which was passed this year and approved by the President of Congress, establishes that we should be paid 100% of our bonus and severance pay, but the Executive Branch is proposing that we only receive 10% this year,” he stated.

According to him, the National Institute of Statistics and Informatics (INEI) employs more than 500 contract workers nationwide, and around 18 of them work at the Arequipa office. He specified that the amount to be received will depend on each employee's salary, so 10% would represent only between 180 and 200 soles for those earning a salary close to 1,800 soles.

Previously they received 300 soles.
Álvarez recalled that previously, contract workers only received a fixed bonus of 300 soles and did not have severance pay. Therefore, he maintained that the approval of Law No. 32563 represented a significant step forward in the recognition of their labor rights. However, he warned that the argument of a lack of budget should not impede its implementation.

The union leader questioned the availability of resources for other sectors of the State while the payment of labor benefits is being postponed. “Our fight is for respect for this law, for the payment of our benefits,” he stated. He also indicated that the union's main demand is the full implementation of the law without any partial payments.

He further reported that the INEI unions are holding meetings with organizations from other public entities to evaluate new protest measures. He added that workers under the 276 regime and other institutions also support this demand, considering that it strengthens labor rights in the public sector.

The protesters warned that they will continue to hold demonstrations until the Executive Branch commits to making the full payment of bonuses and severance pay (CTS) as established by current law.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Single Union of Treasury Workers announces strike on June 15 in Senegal
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Le climat social se tend au ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan. Après le report d’une audience attendue avec le ministre, le Syndicat unique des travailleurs du Trésor annonce le dépôt d’un préavis de grève dès le 15 juin.
Le Syndicat unique des travailleurs du Trésor (SUTT) franchit une nouvelle étape dans son bras de fer avec les autorités du ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan.
Selon le quotidien Vox Populi, l’organisation syndicale a décidé de déposer un préavis de grève dès le lundi 15 juin 2026, à la suite du report d’une audience prévue avec le ministre.
Dans un communiqué, le SUTT dénonce le report de dernière minute de cette rencontre, qui devait permettre un arbitrage sur la crise en cours au sein du département ministériel. Le syndicat souligne qu’il s’agit du deuxième report après celui enregistré le 26 mai dernier.
Pour les responsables syndicaux, cette situation traduit un manque de considération envers les travailleurs du Trésor. Le SUTT estime que les reports successifs contribuent à détériorer davantage le climat social.
L’organisation avertit qu’elle tiendra le ministère responsable de toute aggravation des tensions sociales ou de toute perturbation susceptible d’affecter le fonctionnement des finances publiques.
Fort des décisions prises lors de son assemblée générale extraordinaire du 23 mai, le syndicat entend désormais dérouler son plan d’action. Il appelle l’ensemble des agents à rester mobilisés afin de défendre ce qu’il qualifie de lutte contre le « démantèlement du Trésor ».
Cette nouvelle escalade intervient dans un contexte où les régies financières occupent une place stratégique dans la mobilisation des ressources publiques et la gestion budgétaire de l’État.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Tensions are rising at the Ministry of Economy, Finance, and Planning. Following the postponement of a scheduled meeting with the Minister, the Unified Union of Treasury Workers (SUTT) has announced it will file a strike notice effective June 15.

The Unified Union of Treasury Workers (SUTT) is taking a further step in its standoff with the authorities at the Ministry of Economy, Finance, and Planning.

According to the daily newspaper Vox Populi, the union has decided to file a strike notice effective Monday, June 15, 2026, following the postponement of a planned meeting with the Minister.

In a press release, the SUTT denounces the last-minute postponement of this meeting, which was intended to resolve the ongoing crisis within the ministry. The union points out that this is the second postponement, after the one on May 26.
For union leaders, this situation reflects a lack of consideration for Treasury workers. The SUTT believes that the successive postponements are further deteriorating the social climate.

The organization warns that it will hold the ministry responsible for any escalation of social tensions or any disruption likely to affect the functioning of public finances. Strengthened by the decisions made at its extraordinary general meeting on May 23, the union now intends to implement its action plan. It calls on all employees to remain mobilized in order to defend what it calls the fight against the "dismantling of the Treasury."
This new escalation comes at a time when financial agencies play a strategic role in mobilizing public resources and managing the state's budget.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Organizaciones sociales y religiosas anunciaron la marcha por la Vida, la Familia y las Libertades que se efectuará este sábado 20 de junio a las 17:00 horas, desde la Glorieta de Pancho Villa hasta la Plaza de Armas, donde habrá una concentración.
El pastor Bruno Escobar Ávila, presidente de la Confraternidad Ministerial Evangélica de Chihuahua hizo una invitación a todas las familias chihuahuenses a participar en esta manifestación y dejar en claro a nuestras autoridades del país, que nuestro estado es provida y profamilia.
En su intervención, el presidente de Conciencia Social y Vocero de Cruzada por la Familia, Francisco Javier Valenzuela Casas lamentó la degradación social que vivimos hoy en día, ante los embates hacia la familia, el matrimonio natural y la ideologización e hipersexualización de nuestros niños por la perversa ideología de genero que se promueve en el cine, las series, el internet, pero sobretodo en la Nueva Escuela Mexicana.
Por su parte, la Coordinadora Estatal de Iniciativa Ciudadana, Ruth Sánchez Hernández, indico que en esta marcha se exigirá a las autoridades que se respete el derecho a la vida en todas las etapas del ser humano, desde la concepción, hasta la muerte natural, toda vez que el derecho a la vida está consagrado en nuestra Constitución y tratados internacionales.
La regidora Joni Barajas González, presidente de la Comisión de Comunidades Indígenas y Asuntos Religiosos, señaló que el Ayuntamiento respalda esta actividad que nace de la sociedad, de familias chihuahuenses que quieren salir a las calles a enaltecer los valores fundamentales de la vida, la familia y las libertades.
Con la representación personal del alcalde Marco Bonilla Mendoza, el director de Desarrollo Humano y Educación, Mario García Jiménez, dijo que el Municipio siempre ha puesto en el centro de sus decisiones los valores fundamentales del individuo y se ha trabajado con perspectiva de familia, razón por la cual apoyan este movimiento ciudadano.

TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Social and religious organizations announced the March for Life, Family, and Freedoms, which will take place this Saturday, June 20th, at 5:00 p.m., from the Pancho Villa roundabout to the Plaza de Armas, where a rally will be held.

Pastor Bruno Escobar Ávila, president of the Evangelical Ministerial Fellowship of Chihuahua, invited all families in Chihuahua to participate in this demonstration and make it clear to our national authorities that our state is pro-life and pro-family.

In his remarks, Francisco Javier Valenzuela Casas, president of Social Conscience and spokesperson for Crusade for the Family, lamented the social degradation we are experiencing today, given the attacks on the family, natural marriage, and the indoctrination and hypersexualization of our children by the perverse gender ideology promoted in film, television series, the internet, and especially in the New Mexican School system.

For her part, Ruth Sánchez Hernández, State Coordinator of Citizen Initiative, indicated that this march will demand that authorities respect the right to life at all stages of human existence, from conception to natural death, given that the right to life is enshrined in our Constitution and international treaties.

Councilwoman Joni Barajas González, president of the Commission on Indigenous Communities and Religious Affairs, stated that the City Council supports this activity, which originates from the community, from Chihuahua families who want to take to the streets to uphold the fundamental values ​​of life, family, and freedoms.

Representing Mayor Marco Bonilla Mendoza, the Director of Human Development and Education, Mario García Jiménez, said that the Municipality has always placed the fundamental values ​​of the individual at the center of its decisions and has worked with a family perspective, which is why they support this citizen movement. On behalf of young people, Pedro Alberto Hernández Ostos, leader of Iniciativa Ciudadana (Citizen Initiative), urged this sector of society to demonstrate on June 20th and demand public policies that counteract the serious social problems they face, such as drug addiction, crime, suicide, unplanned pregnancies, and violence, among others.

The organizers also asked attendees to wear white, carry banners and signs in support of life, family, and freedoms, and bring hats, caps, or umbrellas. They announced that hydration stations will be available along the route and seating will be provided in the Plaza de Armas (Main Square) for people with disabilities and senior citizens.

Finally, social and religious organizations reiterated the importance of taking to the streets on June 20th to defend, through peaceful civil resistance, the most important values ​​we hold as individuals: Life, Family, and Freedoms.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Labor protest planned for May 12 at 09:30 at Plaza del Fort Pienc in Barcelona, Spain
MESSAGE_TEXT:
El pulso de la ciudad
Los trabajadores municipales y los profesores forman un frente laboral contra la Administración: convocan una nueva manifestación masiva en Barcelona
Las plantillas del Ayuntamiento de Barcelona y de las escuelas catalanas aúnan fuerzas en una jornada de concentración unitaria que tiene por objetivo revertir tanto el acuerdo para la educación como el último convenio colectivo municipal
Relacionada: Los trabajadores municipales de Barcelona plantan cara al Ayuntamiento: exigen la renegociación del convenio colectivo
Unión laboral entre los principales colectivos en huelga en Catalunya. En frente, el rival a abatir es una Administración con la que no se han producido avances significativos en el marco de las negociaciones tras varios meses de movilizaciones.
La del próximo martes, 12 de mayo, es una jornada de huelga conformada por todo el personal movilizado de Educación, por un lado, y por la plantilla municipal --que agrupa a las trabajadoras de las bibliotecas, el personal de las Oficinas de Atención a la Ciudadanía (OAC), Servicios Sociales, feminismos y escuelas infantiles--, por el otro.
Ambos sectores 'hermanados' buscan redoblar la presión contra el Ayuntamiento de Barcelona y el Govern de la Generalitat, respectivamente, generando fuerza a través del número. Ya ocurrió algo similar a finales de marzo, cuando la gran manifestación del profesorado se encontró y unió fuerzas con la de médicos en huelga.
Esta vez, según ha explicado La Intersindical, los trabajadores del Ayuntamiento conformarán una de las tres columnas, que se unirá a las dos establecidas por los profesores en lucha. En el caso de Educació, convocan los sindicatos USTEC, CGT, Intersindical y ASPEPC-SPS, mientras que son la CGT, La Intersindical y Àbacos quienes lideran los colectivos municipales. Esta comitiva saldrá de la plaza del Fort Pienc, a las 9:30 horas, y se unirá al resto de la manifestación a las 12:00 en la plaza de Urquinaona.
Tres Columnas
Por su parte, CGT ha detallado que las otras dos columnas de manifestantes se concentrarán en la plaza de Espanya y en la estación de El Clot, desde donde marcharán hasta la plaza de Urquinaona, centro neurálgico de toda la movilización. Una vez allí, marcharán hasta la plaza de Sant Jaume.
Esta concentrará a los profesores de toda Catalunya y pretende repetir el hito de finales de marzo, en el que varias decenas de miles de docentes colapsaron el centro de la capital catalana en una manifestación tildada de histórica por el sector educativo.
Situación de bloqueo
Si bien cada uno de los colectivos en lucha tiene elementos particulares, lo cierto es que hay una situación conjunta compartida. Tanto los trabajadores municipales como los del sector público educativo vienen de un ciclo anterior de huelgas. En ambos casos, según denuncian las entidades convocantes, se encuentran ante una "situación de bloqueo" tanto por parte de los gobiernos municipal y autonómico.
La huelga educativa nace de un acuerdo firmado por el Govern con los sindicatos UGT y CCOO que, según el resto de entidades que conforman la parte social, cronificaba la precarización tanto económica como laboral de la plantilla. La agenda de la Administración, por su parte, pasa por comenzar a implantar el acuerdo ya firmado.
En el caso local, los sindicatos movilizados protestan contra un convenio colectivo firmado por el consistorio con UGT, CCOO y CSIF. De nuevo, la estrategia de la Administración pasa por aplicar las nuevas medidas mientras la parte social movilizada denuncia la "degradación del escudo social" de la capital catalana.
En esta línea, los sindicatos reclaman la apertura de espacios de diálogo al gobierno de Collboni, el refuerzo de las plantillas, la dignificación de las escuelas infantiles y el fin de la burocratización, entre otras cuestiones.
Ambas instituciones aseguran estar abiertos a negociar y dialogar con los sindicatos. No obstante, en ninguno de los casos se ha llegado a un punto de entendimiento que permita desconvocar la convocatoria.
Un contexto agravante
Existen agravantes en ambas luchas. En el ámbito municipal, aseguran que el consistorio está alargando la convocatoria del pleno extraordinario convocado por la oposición para, mediante una estrategia legal, que este se solape con el próximo pleno ordinario, diluyendo así el motivo principal por el que la oposición convocó este espacio: que el Ejecutivo rinda cuentas por un conflicto que "lleva en las calles 90 días".
La huelga de Educación, por su parte, se recrudece después de que hace escasos días la CGT descubriera a dos agentes de los Mossos d'Esquadra infiltradas en una asamblea, algo que los sindicatos han condenado e incluso la USTEC ya ha anunciado que judicializará.
Más allá de las grandes convocatorias, cada uno de los colectivos ha arrancado con acciones de protesta propia. A las puertas de la selectividad, las bibliotecas han anunciado cierres de los locales. Por otro lado, el número de claustros que ha anunciado no hacer más actividades extraordinarias como las excursiones.
Con todo, este martes se presenta como una nueva jornada en la que sindicatos y trabajadores miden sus fuerzas contra Ayuntamiento y Generalitat. Ambas partes ponen a prueba de nuevo su capacidad de resistencia en sendos conflictos donde, lo que está en juego, es el modelo de Educación pública en Catalunya y los servicios públicos en Barcelona.

Municipal workers and teachers form a united front against the Administration: they call for a new massive demonstration in Barcelona

Their opponent is an Administration with which no significant progress has been made in negotiations after several months of mobilizations.

Next Tuesday, May 12, will be a day of strike action comprised of all mobilized Education staff, on the one hand, and municipal staff—including library workers, staff from Citizen Service Offices (OAC), Social Services, feminist groups, and nursery schools—on the other.

Both groups, now allied, seek to increase pressure on the Barcelona City Council and the Catalan Government, respectively, by building strength through sheer numbers. This time, according to the Intersindical union, City Hall workers will form one of the three columns, which will join the two columns formed by the striking teachers. Both sides are once again putting their resilience to the test in separate conflicts where what's at stake is the model of public education in Catalonia and public services in Barcelona.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Tear gas deployed during protest outside police station in Manchay area of Pachacamac, Peru
MESSAGE_TEXT:
La muerte de E. J. C. B., el adolescente de 17 años que falleció mientras permanecía detenido en la comisaría de Manchay, volvió a colocar a este sector de Lima Este en el centro de la atención pública. Esta vez, una manifestación convocada para exigir justicia terminó con el lanzamiento de bombas lacrimógenas por parte de efectivos policiales y nuevas críticas a la actuación de las autoridades.
La concentración se desarrolló frente a la dependencia policial de Manchay, en Pachacámac. Familiares, amigos, vecinos y ciudadanos llegaron con pancartas y megáfonos para expresar su respaldo a los padres del menor y reclamar el esclarecimiento de los hechos.
Durante varias horas, los asistentes permanecieron en los exteriores de la comisaría. Sin embargo, conforme avanzó la jornada, se registraron incidentes que derivaron en la intervención policial para dispersar a los manifestantes.
Las imágenes difundidas en redes sociales muestran momentos de tensión y confusión. En los videos se observa a personas retirándose de la zona mientras se percibe el efecto de los gases lacrimógenos utilizados por los agentes del orden.
EL CASO QUE DESATÓ LA INDIGNACIÓN
La protesta tuvo como origen la muerte del adolescente ocurrida el pasado 15 de junio. Según la información conocida hasta el momento, el menor permaneció recluido durante 48 horas en la carceleta de la comisaría de Manchay luego de que la madre de su presunta enamorada lo acusara de haber ingresado a una vivienda para cometer un robo.
Los padres del adolescente rechazan esa versión y han formulado denuncias sobre lo que habría ocurrido durante el tiempo que su hijo permaneció bajo custodia policial.
De acuerdo con sus declaraciones, el menor habría sufrido presuntos maltratos, agresiones físicas y actos de tortura. Asimismo, denunciaron que policías les habrían solicitado dinero a cambio de otorgarle la libertad.
El adolescente fue hallado en estado grave dentro de la dependencia policial y posteriormente trasladado a un hospital, donde se confirmó su fallecimiento. A raíz de ello, la Fiscalía inició una investigación para esclarecer las circunstancias de la muerte.
Mientras la Policía sostiene la hipótesis de una presunta autolesión, la familia rechaza esa explicación. El padre del menor cuestionó la versión policial y sostuvo que la prenda señalada como elemento utilizado para el supuesto acto no contaba con las características descritas por las autoridades.
INVESTIGACIONES Y CUESTIONAMIENTOS
La gravedad del caso llevó al Ministerio del Interior a separar temporalmente al comisario de Manchay y a otros cinco efectivos policiales mientras avanzan las investigaciones.
Paralelamente, el Ministerio Público continúa recopilando testimonios, revisando registros y ejecutando diligencias para determinar qué ocurrió durante las casi 48 horas que el adolescente permaneció bajo custodia.
La Defensoría del Pueblo también intervino y solicitó que las investigaciones se desarrollen con celeridad, independencia y transparencia. El organismo recordó que el Estado tiene la responsabilidad de garantizar la integridad física de toda persona que se encuentre detenida.
En medio del debate, el congresista Alfredo Azurín pidió respetar la presunción de inocencia de los policías involucrados y sostuvo que corresponde al Ministerio Público determinar las responsabilidades sobre la base de pruebas.
Por su parte, el general Eduardo Pérez Rocha señaló que podría haberse producido una presunta negligencia, al recordar que un menor de edad no puede ser ingresado a un calabozo. Además, cuestionó las condiciones de vigilancia que habrían existido durante la permanencia del adolescente en la dependencia policial.
Mientras continúan las diligencias y la comunidad de Manchay mantiene vigente su pedido de justicia, la muerte del adolescente sigue generando interrogantes que esperan respuesta. La familia ha anunciado que continuará participando en movilizaciones y actividades públicas hasta que se esclarezcan los hechos y se determinen las responsabilidades correspondientes.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
The death of E. J. C. B., the 17-year-old who died while in custody at the Manchay police station, has once again placed this area of ​​East Lima in the public eye. This time, a demonstration called to demand justice ended with police officers firing tear gas and renewed criticism of the authorities' actions.

The gathering took place in front of the Manchay police station in Pachacámac. Family members, friends, neighbors, and other citizens arrived with banners and megaphones to express their support for the teenager's parents and demand a thorough investigation.

For several hours, the demonstrators remained outside the station. However, as the day progressed, incidents occurred that led to police intervention to disperse the protesters.
Images circulating on social media show moments of tension and confusion. The videos show people leaving the area as the effects of tear gas used by law enforcement officers are visible.

THE CASE THAT SPARKED OUTRAGE
The protest stemmed from the death of a teenager on June 15. According to information available so far, the minor was held for 48 hours in the holding cell at the Manchay police station after the mother of his alleged girlfriend accused him of breaking into a home to commit a robbery.

The teenager's parents reject this version of events and have filed complaints about what allegedly happened while their son was in police custody.

According to their statements, the minor suffered alleged mistreatment, physical assaults, and acts of torture. They also reported that police officers demanded money in exchange for his release.

The teenager was found in critical condition inside the police station and later transferred to a hospital, where his death was confirmed. As a result, the Prosecutor's Office launched an investigation to clarify the circumstances of the death.

While the police maintain the hypothesis of a possible self-inflicted injury, the family rejects this explanation. The boy's father questioned the police version and argued that the garment identified as the object used in the alleged act did not have the characteristics described by the authorities.

INVESTIGATIONS AND QUESTIONS
The seriousness of the case led the Ministry of the Interior to temporarily suspend the police chief of Manchay and five other officers while the investigations proceed.
At the same time, the Public Prosecutor's Office continues to gather testimonies, review records, and carry out procedures to determine what happened during the nearly 48 hours the teenager was in custody.

The Ombudsman's Office also intervened and requested that the investigations be conducted swiftly, independently, and transparently. The agency reiterated that the State has the responsibility to guarantee the physical integrity of every person who is detained.

Amid the debate, Congressman Alfredo Azurín called for respect for the presumption of innocence of the police officers involved and maintained that it is the Public Prosecutor's Office's responsibility to determine liability based on evidence.

For his part, General Eduardo Pérez Rocha indicated that there may have been negligence, noting that a minor cannot be placed in a holding cell. He also questioned the security conditions that allegedly existed during the teenager's time at the police station.
While the investigation continues and the community of Manchay maintains its demand for justice, the teenager's death continues to raise unanswered questions. The family has announced that it will continue participating in demonstrations and public events until the facts are clarified and the corresponding responsibilities are determined.

La Central Obrera Boliviana (COB) paraliza el centro de La Paz la tarde de este miércoles 6 de mayo de 2026, cuando sus militantes y los maestros urbanos detonan cachorros de dinamita y petardos contra los efectivos de la Unidad Táctica de Operaciones Policiales (UTOP) en las calles Socabaya y Potosí, a una cuadra de la plaza Murillo, mientras intentan ingresar a la Casa Grande del Pueblo para exigir atención a su pliego petitorio.
La movilización genera una tensión extrema en el centro paceño y afecta gravemente la circulación vehicular en la avenida Mariscal Santa Cruz y las calles Camacho y Colón, porque la policía responde con gases lacrimógenos y agentes químicos para dispersar a los manifestantes, lo que obliga a decenas de comerciantes a cerrar sus puestos de manera intempestiva y a los transeúntes a resguardarse en sus domicilios o lugares de trabajo.
A pesar de los refuerzos policiales y de los gases, los manifestantes (que incluyen delegados del Beni y de otras regiones) se reagrupan en la calle Yanacocha y la avenida Mariscal Santa Cruz, mientras el tránsito en el centro permanece colapsado y la tensión aumenta por el lanzamiento de petardos y explosivos de fabricación casera contra los uniformados.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
The Bolivian Workers' Central (COB) paralyzed downtown La Paz on the afternoon of Wednesday, May 6, 2026, when its members and urban teachers detonated sticks of dynamite and firecrackers at officers of the Tactical Police Operations Unit (UTOP) on Socabaya and Potosí streets, one block from Plaza Murillo, as they attempted to enter the Casa Grande del Pueblo (Government House) to demand attention to their list of demands.

The mobilization generated extreme tension in downtown La Paz and severely disrupted traffic on Mariscal Santa Cruz Avenue and Camacho and Colón streets, as police responded with tear gas and chemical agents to disperse the protesters. This forced dozens of vendors to abruptly close their stalls and pedestrians to seek refuge in their homes or workplaces.

Despite police reinforcements and tear gas, the protesters (including delegates from Beni and other regions) regrouped on Yanacocha Street and Mariscal Santa Cruz Avenue, while traffic in the city center remained gridlocked and tensions rose as firecrackers and homemade explosives were thrown at the officers.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Protest blocks area outside Shastrinagar Hospital in Dombivli, Kalyan, Maharashtra, India
MESSAGE_TEXT:
The protest was part of a wider show of support by the medical fraternity following the alleged assault on doctors at the KDMC-run Shastrinagar Hospital, where a Shiv Sena (Eknath Shinde faction) corporator and his associates were accused of attacking doctors and hospital staff.
Speaking during the protest, senior Surgical Oncologist Dr Shekhar Salkar said elected representatives who assault doctors while they are on duty should be disqualified from contesting elections and face stringent punishment.
"The message has to be very clear that nobody can take the law into their own hands. Justice in such cases must be quick. If action is delayed for years, the same cycle repeats. The Goa Medicare Act, 2013 provides good legal protection for doctors, but awareness and implementation need to improve. Prevention and proper security are equally important," he said.
Dr Salkar said doctors across Goa wore black ribbons to express solidarity with their colleagues in Maharashtra. He noted that while protests in Maharashtra had been withdrawn after the government accepted certain demands, the need for stronger protection and speedy justice remained.
He added that a memorandum had also been submitted to the Goa government, seeking effective implementation of safeguards for healthcare workers.
Senior Orthopedic surgeon Dr Dipchand Bhandare alleged that perpetrators of such attacks often escape meaningful punishment because of political patronage.
"Such people receive political protection. They may be arrested, and cases may be filed, but ultimately nothing happens to them. They continue doing what they do and even get elected again. Equally unfortunate is that people witnessing such incidents often remain silent instead of standing up for doctors," he said.
Gynaecologist Dr Sofia Rodrigues, who holds degrees in both medicine and law, said doctors remain one of the most vulnerable professional groups despite dedicating their lives to patient care.
"Doctors are too busy treating people to fight for their own rights. That has made us vulnerable. It is time for doctors to assert their rights through legal processes, RTIs, and other formal mechanisms. Caregivers and lifesavers should never be subjected to violence," she said.
The protest follows Monday's incident at Shastrinagar Hospital in Dombivli, where CCTV footage allegedly showed Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre and several others assaulting doctors inside the hospital.
According to hospital authorities, the incident began after a woman underwent a caesarean section. The newborn required specialised neonatal care after doctors found the umbilical cord wrapped twice around the baby's neck. However, with the hospital's Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) full, doctors advised the family to shift the infant to another medical facility.
Doctors alleged that after they were unable to answer repeated phone calls from the corporator while attending to patients, Mhatre arrived at the hospital with supporters and allegedly assaulted gynaecologists Dr Vaibhav Salunkhe and Dr Srushti Baviskar. Dr Salunkhe reportedly sustained injuries.
Two nurses who attempted to intervene were also allegedly pushed and manhandled. Doctors further alleged that the corporator threatened hospital staff before leaving the premises.
The incident was reported to the Vishnunagar Police, leading to the registration of an FIR.
Police have arrested Ramesh Mhatre, a three-time Shiv Sena corporator, along with several others in connection with the alleged assault. The accused have been booked under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Maharashtra Medicare Service Persons and Medicare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage or Loss to Property) Act, 2010.
Police had earlier arrested three of Mhatre's alleged associates for their role in the attack.
Following his arrest, the 72-year-old corporator was admitted to Thane Civil Hospital after reportedly complaining of chest pain and was kept under medical observation.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Κατασκευές, τρόφιμα-ποτά, επισιτισμός-τουρισμός και εμπόριο είναι οι βασικοί κλάδοι που προχωρούν σήμερα σε πανελλαδικές κινητοποιήσεις, στο πλαίσιο 24ωρης απεργίας.
Κεντρικό σύνθημα η αύξηση μισθών, οι καλύτερες συνθήκες εργασίας και η ενίσχυση με περισσότερα κονδύλια στους τομείς της Παιδείας και της Υγείας. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στις Συλλογικές Συμβάσεις Εργασίας και στην ανάγκη οι ρυθμίσεις τους να καλύπτουν όλους τους εργαζόμενους του κάθε κλάδου.
Στο Ηράκλειο η προσυγκέντρωση των ξενοδοχοϋπαλλήλων θα γίνει στο Εργατικό Κέντρο στις 10 το πρωί και θα ακολουθήσει μηχανοκίνητη πορεία μέχρι το αεροδρόμιο Νίκος Καζαντζάκης, όπου θα πραγματοποιηθεί η κύρια συγκέντρωση.
Αντίστοιχες δράσεις θα γίνουν στα Χανιά, στο Ρέθυμνο και σε άλλες περιοχές του νησιού.
Μετά την ολοκλήρωση της συγκέντρωσης θα ακολουθήσει μηχανοκίνητη πορεία σε τουριστικές περιοχές του Νομού Ηρακλείου.
Οι εργαζόμενοι του τουρισμού και του επισιτισμού διεκδικούν:
• Επέκταση της χρονικής διάρκειας του ταμείου ανεργίας για τους εποχικούς εργαζόμενους
• Κατάργηση της προπληρωμένης κάρτας
• Αφορολόγητο όριο στις 12.000 ευρώ
• Να μην φορολογείται το επίδομα ανεργίας
• Επαναφορά του εφάπαξ στην 20ετία
• Επαναφορά των ΒΑΕ
• Ουσιαστική στελέχωση των ελεγκτικών μηχανισμών
• Καλύτερες συνθήκες εργασίας στους χώρους δουλειάς
• Πραγματική εφαρμογή της ψηφιακής κάρτας εργασίας
• Προστασία των εργασιακών και ασφαλιστικών δικαιωμάτων
Απεργία οικοδόμων
Σε 24ωρη απεργία κατεβαίνουν σήμερα και οι οικοδόμοι, την ώρα που 13 άνθρωποι έχασαν τη ζωή τους στον κλάδο των κατασκευών από την αρχή του έτους.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Leamington faces rail disruption amid strikes
Passengers using Leamington Spa Railway Station are being warned of major disruption this weekend, as strike action by members of the TSSA union affects West Midlands Railway services.
A significantly reduced timetable will operate on Friday 10 July and Saturday 11 July, with all routes via Birmingham Snow Hill suspended on both days.
No trains will run on the Nuneaton to Leamington Spa route.
The industrial action is part of an ongoing dispute over rest day working payments.
Rail union TSSA says its members have not been offered the same agreement available to workers represented by other unions.
On Friday, West Midlands Railway will only be operating three routes.
No trains will run after around 7pm, with many final departures leaving significantly earlier.
Alongside all routes via Birmingham Snow Hill, there will also be no services on the Camp Hill line, Nuneaton to Leamington Spa route, Birmingham New Street to Hereford route, or Birmingham New Street to Shrewsbury route on either strike day.
Chiltern Railway routes are expected to be running as normal.
TSSA general secretary Maryam Eslamdoust said: "These strikes will go ahead as planned because our members have not been given parity with those in other unions – a perfectly reasonable demand.
"The last round of industrial action caused a significant impact to services and the same will happen this time around."
She added: "Of course, as ever our union only takes strike action as a last resort, so we hope that our demands can be met in coming days to avoid any more disruption."
West Midlands Railway is advising customers to check journey planners before travelling.
Tickets dated 10 or 11 July can be used instead on services running on 9 or 12 July, while passengers whose trains are cancelled will be entitled to a full refund.
Jonny Wiseman, WMR customer experience director, said: "We are disappointed TSSA has called further unnecessary strike action which is set to cause significant disruption for our customers. We are working hard to reach a resolution to this dispute and urge TSSA to continue talks.
"We are sorry for the inconvenience this will cause our customers and are doing everything we can to minimise the impact as much as possible.
"If the strike action does go ahead, we will be running a significantly reduced timetable on both dates. Customers are advised to check before they travel by visiting journey planners and our website."

Girona evita el colapso a las puertas del ‘Temps de Flors’: desconvocada la huelga de limpieza
El pacto entre Girona+Neta y el Ayuntamiento ha sido ratificado por el 82% de los trabajadores de la plantilla y pone fin al paro del servicio de tres días
Redacción| jueves, 7 de mayo de 2026, 10:40
La ciudad de Girona respira aliviada. A pocos días de afrontar uno de los eventos más emblemáticos y multitudinarios del año, el ‘Temps de Flors’, la amenaza de una huelga en el servicio de recogida de basuras ha quedado finalmente descartada. La plantilla de Girona+Neta ha aprobado por amplia mayoría el preacuerdo alcanzado entre el comité de empresa y la dirección, lo que permite recuperar la normalidad y evitar un escenario que preocupaba tanto a vecinos como al sector turístico y comercial.
La votación entre los trabajadores se saldó con un respaldo contundente: 138 votos a favor, 30 en contra y un voto en blanco entre los 169 empleados participantes. El resultado supone la desconvocatoria inmediata de la huelga y el regreso al trabajo desde la noche de este miércoles.
Un acuerdo que rebaja la tensión tras semanas de incertidumbre
El conflicto laboral había generado inquietud en la ciudad, especialmente por coincidir con una de las celebraciones más importantes del calendario gerundense. El portavoz del comité, Gregori Soto, valoró positivamente el acuerdo, aunque reclamó tanto a la empresa como al Ayuntamiento que “cumplan con los compromisos adquiridos”.
Por su parte, el alcalde de Girona, Lluc Salellas, celebró que las negociaciones hayan llegado “a buen puerto”, aunque reconoció que la situación “se podría haber evitado”. El consistorio pide ahora rapidez para recuperar plenamente el funcionamiento habitual del servicio de limpieza.
Subida salarial y seis meses para negociar nuevos horarios
Entre las medidas pactadas destaca una subida salarial del 1% para este año, asumida por la empresa, además de la apertura de un periodo de negociación de seis meses para abordar posibles cambios en la organización de horarios y turnos.
El comité considera fundamental que cualquier modificación se haga desde el diálogo y escuchando a la plantilla. “Los trabajadores pueden aportar soluciones reales para mejorar el servicio”, defendió Soto, quien insistió en que la experiencia diaria de los empleados puede ayudar a optimizar la limpieza urbana.
Vacaciones y festivos: los trabajadores mantienen sus derechos
Uno de los puntos más sensibles de la negociación giraba alrededor de las vacaciones y el trabajo en días festivos. Finalmente, el acuerdo mantiene intacto el modelo actual y garantiza que trabajar en festivos seguirá siendo voluntario.
Desde el comité subrayan que han logrado frenar cualquier intento de limitar derechos consolidados. “Las vacaciones y la voluntariedad en festivos son irrenunciables”, remarcaron los representantes sindicales, apelando al marco que establece el Estatuto de los Trabajadores.
Más estabilidad para el personal eventual
Otro de los avances más destacados afecta al personal temporal, una reivindicación histórica dentro de la plantilla. Hasta ahora, muchos trabajadores eventuales no tenían garantías claras de continuidad laboral. El nuevo acuerdo introduce criterios objetivos para facilitar su incorporación progresiva como trabajadores fijos.
La antigüedad será el principal criterio para consolidar plazas, tomando como referencia la primera fecha de contratación temporal. De esta manera, a medida que se produzcan jubilaciones o bajas definitivas, estos empleados podrán integrarse en la plantilla estable.
La medida supone un importante paso adelante en términos de seguridad laboral y estabilidad profesional para decenas de trabajadores.
Mejoras sociales y económicas en el nuevo convenio
El pacto también incorpora mejoras económicas adicionales. La póliza de seguro de vida aumentará en 400 euros por cada año de vigencia del convenio, mientras que el complemento vinculado a la jubilación crecerá 35 euros anuales entre 2026 y 2028.
Además, en los casos de jubilación parcial, dicho premio podrá ser percibido por los herederos legítimos, una de las demandas que permanecía encima de la mesa durante las negociaciones.
Girona recupera la normalidad antes del gran evento floral
La desconvocatoria de la huelga evita un impacto directo sobre la imagen de Girona a las puertas de la celebración del ‘Temps de Flors’, un acontecimiento que cada año atrae a miles de visitantes y que representa uno de los principales escaparates culturales y turísticos de la ciudad.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Girona avoids collapse on the eve of 'Temps de Flors': cleaning strike called off
The agreement between Girona+Neta and the City Council has been ratified by 82% of the workforce, ending the three-day service stoppage
Editorial Staff | Thursday, May 7, 2026, 10:40 AM
The city of Girona breathes a sigh of relief. Just days before one of the most emblematic and well-attended events of the year, 'Temps de Flors' (Flower Festival), the threat of a garbage collection strike has finally been averted. The Girona+Neta workforce overwhelmingly approved the preliminary agreement reached between the works council and management, allowing a return to normalcy and avoiding a scenario that worried residents, as well as the tourism and commercial sectors.

The vote among the workers resulted in resounding support: 138 votes in favor, 30 against, and one abstention among the 169 participating employees. The result means the immediate cancellation of the strike and a return to work starting Wednesday night.

An agreement that eases tensions after weeks of uncertainty.
The labor dispute had generated concern in the city, especially as it coincided with one of the most important celebrations on Girona's calendar. The committee spokesperson, Gregori Soto, welcomed the agreement, although he urged both the company and the City Council to "honor their commitments."

For his part, the mayor of Girona, Lluc Salellas, celebrated that the negotiations had "reached a successful conclusion," although he acknowledged that the situation "could have been avoided." The City Council is now calling for swift action to fully restore normal operations to the cleaning service.

Salary increase and six months to negotiate new schedules.
Among the agreed-upon measures is a 1% salary increase for this year, accepted by the company, as well as the opening of a six-month negotiation period to address potential changes in the organization of schedules and shifts.

The committee considers it essential that any modifications be made through dialogue and by listening to the staff. “The workers can contribute real solutions to improve the service,” argued Soto, who insisted that the employees' daily experience can help optimize urban cleaning.
Vacations and holidays: workers maintain their rights
One of the most sensitive points of the negotiation revolved around vacations and working on holidays. Ultimately, the agreement maintains the current model intact and guarantees that working on holidays will remain voluntary.

The committee emphasizes that they have managed to stop any attempt to limit established rights. “Vacations and voluntary work on holidays are non-negotiable,” stressed the union representatives, appealing to the framework established by the Workers' Statute.

More stability for temporary staff
Another of the most significant advances affects temporary staff, a long-standing demand within the workforce. Until now, many temporary workers lacked clear guarantees of job security. The new agreement introduces objective criteria to facilitate their gradual incorporation as permanent employees.

Seniority will be the primary criterion for securing permanent positions, based on the initial date of temporary employment. This way, as retirements or permanent departures occur, these employees will be able to join the permanent staff.

This measure represents a significant step forward in terms of job security and professional stability for dozens of workers.

Social and economic improvements in the new agreement
The agreement also includes additional economic improvements. The life insurance policy will increase by €400 for each year the agreement is in effect, while the retirement supplement will increase by €35 annually between 2026 and 2028. Furthermore, in cases of partial retirement, this supplement can be received by the legal heirs, one of the demands that remained on the table during negotiations.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Alrededor de 500 trabajadores de Iberdrola Grupo en Castilla-La Mancha secundaron este viernes la huelga general convocada por UGT FICA y CCOO Industria, la segunda de este tipo en la historia de la compañía, en una jornada de protesta que discurrió con concentraciones en Toledo, Albacete y Motilla del Palancar (Cuenca). Los sindicatos cifraron el seguimiento en el 90% de la plantilla sujeta a convenio, una vez descontado el 60% de trabajadores que cubrieron los servicios mínimos establecidos y el personal de alta dirección.
La movilización se produjo exactamente un año después de la primera huelga general en la historia de Iberdrola Grupo, y tiene como detonante el bloqueo absoluto en el que, según las organizaciones sindicales, se encuentra la negociación del convenio colectivo desde que se iniciaron las conversaciones hace 16 meses . La tensión alcanzó su punto álgido esta semana cuando, según los representantes de los trabajadores, la dirección de la empresa realizó por primera vez una propuesta concreta sobre el convenio, lo que los sindicatos interpretan como una prueba del inmovilismo de la compañía.
La responsable de la sección sindical de UGT FICA en Iberdrola Grupo en la región, Olga Arribas , fue una de las portavoces de la concentración en Toledo. Subrayó que la reclamación de los trabajadores no es equiparar salarios entre categorías, sino garantizar que las retribuciones se ajusten a la inflación y a lo acordado en el marco estatal de referencia. "Pedimos que se haga justicia con nuestras retribuciones. No demandamos que todos ganemos lo mismo, simplemente que cobremos acorde a las subidas al Índice de Precios al Consumo y a lo establecido en el Acuerdo Nacional por el Empleo y la Negociación Colectiva (AENC)", declaró Arribas ante los concentrados.
La brecha entre salarios y beneficios, en el centro del conflicto La sindicalista puso el acento en la contradicción que, a juicio de los trabajadores, representa la situación actual: mientras los sueldos de la plantilla crecen a un ritmo de apenas el 0,7% anual , Iberdrola Grupo cerró el último cuatrimestre con 6.285 millones de euros de beneficios netos . "Algo que no se entiende si tenemos en cuenta los 6.285 millones de euros de beneficios netos que obtuvo Iberdrola Grupo en el último cuatrimestre", señaló Arribas, quien insistió en que el seguimiento del paro entre quienes están bajo convenio alcanzó el 90% .
Por su parte, el representante de CCOO Industria en Iberdrola, Ignacio Tirado , calificó de "inaceptable" la propuesta presentada por la empresa y recordó que la compañía "tiene millones de beneficios". Tirado reclamó que esa riqueza generada repercuta en los empleados a través de un reparto más justo de la retribución. El objetivo de los sindicatos, según explicó, es "llegar a un acuerdo que garantice el poder adquisitivo de los empleados y empleadas".
Un conflicto que escala en toda España La huelga del pasado jueves no se limitó a Castilla-La Mancha. La convocatoria afectó a los 10.000 trabajadores de Iberdrola Grupo en toda España, lo que la convierte en el mayor pulso laboral de la compañía en su historia reciente. La pérdida acumulada de poder adquisitivo de la plantilla, estimada por los sindicatos en un 16% en los últimos cinco años , es el argumento central con el que UGT FICA y CCOO Industria justifican la intensidad de las protestas y la necesidad de desbloquear cuanto antes la negociación colectiva.
La doble condición de Iberdrola —empresa de referencia en el sector energético español y una de las más rentables del Ibex 35— añade presión política y mediática al conflicto. Con la negociación abierta y la dirección sin haber formalizado hasta ahora una propuesta sobre el convenio, los sindicatos no descartan nuevas movilizaciones si no se producen avances en las próximas semanas.

TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Around 500 Iberdrola Group workers in Castilla-La Mancha joined the general strike called by the UGT FICA and CCOO Industria unions this Friday, the second of its kind in the company's history. The day of protest included demonstrations in Toledo, Albacete, and Motilla del Palancar (Cuenca). The unions estimated that 90% of the workforce covered by the collective bargaining agreement participated, after deducting the 60% of workers who covered the established minimum services and senior management personnel.

The mobilization occurred exactly one year after the first general strike in the history of Iberdrola Group and was triggered by the complete deadlock in collective bargaining negotiations, according to the unions, which have been in place since talks began 16 months ago. Tensions reached their peak this week when, according to workers' representatives, the company's management made its first concrete proposal regarding the collective bargaining agreement, which the unions interpret as proof of the company's intransigence.

Olga Arribas, head of the UGT FICA union section at Iberdrola Group in the region, was one of the spokespeople for the demonstration in Toledo. She emphasized that the workers' demand is not to equalize salaries across categories, but rather to guarantee that compensation is adjusted for inflation and in accordance with the national framework agreement. "We are asking for fair compensation. We are not demanding that everyone earn the same, simply that we be paid in line with increases in the Consumer Price Index and what is established in the National Agreement for Employment and Collective Bargaining (AENC)," Arribas told the demonstrators.

The gap between wages and benefits at the heart of the conflict. The union representative emphasized the contradiction that, in the workers' view, the current situation represents: while employee salaries are growing at a rate of barely 0.7% annually, Iberdrola Group closed the last quarter with €6.285 billion in net profits. "Something that is incomprehensible considering the €6.285 billion in net profits that Iberdrola Group obtained in the last quarter," Arribas pointed out, insisting that the strike participation rate among those covered by the collective bargaining agreement reached 90%.

For his part, the representative of CCOO Industry at Iberdrola, Ignacio Tirado, described the proposal presented by the company as "unacceptable" and reminded everyone that the company "has millions in profits." Tirado demanded that this generated wealth benefit employees through a fairer distribution of compensation. The unions' objective, as explained, is "to reach an agreement that guarantees the purchasing power of employees."

A conflict escalating across Spain: Last Thursday's strike was not limited to Castilla-La Mancha. The action affected all 10,000 Iberdrola Group employees throughout Spain, making it the company's largest labor dispute in recent history. The accumulated loss of purchasing power for the workforce, estimated by the unions at 16% over the last five years, is the central argument used by UGT FICA and CCOO Industria to justify the intensity of the protests and the need to unblock collective bargaining as soon as possible.
Iberdrola's dual status—as a leading company in the Spanish energy sector and one of the most profitable on the Ibex 35—adds political and media pressure to the conflict. With negotiations ongoing and management yet to formally present a proposal for the collective bargaining agreement, the unions are not ruling out further protests if no progress is made in the coming weeks.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Bei einer Demonstration gegen den neuen Wehrdienst ist in München eine 20-jährige Teilnehmerin vorübergehend von der Polizei festgenommen worden. Anlass war ein Plakat mit der Aufschrift „Merz stirb selbst an der Ostfront“. Das teilte die Polizei München auf Anfrage von Apollo News mit. Die Frau stammt aus München und war Teilnehmerin der Versammlung. Gegen sie wurde ein Ermittlungsverfahren eingeleitet.
Nach Angaben der Polizei wurde sie kurzzeitig mitgenommen, um ihre Identität festzustellen. Im Zuge dessen sei es unter weiteren Teilnehmern zu Unruhe gekommen. Die Beamten hätten deshalb „unmittelbaren Zwang“ anwenden müssen. Weitere Festnahmen habe es nicht gegeben. Während der Demonstration wurden nach Angaben der Polizei außerdem Bengalos und Handfackeln gezündet. Tatverdächtige seien bislang nicht bekannt. Abgesehen davon sei die Versammlung ruhig verlaufen.
In mehreren Städten hatten Jugendliche, linke Gruppen und Friedensinitiativen zu Schulstreiks und Kundgebungen aufgerufen. An der Münchner Demonstration nahmen nach Polizeiangaben rund 600 Personen teil. In Berlin sprach die Polizei von rund 1.200 Teilnehmern, in Hamburg nannte sie rund 2.300 Teilnehmer.
Hintergrund der Proteste ist das seit Jahresbeginn geltende Gesetz über den neuen Wehrdienst. Es sieht unter anderem vor, dass junge Männer einen Fragebogen der Bundeswehr verpflichtend beantworten müssen. Männer, die ab dem 1. Januar 2008 geboren wurden, sollen zudem wieder verpflichtend gemustert werden.
Bei den Protesten kam es auch in anderen Städten zu Auseinandersetzungen um Anti-Merz-Parolen. Nach Darstellung der Streikorganisatoren gegenüber der Jungen Welt verlangte die Polizei in Essen unter Androhung von Anzeigen, ein Banner mit der Aufschrift „Merz leck Eier“ herunterzunehmen. In Münster seien demnach Personalien von Demonstranten aufgenommen worden, die dieselbe Parole riefen. In Wuppertal habe die Polizei wegen entsprechender Schilder mit Strafanzeigen gedroht.
Der Slogan war bereits im März überregional bekannt geworden. Damals hatte die Berliner Polizei gegen einen 18-Jährigen ermittelt, der bei einer Schülerdemonstration ein Plakat mit der Aufschrift „MERZ LECK EIER“ getragen hatte. Das Plakat wurde beschlagnahmt. Die Polizei leitete Ermittlungen wegen des Anfangsverdachts der „üblen Nachrede und Verleumdung gegen Personen des politischen Lebens“ ein.
Bereits vor dem Streik hatten zwei Jugendliche aus der Kieler Schulstreikbewegung in einem Instagram-Video von angeblichen Ansprachen durch Verfassungsschutz und Bundeskriminalamt berichtet. Gegenüber der Berliner Zeitung schilderte einer der beiden, auf dem Schulweg von einem Mann angesprochen worden zu sein, der sich als Mitarbeiter des Verfassungsschutzes ausgegeben habe.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
A 20-year-old woman was temporarily detained by police during a demonstration against the new compulsory military service in Munich. The reason was a poster reading "Merz die on the Eastern Front." Munich police confirmed this to Apollo News. The woman, a Munich resident, was a participant in the rally. Criminal proceedings have been initiated against her.

According to police, she was briefly taken into custody to establish her identity. During this process, unrest broke out among other participants, forcing officers to use "direct force." No further arrests were made. Police also reported that flares and hand-held torches were set off during the demonstration. No suspects have yet been identified. Aside from this, the rally remained peaceful.

In several cities, youth groups, left-wing groups, and peace initiatives had called for school strikes and rallies. Police reported approximately 600 participants in the Munich demonstration. In Berlin, police estimated around 1,200 participants, and in Hamburg, around 2,300.

The protests stem from the new law on compulsory military service, which came into effect at the beginning of the year. Among other things, it stipulates that young men must complete a questionnaire from the German Armed Forces. Men born on or after January 1, 2008, are also subject to mandatory conscription.

The protests also saw clashes in other cities over anti-Merz slogans. According to the strike organizers, speaking to the newspaper Junge Welt, police in Essen demanded, under threat of legal action, that a banner reading "Merz lick balls" be taken down. In Münster, the personal details of demonstrators shouting the same slogan were reportedly recorded. In Wuppertal, police threatened criminal charges for displaying similar signs.

The slogan had already gained nationwide attention in March. At that time, Berlin police investigated an 18-year-old who had carried a sign reading "MERZ LICK EGGS" at a student demonstration. The sign was confiscated. Police have launched an investigation on suspicion of "defamation and slander against public figures."

Even before the strike, two teenagers from the Kiel school strike movement reported in an Instagram video about alleged approaches from the Office for the Protection of the Constitution and the Federal Criminal Police Office. Speaking to the Berliner Zeitung, one of the two described being approached on his way to school by a man who claimed to be an employee of the Office for the Protection of the Constitution.

Residents blocked the Kohlu-Sibi highway in Balochistan’s Kohlu district in protest against a severe shortage of drinking water, accusing the The Public Health Engineering Department (PHED) and district administration of failing to address the crisis.
People from several areas, including Mir Hazar Wadh, took part in the protest and suspended traffic on the highway.
The protesters said residents were struggling to meet their basic need for clean drinking water, adding that the relevant authorities had failed to take effective measures despite being repeatedly informed of the situation.
They said officials from the PHED and other institutions had been approached several times prior to the demonstration, but no practical progress had been made, forcing residents to block the highway.

'Government refuses to listen': Offaly Paramedics participate in National Ambulance Service strike
Offaly Paramedics were part of the National Ambulance Service (NAS) personnel who staged a 24-hour strike on Tuesday, May 12 as a long-running row over pay continues to escalate.
Paramedics took to the picket lines from 8am on Tuesday morning at various ambulance dispatch centres across the country for a period of 24 hours.
Advertisement
Advertisement
They are calling on HSE management to engage with their unions to address this dispute and to implement the introduction of enhanced pay scales for ambulance personnel while also addressing historic pay injustice.
Among those on the picket line in Offaly was recently retired paramedic, Barry Flynn. Mr. Flynn, who was part of the Tullamore Ambulance Station for 26 years said he was there to support his former colleagues because, like them, he has been part of the ambulance service's modernisation over the past 15 to 20 years without reward.
Mr. Flynn offered an insight into what the modernisation has entailed for paramedics. He pointed out that year on year, there has been training which involved on-line modules, pre-training study and classroom sessions where new medications and new clinical skills have been introduced.
Advertisement
Advertisement
This has moved the ambulance service from a basic patient transport service to a clinical service where patients are now treated in their homes and stabilised before being transferred to the hospital, leading to better patient outcomes.
These skills include crews regularly administering increased medications, including injections, and making clinical interventions en route to the hospital.
Additionally, Ambulance crews regularly make decisions regarding the appropriate hospital for the patient, which often involves having telephone conversations from the patient’s home with cardiologists and consultants.
Mr. Flynn explained: “They respect our medical judgement in making such decisions. The general public also respects what we do, and where we have come from, it seems to be that it's just the HSE and the politicians who are dismissive.”
Advertisement
Advertisement
He continued: “For years, ambulance staff have been told to embrace the new skills and training, and the rewards would follow. Crews gladly took on the new skills and medications because they would benefit many of the patients, but they feel a line must be drawn somewhere.”
The crux of this, according to Mr. Flynn, is that a line was drawn following an independent report in 2020 which agreed that there should be a financial reward for the years of extra training, but that pay increase has never materialised.
The HSE are seeking reforms of the service before they introduce any pay increases. However, according to Mr. Flynn, many non-clinical reforms have already taken place during the last number of years also.
These include medication management, how staff book annual leave, how crews submit and view some of their wages, new ambulance technology and the recording of patient care reports.
Advertisement
Advertisement
“We are not anti-reform, but any suggestion that there has been no reform up until now is just not accurate,” said the retired medic.
Mr. Flynn also dismissed suggestions that the strike shows a lack of empathy by ambulance crews.
He pointed out that crews don't want to be on strike. "Our nature is to care for people," he said, adding that many ambulance staff choose to respond voluntarily in their own communities when they are off-duty.
The HSE expressed concerns ahead of the strike about the significant impact the industrial action is likely to have on ambulance services on Tuesday.
Advertisement
Advertisement
They added that people may need to consider making their own way to emergency departments during the 24-hour stoppage.
However, Mr. Flynn confirmed that certain contingency plans were in place throughout the duration of the strike in case of emergency including three ambulances visible at the picket line in Tullamore that were ready to be dispatched if needed.
Independent TD for Offaly, Carol Nolan also weighed in on the ongoing dispute as she stated that the “ambulance strike is the latest example of a Government that refuses to listen.”
She described the 24-hour ambulance service strike as “yet another predictable and entirely preventable crisis caused by years of government inaction on frontline health workers.”
Advertisement
Advertisement
Deputy Nolan was speaking as ambulance crews from the National Ambulance Service took part in industrial action over pay and conditions.
The independent TD expressed: “This strike is not a surprise, but it is the direct result of a government and HSE that have repeatedly failed to listen to the very people keeping our health service alive. Just as we saw with the fuel protestors, warnings were ignored, frustrations were allowed to build for years, and now patients in Offaly, the Midlands and elsewhere are paying the price.”
She added: “Many TDs, including those on the government benches, have been well aware for years that ambulance staff were reaching breaking point. The 2020 Roles and Responsibilities Review promised proper pay scales, recognition of advanced qualifications and a fair wage increase. Six years later, nothing has been delivered.”
“Despite enormous levels of professional burnout, staff have been patient, professional and reasonable, but they now feel that they have been taken for granted.”
Advertisement
Advertisement
Deputy Nolan also highlighted the added pressure already visible in the region, noting that Midlands Regional Hospital Portlaoise is currently experiencing exceptionally high patient admission numbers, with non-urgent cases facing significant delays in the Emergency Department.
Management there is actively urging people to use GP, pharmacist or out-of-hours services instead.
Deputy Nolan conveyed: “This is the reality on the ground right now, even before the strike. The system is already under strain and the government’s failure to resolve this long-running dispute is only making things worse for patients and their families in Offaly and across the Midlands.”
Advertisement
Advertisement
The Offaly TD pointed to her own long record of supporting ambulance staff. In 2019 she publicly highlighted the “entirely unacceptable” conditions they were being forced to work under, including excessive overtime, outdated vehicles and a refusal by the HSE to properly engage with their representatives.
At that time, she called on the then-Minister for Health Simon Harris and the HSE to act before a national strike became inevitable.
“Seven years later the same issues remain unresolved. That tells you everything you need to know about this government’s attitude to frontline workers,” the Offaly TD said.
Deputy Nolan concluded: “I stand with the ambulance crews today. They deserve fair pay, proper recognition and safe working conditions. The government must immediately implement the 2020 review recommendations, engage meaningfully with the unions and end this completely avoidable crisis before further strikes take place.”
Tuesday’s strike was the first of a series of strikes planned if the dispute is not resolved. There are also plans for a 48-hour stoppage beginning on May 19 and a 72-hour stoppage on May 26.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
"Le moindre e-mail d'un parent mécontent va entraîner une suspension" : nouvel appel à la grève dès lundi dans le périscolaire à Paris
Les animateurs sont "en plein craquage", relaie un délégué syndical. En cause, le plan du nouveau maire de Paris, Emmanuel Grégoire, et le climat de suspicion généralisée contre les agents depuis la révélations de plusieurs violences physiques ou sexuelles dans les établissements.
Les sept syndicats des employés du périscolaire à Paris appellent à la grève à partir de lundi 11 mai et jusqu'au 22 mai, rapportent France Inter et France Culture. L'intersyndicale n'est pas convaincue par le plan à 20 millions d'euros du nouveau maire Emmanuel Grégoire. Elle dénonce aussi un climat de suspicion généralisée qui accable les agents depuis les révélations de violences physiques ou sexuelles à l'automne 2025.
"Le moindre e-mail d'un papa ou d'une maman mécontent va entraîner une suspension", affirme Éric Leclerc, directeur d'accueil périscolaire et délégué au sein du syndicat Supap-FSU sur France Inter. Les animateurs sont devenus très fébriles, "en plein craquage", relate-t-il. "Un exemple : deux enfants qui vont se battre dans la cour de récréation, l'animateur va être devant un dilemme. Est-ce que je sépare les enfants au risque de saisir l'épaule ou le bras d'un enfant et d'être accusé de violence ? Un enfant de maternelle qui va avoir un accident, un pipi, est-ce que je le change ?"
Suspendu pour avoir élevé la voix ?
"Ce qu'on conteste, c'est que dès qu'il y a un signalement sur quoi que ce soit, on suspend automatiquement", abonde au micro de France Culture, Alexandre Herzog, directeur périscolaire d’une école parisienne et délégué syndical à la CGT. "Aujourd'hui, des collègues sont suspendus parce qu'ils ont élevé la voix sans même hurler sur un enfant. On ne peut pas traiter de la même manière un agent qui aurait élevé la voix ou crié ou attrapé de la mauvaise manière un enfant, et un autre agent qui, sciemment, aurait nui à l'intégrité physique d'un enfant", déplore-t-il.
"Quand un enfant parle, c'est qu'il a signalé des faits et il est normal qu'une institution prenne des mesures conservatoires le temps de vérifier les faits", rétorque Barka Zerouali. Celle qui a cofondé le collectif #MeTooÉcole en novembre 2025 ne comprend pas les revendications des syndicats. Selon elle, demander la fin des suspensions systématiques des agents quand les signalements ne portent pas sur des violences sexuelles équivaut à mettre en doute la parole des enfants.
"Suspendre temporairement un adulte, ce n'est pas le condamner, c'est appliquer un principe de précaution."
Barka Zerouali, cofondatrice le collectif #MeTooÉcoleà France Culture
C'est "ce pourquoi on se bat depuis plusieurs mois, une tolérance zéro", ajoute Barka Zerouali.
Pour la mairie, l'idée est de rétablir la confiance
Contactée par France Inter, la mairie de Paris assume de ne prendre aucun risque. "C'est un principe de précaution puisque derrière, il peut y avoir une plainte qui est déposée et donc on suspend le temps d'éclaircir la situation", explique Anne-Claire Boux, adjointe au maire de Paris en charge des affaires scolaires et de la petite enfance. Les mesures prises par la Ville de Paris doivent "permettre de pouvoir rétablir cette confiance".
L'élue se dit cependant prête à plus de discernement quand il s'agit de gestes brusques, plus que de violence physique. Elle promet aussi des annonces en juillet sur les conditions de travail, la réduction de la précarité et autres revendications syndicales. Les deux tiers des 16 000 agents du périscolaire parisien sont des vacataires. Les syndicats s'attendent à un mouvement bien suivi pour cette grève, rapporte France Inter. Chaque agent peut ne débrayer qu'une heure par jour, à midi par exemple, ce qui suffit à désorganiser l'accueil des enfants. Les syndicats prévoient également de manifester le 19 mai devant la Direction des affaires scolaires (Dasco) de la ville de Paris.
Depuis le début de l'année 2026, 78 agents de la ville de Paris ont été suspendus dans les écoles parisiennes, dont 31 pour des suspicions de violences sexuelles, des chiffres traduisant un caractère "systémique", selon Emmanuel Grégoire. "Priorité absolue" de son début de mandat, le nouveau maire socialiste de Paris se rend lundi à l'école Saint-Dominique (7e arrondissement) pour échanger avec le personnel et les familles, après le dépôt d'une trentaine de plaintes pour viols, agressions sexuelles et violences sur des enfants de cette école maternelle.
