TRANSLATED_TEXT:
The day began with a peaceful march to the Gerona neighborhood in Zone 1 of the capital city, where the Public Prosecutor's Office headquarters is located, to reject Consuelo Porras's administration and denounce the criminalization of the student movement. During the protest, they highlighted the criminal proceedings opened following the fraud in the USAC rector's office and demanded that the new administration of the Public Prosecutor's Office put an end to the actions against students, journalists, indigenous communities, and human rights defenders.

By Alexander Valdéz
Early Saturday morning, a group of students from the University of San Carlos held a peaceful march that traveled through various streets and avenues in Zone 1 of the capital city until reaching the Gerona neighborhood, in front of the Public Prosecutor's Office. With banners, slogans, and messages of rejection, the students indicated that the demonstration sought to highlight the discontent with Consuelo Porras's eight years in office.

During the demonstration, students denounced the criminalization of the student movement at the University of San Carlos (USAC) that opposes the appointment of Walter Mazariegos as rector. They also recalled the criminal proceedings initiated against students and professionals following the occupation of university facilities in 2022.

“The purpose of this march is to demand that the new administration of the Public Prosecutor's Office cease criminalizing students, human rights defenders, Indigenous peoples, environmentalists, and journalists,” they stated.

The student mobilization joined another demonstration organized by citizens and civil society organizations outside the Public Prosecutor's Office, where a symbolic farewell to Porras's administration took place. They also demanded that the new authorities of the Public Prosecutor's Office not replicate the patterns of criminalization and persecution denounced in recent years against students, justice officials, journalists, activists, and human rights defenders.

In Quetzaltenango
Just as in Gerona, downtown Quetzaltenango became a second meeting point for various social groups, students, Indigenous authorities, and citizens who held protests against Porras's tenure as Attorney General. With banners, slogans, and public statements, attendees expressed their discontent with the years of criminalization and persecution against various social and political sectors of the country.

In their speeches, they demanded that the new Attorney General guarantee respect for human rights, halt judicial persecution, and create conditions for the safe return of journalists, human rights defenders, and justice officials who remain in exile.

New Attorney General
Starting this Sunday, Gabriel García Luna will assume leadership of the Public Prosecutor's Office, with high expectations for an end to criminalization and the restoration of trust in the justice system. Porras's departure comes amid strong national and international criticism of the direction the Public Prosecutor's Office has taken in recent years, marked by decisions that have led to an authoritarian backslide.

Civil society has pointed out that during this eight-year administration, the prosecutorial career path was weakened, corruption investigations were dismantled, and criminalization processes were promoted against justice officials, journalists, activists, human rights defenders, and students of the University of San Carlos.

Changes and restructurings were a constant during Porras's tenure. Prosecutors and former prosecutors consistently denounced dismissals, transfers, and reassignments of specialized personnel without prior disciplinary proceedings, especially against employees considered inconvenient for the administration.

Gabriel García Luna's first appointments at the Public Prosecutor's Office
Along with the new Attorney General, new officials will also assume key positions. Among the names that began to emerge this weekend are: Edwin Santiago Chavajay Chavajay will be the Secretary General; Shirley García Ovalle will head the Secretariat of International Affairs and Cooperation; Salvador Guzmán will assume the position of First Deputy Secretary General; and Rony López Galindo will lead the Secretariat of Information Technology Affairs.

The artistic expression activities will continue throughout Saturday afternoon and evening until midnight. At that time, fireworks will be set off to announce the change of leadership at the Public Prosecutor's Office.

- Die diskutierten sozialpolitischen Vorhaben der Bundesregierung, die aus seiner Sicht zentrale Säulen des Sozialstaats – Kranken-, Renten- und Pflegeversicherung – weiter schwächen.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Garbage piles up after sanitation workers resume indefinite strike from July 7 in Doraha, Punjab, India
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Doraha raises a stink as sanitation workers’ stir enters Day 7
Doraha residents say heaps of garbage can be seen at collection points, on roads and in residential areas
Garbage once again started piling up in Doraha after sanitation workers resumed their indefinite strike from July 7 in view of the state government “failing to meet their demands that had been accepted”.
Earlier, sanitation workers’ union was on strike for 15 days, from June 6 to June 21.
This time around, garbage has not been lifted from the town for seven days now, presenting a sorry state of affairs.
Residents say heaps of garbage can be seen at collection points, on roads and in residential areas. While the protesters are adamant to continue their strike, come what may, residents urged the state government to intervene before the situation gets out of control.
Aam Aadmi Party MLA from Payal Manwinder Singh Giaspura, however, feigned ignorance and said he was not aware sanitation workers were on strike. “As far as their demands are concerned, they have already been accepted and shall be granted soon,” the MLA added.
The sanitation workers said they had already waited for nearly a month for fulfilment of their demands.
“We were promised that sewer workers and sweepers who have worked under private contractors for three years will now be brought under state government employment. Salaries would be credited into their bank accounts without any middleman. The monthly salary was to be raised to Rs 15,100. We were also assured the workers would now be entitled to statutory benefits, including provident fund, group health insurance, gratuity, maternity leaves and casual leaves, as per the law. The government also assured any employee who completes ten years of service will be regularised and absorbed into government service. The government assured fulfilment at the earliest, but nothing has materialised on the ground,” said Rocky Sahota, district secretary, Safai Sewak Union, Punjab.
“We waited patiently and more than a month passed without any positive signals. Hence, we resumed our strike,” he added.
“We don’t like the public facing inconvenience but we are a part of the society as well and have every right to fight for our just demands. We are out of the most deprived sections and need immediate government attention. We have been working day in and day out in deplorable conditions to keep the town clean and residents’ disease-free. But our efforts have borne no fruit. When the government fails to honour its promises, we are compelled to continue our struggle. We will not halt the strike until concrete action is taken,” one of the protesters said.
“One can imagine the authorities’ lack of concern regarding the town’s deteriorating sanitation. On one hand, the government talks about improving health through better sanitation facilities; and on the other, it shows no urgency in resolving the strike which has entered its seventh day,” said another protester.
Residents said they were “fed up” as the town’s condition continued to worsen by the day.
“The authorities should not allow the matter to drag on. Garbage is lying unattended in several localities and foul smell is becoming unbearable. We fail to understand why the government is not paying heed to the demands of sanitation workers,” said Khushaal Jaggi, a resident.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
"Que ça change", environ 150 personnes rassemblées devant le tribunal judiciaire de Dijon contre les violences sexuelles
Publié le
Environ 150 personnes se sont à nouveau mobilisées, ce lundi, devant le tribunal judiciaire de Dijon, une dizaine de jours après le meurtre de de Lyhanna. Pour rendre hommage à la collégienne mais aussi pour demander l'examen d'une loi intégrale contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles.
Il y avait certes un peu moins de monde que le 8 juin dernier, pour la première manifestation en hommage à Lyhanna , la jeune fille de 11 ans retrouvée morte dans le Gers . Mais la mobilisation était à nouveau d'ampleur, ce lundi, devant le tribunal judiciaire de Dijon, puisqu'environ 150 personnes se sont réunies, pancartes en main pour beaucoup, pour demander, notamment, la mise en place d'une loi intégrale contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles.
Plusieurs prises de paroles se sont succédé devant l'entrée du tribunal, provoquant parfois quelques larmes dans l'assemblée. Chez Véronique, certains discours rouvrent certaines plaies, pas totalement cicatrisées, pour cette proche de victimes : "Il y en autour de moi, oui, ça c'est sûr. Sur plusieurs générations aussi et ça n'avance pas. Ça ne change pas. Il faut faire quelque chose." En particulier sur l'écoute des victimes et la durée de traitement des procédures judiciaires. "Quand on voit les traumatismes que ça génère, on ne peut pas, par respect pour l'enfant, laisser le temps au temps et dire 'Eh bien, on attend que la procédure suive'. Non. Parce que tout le monde autour de ces enfants et cet enfant ne vit plus. C'est de la survie", poursuit la retraitée dijonnaise.
Cette demande de Véronique, justement, fait partie des mesures présentes dans le projet de loi intégrale , pas encore discuté par le Parlement. "On veut que les procédures aient lieu, rien que ça, et qu'elles s'accélèrent. On veut aussi que le mis en cause soit systématiquement auditionné, qu'il y ait des vrais actes d'enquête demandés par les juges d'instruction. Et ça, aujourd'hui, ça n'a pas lieu en fait", rappelle Emmanuelle Dancourt, présidente de l'association Metoo médias et favorables au texte.
"On ne s'en sortira pas sans qu'il y ait une volonté politique. C'est pour ça qu'on on met la pression" - Emmanuelle Dancourt
La journaliste a d'ailleurs "bon espoir" que ce projet de loi soit étudié par le Parlement : "J'y crois parce qu'il y a dix jours, j'étais avec la coalition féministe devant l'Assemblée nationale à manifester. On devait être une trentaine, dont une dizaine de parlementaires qui ont co-signé la loi intégrale. Il y avait quelques journalistes, mais alors on avait l'impression de crier dans le vide. Et deux jours après, Lyhanna est morte. Et là, on a vu le changement total. D'un seul coup, les politiques se sont saisis du sujet qu'on porte depuis deux ans quand même. Mais de toute façon, on ne s'en sortira pas sans qu'il y ait une volonté politique. Et c'est pour ça qu'on on met la pression."
"Quand on est capable de mettre 6 milliards d'euros dans des Jeux olympiques qui étaient super, mais qu'on n'est pas capables de mettre la moitié, 3 milliards d'euros pour protéger nos enfants, pour protéger les victimes de violences sexistes et sexuelles, qu'est ce que ça dit de notre pays ? Ça dit qu'on ne s'en occupe pas, ça dit qu'il n'y a pas de volonté politique", poursuit Emmanuelle Dancourt.
A Dijon, un rassemblement contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles se tiendra d'ailleurs chaque lundi soir à 19h jusqu'à l'obtention de cette loi intégrale.

"Time for Change": Around 150 People Gather in Front of the Dijon Courthouse to Protest Sexual Violence
Published on
Around 150 people gathered again this Monday in front of the Dijon courthouse, about ten days after the murder of Lyhanna. They were there to pay tribute to the middle school student and also to demand the consideration of a comprehensive law against gender-based and sexual violence.
While there were slightly fewer people than on June 8th for the first demonstration in tribute to Lyhanna, the 11-year-old girl found dead in the Gers region, the mobilization was once again significant this Monday in front of the Dijon courthouse. Around 150 people gathered, many holding signs, to demand, in particular, the implementation of a comprehensive law against gender-based and sexual violence.
Several speeches were given in front of the courthouse entrance, sometimes bringing tears to the eyes of those present. For Véronique, certain discussions reopen old wounds, not yet fully healed, for this relative of victims: "There are victims around me, yes, that's for sure. Across several generations, and nothing's moving forward. Nothing's changing. Something has to be done." In particular, regarding listening to victims and the length of legal proceedings. "When you see the trauma it causes, we can't, out of respect for the child, just let things take their course and say, 'Well, we'll wait for the legal process to run its course.' No. Because everyone around these children, and the child themselves, is no longer truly living. It's about survival," the retired woman from Dijon continues. This very request from Véronique is one of the measures included in the comprehensive bill, which has not yet been debated in Parliament. "We want the procedures to take place, nothing more, and for them to be expedited. We also want the accused to be systematically questioned, for there to be real investigative actions ordered by the investigating judges. And that, today, is not actually happening," recalls Emmanuelle Dancourt, president of the MeToo media association and supporter of the bill.

"We won't get anywhere without political will. That's why we're putting on the pressure," said Emmanuelle Dancourt. The journalist is also "hopeful" that this bill will be examined by Parliament: "I believe it will happen because ten days ago, I was with the feminist coalition in front of the National Assembly, demonstrating. There were about thirty of us, including around ten members of parliament who co-signed the entire bill. There were a few journalists, but at the time, we felt like we were shouting into the void. And two days later, Lyhanna died. And then we saw the complete change. Suddenly, politicians took up the issue we've been championing for two years now. But in any case, we won't get anywhere without political will. And that's why we're putting on the pressure."

"When we're capable of spending 6 billion euros on fantastic Olympic Games, but we can't spend half that amount, 3 billion euros, to protect our children, to protect victims of gender-based and sexual violence, what does that say about our country? It says we're not taking care of it, it says there's no political will," continues Emmanuelle Dancourt.

In Dijon, a rally against gender-based and sexual violence will be held every Monday evening at 7 p.m. until this comprehensive law is passed.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Mit Feuerwehrautos, Rettungswagen und Straßenreinigungs-Fahrzeugen haben in Berlin Kommunalpolitiker aus NRW und anderen Bundesländern für eine finanzielle Soforthilfe demonstriert. Die Politiker des Aktionsbündnisses «Für die Würde unserer Städte» fuhren in einer Kolonne aus rund 20 Fahrzeugen am Vormittag vor dem Kanzleramt und dem Finanzministerium auf.
«Wir sind hier, um auf die dringende Finanznot der Städte aufmerksam zu machen», sagte der Oberbürgermeister von Oberhausen, Thorsten Berg (SPD). «Wir sind in einer ganz dramatischen Lage.» Die Städte hätten im vergangenen Jahr ein kommunales Defizit von 32 Milliarden Euro verzeichnet - das sei so viel wie noch nie gewesen. Bund und Länder müssten dringend ihre Verantwortung übernehmen.
Martin Murrack (SPD), Stadtdirektor und Kämmerer in Duisburg, sagte: «Wir haben das Gefühl, dass in Berlin alle Bescheid wissen, aber es bewegt sich trotzdem nichts. Daher zeigen wir heute, welche Leistungen die Kommunen alle erbringen müssen: mit Feuerwehr, mit Ordnungsamt, mit Straßenreinigung. Um klarzumachen: Wir sind wichtig und wir wollen auch weiter leistungsfähig bleiben. Aber dafür brauchen wir Geld.»
«Rettet die Kommunen» und «Keine Zukunft mit leeren Kassen» stand auf Transparenten, die die Demonstranten mitgebracht hatten. Der Initiative gehören nach eigenen Angaben vor allem Städte an, die geringere Steuereinnahmen und hohe Sozialausgaben haben. Insgesamt sind es 73 Kommunen aus acht Bundesländern, darunter Bochum, Mönchengladbach, Hagen, Schwerte und Neustadt an der Weinstraße.
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) und die Ministerpräsidenten hatten sich auf eine Neuregelung der Bund-Länder-Finanzen verständigt. Künftig soll gelten: «Wer bestellt, bezahlt». Der Bund soll den Großteil der Mehrkosten tragen, die Ländern und Kommunen durch Gesetzesänderungen auf Bundesebene entstehen.
Die Vertreter des Aktionsbündnisses hatten schon vor dem Start ihrer Reise nach Berlin deutlich gemacht, dass dies zwar ein Schritt für weniger zusätzliche Belastung in der Zukunft sei. Es reiche aber aktuell nicht aus, um die aktuelle Finanznot zu überwinden.

TRANSLATED_TEXT:
With fire trucks, ambulances, and street cleaning vehicles, local politicians from North Rhine-Westphalia and other German states demonstrated in Berlin for immediate financial aid. The politicians from the "For the Dignity of Our Cities" action alliance drove in a convoy of around 20 vehicles to the Federal Chancellery and the Finance Ministry this morning.

"We are here to draw attention to the urgent financial crisis facing our cities," said Thorsten Berg (SPD), the mayor of Oberhausen. "We are in a truly dramatic situation." He stated that cities recorded a municipal deficit of 32 billion euros last year – the highest ever recorded. The federal and state governments must urgently assume their responsibilities.

Martin Murrack (SPD), city manager and treasurer of Duisburg, said: "We have the feeling that everyone in Berlin is aware of the situation, but nothing is being done. Therefore, today we are demonstrating the services that municipalities must provide: with fire departments, public order offices, and street cleaning. To make it clear: We are important, and we want to remain efficient." But we need money for that.”

“Save the municipalities” and “No future with empty coffers” were written on banners carried by the demonstrators. According to its own statements, the initiative primarily comprises cities with lower tax revenues and high social welfare expenditures. In total, it includes 73 municipalities from eight federal states, among them Bochum, Mönchengladbach, Hagen, Schwerte, and Neustadt an der Weinstraße.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) and the state premiers had agreed on a new regulation for federal-state finances. In the future, the principle will be: “Whoever orders, pays.” The federal government is to bear the majority of the additional costs incurred by states and municipalities due to legislative changes at the federal level.

Even before the start of their trip to Berlin, the representatives of the action alliance had made it clear that while this was a step toward reducing future additional burdens, it was not enough to overcome the current financial crisis.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Σε μια πρωτόγνωρη για την καλοκαιρινή περίοδο κινητοποίηση προχώρησαν οι αγρότες της ευρύτερης περιοχής των Φαρσάλων , πραγματοποιώντας συλλαλητήριο με τρακτέρ στο κέντρο της πόλης.
Η δράση οργανώθηκε έπειτα από κάλεσμα της Ενωτικής Ομοσπονδίας Αγροτικών Συλλόγων (Ε.Ο.Α.Σ.) Νομού Λάρισας και των Αγροτών της επαρχίας Φαρσάλων . Από τις πρωινές ώρες, αγροτικά μηχανήματα συγκεντρώθηκαν στον κυκλικό κόμβο του Ανωχωρίου και στη συνέχεια σχημάτισαν κομβόι με προορισμό το κέντρο της πόλης, όπου πραγματοποιήθηκε η κεντρική συγκέντρωση διαμαρτυρίας.
Τα τρακτέρ παρέμειναν σταθμευμένα σε κεντρικά σημεία των Φαρσάλων, στέλνοντας ηχηρό μήνυμα για τα προβλήματα που αντιμετωπίζει ο πρωτογενής τομέας. Οι συμμετέχοντες ανέδειξαν σειρά αιτημάτων που σχετίζονται με τη βιωσιμότητα της αγροτικής παραγωγής, το αυξημένο κόστος καλλιέργειας και τη διασφάλιση αξιοπρεπών συνθηκών εργασίας.
Όπως τόνισαν οι ίδιοι, ο αγώνας τους αφορά την επιβίωση των αγροτικών εκμεταλλεύσεων και τη δυνατότητα να συνεχίσουν να εργάζονται και να παράγουν στον τόπο τους, υπογραμμίζοντας την ανάγκη για ουσιαστική στήριξη του αγροτικού κόσμου. Πρόθεση των αγροτών είναι να αφήσουν τα τρακτέρ τους στο κέντρο των Φαρσάλων για 24 ώρες, ενώ τα τρακτέρ τους βγάζουν το απόγευμα οι αγρότες της ΕΟΑΣΝΛ στον κόμβο Πλατυκάμπου και στην εθνική οδό Λάρισας- Κοζάνης , στον Τυρναβο .

In an unprecedented mobilization for the summer period, farmers from the wider region of Farsala proceeded with a tractor rally in the city center.
The action was organized following a call from the United Federation of Agricultural Associations (E.O.A.S.) of Larissa Prefecture and the Farmers of the Farsala district. Since the morning hours, agricultural machinery gathered at the Anochori roundabout and then formed a convoy heading to the city center, where the central protest rally took place.

Convocan a protesta contra Sube-T, la vialidad elevada de cobro que impulsa el gobierno de Marina del Pilar

TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Protest Called Against Sube-T, the Elevated Toll Road Promoted by Marina del Pilar's Government

Tijuana – Business owners and residents of the Rinconada Otay neighborhood have called for a protest next Saturday, July 11, at 7:00 a.m., to denounce the negative impacts they claim are being caused by the construction of the Nodo Morelos-Otay elevated roadway (Sube-T).

The project is part of a larger elevated roadway that will operate by charging a toll of approximately 113 pesos.

The protesters stated that the demonstration aims to highlight the negative impacts the construction is having on the area, both for residents and businesses located there.

According to the organizers, more than 50 businesses would be affected because the bridge will descend through the Plaza Constituyentes parking lot, a situation they claim will compromise customer access and the operation of their establishments.

In addition to the impacts of the construction, some residents have expressed their opposition to the project because the elevated roadway will be a toll road, which they believe will represent a financial burden for those who use that route daily.

The organizers called on residents, business owners, and citizens to participate in the demonstration to demand that the authorities address their concerns and review the impacts they maintain the project will have.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
دعوة لحضور المحاكمة والتضامن عبر وقفة احتجاجية

يقف أحد رفاقنا أمام المحكمة يوم 24.06 الساعة 9:30 صباحًا، لمواجهة تهمتين منفصلتين تتعلقان بمظاهرتين مختلفتين، وكلتاهما جرتا في سبتمبر/أيلول 2024.

يُتهم الرفيق بإهانة عناصر الشرطة، وتهديدهم، ومقاومة الاعتقال.

في إحدى المظاهرتين، التي جرت في 21.09.2024، فرضت الشرطة طوقًا على نحو 60 شخصًا داخل محطة مترو يوركشتراسه (U-Bahn Yorckstraße)، واحتجزتهم لأكثر من ساعتين، ومنعتهم من الوصول إلى الاحتياجات الأساسية. كما اعتدت بعنف على عدد من الأشخاص، ما أدى إلى نقل بعضهم إلى المستشفى، بعد أن أعاقت بشكل متعمد وصول فرق الإسعاف.

قام رفيقنا بتصوير الشرطة وهي تسحب شابًا فلسطينيًا من محطة المترو وتعتدي عليه بالضرب وهو على الأرض. ودفعه أفراد الشرطة عدة مرات، وبعد أن فشلوا في منعه من التصوير، اعتقلوه وصادروا هاتفه. واستخدموا تهمة "إهانة الشرطة" كذريعة، كما يفعلون في كثير من الأحيان.

في أول جلستي محاكمة، طلب الادعاء فرض عقوبة مشددة دون تقديم أدلة تثبت الاتهامات، بينما أدلى أحد أفراد الشرطة بشهادة متناقضة؛ إذ قال من جهة إنه لا يتذكر الوقائع، ومن جهة أخرى إنه يخضع للعلاج النفسي بسبب التهديدات المزعومة. كما أن مقطع الفيديو الذي أرادت الشرطة تقديمه كدليل لم يكن موجودًا على هاتف المتهم، رغم أن الهاتف ظل مُصادرًا لمدة عامين.

سندافع عن رفيقنا كما ندافع عن جميع أفرادنا!

Call to Attend the Trial and Show Solidarity Through a Protest

One of our comrades will appear in court on June 24th at 9:30 a.m. to face two separate charges related to two different demonstrations, both of which took place in September 2024.

He is accused of insulting and threatening police officers, and resisting arrest.

During one of the demonstrations, which occurred on September 21st, 2024, police surrounded approximately 60 people inside the Yorckstraße U-Bahn station, detaining them for over two hours and preventing them from accessing basic necessities. They also violently assaulted several people, resulting in some being hospitalized, after deliberately obstructing the arrival of ambulance crews.

Our comrade filmed police dragging a young Palestinian man from the U-Bahn station and assaulting him while he was on the ground. The officers pushed him repeatedly, and when they failed to stop him from filming, they arrested him and confiscated his phone. They used the charge of "insulting the police" as a pretext, as they often do.

In the first two court sessions, the prosecution requested a harsh sentence without presenting any evidence to support the charges. One of the police officers gave contradictory testimony; he claimed on one hand that he did not remember the events, and on the other hand that he was undergoing psychological treatment due to the alleged threats. Furthermore, the video the police wanted to present as evidence was not found on the defendant's phone, even though the phone had been confiscated for two years.

We will defend our comrade as we defend all our members!

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Political activists from Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir gather outside Pakistani Consulate in Bradford, UK to condemn ongoing crackdown on protesters in region
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Bradford [UK], June 12 (ANI): Political activists from Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) gathered outside the Pakistani Consulate in Bradford, United Kingdom, to condemn the ongoing crackdown on protesters in the region. Demonstrators raised anti-Pakistan slogans and strongly criticised the Pakistani military leadership over the use of force against civilians participating in protests in Rawalakot and Kotli.
The protest on Thursday saw demonstrators alleging that security forces carried out a violent response to largely peaceful demonstrations, resulting in several deaths and numerous injuries. Participants called for accountability, justice for the victims, and greater international attention to the situation in PoJK. Speakers at the gathering urged human rights organisations and the international community to investigate the reported incidents and address concerns over the treatment of civilians in the region.
Providing heavyweight political backing to these demands, British MP Bob Blackman launched a blistering attack on the Pakistani security apparatus for using live ammunition against these peaceful protesters, branding the crackdown an egregious act of state-sponsored violence.
In an exclusive interview with ANI, the senior Conservative lawmaker expressed deep alarm over the escalating atrocities and the rising casualties being suppressed by authorities. He noted that while official figures claim nine deaths, local accounts report over 30 people killed and hundreds injured.
'This is a despicable attack on civilians, most of whom, of course, are concerned about having enough food to eat and having the position whereby their human rights are protected,' Blackman told ANI, exposing the severe economic and humanitarian crisis under Pakistani administration.
The instability has rapidly escalated into an international diplomatic issue, with Blackman confirming that British nationals are among those targeted and injured in the violence--a development he described as 'a direct concern to the United Kingdom'.
Taking immediate legislative action against Islamabad's brutality, Blackman formally requested the Foreign Secretary to address the House of Commons and demand answers.
'I asked the leader of the house to arrange for the foreign secretary to make a statement next week on what action she has taken to call in the Pakistani high commissioner and give them a dressing down on this,' he stated.
In a significant diplomatic shift that underscores Pakistan's growing isolation, the MP revealed that 30 British lawmakers, including those historically aligned with Islamabad, have written to the Foreign Secretary to express their outrage, signalling a rare and unified condemnation of the high-handedness.
Reiterating the historical context of the dispute, Blackman forcefully challenged Islamabad's locus standi, asserting that 'since 1947 Pakistan has illegally occupied this part of India'.
Calling for the full implementation of UN resolutions, the British lawmaker advocated that the Pakistani military 'should leave the Kashmir Valley' and that the territory be 'reunited as part of sovereign India'. He further warned of a dangerous escalation if forces continue to pursue peaceful protesters into their homes and hospitals.
In stark contrast to Pakistan's internal turmoil and aggressive state actions, Blackman offered glowing praise for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, celebrating his tenure as India's longest-serving directly elected Prime Minister.
The UK lawmaker lauded PM Modi's work ethic and diplomatic success, asserting that India is 'going from strength to strength' under his 'beneficial leadership'.
Highlighting the wider regional threat posed by the malicious China-Pakistan axis, the MP strongly advocated integrating a rising India into advanced global security frameworks similar to the 'Five Eyes' alliance to ensure regional stability and safeguard democratic interests against hostile neighbours. (ANI)

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Πανελλαδική απεργία στο δημόσιο σήμερα, στο πλαίσιο κινητοποίησης της ΑΔΕΔΥ. Συλλαλητήριο στις 10:30 στην πλατεία Κλαυθμώνος.
Οι εκπρόσωποι των δημοσίων υπαλλήλων διεκδικούν μεταξύ άλλων αυξήσεις 20% στις αποδοχές, επαναφορά του 13ου και 14ου μισθού και μαζικές προσλήψεις μόνιμου προσωπικού, ιδιαίτερα σε υγεία και παιδεία.
Στην απεργία συμμετέχουν δάσκαλοι, καθηγητές, υγειονομικοί, γιατροί, εργαζόμενοι σε δήμους και περιφέρειες, υπουργεία, εφορίες και ασφαλιστικά ταμεία.
Κανονικά λειτουργούν τα μέσα μαζικής μεταφοράς.
Τις συνθήκες του τραγικού περιστατικού στην Ηλιούπολη, όπου δύο 17χρονες έπεσαν στο κενό από ταράτσα εξαώροφης πολυκατοικίας, με αποτέλεσμα η μία να χάσει τη ζωή της και η δεύτερη να δίνει μάχη στο νοσοκομείο ΚΑΤ, ερευνούν οι αρχές.
Στις οικογένειες των δύο κοριτσιών παρέχεται ψυχολογική υποστήριξη, ενώ σύμφωνα με άτυπη ενημέρωση από το υπουργείο Παιδείας, διευρυμένο κλιμάκιο, με ψυχολόγους και κοινωνικούς λειτουργούς, θα μεταβεί στο σχολείο των δύο μαθητριών στην Ηλιούπολη.
Το διπλωματικό αδιέξοδο για τον πόλεμο στη Μέση Ανατολή συνεχίζεται.
Το Ιράν, μέσω του επικεφαλής διαπραγματευτή και προέδρου του κοινοβουλίου του, Μοχαμάντ Μπαγέρ Γαλιμπάφ, αποκλείει συμβιβασμό, μετά την απόρριψη των προτάσεών του από τον Ντόναλντ Τραμπ ως “εντελώς απαράδεκτες”.
Η Τεχεράνη απαιτεί άμεσο τερματισμό του πολέμου σε όλη την περιοχή, συμπεριλαμβανομένου του Λιβάνου, όπου οι αιματηρές επιθέσεις του Ισραήλ συνεχίζονται, με θύματα καθημερινά.
Η Σαουδική Αραβία εξαπέλυσε πολυάριθμους–μυστικούς ως τώρα–βομβαρδισμούς εναντίον του Ιράν τον Μάρτιο, σύμφωνα με το πρακτορείο Ρόιτερς, που επικαλείται δυο «δυτικούς αξιωματούχους».
Χθες, η Wall Street Journal είχε αποκαλύψει πως και τα Ηνωμένα Αραβικά Εμιράτα είχαν βομβαρδίσει το Ιράν.
Στο Πεκίνο απόψε ο Ντόναλντ Τραμπ, σε μια κρίσιμη επίσκεψη τόσο για τις εξελίξεις στη Μέση Ανατολή όσο και για την παγκόσμια οικονομία.
Ο Αμερικανός πρόεδρος δήλωσε ότι θα έχει μια μακρά συνομιλία με τον Κινέζο ομόλογό του για τον πόλεμο στο Ιράν, ωστόσο πρόσθεσε ότι δεν πιστεύει ότι η Κίνα θα βοηθούσε στον τερματισμό του.
Σημείωσε ακόμη πως θα ζητήσει από τον Σι Τζινπίνγκ «να ανοίξει» περισσότερο την οικονομία της Κίνας σε εταιρείες των ΗΠΑ.
Αντιδράσεις μελών της αμερικανικής Βουλής των Αντιπροσώπων για τις δημόσιες τοποθετήσεις του πρεσβευτή των ΗΠΑ στην Άγκυρα, Τομ Μπάρακ, τόσο για το ενδεχόμενο ένταξης της Τουρκίας στο πρόγραμμα των F35 όσο και για τον ρόλο της Χεζμπολάχ στο λιβανικό μέτωπο.
Με επιστολή τους, που κυκλοφορεί στο Κογκρέσο για τη συλλογή υπογραφών, καλούν το Στέιτ Ντιπάρτμεντ να ξεκαθαρίσει αν οι δημόσιες δηλώσεις του πρέσβη στην Τουρκία, αντανακλούν την επίσημη γραμμή της αμερικανικής κυβέρνησης.
Βρετανός τουρίστας τέθηκε σε καραντίνα σε νοσοκομείο του Μιλάνου, καθώς είχε επαφή –σε αεροσκάφος με προορισμό το Γιοχάνεσμπουργκ– με ηλικιωμένη που πέθανε από χανταϊό.
Στο μεταξύ στη Σικελία, τουρίστρια από την Αργεντινή που εμφάνισε πνευμονία υποβλήθηκε σε εργαστηριακές εξετάσεις για να εξακριβωθεί αν είναι φορέας στελέχους του χανταϊού.
Στις κάλπες προσέρχονται σήμερα οι φοιτητές στα πανεπιστήμια όλης της χώρας.
Οι φετινές εκλογές διεξάγονται σε ένα ιδιαίτερα φορτισμένο κλίμα, με την αντιπαράθεση για το άρθρο 16 να βρίσκεται στο «κόκκινο», και στη «σκιά» των σοβαρών επεισοδίων σε Αριστοτέλειο Πανεπιστήμιο Θεσσαλονίκης και Πανεπιστήμιο Δυτικής Αττικής, όπου εισέβαλαν ομάδες ατόμων που φορούσαν κράνη, προκαλώντας επεισόδια και τραυματισμούς. Επτά φοιτητές μεταφέρθηκαν στο νοσοκομείο Παπαγεωργίου και άλλοι δυο στο Θριάσιο.
Οι κάλπες θα είναι ανοιχτές έως τις 19:00 το απόγευμα, με τους φοιτητικούς συλλόγους να καλούν σε μαζική συμμετοχή.
Εντός του Ιουνίου αναμένεται να τεθεί σε ισχύ η νέα έκτακτη ρύθμιση χρεών σε 72 δόσεις για ληξιπρόθεσμες οφειλές προς εφορία και ΕΦΚΑ που έχουν βεβαιωθεί έως και τις 31
Δεκεμβρίου 2023 και παραμένουν αρρύθμιστες.
Το νομοσχέδιο του υπουργείου Οικονομικών, που την περιλαμβάνει, τίθεται εντός της εβδομάδας σε δημόσια διαβούλευση.
Σε αυτό, προβλέπεται ακόμη η δυνατότητα ένταξης στον εξωδικαστικό μηχανισμό περισσότερων οφειλετών για χρέη σε τράπεζες, servicers και δημόσιο, καθώς και η άρση – υπό προϋποθέσεις – του ακατάσχετου λογαριασμού.
Πάνω από 2,5 εκατομμύρια δικαιούχοι εντάχθηκαν στο Fuel Pass 3, με το συνολικό ύψος της ενίσχυσης να ξεπερνά τα 113 εκατομμύρια ευρώ.

Ecologistas y animalistas se unen contra la caza en Madrid
Más de un centenar de organizaciones saldrán este sábado a las calles de la capital contra la nueva Ley de Caza impulsada por el Gobierno regional.
Ecologistas, animalistas, senderistas y vecinos del mundo rural se manifestarán este sábado 30 de mayo en Madrid contra la nueva Ley de Caza y Pesca Fluvial que prepara la Comunidad de Madrid. La protesta, que busca frenar la norma, arrancará a las 12:00 horas en la Plaza de Callao y terminará frente a la sede de la Consejería de Medio Ambiente. La movilización quiere presionar al Gobierno regional antes de que la ley siga avanzando en la Asamblea de Madrid.
La convocatoria ha sido organizada por la Plataforma Ecologista Madrileña, la Asociación Empatía y la Plataforma No a la Caza (NAC). Según las entidades convocantes, es la primera vez que el movimiento ecologista y el animalista unen fuerzas en la región para protestar contra una normativa cinegética. La alianza entre ambos colectivos es histórica y busca reunir a miles de personas en el centro de la capital.
Los colectivos denuncian que el texto legal ha sido redactado "al dictado del lobby de la caza" y critican que el Gobierno regional solo haya escuchado al sector cinegético durante su elaboración. Según recuerdan, los cazadores representan apenas el 0,63 % de la población madrileña, aunque controlan más del 70 % del territorio de la comunidad. Las críticas se centran directamente en el PP y en su mayoría absoluta en la Asamblea.

LOS40
La futura ley permite la caza mayor durante todos los días del año
La futura ley sustituirá a la normativa franquista de 1970 e introduce cambios muy polémicos. Entre ellos, amplía el número de especies cazables de 24 a 31 y permite la caza mayor durante todos los días del año. Además, autoriza el uso de drones, visores nocturnos y dispositivos térmicos para localizar animales. Los ecologistas creen que la norma elimina cualquier tregua para la fauna.
Una ley que afecta a todos
Las organizaciones convocantes denuncian además que se recuperan modalidades consideradas especialmente crueles, como la caza de paloma con cimbel o la perdiz con reclamo, donde se utilizan animales vivos como señuelo. También alertan de que podrán emplearse hasta 500 perros en algunas monterías, algo que consideran incompatible con el bienestar animal. La polémica también ha llegado a las redes sociales, donde muchos usuarios ya muestran su rechazo al proyecto.
Otro de los puntos más criticados es la limitación del acceso ciudadano a caminos públicos y márgenes de ríos durante las jornadas de caza. Según los colectivos, la norma penaliza la presencia de personas no cazadoras en determinadas zonas cinegéticas y reduce el uso libre del entorno natural. Senderistas, ciclistas y fotógrafos de naturaleza también se sienten afectados por las nuevas restricciones.
Los convocantes aseguran que la manifestación está abierta a cualquier persona que considere que el territorio público "no puede entregarse en exclusiva a una minoría armada". A la movilización ya se han adherido más de un centenar de organizaciones ecologistas, sociales y animalistas de toda España. La protesta promete convertirse en una de las más multitudinarias del sector en los últimos años.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Environmentalists and animal rights activists unite against hunting in Madrid
More than a hundred organizations will take to the streets of the capital this Saturday to protest the new Hunting Law promoted by the regional government.
Environmentalists, animal rights activists, hikers, and residents of rural areas will demonstrate this Saturday, May 30, in Madrid against the new Hunting and River Fishing Law being prepared by the Community of Madrid. The protest, which aims to halt the legislation, will begin at 12:00 noon in Plaza de Callao and will end in front of the headquarters of the Ministry of the Environment. The mobilization seeks to pressure the regional government before the law advances further in the Madrid Assembly.

The demonstration has been organized by the Madrid Ecologist Platform, the Empathy Association, and the No to Hunting Platform (NAC). According to the organizing groups, this is the first time the environmental and animal rights movements have joined forces in the region to protest against hunting regulations. The alliance between the two groups is historic and aims to bring together thousands of people in the heart of the capital.

The groups denounce that the legal text was drafted "at the behest of the hunting lobby" and criticize the regional government for only listening to the hunting sector during its drafting. They point out that hunters represent barely 0.63% of the Madrid population, although they control more than 70% of the region's territory. The criticism is directed squarely at the People's Party (PP) and its absolute majority in the Assembly.

LOS40
LOS40
The future law allows big game hunting every day of the year
The future law will replace the Francoist regulations of 1970 and introduces highly controversial changes. Among them, it expands the number of huntable species from 24 to 31 and allows big game hunting every day of the year. Furthermore, it authorizes the use of drones, night-vision goggles, and thermal imaging devices to locate animals. Environmentalists believe the law eliminates any respite for wildlife.

A Law Affecting Everyone
The organizing groups also denounce the reinstatement of hunting methods considered especially cruel, such as pigeon hunting with decoys or partridge hunting with calls, where live animals are used as bait. They also warn that up to 500 dogs may be used in some hunts, something they consider incompatible with animal welfare. The controversy has also reached social media, where many users are already expressing their rejection of the bill.

Another point of contention is the restriction of public access to roads and riverbanks during hunting days. According to the groups, the law penalizes the presence of non-hunters in certain hunting areas and reduces the free use of the natural environment. Hikers, cyclists, and nature photographers also feel affected by the new restrictions.

The organizers assert that the demonstration is open to anyone who believes that public land "cannot be handed over exclusively to an armed minority." More than a hundred environmental, social, and animal rights organizations from across Spain have already joined the mobilization. The protest promises to be one of the largest in the sector in recent years.

أوضحت "رابطة الأساتذة المتعاقدين في التعليم الأساسي الرسمي"، في بيان، أن "بعض المنصات تداول اليوم مقاطع مصوّرة لطلاب معترضين على ما قامت به روابط التعليم الرسمي التابعة للسلطة، بعدما نزلت إلى اعتصام الطلاب أمام وزارة التربية صباح اليوم، ووجّهوا النقد إلى الروابط، رافضين تحدثها باسم تحركهم، معتبرين أن ذلك يشكّل استغلالًا لتحرك الطلاب. كما وأشاروا إلى أن هذه الروابط لا تملك أي سلطة على الأساتذة والمديرين، وأنها لطالما تخلّت عن تحركات الأساتذة، واعتبروا أن إعلانها مقاطعة الامتحانات الرسمية في حال عدم منح إفادات لجميع الطلاب ليس سوى ذرًّا للرماد في العيون ومحاولة لاستغلال التحرك وتعويم أنفسهم".

كما وأكدت الرابطة في الوقت نفسه أنها "تؤمن بأهمية التعاون والتنسيق بين الطلاب والأساتذة عندما يكون قائمًا على اتفاق مسبق وأهداف تربوية ونقابية مشتركة، لا على ادعاء تمثيل طرف للآخر أو التحدث باسمه. و لكن روابط التعليم الرسمي التابعة للسلطة أرادت، لغاية في نفس يعقوب، المشاركة في هذا التحرك وإعطاء موقفها زخمًا إعلاميًا، فادّعت أن التحرك باسم روابط التعليم الرسمي، بدلًا من تحديد الجهات الداعية إليه، احترامًا للمصداقية والتمثيل النقابي وحرية الرأي، ولا سيما أن رابطة الأساتذة المتعاقدين لم تشاركها هذا الموقف".
وتابع البيان: "بعد انتشار مواقف الطلاب المعارضة لما سُمّي (روابط التعليم الرسمي)، نوضح للرأي العام حقيقة ما جرى. فقد أعلنت رابطة الأساتذة المتعاقدين، في بيانها الصادر بتاريخ 29 حزيران 2026، دعمها الكامل لمطالب الطلاب المحقة، واحترامها لاستقلالية تحركاتهم، مؤكدة أن دورها هو مساندة هذه المطالب لا استثمارها أو التحدث باسم أصحابها. ولا يمكن إغفال أن التحرك كان، في الأساس، تحركًا طلابيًا، فيما اقتصر حضور روابط التعليم الرسمي التابعة للسلطة على عدد من الأساتذة لا يتجاوز أصابع اليد. والأكثر غرابةً، بل المعيب، أنهم بدلًا من اختيار ممثل واحد لإلقاء كلمة باسم الأساتذة، تهافتوا على إلقاء الكلمات، فتحدث كل واحد منهم على أنه ممثل لرابطة أو مجموعة أو لجنة، في مشهد عكس سعيًا إلى ظهور إعلامي آثار غضب الطلاب بحسب ما وصف أحدهم المشهد. وتصدّر هؤلاء المشهد، وتحدثوا باسم الطلاب ومن ثم طرحوا مطالب تتعلق بزيادة الأجور، وأخذ كل منهم يفيض بمطالبه كيفما يشاء... ومن هنا، يبدو اعتراض الطلاب على هذا السلوك وغضبهم منه أمرًا مفهومًا. وعليه، فإن من يدّعي الدفاع عن الطلاب كان الأولى به أن لا يوقف الإضرابات والاعتصامات التي نُظّمت للمطالبة بزيادة الأجور (الست رواتب) بصورة فجائية قبل الحرب، ومن ثم جرى تفعيلها في عزّ الحرب قبل إيقافها وقبل إقرار الزيادة، ما لم يحصد سوى خسارة عشرات الساعات التعليمية للأساتذة المتعاقدين. كما كان الأولى به أن يطالب بفتح ملفات الهدر والفساد في وزارة التربية، ومحاسبة المسؤولين عن السياسات التي أوصلت القطاع التربوي والطلاب إلى هذا الواقع، ليكون لمشاركته اليوم ما يصدّق من غيرة على مصلحة الطلاب، بدلًا من تصريحات بروباغاندية كما وصفها الطلاب اليوم".
وتابع: "كما وأن هذه الروابط كانت من أوائل المطالبين بإجراء الامتحانات الرسمية الموحدة يوم كنّا نرفضها، وهو ما يزيد الاستغراب من هذا الموقف الذي جعلها تظهر فجأة بمظهر الغيورين على الطلاب".
وختم: "إن رابطة الأساتذة المتعاقدين تجدّد تأكيدها أن الدفاع عن حقوق الأساتذة والطلاب لا يكون باستغلال تحركاتهم، بل بالالتزام بالشفافية، واحترام التمثيل النقابي الحقيقي، وخوض نضال جدي من أجل العدالة والحقوق والمحاسبة".

MORELOS (apro).- Habitantes de la colonia Patios de la Estación, una de las colonias más vulnerables, y de otras zonas de Cuernavaca marcharon por las principales calles del centro de la ciudad para exigir al gobierno de Morelos el cumplimiento de programas sociales que, aseguran, fueron comprometidos por la actual administración estatal.
La movilización recorrió las calles Gutenberg y Galeana, donde los inconformes realizaron un cierre parcial de la vialidad. Posteriormente, se trasladaron a la explanada de la Plaza de Armas “General Emiliano Zapata”, frente al Palacio de Gobierno, donde instalaron una protesta para exigir respuesta a sus demandas.
Samuel Jaramillo Salgado, uno de los representantes vecinales de Patios de la Estación, afirmó que más de 3 mil familias están a la espera de apoyos de canasta básica, mientras que alrededor de 500 familias requieren láminas galvanizadas para atender necesidades derivadas de la temporada de lluvias.
Durante su intervención, Jaramillo Salgado sostuvo que los apoyos reclamados forman parte de compromisos sociales que, según dijo, fueron planteados durante el proceso electoral por la actual administración estatal y que la colonia respaldó en las urnas al proyecto de la Cuarta Transformación.

MORELOS (apro) – Residents of the Patios de la Estación neighborhood, one of the most vulnerable in the state, and other areas of Cuernavaca marched through the main streets of the city center to demand that the Morelos state government fulfill social programs that, they claim, were promised by the current state administration.

The march proceeded along Gutenberg and Galeana streets, where the protesters partially blocked the roadway. They then moved to the esplanade of the Plaza de Armas “General Emiliano Zapata,” in front of the Government Palace, where they staged a protest to demand a response to their demands.

Samuel Jaramillo Salgado, one of the neighborhood representatives from Patios de la Estación, stated that more than 3,000 families are waiting for basic food assistance, while approximately 500 families need galvanized roofing sheets to address needs arising from the rainy season. During his address, Jaramillo Salgado maintained that the requested support is part of social commitments that, he said, were made during the electoral process by the current state administration, and that the community supported the Fourth Transformation project at the polls.

“We are here to engage in dialogue with our governor, but if they don't fulfill their promises time and time again, we will protest, because the people are hungry, and I represent the most vulnerable,” he said.

“I am not directly attacking the governor. I am simply informing her of what her officials are doing, officials whom perhaps she appointed and whose behavior she is unaware of,” he declared.
The head of the Morelos DIF System, Jorge Erick Alquicira Cedillo, arrived at the protest site and spoke with the demonstrators. He later informed the media that the distribution of basic food baskets had been delayed due to problems with the supplier and logistical issues.

Έβδομη ημέρα απεργίας πείνας και δίψας στη ΒΙΑΛ Χίου
Σε απεργία πείνας και δίψας βρίσκονται εδώ και έξι μέρες αιτούντες άσυλο στη Χίο. Διαμαρτυρόμενοι για την απόρριψη των αιτήσεων ασύλου στην Ελλάδα 49 υπήκοοι Σενεγάλης -45 άντρες και 4 γυναίκες- φέρονται να αρνούνται φαγητό και νερό από τις 28 Μαΐου. Τουλάχιστον 18 άτομα έχουν ήδη μεταφερθεί στο νοσοκομείο και, σύμφωνα με πληροφορίες, το επόμενο βήμα είναι να αρνηθούν περαιτέρω ιατρική περίθαλψη καθώς συνεχίζουν την απεργία. Σύμφωνα με εκπροσώπους της ομάδας, αυτή την εβδομάδα υπήρξαν συναντήσεις με τη διοίκηση του καμπ και εκπροσώπους του υπουργείου Μετανάστευσης, οι οποίες ωστόσο δεν είχαν αποτέλεσμα και έτσι αποφάσισαν να συνεχίσουν την απεργία πείνας.
Ως το τέλος
Η κοινότητα αναφέρει ότι και τα 49 άτομα έχουν λάβει δεύτερη απορριπτική απόφαση για τις αιτήσεις ασύλου τους. Συμπληρώνουν ότι ακόμη δεκαπέντε άνθρωποι τελούν ήδη υπό κράτηση και έχουν μεταφερθεί σε κλειστές εγκαταστάσεις Προαναχωρησιακών Κέντρων. Φυσικά εκφράζονται αυξανόμενες ανησυχίες για την υγεία όσων συμμετέχουν στην απεργία.
«Ολοι οι Σενεγαλέζοι θα πεθάνουν εδώ εάν δεν λάβουν βοήθεια μετά από αυτή τη δημοσιοποίηση» φέρεται να δήλωσε σε μέλη ΜΚΟ ένας απεργός πείνας, ενώ περιγράφοντας τα αιτήματά τους ακόμη ένας φέρεται να δήλωσε: «Τα βάσανά μας είναι πολύ δυνατά, αλλά δεν έχουμε επιλογή» – και όλοι είναι αποφασισμένοι να φτάσουν ώς το τέλος.
«Ζητούμε δίκαιες, ίσες και ατομικές αξιολογήσεις όλων των αιτήσεων ασύλου και ζητούμε από τους ανθρώπους να κοινοποιήσουν αυτή την ιστορία ώστε να ακουστούν οι φωνές αυτής της κοινότητας» δηλώνουν από τη ΜΚΟ «Refugee Biryani Bananas», η οποία και δημοσίευσε σχετικά βίντεο στις σελίδες των κοινωνικών δικτύων με εξουθενωμένους ανθρώπους στα πρόθυρα της κατάρρευσης.
Πολιτική αστάθεια
Θυμίζουμε ότι η Σενεγάλη, παρότι θεωρούνταν ειρηνικός τόπος, τα τελευταία πέντε χρόνια μαστίζεται από πολιτική αστάθεια και εσωτερικές ταραχές που ξεκίνησαν το 2021 με τη σύλληψη του ηγέτη της αντιπολίτευσης και διήρκεσαν έως και το 2024. Διάστημα στο οποίο σημειώθηκε και η φυγή χιλιάδων ανθρώπων από τη χώρα, είτε υπό τον φόβο πολιτικών διώξεων είτε από τη φτώχεια που προκάλεσαν σε μεγάλα τμήματα του πληθυσμού οι ταραχές και οι διώξεις.
Η χώρα πλέον μαστίζεται από ανεργία κυρίως των νέων αφού έχει καταρρεύσει και η παραδοσιακή αλιεία, με τα αλιεύματα να έχουν μειωθεί δραματικά μετά και την αδειοδότηση μεγάλων αλιευτικών σκαφών που επιχειρούν ανεξέλεγκτα στα παράλια της Σενεγάλης.

Seventh day of hunger and thirst strike at VIAL Chios
Asylum seekers on Chios have been on hunger and thirst strike for six days. Protesting the rejection of their asylum applications in Greece, 49 Senegalese nationals -45 men and 4 women- have reportedly been refusing food and water since May 28. At least 18 people have already been taken to hospital and, according to information, the next step is to refuse further medical treatment as they continue their strike. According to representatives of the group, this week there were meetings with the camp administration and representatives of the Ministry of Immigration, which, however, were unsuccessful and so they decided to continue the hunger strike.
Until the end
The community reports that all 49 people have received a second rejection decision for their asylum applications. They add that another fifteen people are already in detention and have been transferred to closed Pre-Removal Center facilities. Of course, there are growing concerns about the health of those participating in the strike.
“All Senegalese will die here if they do not receive help after this publication,” one hunger striker reportedly told NGO members, while describing their demands, another reportedly said: “Our suffering is very strong, but we have no choice” – and all are determined to see it through to the end.
“We demand fair, equal and individual assessments of all asylum applications and we ask people to share this story so that the voices of this community can be heard,” said the NGO “Refugee Biryani Bananas”, which published relevant videos on social media pages with exhausted people on the verge of collapse.
Political instability
We recall that Senegal, despite being considered a peaceful place, has been plagued by political instability and internal unrest for the last five years that began in 2021 with the arrest of the opposition leader and lasted until 2024. Valladolid mobilizes to "not take a step backward" on freedoms and to protest against war
Thousands of people fill the city center to demand a living wage and advance rights such as access to housing and gender equality
Valladolid
María Jesús Hernández arrives early to the Recoletos sidewalk. She is one of the most veteran faces of May Day in Valladolid... just as the clock strikes noon, before thousands more—six thousand according to the organizers—fill the city center for the Labor Day demonstration. "Coming should be almost mandatory. We are in a very complicated moment," she says. Why? "The far right is trying to seize power in a rather ugly way. We have to defend, more than ever, everything that has been achieved over many years so that it isn't swept away in a short time. We cannot allow ourselves to take a step backward on our rights," she adds.

'Rights, not trenches' is precisely the slogan chosen by the UGT and CC OO trade unions for 2026. "We are focusing on the issues most relevant to workers, while also taking a broader view. This May Day is about saying no to war. We, the workers, are the ones who pay the price for this war, making it harder for us to make ends meet. We must stop these war policies," declares Óscar Lobo, the regional secretary of UGT. "Under this slogan, we are addressing the reactionary wave of the far right that wants to engage in dialogue with democracy. Class-based unionism will stand against all those who seek to eliminate people's rights," adds his counterpart at CC OO, Ana Fernández.
Among the "most immediate" problems, housing has taken center stage, becoming a "social emergency." "Without housing, there is no life project. And without a life project, there is no social cohesion or democracy," states the manifesto. Young people also have something to say here, which is why Rosa Cobo, 28, highlights this as one of the difficulties. “It seems the working class has lost its fighting spirit, but it’s increasingly important that we take to the streets. We’re facing a context of war, rising prices, low wages, and housing problems. There are plenty of reasons. Furthermore, we know that the struggle of the working class can achieve improvements, as it has in the past. It’s important that we keep this in mind, especially young people, who are the most vulnerable to precarious employment. We can’t lose our fighting spirit,” she points out.

Related news: Félix Muñoz, 23, who, along with his partner, is a member of the Young Communist Collective of the Communist Workers' Party of Spain, also offers a different perspective. “Young people are increasingly mired in precarity. It’s harder to find decent jobs, to become independent, to find a home where you can start a family, where you can be yourself.” “With the work of the working class, little by little, young people will become more assertive, more revolutionary, and their goals will be achieved,” he adds.

Daniel de las Heras, who recently turned 18, is also aware of this. “Over time, workers’ rights have improved, but if they aren’t defended and the fight doesn’t continue, there will be opportunists who will violate them,” he states. “We think we’ve won everything, but no, if we don’t keep fighting, we risk having our rights taken away,” adds 22-year-old Adrián Valentín. And are young people aware of these issues? “Many aren’t committed, perhaps due to indifference or lack of information, also because of social media. If you’re out in the streets every day, you’ll see the problems that people and the working class face,” they reply. Electoral Pacts
Political representation was also present in Valladolid, with the attendance of the Secretary General of the PSOE in Castile and León, Carlos Martínez, and the Minister of Equality, Ana Redondo. "The advances of Spanish democracy are also a fundamental pillar, as are the labor unions. Their role must be recognized at a time when it seems that some want to occupy certain spaces in institutions, precisely to undermine their work and workers' rights," the Secretary General emphasized.

The Minister of Equality focused her message on the results of Spain's "economic model." "We are talking about more than twenty million jobs, with record numbers of female workers. We are a resilient country in the midst of a crisis; this is a day to be proud of, to know that we are on the right track, that others are trying to follow in our footsteps and heed our recommendations. We are aware of the difficulties, the uncertainties. There are many things to improve and many things on which to continue working and moving forward," Ana Redondo pointed out. "Far-right parties in Spain are generating a climate of tension and political polarization marked by the advance of reactionary positions"
May 1st Manifesto
Political representatives have also not escaped the current political situation in Castile and León and the horizon that opened up more than a month ago with the last regional elections. "We are aware that we are at the mercy of the partisan interests of Feijóo and Abascal. Nothing will happen in the region without their approval. If putting Castile and León on hold is already a tragedy, what we hear in the background is even more so. That in order to seize power at all costs, Mr. Mañueco is abstaining, doing what he likes best: not working and handing this region over to the far right and its principles," Martínez criticized. For his part, the general coordinator of United Left in Castile and León, Juan Gascón, also criticized the People's Party (PP) and Vox for not yet having reached a governing agreement a month and a half after the last regional elections, held on March 15. "It seems there is no interest in Castile and León and that we are subordinating the interests of our region to the other two regions, as is the case with Andalusia," he stated.

In their joint manifesto, the Workers' Commissions (CCOO) and the General Union of Workers (UGT) also emphasized the "proliferation of far-right parties" in Spain. "They are generating a climate of tension and political polarization marked by the advance of reactionary positions that feed on sexism, LGBTQ+phobia, classism, and racism, wrapped in a stale and nostalgic nationalism of a past that some seek to resurrect," they stressed.

Bolivien-Proteste: Eskalation führt zu Engpässen
In Bolivien sieht sich Präsident Rodrigo Paz sechs Monate nach seinem Amtsantritt mit eskalierenden Protesten und Strassenblockaden konfrontiert.
Die bereits seit zwei Wochen andauernden Strassensperren durch Demonstranten rund um die Hauptstadt La Paz führen mittlerweile zudem zu einem Mangel an Lebensmitteln und Treibstoff in der Metropole.

Einige Gruppen protestieren gegen die steigenden Lebenshaltungskosten und fordern Lohnerhöhungen, andere wollen den Rücktritt des Präsidenten erreichen. Six months after taking office, President Rodrigo Paz in Bolivia is facing escalating protests and road blockades.

In addition to miners, farmers, and teachers, supporters of former President Evo Morales are also participating in the protests in the South American country. Some groups are protesting against the rising cost of living and demanding wage increases, while others want the president to resign. The country has been mired in a deep economic crisis for years, which repeatedly triggers protests.

Washington criticizes alleged destabilization attempt

President Paz's government calls for dialogue

Verdi ruft zu Warnstreik an Unikliniken auf
Operation verschoben? Der Verdi-Streik an vier Unikliniken sorgt für Unruhe – und das mitten im Tarifstreit um mehr Geld für 26.000 Beschäftigte.
Von red/dpa/lsw
Es drohen längere Wartezeiten und verschobene Eingriffe: An den Universitätskliniken in Freiburg, Heidelberg, Ulm und Tübingen könnte es am Montag und Dienstag zu Einschränkungen kommen. Hintergrund ist ein zweitägiger Warnstreikaufruf der Gewerkschaft Verdi für die Beschäftigten in der laufenden Tarifrunde.
Die Notfallversorgung und lebenswichtige Behandlungen sollen weiter gewährleistet bleiben. Es könne aber zu Einschränkungen oder Verzögerungen bei nicht lebensnotwendigen Operationen kommen, sagte ein Verdi-Sprecher in Stuttgart.
Als Grund für den erneuten Ausstand nannte die Gewerkschaft, dass der Arbeitgeberverband (AGU) der vier Unikliniken bisher kein Angebot vorgelegt und den Rationalisierungsschutz-Tarifvertrag gekündigt habe. „Weiter wurde angedroht, dass jeder weitere Streiktag ein mögliches Ergebnis schmälern werde.“
AGU-Vorstand Udo Kaisers forderte Verdi auf, den Warnstreik abzusagen. „Bitte bedenken Sie, dass Streikmaßnahmen durch die damit notwendigen Absagen von Eingriffen beziehungsweise ausufernde Wartezeiten für Patientinnen und Patienten und deren Angehörige außerordentlich belastend sein können.“
Rund 26.000 Beschäftigte betroffen
Hintergrund des Warnstreiks ist der festgefahrene Tarifstreit für rund 26.000 Beschäftigte der vier Unikliniken. Verdi fordert 7,5 Prozent mehr Geld, mindestens aber 320 Euro zusätzlich pro Monat für die Beschäftigten. Auszubildende sowie Praktikantinnen und Praktikanten sollen monatlich 250 Euro mehr erhalten. Zudem verlangt die Gewerkschaft für Azubis einen Mobilitätszuschuss in Höhe des Deutschlandtickets.
Die nächste Verhandlungsrunde ist laut dem Arbeitgeberverband der Universitätskliniken am 17. Juni. SAN JUAN DE LA MAGUANA.- Diversas organizaciones sociales, comunitarias, campesinas y ambientales convocaron a una huelga general de 24 horas para el próximo 27 de abril en este municipio, en rechazo a la pretensión de explotación minera en la comunidad de Los Romeros por parte de la empresa transnacional Gold Quest.

En ese sentido, reiteraron que San Juan es una provincia esencialmente agrícola, cuya sostenibilidad depende del acceso y la conservación del agua, por lo que advierten que no permitirán actividades que comprometan ese recurso.
La huelga se iniciará a las 6:00 de la mañana e incluirá el cierre de comercios, paralización del transporte y suspensión de labores en distintos sectores, como parte de una estrategia de presión para exigir la cancelación definitiva del proyecto minero.
Asimismo, hicieron un llamado a la población a respaldar de manera pacífica la jornada, al tiempo que exhortaron al Gobierno a escuchar el reclamo de las comunidades y priorizar políticas de desarrollo sostenible.

24-Hour Strike Called in San Juan de la Maguana Against Mining Project in Los Romeros
By Armando Pascual Made
SAN JUAN DE LA MAGUANA – Various social, community, peasant, and environmental organizations have called for a 24-hour general strike on April 27 in this municipality, in protest against the proposed mining operation in the community of Los Romeros by the transnational company Gold Quest.

The protest aims to draw the attention of authorities and the national public to what the organizers describe as a direct threat to natural resources, especially water, considered vital for the province's agricultural production.

The organizers maintain that the potential establishment of mining operations in the area would jeopardize the headwaters of important water sources that feed the San Juan Valley, affecting food security, the local economy, and the environmental balance. In this regard, they reiterated that San Juan is an essentially agricultural province, whose sustainability depends on access to and conservation of water, and therefore warned that they will not allow any activities that compromise this resource.

The strike will begin at 6:00 a.m. and will include the closure of businesses, a transportation shutdown, and a work stoppage in various sectors, as part of a pressure campaign to demand the definitive cancellation of the mining project.

They also called on the public to peacefully support the strike, while urging the government to listen to the communities' demands and prioritize sustainable development policies.

The organizations indicated that they will continue mobilizing until the protection of natural resources is guaranteed and any extractive initiatives in the area are ruled out.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
COCOMI condemns assault on representatives during protest, says stand on Manipur crisis unchanged
The Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity on April 25 condemned the assault on some of its representatives during a statewide protest rally and clarified that there has been no change in the organisation’s stand regarding the ongoing crisis in Manipur.
The peaceful statewide protest rally organised by the Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI) turned ugly and violent as one of the organisers was assaulted by agitators.
Today, a massive protest rally was organised by COCOMI with the intention of marching to the Chief Minister’s bungalow and submitting a memorandum containing seven questions with respect to the present crisis, implementation of the NRC, and the Tronglaobi incident. During the protest, a leader of the COCOMI student wing was assaulted at Khwairamband Ima Market after unrest broke out among groups of agitators due to dissatisfaction over the handling of the protest and misunderstandings.
Addressing the media in connection with the assault incident, COCOMI convenor Y.K. Dhiren on Saturday clarified that representatives of the organisation met Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh and submitted a memorandum following the mass rally in Imphal. Upon returning after the meeting, the COCOMI representatives informed the public that their agitation would continue as the government had not given any concrete response. However, some people among the agitators made various allegations against COCOMI representatives, which later led to violence and the assault of a COCOMI volunteer.
“After properly explaining to the public about the submission of the memorandum to the Chief Minister, some people made false allegations that COCOMI takes money from the government and receives benefits from the government. Such false allegations prompted some agitators to assault our member. COCOMI considers this as propaganda being spread to sabotage our movement,” he said, while clarifying that there had been no change in the organisation’s stand. He added that people should not spread statements driven by emotion and sentiment that could malign the image of COCOMI.
COCOMI denounced the act, terming it unacceptable, and urged all participants to maintain discipline and uphold peaceful means of protest.
He reiterated that no concrete resolution has been achieved in the Manipur crisis since May 3, 2023, alleging that a lack of decisive political will and conflicting narratives have hindered peace efforts, which the organisation termed a “proxy war” affecting indigenous communities. Dhiren also referred to the April 7 Tronglaobi incident, where an explosion killed two siblings and critically injured their mother, and alleged that subsequent protests saw security forces open fire, leading to civilian casualties.

Am 27. Juni wird die Fernpass straße (B 179) von 10 bis 12 Uhr zwischen Reutte und Nassereith für den Verkehr komplett gesperrt. Nach der Brenner-Blockade Ende Mai droht die nächste Einschränkung auf einer wichtigen Alpenroute: Wegen einer Demonstration wird die Fernpass straße in Tirol an mindestens einem, möglicherweise aber zwei Reisesamstagen in den Sommerferien vormittags für zwei Stunden gesperrt.
Grund ist am 27. Juni eine Anwohner-Demonstration aus Protest gegen die Verkehrsflut und geplante Tunnelprojekte. Anlass sind zwei Versammlungen beim Rastland in Nassereith und am Katzenberg. Die Bürgerinitiative Gurgltal-Außerfern-Mieminger Plateau demonstriert an den beiden Standorten gegen die Ausbau-Pläne des Landes am Fernpass mit zwei Tunnelprojekten und der Einführung einer Maut.
Die Bezirkshauptmannschaften Reutte und Imst verfügen nun auch eine gleichzeitige Sperre des Hahntennjochs, um ein Ausweichen über die enge Straße zu vermeiden. Vorbild ist die Brennerdemo vom 30. Mai. Die Komplettsperre an einem der wichtigsten Alpenpässe hatte für viel Aufmerksamkeit gesorgt.
Ein Gericht hatte erstmals eine Demonstration direkt auf der Autobahn genehmigt. Nach massiven Stauwarnungen hatten die meisten Autofahrer wohl ihre Reisen verschoben - die Straßen blieben unerwartet leer. Was wird genau gesperrt und wann? Am Samstag, 27.
Juni, wird die Fernpassstraße (B 179) von 10 bis 12 Uhr zwischen Reutte und Nassereith für den Verkehr komplett gesperrt. Gleichzeitig wird das Hahntennjoch (L246) gesperrt, um ein Ausweichen über die enge Straße zu vermeiden. Die Sperren gelten grundsätzlich für den gesamten Verkehr. Einsatzfahrzeuge dürfen die Sperre im Einsatz passieren.
Zudem gilt, dass AnrainerInnen, die entlang der Hahntennjochstraße wohnen, die Straße auch während der festgelegten Sperrzeiten nutzen können. Zwischen den beiden Sperren im Bereich Reutte/Katzenberg sowie Nassereith/Rastland kann die Fernpassstraße in Zwischentoren ohne Einschränkungen genutzt werden. Das bedeutet, es ist beispielsweise auch zwischen 10 und 12 Uhr möglich, von Heiterwang nach Biberwier zu fahren.
Eine An- oder Abreise aus der Region Zwischentoren ist über die Ehrwalder Straße (B 187) - Richtung Garmisch-Partenkirchen - oder die Berwang-Namloser Straße (L 21) - Richtung Lechtal - möglich. Eine weitere zweistündige Demo am Fernpass haben Bürgerinitiativen für den 1. August angemeldet. Tirol will erst die Erfahrungen der ersten Demo abwarten und dann über den 1.
August entscheiden. Der Termin fällt auf den Beginn der Sommerferien in den deutschen Bundesländern Hessen, Rheinland-Pfalz und Saarland. Vor allem am Samstagvormittag wird auf der Strecke entsprechender Reiseverkehr erwartet. Anders als bei der ganztägigen Brenner-Sperre handelt es sich am Fernpass zwar nur um eine zweistündige Unterbrechung.
Dennoch könnten sich schon vor Beginn der Sperre Staus bilden, auch nach der Freigabe sei mit Verzögerungen zu rechnen, warnt etwa der deutsche Autofahrerclub ADAC. Durchreisenden wird empfohlen, die Fernpassstrecke an diesem Tag komplett zu meiden bzw. großräumig zu umfahren. ADAC und Polizei raten an diesem Tag von nicht erforderlichen Fahrten in Richtung Tirol ab. Wer seine Reise früh am Morgen antritt oder auf einen anderen Zeitpunkt verlegt, hat die größten Chancen, gut durchzukommen.
Auch der ÖAMTC riet dazu, nötige Fahrten zu verlegen. Wer dennoch just zu der Zeit fahren muss, sollte großräumig ausweichen. Ein Rat lautete schon bei der Brenner-Sperrung: ausreichend Getränke und Proviant mitnehmen und das Auto volltanken. Laut dem Land Tirol wird die Polizei an der Grenze zu Deutschland bei Vils/Füssen kontrollieren und Informationen zur Sperre geben.
Einsatzfahrzeuge könnten passieren, Ausnahmen für Anwohner gibt es nicht. Die deutsche Autobahn-Gesellschaft des Bundes unterstütze die dortige Polizei und werde unter anderem am Autobahnkreuz Memmingen sowie am Autobahndreieck Allgäu auf Anzeigetafeln auf die Sperre hinweisen, sagt Josef Seebacher, Sprecher der Autobahn Südbayern. Sollte Tirol hinter dem Grenztunnel Füssen den Verkehr stark dosieren und damit für Staus vor dem Tunnel auf deutscher Seite sorgen, könnte die Polizei notfalls den Verkehr ausleiten und zurückschicken.
Der Reuttener Bezirkspolizeikommandant Michael Eder geht davon aus, dass wegen der Beschilderung auf deutscher Seite die aus Deutschland kommenden Fahrzeuge im Idealfall in Deutschland bleiben. Angehalten würden die Grenze passierende Fahrzeuge bei Reutte-Süd.
Allerdings handle es sich nur um eine zweistündige Sperre, betonte auch Eder den Unterschied zur Brenner-Situation zuletzt. Bei der Fernpassroute handelt es sich wie beim Brenner um eine wichtige Nord-Süd-Verbindung durch Tirol für Durchreiseverkehr. Dennoch galt die Sperre und die befürchteten Auswirkungen auf den grenzüberschreitenden Verkehr als nicht vergleichbar mit der Brenner-Demonstration Ende Mai

Traders across Pakistan have announced a protest against the government’s decision to close markets at 8 pm before Eid, saying that business activities continue until late at night during Eid and traders are facing huge financial losses due to limited working hours.
While Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervez Malik said in his recent statement that the decision to close markets at 8 pm was taken as part of an austerity campaign to overcome the energy crisis, so that the prices of petroleum products and electricity do not have to increase unbearably.
Due to the war that started after the US and Israel attacked Iran, the government in Pakistan had ordered all markets, markets and shopping malls to close at 8 pm from April 7, 2026, while restaurants and wedding halls would close at 10 pm.
This order is being implemented, but as Eid approaches, the implementation of this decision seems to be causing difficulties for traders and buyers. To which traders and buyers have reacted strongly.
Kashif Chaudhry, President of the Central Organization of Traders of Pakistan, said in a conversation with Independent Urdu that ‘business hours should be allowed to remain open until 10 pm and restaurants until 12 am, while the smart lockdown should be completely lifted on the occasion of Eid.’

He said that ‘the government is given a three-day deadline. If the demands are not accepted, a nationwide protest will be launched. This time, there will be no shutter-down strike, but markets will be forcibly opened and if cases are registered against traders, the relevant police stations will be surrounded.’

According to trader leaders, the government should give special concessions during the Eid shopping season so that citizens can shop easily and the business class can get relief.
Laeeq Ahmed, a trader leader of Mall Road Lahore, said while talking to Independent Urdu that ‘Eid is near, but despite the presence of stock in shops, sales have decreased by 75 percent. Where will they meet the rent, taxes and expenses? The government closes shops at 8 pm, which is the time for shopping in the summer season.’
The buyers also expressed strong reactions to the early closure of the markets, saying that they are having to leave work and go shopping. Because the markets close early, it is difficult to go in the evening. Petrol is being used more by making several rounds instead of one. Therefore, the government should lift this ban on the occasion of Eid.
According to the business leaders, the closure of the markets at 8 pm is causing a loss of billions of rupees. Which is also likely to lead to a significant reduction in tax revenue because if there is no business, how will they pay taxes?
Government officials maintain that the aim of closing the markets early is to save energy and improve traffic and security arrangements. However, the traders have rejected this position and demanded that business hours be allowed to be extended until late at night until Eid.

Xico, Ver.-Padres de familia de la Escuela Primaria “María Enriqueta” de Xico , tomaron este viernes 8 de mayo las instalaciones del plantel para exigir a las autoridades educativas la asignación inmediata de un maestro de Educación Física.
Los inconformes se manifestaron a las afueras de la institución y señalaron que desde hace un año la escuela carece de un docente titular en esta materia , situación que ha afectado directamente a los 146 alumnos inscritos.
“N os estamos manifestando porque los niños se han visto afectados por esta situación. No es justo que continúen sin clases de educación física ”, expresó uno de los padres de familia durante la protesta.
De acuerdo con los manifestantes, los trámites administrativos ya fueron realizados y únicamente falta que el inspector de Educación Física, José Saúl Sánchez Luna, concluya el procedimiento correspondiente para concretar la asignación del maestro.
Los padres exigieron u na respuesta inmediata por parte de las autoridades educativas para regulariza r las clases y garantizar el derecho de las y los estudiantes a una educación integral.
Cabe destacar que la primaria “María Enriqueta” es considerada una de las instituciones educativas más importantes del municipio de Xico, debido a su modelo inclusivo, ya que atiende a niñas y niños con diferentes capacidades y espectros de diferentes tipos.
