MESSAGE_TEXT:
Por: Michel Vargas
Acapulco; Gro,. A 8 de julio del 2026.- Trabajadores de la Dirección de Servicios Públicos Municipales de Acapulco realizaron una protesta para exigir la destitución del coordinador Gustavo Radilla Callado, a quien señalaron por presunto hostigamiento laboral, falta de apoyo al personal y condiciones de trabajo que calificaron como precarias.
La manifestación inició alrededor de las 07:00 de la mañana el fallecimiento de una empleada del área operativa, ocurrido hace unos días. Asimismo, reclamaron la falta de apoyo institucional hacia la familia de su compañera fallecida, situación que según comentaron generó el movimiento.
Durante la movilización, los inconformes denunciaron que la mayoría del personal pertenece a la lista de raya o es supernumerario, por lo que carecen de prestaciones básicas como seguro social, seguro de vida y condiciones adecuadas de seguridad para desempeñar sus funciones.
En declaraciones ante medios, el trabajador Hugo Palma, explicó que la protesta busca defender los derechos laborales del personal operativo y evitar que se repitan casos similares. Comentó que la trabajadora Ana Mora, quien laboró durante 21 años en la dependencia, murió tras ser atropellada mientras realizaba labores de barrido en las inmediaciones del Mercado Central en el área Pescados, sobre la avenida Constituyentes. Aseguró que la coordinación no brindó el respaldo suficiente a la familia tras el accidente.
“Los que estuvimos ayer con su familia acompañando, nos dimos cuenta que hubo una respuesta tardía de parte de la coordinación, por lo cual estamos pidiendo el apoyo a la compañera. Este movimiento es por la compañera y para su familia. La compañera era de la lista de raya y por eso es nuestra molestia, porque si hubiera sido un compañero de base o un compañero de aquí de la oficina, pues hubieran dado más apoyo”, dijo.
Los manifestantes también denunciaron presuntas jornadas de trabajo bajo condiciones de riesgo, sin protocolos de seguridad ni el equipo necesario para realizar sus labores. Afirmaron que frecuentemente son enviados a zonas de alta circulación vehicular, como puentes y mercados, sin señalización, patrullas de apoyo o medidas preventivas. Además, señalaron que deben adquirir por cuenta propia uniformes, escobas, carritos para basura y otros materiales indispensables para desempeñar sus funciones.
Respecto al accidente, los trabajadores indicaron que el conductor de un camión urbano habría atropellado a Ana Mora mientras barría la vía pública y posteriormente realizó una maniobra en reversa que volvió a impactarla.
Finalmente, los trabajadores se movilizaron al ayuntamiento de la Avenida Cuauhtémoc para hacer un llamado al gobierno municipal y atiendan sus demandas y establecer un plan de trabajo que garantice prestaciones, seguridad social, equipo de protección, protocolos de actuación en caso de accidentes y reiteraron su exigencia de que Gustavo Radilla Callado sea separado del cargo.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
By: Michel Vargas
Acapulco, Guerrero, July 8, 2026 - Workers from the Acapulco Municipal Public Services Department held a protest demanding the removal of coordinator Gustavo Radilla Callado, whom they accused of workplace harassment, lack of support for staff, and what they described as precarious working conditions.

The demonstration began around 7:00 a.m. following the death of an employee from the operations area a few days prior. They also protested the lack of institutional support for the family of their deceased colleague, a situation they said sparked the movement.

During the protest, the demonstrators denounced the fact that most of the staff are either on the day-to-day payroll or temporary workers, and therefore lack basic benefits such as social security, life insurance, and adequate safety conditions to perform their duties.

In statements to the media, worker Hugo Palma explained that the protest aims to defend the labor rights of the operational staff and prevent similar cases from recurring. He commented that Ana Mora, a worker who had been with the department for 21 years, died after being run over while sweeping near the Central Market in the Fish Market area, on Constituyentes Avenue. He asserted that the department did not provide sufficient support to the family after the accident.

“Those of us who were with her family yesterday realized that there was a delayed response from the department, which is why we are asking for support for our colleague. This movement is for our colleague and her family. She was on the payroll, and that's why we are upset, because if it had been a permanent employee or a colleague from here in the office, they would have provided more support,” he said.

The protesters also denounced alleged work shifts under hazardous conditions, without safety protocols or the necessary equipment to perform their duties. They stated that they are frequently sent to high-traffic areas, such as bridges and markets, without signage, support patrols, or preventive measures. Furthermore, they pointed out that they have to purchase their own uniforms, brooms, garbage carts, and other essential materials to perform their duties.

Regarding the accident, the workers indicated that the driver of a city bus allegedly ran over Ana Mora while she was sweeping the street and then reversed, hitting her again.

Finally, the workers marched to the city hall on Cuauhtémoc Avenue to call on the municipal government to address their demands and establish a work plan that guarantees benefits, social security, protective equipment, and protocols for action in case of accidents. They reiterated their demand that Gustavo Radilla Callado be removed from his position.

Baden-Württemberg: Das bedeuten die Warnstreiks an Unikliniken für Patienten
- Warnstreiks an vier Unikliniken in Baden-Württemberg führen zu Einschränkungen und Wartezeiten.
- Freiburg und Ulm: Montag bis Mittwoch kompletter Streik – Heidelberg und Tübingen teils kürzer.
- Notfallversorgung bleibt laut Verdi gesichert, doch OP-Säle und Bettenkapazitäten schrumpfen.
- Dritte und vorerst letzte Verhandlungsrunde am Mittwoch, begleitet von einer Protestaktion.
- Verdi fordert 7,5 % mehr Lohn bzw. mind. 320 €, Arbeitgeber verweisen auf Finanzlage.
Die Zusammenfassung wurde durch künstliche Intelligenz erstellt.
Patientinnen und Patienten an vier Universitätskliniken in Baden-Württemberg müssen sich von heute an auf Einschränkungen und längere Wartezeiten einstellen. Die Gewerkschaft Verdi ruft die Beschäftigten an den Kliniken in Freiburg, Heidelberg, Ulm und Tübingen zu mehrtägigen Warnstreiks auf.
In Freiburg und Ulm sollen die Kliniken Montag, Dienstag und Mittwoch komplett bestreikt werden, in Heidelberg und Tübingen wird einem Gewerkschaftssprecher zufolge Montag und Dienstag komplett gestreikt und am Mittwoch nur teilweise. Am Mittwoch treffen sich Gewerkschaft und Arbeitgeber demnach zur dritten und vorerst letzten Verhandlungsrunde. Dort will die Gewerkschaft dann auch vor Ort mit einer Protestaktion auf die Arbeitgeber Druck machen.
Verdi: „Die Leute sind sauer“
Patientinnen und Patienten müssen sich wegen des Warnstreiks wohl auf Einschränkungen einstellen. Die Notfallversorgung ist nach Angaben der Gewerkschaft immer gewährleistet. Man rechne aber damit, dass an den Kliniken zahlreiche OP-Säle geschlossen bleiben müssten. Auch sei damit zu rechnen, dass nicht alle Betten belegt werden könnten.
Die Gewerkschaft rechnet mit einer starken Beteiligung an der Streikaktion. „Die Arbeitgeber haben alles getan, damit die Leute sauer sind. Wir gehen davon aus, dass wir mehr Streikende haben werden als bei den Streiktagen davor“, sagte Verdi-Verhandlungsführer Jakob Becker. Die Arbeitgeber wollten Reallohnverluste für fast drei Jahre festschreiben, eine Option auf eine 45-Stunden-Woche, eine Jahressonderzahlung an Krankentage koppeln und den Schutz bei drohendem Personalabbau verschlechtern, so die Kritik des Gewerkschafters.
Arbeitgeber verweisen auf schlechte Finanzlage
Hintergrund des Ausstands sind die Tarifverhandlungen für rund 26.000 Beschäftigte der vier Unikliniken. Verdi fordert 7,5 Prozent mehr Geld, mindestens aber 320 Euro zusätzlich pro Monat für die Beschäftigten. Auszubildende sowie Praktikantinnen und Praktikanten sollen monatlich 250 Euro mehr erhalten. Zudem verlangt die Gewerkschaft für Azubis einen Mobilitätszuschuss in Höhe des Deutschlandtickets.
Die Arbeitgeber hatten in der zweiten Verhandlungsrunde ein Angebot vorgelegt, das unter anderem eine Einmalzahlung von 400 Euro und eine Gehaltssteigerung von 4,75 Prozent in drei Schritten vorsieht. Die Arbeitgeber verweisen auf die schwierige Finanzlage der Kliniken und auf erwartete Auswirkungen der Gesundheitsreform der Bundesregierung.

- Warning strikes at four university hospitals in Baden-Württemberg are leading to disruptions and waiting times.

- Freiburg and Ulm: Complete strike Monday to Wednesday – Heidelberg and Tübingen, some strikes will be shorter.

- Emergency care remains guaranteed, according to Verdi, but operating rooms and bed capacity are shrinking.

- Third and, for now, final round of negotiations on Wednesday, accompanied by a protest.

Patients at four university hospitals in Baden-Württemberg should expect disruptions and longer waiting times starting today. The Verdi union is calling on employees at the hospitals in Freiburg, Heidelberg, Ulm, and Tübingen to participate in several days of warning strikes.

In Freiburg and Ulm, hospitals are scheduled to be completely shut down on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. In Heidelberg and Tübingen, according to a union spokesperson, there will be a complete strike on Monday and Tuesday, with a partial strike on Wednesday. On Wednesday, the union and employers will meet for the third and, for now, final round of negotiations. The union also plans to put pressure on employers with a protest at the hospitals.

Verdi: "People are angry"
Patients should expect disruptions due to the warning strike. According to the union, emergency care will always be guaranteed. However, they anticipate that numerous operating rooms at the hospitals will have to remain closed. It is also expected that not all beds will be available.

The union anticipates strong participation in the strike. "The employers have done everything to make people angry. We expect to have more strikers than on previous strike days," said Verdi negotiator Jakob Becker. The employers wanted to lock in real wage losses for almost three years, link an option for a 45-hour week, ties annual bonuses to sick days, and weaken protections in the event of threatened staff reductions, according to the union representative.

Employers cite poor financial situation

The strike stems from the collective bargaining negotiations for approximately 26,000 employees at the four university hospitals. Verdi is demanding a 7.5 percent pay increase, but at least an additional €320 per month for employees. Trainees and interns should receive €250 more per month. The union is also demanding a mobility allowance for trainees equivalent to the cost of a Germany-wide public transport pass.

In the second round of negotiations, the employers presented an offer that included a one-time payment of €400 and a 4.75 percent salary increase in three stages. The employers cite the difficult financial situation of the hospitals and the anticipated impact of the federal government's healthcare reform.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
QUETTA: The Central Traders Association of Balochistan has announced a province-wide shutter-down strike on July 17 and district-level protest demonstrations on July 15 in support of the families of police personnel killed in the Ziarat tragedy.
In a joint statement, the association’s president Rahim Kakar, along with senior office-bearers including Hazrat Ali Achakzai, Yasin Mengal, Imran Tareen, Haji Saadullah Achakzai, Haji Hashim Kakar, and others, declared full support for the protest movement launched by the victims’ families and the All Parties and Martyrs of Mangi Protest Committee.
The association directed all market associations, city units, and district chapters across Balochistan to organize solidarity demonstrations on July 15 and ensure the complete closure of businesses during the July 17 province-wide strike.
The statement described the killing of a large number of police personnel in the Mangi area of Ziarat as one of the most tragic incidents in Balochistan’s history, adding that the victims’ families were pursuing a constitutional, democratic, and humanitarian struggle for justice.
The traders’ body expressed full solidarity with the bereaved families and endorsed what it described as their legitimate demands.
The association also voiced serious concern over the deteriorating law and order situation in Balochistan, stating that traders, transporters, farmers, laborers, government employees, and ordinary citizens all face growing insecurity.
According to the statement, frequent attacks on national highways, armed robberies, the burning of cargo vehicles, kidnappings, terrorist incidents, and targeted killings have severely disrupted business activity and weakened the province’s economy. It added that unsafe highways have made travel between cities increasingly dangerous, while disruptions to the transportation of goods have placed the business community under severe financial pressure.
The association further claimed that the government’s writ appears to be weakening and warned that failure to restore peace and security could have long-term consequences for trade, investment, employment, and the overall economy of both Balochistan and Pakistan.
The traders urged the federal and provincial governments to immediately accept the families’ demands, ensure justice for the victims, restore law and order, secure national highways, and guarantee the safety of traders, transporters, government employees, and the general public.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Extinction Rebellion blokkeert snelweg: Demonstranten blijven volharden
UTRECHT – Demonstranten van Extinction Rebellion blokkeren momenteel de A12 bij Utrecht, wat leidt tot verstoringen op de snelweg. Ondanks herhaalde oproepen van de politie om de snelweg te verlaten, blijven veel actievoerders vastberaden op hun plek. Sommigen van hen spelen een kaartspel, hebben puzzelboekjes meegenomen of lezen zelfs een roman, zoals gemeld door een verslaggever ter plaatse. De blokkade trekt de aandacht van voorbijrijdende automobilisten, die veel middelvingers tonen, maar er zijn ook enkele duimen omhoog als teken van steun.
De politie heeft al drie actievoerders aangehouden, die als eerste de A12 opliepen en zo de blokkade begonnen. De drie zijn overgebracht naar een politiebureau en opgesloten. De politie maakt zich klaar om de overige demonstranten te verwijderen en de blokkade op te heffen. Het is nog niet duidelijk hoeveel actievoerders er in totaal zullen worden aangehouden.
De politie heeft de demonstranten opnieuw aangesproken en hen verzocht de snelweg te verlaten en plaats te nemen in de touringbussen die klaarstaan. De oproep werd herhaald met de waarschuwing dat, als dit niet vrijwillig gebeurt, de politie de demonstranten in de bussen zou kunnen zetten, waarbij geweld ingezet kan worden als dat nodig is.
Ondanks de politie-inzet blijven de demonstranten standhouden. Ze krijgen gemengde reacties van het verkeer: enerzijds veel middelvingers van passerende automobilisten, anderzijds een enkele duim omhoog. Intussen wordt er gepicknickt op het asfalt en in de berm. De blokkade blijft voorlopig van kracht en de politie blijft zich voorbereiden op verdere stappen.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Extinction Rebellion blocks highway: Protesters persist
UTRECHT – Extinction Rebellion protesters are currently blocking the A12 near Utrecht, leading to disruptions on the highway. Despite repeated calls from the police to leave the highway, many activists remain determined in their spot. Some of them are playing card games, have brought puzzle books, or are even reading a novel, as reported by a reporter on the scene. The blockade is attracting the attention of passing motorists, who are showing many middle fingers, but there are also a few thumbs up as a sign of support.

The police have already arrested three activists who were the first to walk onto the A12 and thus started the blockade. The three have been taken to a police station and detained. The police are preparing to remove the remaining protesters and lift the blockade. It is not yet clear how many activists will be arrested in total.

The police have addressed the protesters again and requested them to leave the highway and board the waiting tour buses. The call was repeated with the warning that, if this does not happen voluntarily, the police could put the demonstrators on buses, using force if necessary.

Despite the police presence, the demonstrators continue to stand their ground. They are receiving mixed reactions from traffic: on the one hand, many middle fingers from passing motorists; on the other, the occasional thumbs up. Meanwhile, people are picnicking on the asphalt and in the verges. The blockade remains in effect for the time being, and the police continue to prepare for further action.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
El alcalde de Lima, Renzo Reggiardo, informó que se analizarán posibles medidas para resguardar el centro de la ciudad ante la eventual realización de marchas convocadas para este miércoles 15 de julio.
Reggiardo precisó que aún no existe una decisión definitiva sobre las medidas que se aplicarán. Sin embargo, indicó que se coordinará con la Policía Nacional para determinar si será necesario restringir el tránsito vehicular, como ocurrió en anteriores movilizaciones protagonizadas por militantes de Juntos por el Perú en las calles de la capital.
“Una vez que tengamos claridad respecto a esos anuncios, vamos a tomar las decisiones necesarias, así sean más duras. Espero que no tengamos que tomar medidas como el cierre al acceso vehicular al centro de la ciudad, que ya la hemos tomado en dos oportunidades, pero han permitido cuidar el patrimonio de la ciudad capital”, declaró a la prensa tras una actividad en la plaza Mayor.
En otro momento, el alcalde de Lima cuestionó la eventual decisión del presidente José María Balcázar de conceder un indulto a Pedro Castillo y consideró que hacerlo sería “insano”.
“Absolutamente insano si se da una medida de esa naturaleza por parte del Gobierno. Creo que sería gravísimo que un Gobierno que está terminando funciones realice una acción como esa. No podemos estar los peruanos en este tipo de situaciones”, agregó el burgomaestre.
Este miércoles 15 de julio, el Jurado Nacional de Elecciones (JNE) entregará las credenciales a Keiko Fujimori en el Teatro Municipal de Lima, en una jornada en la que también se prevé la realización de posibles movilizaciones.
Roberto Sánchez, líder de Juntos por el Perú y excandidato presidencial, anunció este mes una serie de movilizaciones sociales programadas en Lima y distintas regiones del país.
Sánchez señaló que estas jornadas de protesta buscan principalmente expresar respaldo a los ciudadanos y dirigentes de su agrupación que afrontan denuncias penales tras haber participado en anteriores manifestaciones.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
The mayor of Lima, Renzo Reggiardo, announced that possible measures to protect the city center will be analyzed in anticipation of marches scheduled for Wednesday, July 15.

Reggiardo clarified that no final decision has yet been made regarding the measures to be implemented. However, he indicated that he will coordinate with the National Police to determine if it will be necessary to restrict vehicular traffic, as occurred during previous demonstrations led by members of the Together for Peru coalition in the capital.

"Once we have clarity regarding these announcements, we will make the necessary decisions, even if they are more stringent. I hope we won't have to take measures such as closing vehicular access to the city center, which we have already done twice, but which have allowed us to protect the heritage of the capital city," he told the press after an event in the Plaza Mayor.

At another point, the mayor of Lima questioned President José María Balcázar's potential decision to grant a pardon to Pedro Castillo, deeming it "insane."

"Absolutely insane if the government takes such a measure. I believe it would be extremely serious for a government that is ending its term to carry out such an action. We Peruvians cannot be in this type of situation," the mayor added.

This Wednesday, July 15, the National Elections Board (JNE) will present credentials to Keiko Fujimori at the Municipal Theater of Lima, on a day that is also expected to see possible demonstrations.

Roberto Sánchez, leader of Together for Peru and former presidential candidate, announced this month a series of social mobilizations planned in Lima and various regions of the country.

Sánchez indicated that these protests primarily aim to express support for citizens and leaders of his group who face criminal charges after participating in previous demonstrations.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Συγκέντρωση, κινητοποίηση πραγματοποίησε την Παρασκευή (01.05.26) το Εργατικό Κέντρο Αγρινίου, στο πλαίσιο της Εργατικής Πρωτομαγιάς, θέτοντας στο επίκεντρο αιτήματα για αυξήσεις σε μισθούς και συντάξεις, βελτίωση των συνθηκών εργασίας και ουσιαστικά μέτρα στήριξης των νοικοκυριών.
Η κινητοποίηση, ως είθισται, είχε, παράλληλα έντονο συμβολικό χαρακτήρα, καθώς αποτέλεσε φόρο τιμής στα 140 χρόνια από τα γεγονότα της 1ης Μαΐου 1886 στο Σικάγο και τον αγώνα των εργατών για την καθιέρωση του οκταώρου.
Ιδιαίτερη αναφορά έγινε επίσης στη μεγάλη καπνεργατική απεργία του 1926 στο Αγρίνιο, πριν 100 χρόνια, και τη δολοφονημένη καπνεργάτρια Βασιλική Γεωργαντζέλη και το νεολαίο Θεμιστοκλή Καρανικόλα
Η ιστορική αναδρομή περιλάμβανε ακόμη τα γεγονότα του Μάη του 1936 στη Θεσσαλονίκη, καθώς και τους 200 εκτελεσμένους της Πρωτομαγιάς του 1944, συνδέοντας τους αγώνες του παρελθόντος με τις διεκδικήσεις του σήμερα.
Στο πλαίσιο της κινητοποίησης εκφράστηκε, επίσης, η αντίθεση στους πολέμους που βρίσκονται σε εξέλιξη στη Μέση Ανατολή και την Ουκρανία, με το Εργατικό Κέντρο να τονίζει την ανάγκη απεμπλοκής από πολεμικούς σχεδιασμούς.
Όπως επισημάνθηκε, οι σύγχρονες διεκδικήσεις επικεντρώνονται στην ενίσχυση των εισοδημάτων, τη στήριξη της δημόσιας παιδείας και υγείας, καθώς και στη βελτίωση του εργασιακού πλαισίου. Μεταξύ άλλων, τίθενται τα θέματα για την καθιέρωση 7ωρης ημερήσιας εργασίας, πενθήμερης απασχόλησης και 35ωρης εβδομαδιαίας εργασίας, επαναφορά του 13ου και 14ου μισθού και σύνταξης, καθώς και υπογραφή συλλογικών συμβάσεων εργασίας με διεύρυνση δικαιωμάτων.
Παράλληλα, ζητείται η ενίσχυση των μέτρων υγείας και ασφάλειας στους χώρους εργασίας, η κατάργηση του ΦΠΑ σε βασικά είδη λαϊκής κατανάλωσης και η κατάργηση του Ειδικού Φόρου Κατανάλωσης στα καύσιμα, στο πλαίσιο μιας συνολικής πολιτικής στήριξης των εργαζομένων και των νοικοκυριών, όπως επίσης για την κατάργηση του ΦΠΑ στα είδη πλατιάς λαϊκής κατανάλωσης και την κατάργηση του ΕΦΚ στα καύσιμα.
Ο Πρόεδρος του Εργατικού Κέντρου Κώστας Παπακωνσταντίνου μεταξύ άλλων τόνισε:
«Tην 1η Μάη του 2026 πιάνουμε το αιματοβαμμένο κόκκινο νήμα που συνδέει τους αγώνες της τάξης μας για έναν κόσμο στον μπόι των ονείρων και των ανθρώπων. Βαδίζουμε στον δρόμο της ανατροπής που χάραξαν οι ήρωες και πρωτοπόροι της ταξικής πάλης, από τους εργάτες του Σικάγου του 1886 μέχρι τους 200 κομμουνιστές που εκτελέστηκαν στην Καισαριανή την Πρωτομαγιά του 1944. Τώρα είναι η ώρα να βγει με ορμή στο προσκήνιο η εργατική τάξη, να συγκρουστεί με την πολιτική του κέρδους που εγκληματεί καθημερινά στις χώρες δουλειάς, τσακίζει μισθούς, εργασιακά και λαϊκά δικαιώματα που σέρνει το λαό στα σφαγεία του ιμπεριαλιστικού πολέμου.
Η φετινή εργατική πρωτομαγιά έρχεται μετά από το ελπιδοφόρο μήνυμα οργάνωσης, αγωνιστικής ανάτασης και μάχης που εκφράστηκε στη μεγαλύτερη πανεργατική σύσκεψη που έχει πραγματοποιηθεί ποτέ στην Ελλάδα στις 4 Απρίλη στην Καισαριανή, που διοργανώθηκε μετά
από κάλεσμα του Πανεργατικού Αγωνιστικού Μετώπου. Η συμμετοχή 720 σωματείων, ομοσπονδιών, εργατικών κέντρων, μεταξύ αυτών και του Αγρινίου, μαζί με άλλα σωματεία της πόλης και πάνω από 2.000 συνδικαλιστών, έδειξε ότι υπάρχουν οι προϋποθέσεις οι εργαζόμενοι και τα συνδικάτα τους να βάλουμε τη δική μας σφραγίδα και να καθορίσουμε προς όφελός μας τις εξελίξεις».
Χαιρετισμό στην κινητοποίηση του Εργατικού Κέντρου έκανε η εκπρόσωπος των μαθητών, Δανάη Ρίζου ο Πρόεδρος της Ομοσπονδίας Αγροτικών Συλλόγων Αιτωλοακαρνανίας, Σπύρος Κοτοπούλης, ενώ η κινητοποίηση ολοκληρώθηκε με πορεία στους κεντρικούς δρόμους του Αγρινίου.

The Agrinio Labor Center held a rally and mobilization on Friday (01.05.26), in the context of Labor Day, focusing on demands for increases in wages and pensions, improvement of working conditions and substantial measures to support households.
The mobilization, as usual, also had a strong symbolic character, as it was a tribute to the 140th anniversary of the events of May 1, 1886 in Chicago and the struggle of workers for the establishment of the eight-hour workday.
Special mention was also made of the great tobacco workers' strike of 1926 in Agrinio, 100 years ago, and the murdered tobacco worker Vasiliki Georgantzeli and the young Themistoklis Karanikolas.
The historical retrospective also included the events of May 1936 in Thessaloniki, as well as the 200 executed on May Day 1944, connecting the struggles of the past with the demands of today.
In the context of the mobilization, opposition to the ongoing wars in the Middle East and Ukraine was also expressed, with the Labor Center emphasizing the need to disengage from war plans.
As noted, modern demands focus on increasing incomes, supporting public education and health, as well as improving the working environment. Among other things, the issues raised are the establishment of a 7-hour workday, a five-day workweek and a 35-hour workweek, the reinstatement of the 13th and 14th salary and pension, as well as the signing of collective labor agreements with expanded rights.
At the same time, the strengthening of health and safety measures in the workplace, the abolition of VAT on basic consumer goods and the abolition of the Special Consumption Tax on fuel, within the framework of a comprehensive policy of support for workers and households, as well as the abolition of VAT on consumer goods and the abolition of the VAT on fuel, are requested.
The President of the Labor Center, Costas Papakonstantinou, among other things, emphasized:
"On May 1, 2026, we grasp the blood-stained red thread that connects the struggles of our class for a world in the stature of dreams and people. We walk on the path of overthrow that was charted by the heroes and pioneers of the class struggle, from the workers of Chicago in 1886 to the 200 communists who were executed in Kaisariani on May Day 1944. Now is the time for the working class to come to the fore with momentum, to clash with the policy of profit that commits crimes daily in the countries of work, crushes wages, labor and popular rights that drags the people into the slaughterhouses of imperialist war.
This year's May Day workers' day comes after the hopeful message of organization, militant upliftment and struggle expressed at the largest pan-workers' meeting ever held in Greece on April 4 in Kaisariani, which was organized following the call of the Pan-Workers' Struggle Front. The participation of 720 unions, federations, workers' centers, including Agrinio, along with other unions in the city and over 2,000 trade unionists, showed that the conditions exist for us, the workers and their unions, to put our own stamp and determine developments to our benefit. The mobilization of the Labor Center was welcomed by the student representative, Danae Rizou, and the President of the Federation of Agricultural Associations of Aitoloakarnania, Spyros Kotopoulis, while the mobilization concluded with a march through the main streets of Agrinio.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
FIC Report (Kwara State) – Members of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on Monday morning staged a protest at the entrance of the Lower Niger River Basin Development Authority (LNRBDA) in Ilorin over what they described as anti-worker policies introduced by the Managing Director of the agency, Olushola George Olumoroti.
The protesting workers, under the Nigeria Union of Agriculture and Allied Employees (NUAAE), also accused the management of financial mismanagement within the organisation.
Carrying placards with different messages, the workers called for the immediate removal of the Managing Director, insisting that he lacked the capacity to continue leading the authority. Some of the placards condemned alleged corruption, victimisation of staff, and disregard for labour laws and due process within the establishment.
The protest, themed around opposition to the Managing Director’s alleged anti-labour actions against NUAAE members, led to a complete shutdown of the authority’s entrance and exit gates, preventing movement in and out of the premises. The demonstration was led by the Kwara State Chairman of the NLC, Comrade Muritala Saheed Olayinka.
Speaking during the protest, Olayinka criticised the management for allegedly undermining workers’ welfare and rights.
Also addressing the protesters, the Chairperson of the NLC Women Committee in the state, Comrade Victoria Agboola, accused the management of victimising employees and demoting union leaders who opposed certain policies. She warned that allowing such practices to continue could negatively affect the future of the authority.
Reported by:
Aina Y.B (ACI&PRO)
FIC, Ilorin.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Córdoba, Ver.- La exigencia de justicia volvió a escucharse en el parque 21 de Mayo, donde periodistas de Córdoba y la región se concentraron para condenar el asesinato del reportero Luis Ángel López y demandar resultados concretos en las investigaciones de agresiones contra comunicadores en Veracruz.
Durante la manifestación, los asistentes señalaron que ejercer el periodismo se ha convertido en una actividad de riesgo debido a la violencia y a la falta de castigo para quienes atentan contra la libertad de expresión. Advirtieron que la impunidad sigue siendo uno de los principales problemas que enfrenta el gremio.
Hugo Morales Alejo expresó que cada crimen contra un periodista representa una pérdida para la sociedad, pues se silencia una voz encargada de informar y documentar hechos de interés público. Por ello, pidió que el homicidio de Luis Ángel López no quede sin resolver.
Los comunicadores criticaron la escasez de resultados en las investigaciones relacionadas con periodistas asesinados y desaparecidos, situación que, afirmaron, genera desconfianza y alimenta el temor entre quienes realizan coberturas informativas en distintas regiones del estado.
Asimismo, exigieron que las autoridades estatales y federales refuercen las acciones para garantizar la seguridad de los reporteros y asegurar que los responsables de las agresiones enfrenten la justicia.
Durante el pronunciamiento también se pidió la localización con vida de la periodista Roxana, desaparecida desde hace dos semanas, al considerar que cada caso sin resolver representa una herida abierta para el gremio y para la sociedad.
Los asistentes señalaron que la libertad de expresión no puede ejercerse plenamente mientras persistan las amenazas, las agresiones y el miedo entre quienes tienen la responsabilidad de informar a la ciudadanía.
La protesta concluyó con un llamado a las autoridades para romper el ciclo de impunidad que ha marcado numerosos casos de violencia contra periodistas y con la exigencia de justicia para Luis Ángel López y para todos los comunicadores que han sido víctimas de la inseguridad en Veracruz.
Ari Marini
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Cordoba, Veracruz – The demand for justice echoed once again in Parque 21 de Mayo, where journalists from Cordoba and the surrounding region gathered to condemn the murder of reporter Luis Ángel López and demand concrete results in the investigations of attacks against journalists in Veracruz.

During the demonstration, attendees pointed out that practicing journalism has become a risky activity due to the violence and the lack of punishment for those who attack freedom of expression. They warned that impunity remains one of the main problems facing the profession.

Jubilados de confianza de la CFE en Durango denuncian robo en sus pensiones tras reforma
DENICE RAMÍREZ
Los topes a las pensiones tras la reforma al artículo 127 provocaron manifestaciones a nivel nacional, por lo que jubilados de confianza de la Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE) en Durango también se unieron al movimiento para denunciar lo que consideran un “robo a sus pensiones”.
Algunos integrantes del Movimiento Nacional de Jubilados de Confianza de la CFE dieron a conocer su inconformidad en diferentes espacios en lo local.
El vocero del movimiento, Jesús Héctor Acevedo Chapa, indicó que en Durango son al menos 200 los jubilados de confianza afectados; además, también se incluyen jubilados de confianza de Pemex, Banobras y del Sindicato de Electricistas.
Explicó que el tope a las pensiones los deja en una situación de indefensión y, sobre todo, representa un robo a su patrimonio y un atropello, luego de años de trabajo.
“La pensión es un patrimonio, nos están robando nuestro patrimonio”, afirmó.
Esperan que legisladores locales y nacionales se manifiesten en contra y, sobre todo, presenten una iniciativa para que se quite la retroactividad y se tome en cuenta el artículo 14 de la Constitución, el cual establece que ninguna ley puede aplicarse en perjuicio de los trabajadores.
La principal preocupación, señaló, es que se les están vulnerando derechos ya adquiridos mediante contratos y convenios respaldados por las propias autoridades laborales.
El artículo 127 ya establecía que ningún servidor público podía recibir una remuneración o pensión mayor a la establecida para el Presidente; sin embargo, con la reciente reforma se determina que ninguna pensión o jubilación para exservidores públicos de confianza puede exceder el 50 por ciento de la remuneración establecida para el Presidente de la República.
La reforma a este artículo de la Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, impulsada por el Gobierno Federal para reducir las llamadas “pensiones doradas”, ya fue publicada en el Diario Oficial de la Federación desde el pasado 11 de abril de 2026 y se dieron 90 días para su ajuste.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Retired CFE Management Employees in Durango Denounce Pension Theft Following Reform
DENICE RAMÍREZ
Pension caps imposed after the reform to Article 127 sparked nationwide protests, and retired management employees of the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) in Durango have joined the movement to denounce what they consider a "theft of their pensions."

Some members of the National Movement of Retired Management Employees of the CFE voiced their discontent in various local forums.

The movement's spokesperson, Jesús Héctor Acevedo Chapa, indicated that at least 200 retired management employees are affected in Durango; this also includes retired management employees from Pemex, Banobras, and the Electrical Workers Union.

He explained that the pension cap leaves them defenseless and, above all, represents a theft of their assets and an injustice after years of service. “Our pensions are our assets; they are stealing our assets,” he stated.

They hope that local and national legislators will speak out against this and, above all, introduce legislation to eliminate the retroactive application of the law and ensure compliance with Article 14 of the Constitution, which establishes that no law can be applied to the detriment of workers.

The main concern, he pointed out, is that their acquired rights, secured through contracts and agreements endorsed by the labor authorities themselves, are being violated.

Article 127 already stipulated that no public servant could receive a salary or pension higher than that established for the President; however, the recent reform stipulates that no pension or retirement benefit for former public servants in positions of trust can exceed 50 percent of the salary established for the President of the Republic.

The reform to this article of the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States, promoted by the Federal Government to reduce so-called "golden pensions," was published in the Official Gazette of the Federation on April 11, 2026, and a 90-day period was granted for its implementation.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
وجد ديوان كاتب الدولة المكلف بالصناعة التقليدية والاقتصاد الاجتماعي والتضامني، لحسن السعدي، نفسه في قلب عاصفة نقابية جديدة، بعدما وجهت إليه النقابات الأكثر تمثيلية بالقطاع اتهامات بالتدخل في تدبير الشؤون الإدارية واستهداف العمل النقابي، قبل أن تعلن الانتقال إلى خطوات احتجاجية ميدانية تشمل حمل الشارة الحمراء وتنظيم وقفة وطنية أمام مقر كتابة الدولة بالرباط.
وجاء هذا التصعيد في وقت تتحدث فيه النقابات عن انسداد قنوات الحوار الاجتماعي وتراكم ملفات مهنية واجتماعية ظلت، بحسب تعبيرها، حبيسة الوعود واللجان، وسط تنامي حالة التذمر في صفوف موظفي القطاع ومستخدمي غرف الصناعة التقليدية.
وفي بيان توصل به نيشان، قال التنسيق النقابي الثلاثي بقطاع الصناعة التقليدية والاقتصاد الاجتماعي والتضامني إن حالة الاحتقان داخل القطاع بلغت مستويات مقلقة بسبب استمرار التأخر في معالجة عدد من الملفات العالقة، وفي مقدمتها وضعية الموظفين العرضيين السابقين تجاه النظام الجماعي لمنح رواتب التقاعد، إلى جانب اختلالات مرتبطة بالانتقالات والترقيات ومناصب المسؤولية والتكوين المستمر.
ولم يكتف التنسيق النقابي بتوجيه انتقادات إلى طريقة تدبير هذه الملفات، بل صعّد لهجته باتهام ديوان كاتب الدولة بالتدخل في الشؤون الإدارية للقطاع واستهداف التنسيق النقابي الثلاثي، معتبراً أن ذلك يتعارض مع المقتضيات القانونية المنظمة لاختصاصات أعضاء الدواوين الوزارية.
كما اتهم رئيس قسم الموارد البشرية باستعمال سلطته الإدارية في ممارسة ضغوط على عدد من الموظفين عبر بعض المديرين الترابيين، من أجل فرض ما وصفه بـ”واقع نقابي مصطنع” وإنشاء مكاتب صورية، وهي ممارسات قال إنها تمس بمبادئ الحياد الإداري والحرية النقابية.
وسجل البيان استمرار تعثر عدد من الملفات الأخرى، من بينها ملف التعويضات الخاصة بمستخدمي غرف الصناعة التقليدية، والتغطية الصحية والتقاعد، وإخراج النظام الأساسي للمستخدمين، فضلاً عن ما اعتبره تجاهلاً لمطالب مرتبطة بالتكوين المهني والأعمال الاجتماعية.
وأمام ما وصفه باستمرار سياسة التسويف وعدم التفاعل الإيجابي مع مطالب الشغيلة، أعلن التنسيق النقابي إطلاق برنامج نضالي أولي يتضمن حمل الشارة الحمراء بمختلف المصالح المركزية والخارجية للقطاع يوم 25 يونيو الجاري، مع تنظيم وقفة احتجاجية وطنية أمام مقر كتابة الدولة بالرباط سيُعلن عن تاريخها لاحقاً.
ويأتي هذا التطور ليضع كتابة الدولة المكلفة بالصناعة التقليدية أمام أول مواجهة نقابية واسعة خلال الأشهر الأخيرة، في وقت تراهن فيه النقابات على دفع الوزارة إلى فتح حوار اجتماعي “جاد ومنتج” يفضي إلى تسوية الملفات العالقة واحتواء منسوب الاحتقان المتصاعد داخل القطاع.

The office of the Secretary of State for Traditional Industry, Social Economy, and Solidarity, Lahcen Saadi, has found itself at the center of a new union storm. The most representative unions in the sector have accused him of interfering in administrative affairs and targeting union activity, before announcing a shift to on-the-ground protest actions, including wearing red armbands and organizing a national sit-in in front of the Secretary of State's office in Rabat.

This escalation comes at a time when unions are reporting a breakdown in social dialogue and a backlog of professional and social issues that, according to them, remain mired in promises and committees. This is occurring amidst growing discontent among sector employees and staff of the Chambers of Traditional Industry.

In a statement received by Nishan, the tripartite union coordination in the traditional industry and social economy sector said that the tension within the sector has reached alarming levels due to the continued delays in addressing several outstanding issues. These include the status of former temporary employees with regard to the collective pension scheme, as well as irregularities related to transfers, promotions, positions of responsibility, and continuing education. The union coordination committee did not merely criticize the handling of these files, but escalated its rhetoric by accusing the office of the Secretary of State of interfering in the sector's administrative affairs and targeting the tripartite union coordination committee. The committee asserted that this contravened the legal provisions governing the responsibilities of members of ministerial offices.

It also accused the head of the Human Resources Department of abusing his administrative authority to exert pressure on several employees through certain regional directors, in order to impose what it termed an "artificial union reality" and establish sham offices. These practices, the committee argued, violated the principles of administrative neutrality and union freedom.

The statement also noted the continued stagnation of several other files, including those related to compensation for employees of the Chambers of Traditional Industry, health insurance and retirement benefits, and the issuance of the employee statute. Furthermore, it highlighted what it considered the disregard for demands related to vocational training and social services. Faced with what it described as a continued policy of procrastination and a lack of positive engagement with workers' demands, the union coordination announced the launch of an initial protest program. This program includes wearing red armbands at various central and regional offices within the sector on June 25th, along with a national protest in front of the State Secretariat in Rabat, the date of which will be announced later.

This development marks the first major union confrontation with the State Secretariat for Traditional Industries in recent months, at a time when unions are hoping to push the ministry to engage in a "serious and productive" social dialogue that will resolve outstanding issues and contain the rising tension within the sector.

Ver.di Herne ruft zur Teilnahme auf
Ruhrpott Rebellion 2026 in Bochum

Gleichzeitig fließen enorme öffentliche Mittel in die militärische Aufrüstung, anstatt in zukunftsfähige Infrastruktur investiert zu werden.

In der Tradition historischer gewerkschaftlicher Kämpfe im Ruhrgebiet gelte es nun, die erkämpften Errungenschaften aktiv zu verteidigen. Die „Ruhrpott-Rebellion“ soll ein unüberhörbares Signal gegen Sozialabbau und wachsende Ungleichheit setzen.

Ver.di Herne calls for participation

Ruhrpott Rebellion 2026 in Bochum
The ver.di Herne local branch is calling for a clear rethink of current politics and urges all members and citizens to join the union initiative "Ruhrpott Rebellion 2026." The demonstration and rally, under the motto "solidarity, loud, and uncomfortable," will take place on Friday, July 10, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. at Dr.-Ruer-Platz in Bochum.

The union is observing the growing pressure on social security with great concern. While demands for longer working hours, a higher retirement age, and cuts to social benefits are growing louder, societal wealth is becoming increasingly concentrated. At the same time, enormous public funds are flowing into military rearmament instead of being invested in future-proof infrastructure.

“Investments in good jobs, education, healthcare, long-term care, and affordable housing must finally be given priority. Social security and strong collective bargaining agreements are not mere cost factors, but the foundation for social cohesion and our democracy,” explains the ver.di local executive committee.

In the tradition of historical trade union struggles in the Ruhr region, it is now crucial to actively defend the hard-won gains. The “Ruhrpott Rebellion” aims to send an unmistakable signal against social cutbacks and growing inequality.

Panama: Farmers protest against dam plan to feed canal
A colorful march of farmers flooded the streets yesterday, with some participants on horseback, as part of a mobilization against the promoted plan to build a dam on the Rio Indio, with the aim of guaranteeing the smooth operation of the Panama Canal in the event of drought.
The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) considers the dam on the Rio Indio, about 70 kilometers northeast of the capital, a “strategic project” for the operation of the ocean passage for the next 50 years.
But farmers in the area emphasize that the project will force them to abandon their lands. “This choice,” building a dam, “is difficult,” said Claudino Dominguez, a 65-year-old farmer who took part in the demonstration in the municipality of Limón, in the central Chagres region.
The farmers fear they will never find fields as fertile as the ones they are working on again and refuse to move to drier areas, where “not even cassava grows, even if you fertilize it,” he said.
“I am fighting for our fields, for our rivers, for our farmers,” said Elias Serrano, 75, another resident of the area.
The project, for which the investment is expected to reach 1.6 billion dollars, is scheduled to begin in 2027 and be completed in 2032; it is expected to occupy an area of ​​46,000 acres.
According to the design, the water that the dam will hold will be channeled through an underground tunnel into Gatun Lake, in the canal basin.
The construction of the dam will force some 2,500 residents to abandon their lands and/or homes, according to the ACP. The aim is to prevent the consequences of extreme droughts in the future, such as the one in 2023, which had drastically reduced ship traffic in the canal – a major consumer of water, as it is needed for its mechanism to operate.

Metalworkers in the Balearic Islands announce four-day strike
They accuse employers of failing to make progress in negotiations to approve the sector's collective bargaining agreement
Metalworkers in the Balearic Islands have called a four-day strike, which would begin on July 27 and end on July 30. The action would affect approximately 39,000 workers in this sector.

This labor mobilization is supported by the unions UGT, USO, CC OO, and Fica Industria, which are present at the negotiating table with the two employers' associations, Asema and Febame. Both sides have been negotiating the renewal of a new collective bargaining agreement for the sector for six months, but negotiations are currently at a standstill, as they have not reached an agreement that benefits both workers and employers.

According to Iñaki Huarte of CC OO and Roberto Serrano of UGT, the disagreement centers on the so-called absorption and compensation supplement. It's a supplement included in the payroll of employees in the metal sector and stipulated in the latest collective bargaining agreement.

Union representatives want this supplement eliminated because they claim it's the reason workers aren't seeing the salary increase agreed upon with employers. The union representatives explained that while this increase is applied to workers' base pay, employers reduce this double supplement, so employees don't notice any pay raise. The union representatives want this double supplement eliminated and the entire salary increase applied to the base pay. This way, employees will actually see the pay raise.
The employers are unwilling to accept these demands. This explains why negotiations have been stalled for months, although both sides remain interested in reaching an agreement to sign the new collective bargaining agreement. While the companies want this agreement to last four years, the workers will only accept a maximum of three. Following the strike announcement, a conciliation meeting was held this morning at the Tamir union hall to try to reach an agreement between the two sides. The outcome of the negotiations has not yet been reported, but the unions have made it clear that if these supplements are not eliminated, the strike will proceed.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Keine Sachschäden bei unbewilligter Antifa-Demo in Bern
Am «antifaschistischen Nachmittagsspaziergang» vom Samstag in Bern sind nach Angaben der Polizei vom Sonntag keine Sachbeschädigungen verübt worden. An der unbewilligten Kundgebung von Linksaussen-Gruppierungen hatten mehrere hundert Personen teilgenommen.
Die Polizei war mit einem grösseren Aufgebot vor Ort. Sie liess die Demonstrierenden gewähren, wie ein Reporter der Nachrichtenagentur Keystone-SDA berichtete. Der öffentliche und private Verkehr war zeitweise stark eingeschränkt.
In Aufrufen zur Demo wurde unter anderem vor einem weltweiten Rechtsruck gewarnt. Staatliche Gewalt und Aufrüstung seien im bürgerlichen Staat legitimiert, während Proteste kriminalisiert würden. Das Geld für Rüstungsbudgets fehle letztlich in der sozialen Infrastruktur und im Gesundheitssystem.
«Selbstverständlich antifaschistisch» lautete der Slogan auf dem Banner des vermummten Frontblocks, der den Umzug anführte. Dahinter gab es einen «queeren Schwarm», einen anti-imperialistischen Block («Antifa bedeutet Intifada») und einen Kinderblock.
Die Polizei stellte sicher, dass der Umzug nicht am Bundeshaus vorbeiführen konnte. Dort war eine bewilligte Veranstaltung des Vereins «Gebet für die Schweiz» mit etwa 200 Teilnehmenden im Gang.
Die Kantonspolizei Bern teilte am Sonntagvormittag auf Anfrage der Nachrichtenagentur Keystone-SDA mit, dass sie keine Kenntnisse von Sachbeschädigungen habe. Es sei zu keinen Anzeigen gekommen. Auch seien keine Personen auf eine Polizeiwache gebracht worden.
Die anarchistische Gruppe Bern hatte mitgeteilt, dass sie im Rahmen der Kundgebung den Eingang der Fremdenpolizei zugemauert habe. Die Kantonspolizei wertete dies als «Verunreinigung von fremden Eigentum». Das Tiefbauamt sei zur Entfernung aufgeboten worden.
Die Antifa-Demo führte auch am Berner Rathaus vorbei. Vor dem Gebäude hatten sich Polizisten in Kampfmontur aufgestellt. Die Stimmung blieb friedlich.
Im bernischen Grossen Rat wird in der Juni-Session ein Vorstoss für ein Verbot der Antifa diskutiert. Der Regierungsrat unterstützt die Forderung des SVP-Grossrats Thomas Fuchs.
Der Bundesrat hatte im März einen ähnlichen Vorstoss aus dem Nationalrat abgelehnt. Er begründete dies damit, dass die Antifa keine Organisation im engeren Sinn sei, sondern eine heterogene Bewegung beziehungsweise ein loses internationales Netzwerk ohne klare Organisationsstruktur.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
No property damage at unauthorized anti-fascist demonstration in Bern
According to police reports on Sunday, no property damage occurred during Saturday's "anti-fascist afternoon stroll" in Bern. Several hundred people participated in the unauthorized demonstration organized by far-left groups.

Police were present in force. They allowed the demonstrators to proceed, as reported by a Keystone-SDA news agency reporter. Public and private transportation was severely disrupted for a time.

Calls to the demonstration included warnings about a global shift to the right. State violence and rearmament were legitimized in bourgeois states, while protests were criminalized. The money spent on military budgets was ultimately lacking in social infrastructure and the healthcare system.

"Naturally anti-fascist" was the slogan on the banner of the masked front group that led the march. Behind them was a "queer swarm," an anti-imperialist bloc ("Antifa means Intifada"), and a children's bloc.

The police ensured that the march could not pass by the Federal Parliament Building. An authorized event organized by the association "Prayer for Switzerland," with approximately 200 participants, was underway there.

The Bern cantonal police told the Keystone-SDA news agency on Sunday morning that they had no knowledge of any property damage. No charges had been filed, and no one had been taken to a police station.

The Bern anarchist group had reported that they had bricked up the entrance to the immigration office during the demonstration. The cantonal police considered this "defacement of property." The civil engineering office was called in to remove the brick.

The Antifa demonstration also passed by Bern's City Hall. Police officers in riot gear were stationed in front of the building. The atmosphere remained peaceful.

The Bernese Grand Council will debate a motion to ban Antifa during its June session. The cantonal government supports the demand put forward by SVP Grand Councillor Thomas Fuchs.

In March, the Federal Council rejected a similar motion from the National Council. It justified its decision by stating that Antifa is not an organization in the strict sense, but rather a heterogeneous movement or a loose international network without a clear organizational structure.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Thousands march in Durban as ActionSA accuses government of border failure
ActionSA KwaZulu-Natal leader Zwakele Mncwango says South Africa has been "invaded" by undocumented immigrants
Image: Hope Ntanzi/IOL
ActionSA KwaZulu-Natal leader Zwakele Mncwango says South Africa has been "invaded" by undocumented immigrants, accusing the government of failing to protect the country's borders as thousands of people took part in an anti-illegal immigration march in Durban on Tuesday.
The march began at King Dinuzulu Park before proceeding through the Durban CBD and ending at the SAPS Point Road police station, where organisers handed over a memorandum.
During the process, the crowd refused to be addressed by eThekwini Mayor Cyril Xaba and Deputy Minister of Police Cassel Mathale.
Many businesses in the CBD, including shops owned by foreign nationals, closed on Monday as a precaution.
Speaking at the demonstration, Mncwango said there was "nothing wrong" with people entering South Africa legally, but argued that the country could no longer accept illegal immigration.
"We have been very consistent on the issue of illegal immigration. Our country has been invaded, but one must also clarify this point: there's nothing wrong if people come from other countries legally," Mncwango said.
"We must accept that right now we can't accept the current situation of illegal immigrants. We have so many illegal foreigners, and it's a threat to our country".
Mncwango also accused the government of failing to secure the country's borders and dismissed intelligence reports warning of possible violence and looting linked to the march.
"The government has shown its failure. They have failed to safeguard our country, and even now the intelligence that told them there would be anarchy and looting is wrong, because the leadership of March and March has been saying that they are organising a peaceful march," he said.
He further criticised the government’s security preparations, saying the estimated R6 billion allocated for monitoring the marches was a waste of public money.
"It's a waste of money in my view, but obviously they are saying they are using intelligence, but we are saying let's prove them wrong".
IOL Business

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Burgemeester kondigt noodbevel af bij demonstratie tegen azc op rotonde Apeldoorn
APELDOORN - Op de rotonde in de Apeldoornse wijk De Maten is opnieuw gedemonstreerd tegen de komst van een azc. Volgens een 112-verslaggever hadden er zich zo'n 200 demonstranten verzameld bij de rotonde. Tegen het einde van de avond kondigde de burgemeester een noodbevel af en werd de demonstratie op last van de burgmeester beëindigd.
Rond 19.00 uur begon de demonstratie tegen de plannen van de gemeente om asielzoekers tijdelijk onder te brengen in een schoolgebouw. De rotonde werd afgesloten voor verkeer. De ME was aanwezig om de situatie in de gaten te houden.
Vlaggen en vuurwerk
Demonstranten hadden vlaggen en spandoeken met teksten als 'Send them home' en "Azc nee, weg ermee'. Een aantal van hen liep met fakkels en stak vuurwerk af. Vanaf de rotonde liepen de demonstranten een rondje door de wijk en naar het centrum. Vanaf het centrum liep de groep weer terug.
Noodbevel en enkele aanhoudingen
Daarna kondigde de burgemeester een noodbevel af, wat betekent dat iedereen het gebied moet verlaten. Er werd veelal gehoor gegeven aan de instructies van de politie, maar niet door iedereen. Daarom werd een aantal personen aangehouden, zo meldt een woordvoerder van de politie.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Mayor issues emergency order at demonstration against asylum seeker center at Apeldoorn roundabout
APELDOORN - Demonstrations against the arrival of an asylum seeker center took place again at the roundabout in the De Maten district of Apeldoorn. According to a 112 reporter, about 200 demonstrators had gathered at the roundabout. Towards the end of the evening, the mayor issued an emergency order, and the demonstration was ended by order of the mayor.

The demonstration against the municipality's plans to temporarily house asylum seekers in a school building began around 7:00 PM. The roundabout was closed to traffic. Riot police were present to monitor the situation. Flags and fireworks

Demonstrators carried flags and banners with slogans such as 'Send them home' and 'Asylum seeker center no, get rid of it'. A number of them walked with torches and set off fireworks. From the roundabout, the demonstrators walked a loop through the neighborhood and towards the city center. From the center, the group walked back.

Emergency order and several arrests
Afterwards, the mayor issued an emergency order, which means that everyone must leave the area. The police's instructions were largely followed, but not by everyone. Therefore, a number of people were arrested, a police spokesperson reports.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
La digna movilización de miles de maestros y maestras del sur de México sigue manteniéndose firme tras más de dos semanas de protestas en Ciudad de México, pues el gobierno encabezado por la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, no logra dar solución a su principal demanda, la abrogación de la Ley del ISSSTE del 2007, promulgada por el entonces presidente Felipe Calderón Hinojosa (PAN).
La noche del 17 de junio de 2026, la Comisión Nacional Única de Negociación (CNUN) de la CNTE informó hacia la media noche, que la quinta reunión con el Gobierno Federal en la Secretaría de Gobernación (SEGOB) concluyó sin acuerdo “El Gobierno descartó abrir una ruta para la abrogación de la Ley del ISSSTE”, además denunció que ese día Integrantes de la Coordinadora Estatal de Trabajadores de la Educación de Guerrero (CETEG) fueron encapsulados y amenazados por la policía en Avenida del Imán, Ciudad de México.
“Llegaron a golpear, a destruir el equipo y a llevarse la cooperación que tenemos de los maestros y maestras que nos ayudan con el movimiento. Se llevaron todo lo que tenemos para comida, pasaje, etcétera”, señaló la Coordinadora en una transmisión en vivo.
Durante la represión policiaca varios docentes también fueron golpeados por los elementos y otros fueron sustraídos de sus pertenencias, incluidos celulares y los recursos reunidos para los viáticos del magisterio, además de que los oficiales dañaron y cortaron los cables del equipo de audio empleado en las protestas.
Ante ello, Elvira Veleces, dirigente de la Sección 14 de Guerrero, condenó la acción de la policía y la criminalización de la protesta, y recordó que las acciones de la CNTE son pacíficas y responsabilizaron directamente al Gobierno Federal y al Gobierno de la Ciudad de México por este desplegado “ 7800 elementos desplegaron en toda la ciudad para contener el movimiento de la gente” dijo.
Asimismo denunció que a 18 días del comienzo de su movilización el maestro Octavio Romero Gerónimo, atacado el primero de junio con un petardo en la Mejilla y que lo dejó en el hospital y graves heridas en la cara no ha recibido reparación del daño ni castigo a los culpables.
Ante estos hechos y los nulos avances en las mesas de trabajo, este jueves 18 de junio la CNTE tomó las oficinas principales de las Administradoras de Fondos para el Retiro (AFORE) ubicadas en el corredor financiero de Paseo de la Reforma. Según el plan de acción de la Dirección Política Nacional del magisterio disidente, los bloqueos e instalaciones de plantones comenzarían a las 10:00 horas del 18 de junio de 2026, distribuidos por contingentes estatales bajo la consigna de exigir la devolución total del control de sus pensiones. El despliegue operativo contempla el cerco de siete sedes financieras en Paseo de la Reforma y la alcaldía Álvaro Obregón.
Por su parte, el Gobierno Federal planteó la instalación de mesas tripartitas para atender temas locales y mesas temáticas sobre justicia y reparación del daño, además de una calendarización de reuniones acordada entre la SEP y la SEGOB. Sobre la mesa permanecen también la oferta de derogación de la Unidad del Sistema para la Carrera de las Maestras y los Maestros (USICAMM) y la creación de una aseguradora pública que administre las pensiones de los docentes.
Entre las principales exigencias del movimiento permanecen la abrogación de la Ley del ISSSTE de 2007, la eliminación de los mecanismos de evaluación y promoción docente, el cese de descuentos salariales y la reinstalación de trabajadores cesados. La continuidad de la huelga, según la dirigencia magisterial, será definida por la Asamblea Nacional Representativa en sus espacios internos de deliberación.

TRANSLATED_TEXT:
The dignified mobilization of thousands of teachers from southern Mexico remains steadfast after more than two weeks of protests in Mexico City, as the government led by Mayor Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo has failed to address their main demand: the repeal of the 2007 ISSSTE Law, enacted by then-President Felipe Calderón Hinojosa (PAN).

On the night of June 17, 2026, the National Unified Negotiation Commission (CNUN) of the CNTE reported around midnight that the fifth meeting with the Federal Government at the Ministry of the Interior (SEGOB) concluded without an agreement. "The Government ruled out opening a path for the repeal of the ISSSTE Law," the CNUN stated. It also denounced that on that same day, members of the State Coordinating Committee of Education Workers of Guerrero (CETEG) were surrounded and threatened by police on Avenida del Imán in Mexico City.

“They came to beat us, destroy our equipment, and take the donations we receive from the teachers who help us with the movement. They took everything we have for food, transportation, and so on,” the Coordinator stated in a live broadcast.

During the police repression, several teachers were also beaten by officers, and others had their belongings stolen, including cell phones and the funds collected for teachers' travel expenses. Furthermore, the officers damaged and cut the cables of the audio equipment used in the protests.

In response, Elvira Veleces, leader of Section 14 in Guerrero, condemned the police action and the criminalization of the protest. She reiterated that the CNTE's actions are peaceful and directly blamed the Federal Government and the Mexico City Government for this deployment. “7,800 officers were deployed throughout the city to contain the people's movement,” she said. The CNTE also denounced the fact that, 18 days after the start of their mobilization, teacher Octavio Romero Gerónimo, who was attacked on June 1st with a firecracker to the cheek, leaving him hospitalized with serious facial injuries, has not received any compensation for the damages nor has the perpetrators been punished.

Given these events and the lack of progress in the working groups, on Thursday, June 18th, the CNTE occupied the main offices of the Retirement Fund Administrators (AFOREs) located in the Paseo de la Reforma financial district. According to the action plan of the National Political Directorate of the dissident teachers' movement, the blockades and sit-ins would begin at 10:00 AM on June 18, 2026, distributed by state contingents under the demand for the full return of control over their pensions. The operational deployment includes the encirclement of seven financial institutions on Paseo de la Reforma and in the Álvaro Obregón borough.

For its part, the Federal Government proposed the establishment of tripartite working groups to address local issues and thematic working groups on justice and reparations, in addition to a schedule of meetings agreed upon between the Ministry of Public Education (SEP) and the Ministry of the Interior (SEGOB). Also on the table are the proposals to repeal the Unit of the System for the Professional Development of Teachers (USICAMM) and the creation of a public insurance company to manage teachers' pensions.

Among the movement's main demands are the repeal of the 2007 ISSSTE Law, the elimination of teacher evaluation and promotion mechanisms, the cessation of salary deductions, and the reinstatement of dismissed workers. According to the teachers' leadership, the continuation of the strike will be decided by the National Representative Assembly in its internal deliberations.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Skip to content
Peco workers rally before taking strike vote amid tense negotiations
Over a hundred workers and supporters gathered on Saturday morning to kick off a strike authorization vote.
Over 100 Peco workers and supporters gathered in a parking lot in Plymouth Meeting on Saturday morning as a food truck doled out Old Original Nick’s Roast Beef sandwiches and some played cornhole.
Workers weren’t just there to enjoy the food; they were there to cast a vote and decide whether their union would authorize a strike.
Some in attendance held signs that read: “Fair contract now,” and “Ready to strike if we have to.” Bon Jovi’s “Livin’ On A Prayer” could be heard playing through a speaker.
The roughly 1,500 workers represented by IBEW Local 614, which includes gas and electric field workers as well as call center employees, are seeking higher wages and improvements to benefits in a new contract.
The workers’ most recent five-year contract expired on March 31 and negotiations, which started in January, have led to some tentative agreements, a Peco spokesperson said Friday. Wages and benefits have become sticking points in bargaining, the union has said.
“We always show up when Peco needs us, and they are not showing up for our workers,” said Larry Anastasi, the union’s local president on Saturday morning in the parking lot during a news conference. “We intend to get a strike authorization vote today, and one day, and one day soon, you’re going to hear from us again.”
Passing a strike authorization vote does not mean workers will necessarily walk off the job — unions can pass the vote to gain leverage in negotiations.
Ahead of the Saturday vote, Peco spokesperson Candice Womer called a strike authorization vote a “procedural step.”
“We respect the role of the union and the collective bargaining process, and we remain committed to engaging in good-faith negotiations to reach an agreement that is fair to our employees, while supporting the long-term needs of our customers and the communities we serve,” said Womer in a statement on Friday.
Voting was scheduled to take place on Saturday, with the results available that evening. If workers vote to authorize a strike, and they do walk off the job, it would be the first time employees do so in the company’s history.
» READ MORE: Here’s everything to know about the potential Peco worker strike
On Saturday, Peco spokesperson Matt Rankin said the company was well-prepared and had “contingency staffing plans in place to ensure that our customers’ electric and natural gas services are not affected.”
What has happened in negotiations so far?
In 2004, Peco workers voted to join the union and, according to union president Anastasi, then ratified their first contract with the company in 2007.
It’s the first time in the union’s history that a contract with Peco has expired while another one is not already agreed upon.
Since bargaining began earlier this year, 17 negotiating sessions have taken place, all in-person, noted Womer. The most recent one was on May 27, and the next session is planned for June 3, with additional dates scheduled in June and July.
Negotiations turned ugly last month, as both the union and Peco filed unfair labor practice charges with the National Labor Relations Board.
Womer said this week that Peco’s focus “continues to be on productive, ongoing negotiations.”
Workers are seeking a uniform retirement plan in a new contract, higher wages, and improvements in healthcare benefits. Currently, some workers have a pension, but roughly 600 of them who joined the union in recent years do not. Among those who do have one, there are also different plans.
“PECO continues to offer competitive wages and benefits that compare favorably with industry peers across the region,” Womer said, adding that the company also provides training programs that support performance and safety.
Linemen, who are some of the union’s highest-paid members, made an average of more than $243,500 last year in wages, including overtime, the company has said.
Joy Rodriguez, a Peco customer service representative was ready to strike, they said on Saturday.
“Me and my colleagues will be here fighting for what we deserve until the company comes to the table and agrees to treat us fairly moving forward,” said Rodriguez.
Danny Bauder, president of the Philadelphia Council AFL-CIO called out on Saturday morning to those who had assembled in the parking lot for the news conference: “What do we want?” The crowd responded, “Contract!”
“When do we want it?” Bauder followed up. “Now,” the crowd responded.
» READ MORE: These Peco employees do dangerous work at all hours. Their union is pushing for a better retirement package.
In Southeastern Pennsylvania, Peco provides natural gas to 553,000 customers and electricity to 1.7 million.
Last year, Peco brought in $814 million in net income, a 48% increase from the previous year, parent company Exelon reported. In March, amid contract negotiations, the company requested a rate increase which would have affected gas and electricity customers, citing upgrades needed, including because of demand. It later withdrew the request amid public backlash.
The union contract negotiations have also been happening against the backdrop of AI data centers being proposed throughout the region, which are expected to drive up energy demand, and as Peco’s CEO stepped down from his role.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Dozens of NV Energy customers, including seniors, wait outside for chance to speak at Public Utilities Commission of Nevada’s annual consumer hearing on West Diablo Drive in Las Vegas Valley, NV
MESSAGE_TEXT:
NV Energy customers wait in triple-digit heat for public hearing
Dozens of customers, including seniors, waited outside as PUCN held meeting on controversial demand charge
LAS VEGAS (FOX5) — Dozens of NV Energy customers, including many seniors, were left waiting outside in triple-digit heat for a chance to speak at the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada’s annual consumer hearing.
The commission had only one room open with limited seating. Customers were only allowed inside when it was their turn to speak. Outside, police presence increased and prime parking spaces were blocked off.
Metro police confirmed they were assigned to block off West Diablo Drive to ensure there were no issues.
The hearing came one day after customers gathered to protest NV Energy’s daily demand charge. Residents, workers, faith leaders and community advocates rallied outside the PUCN offices, calling on regulators to scrap the proposed rate structure and expand opportunities for public input.
The billing model
The daily demand charge is a new rate structure that would charge customers based on their highest 15-minute spike in energy use each day. The pricing policy has been delayed amid community pushback.
Critics say it will punish working families for simply cooking dinner and doing laundry at the same time.
NV Energy refuted those claims and said many customers will not see a significant increase in their billing. The demand rate was put in place to ensure all customers, including solar customers, pay their fair share.
“There will be little to no impact or change for the majority of customers,” said Katie Nannini, director of communications for NV Energy. “The push for this was to make sure that all customers are paying for the infrastructure that it cost to deliver energy.”
Speakers at the rally also called for greater transparency from both NV Energy and the utilities commission. Organizers said the commission scheduled only one public hearing during daytime hours despite heightened concern over rising energy bills and extreme summer heat.
Leslie Vega, a community organizer at the Progressive Leadership Alliance of Nevada, waited outside for several hours.
“There are supposed to be two consumer sessions typically; the commissioners allow a 1 p.m. and a 6 p.m. They canceled the 6 p.m. meeting, and they closed one of the hearing rooms for the 1 p.m., and now they have had folks waiting out here for about an hour,” Vega said. “Unheard, unprioritized, and I am losing confidence.”
The rally followed a protest earlier this month at an electric utility conference at the Fontainebleau in Las Vegas, where demonstrators urged NV Energy’s CEO to cancel the daily demand charge.
The PUCN said it would need questions submitted by email before providing a written statement about how the hearing was handled.
Property management confirmed that people were required to wait outside due to safety concerns.
NV Energy said it has no plans to host a consumer session of its own. The utility is also seeking approval to collect an additional $500 million from Nevada ratepayers for wildfire insurance.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Mount Nittany workers vote to begin five-day strike on July 27
STATE COLLEGE — Hospital workers at Mount Nittany Medical Center voted overwhelmingly to begin a five-day strike on July 27, arguing better working conditions are essential to quality patient care.
The workers spoke about the “difficult” decision at a press conference on Thursday afternoon, where they called on Mount Nittany executives to invest in all workers, patients and community care.
SEIU Healthcare PA said 950 union-represented workers approved the strike authorization by a 98% vote.
“The fourth most profitable hospital in Pennsylvania with a total profit margin over 30%, Mount Nittany has more than enough resources to reach an agreement that moves community care forward,” the hospital workers union said in a statement.
Workers said they still hope to reach a fair agreement but were left with no choice but to authorize a strike after Mount Nittany executives offered annual raises during Monday’s negotiations that they said do not keep pace with the 4.2% inflation rate.
“I chose Mount Nittany because I wanted to care for the community I love with the highest standards of care,” said Jess Mulroy, a registered nurse at Mount Nittany for 10 years and a Vice President of the SEIU Healthcare PA union chapter at the medical center. “All of us, from patient-facing care to maintenance, lab and nutrition, take pride in the care we provide patients. But I’m getting more and more worried that the standards this hospital used to be known for will fall backward without a serious, fair investment in the workforce. While Mount Nittany focuses on new buildings, towers and expansions, many essential workers are struggling to keep up with rising costs and bills. We are calling on this hospital not to forget their roots — the workforce who won them five stars. We are taking a stand for our priorities, which are our patients, our community and quality jobs.”
In a statement sent to The Express on Tuesday, a spokesperson for Mount Nittany said the health system has comprehensive plans in place to ensure patients continue to receive safe and high quality care with as little disruption as possible. They said the hospital, emergency department, physician practices and outpatient clinics will continue to operate as normal, and that patients should keep their scheduled appointments unless they are contacted directly by Mount Nittany Health.
“Our focus remains on caring for our community while remaining committed to reaching an agreement,” Mount Nittany said. “Throughout negotiations, our proposals have included significant investments in our employees, and our goal is to reach a fair and sustainable agreement that recognizes the contributions of our employees while ensuring we can continue serving our community as an independent health system.”
SEIU Healthcare PA says Mount Nittany Medical Center is very financially healthy and has the resources to invest in all workers who make the hospital run. The union said the rising cost of living in Centre County, including housing, gas, groceries and utilities, has forced many workers to live farther away and commute longer distances.
“While workers have been struggling, Mount Nittany made $509 million in total revenue and $183 million in profits in fiscal year 2025,” a SEIU Healthcare PA spokesperson said.
Mount Nittany Medical Center also controls 70% of inpatient market share and is the largest private employer in Centre County. Workers say that the hospital’s conduct sets the standard for both healthcare and jobs in the region and feel that as a tax-exempt organization, Mount Nittany has a responsibility to make a fair investment in its workforce and the quality care they provide.
Almost all of the staff at Mount Nittany Medical Center throughout every department are represented by their union, SEIU Healthcare Pennsylvania. The workers include registered nurses, emergency department technicians, lab technicians, skilled maintenance, pharmacists, certified nurse aides, environmental services aides (who clean and disinfect the hospital), radiology technologists and dietary aides, among many other essential job titles.
Negotiations for a new union contract began on April 29 and their contract expired on June 30. Workers say they are committed to continue bargaining in good faith and are hopeful that management returns to negotiations to reach an agreement that invests in all workers so they can provide the care their community depends on.
