MESSAGE_TEXT:
Rep. Angie Nixon, D-Jacksonville, was arrested Friday evening by Capitol Police after about five hours of staging a sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' office.
She began her protest around noon, hoping to speak with a DeSantis staff member to discuss affordability in Florida. Nixon said two protesters who were with her at the time were arrested. At the time of her arrest, five supporters and a group of media members were told to leave the Capitol.
"I'm here because we have continually failed to do the business of the people in this legislative body, in this governor's office," she told the News Service of Florida before her arrest. "I'm here because they, instead of addressing the rising costs and the fact that people can no longer to afford to be alive, to stay in Florida ... they instead want to rid maps in support of what Donald Trump wants."
At the time of her arrest it was unclear what charges she would face or where should would be taken.
Nixon is running for the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate.
On Thursday Nixon was reprimanded by the House Rules and Ethics Committee for her loud protest on the House floor last month that disrupted the vote on new congressional district maps.
The incident wasn’t the first time Nixon caused a commotion on the House floor over redistricting. She led a protest in 2022 when the old districts were approved. The House briefly recessed but returned one hour later to approve the map.
"It doesn't have to be this way, and so that is why I'm here," Nixon said.
A request for comment from the governor's office was not immediately returned Friday afternoon.

(COLORADO SPRINGS) — Palmer High School seniors in Colorado Springs staged a silent protest during their graduation ceremony this year against a new academic recognition policy from District 11. The policy recognizes students with a 3.75 GPA or higher with different colored gowns and front-row seating, which some students felt created division.
Some of the graduating students, including senior class leaders, swapped their gold academic gowns for brown ones after the tassel turn to express their stance on the district’s decision.
District 11 implemented the new policy as a method to acknowledge academic achievements without the use of graduation cords. However, some students and parents raised concerns that the change fostered division within a ceremony intended to celebrate the entire graduating class as a unit.
Approximately 53 students were initially honored with the gold gowns under this new recognition practice.
Students said the new policy change was announced sometime in January. Palmer High School Senior Class President Darnell Robinson said that many students felt undervalued and unseen by the new system. He expressed his and his peers’ desire to take action to ensure student voices were considered.
Student Body President Greta Kelly at Palmer High School highlighted that a strong part of Palmer’s culture is inclusivity and unity, which students wished to maintain during graduation. “We all want to be united in celebration, and we all realize that we’ve all taken different paths in order to get to where we are today,” Kelly said, emphasizing that all graduates contribute to the Palmer community and should celebrate as one.
During the silent protest, many students switched from their gold gowns to brown gowns. Robinson and Kelly were among those who changed their gowns. Robinson stated that he wanted to show that despite wearing a gold gown, he was there for everyone, asserting, “we are all one in the same. We are all Palmer graduates.”
Kelly described the gown change after the tassel turn as a “great connection to the rest of my peers,” and also as a statement that student voice should be incorporated into decisions, particularly those regarding graduation.
Students had previously encouraged the district to reconsider its approach during an April 1 Board of Education meeting. At that meeting, Superintendent Michael Gaal explained his support for the robes, noting that “The challenge with cords is then many of our children are recognized for achievements through other means by cords, and so now it is either just the number of cords or color of cords, which means, again, that the high commitment to academic excellence would not be seen.” His reasoning was that using different colored robes clearly highlights academic excellence.
District 11 issued a statement indicating that the recognition practices were put into effect for graduates across seven high schools and five commencement ceremonies. Students at Palmer High School were able to convince alumni to donate their brown gowns for the protest. While the district says that reading academic achievements with each name would take too much time, students continue to advocate for academic recognition through cords or other methods.
Margaret Sheridan, a junior at Palmer High School, hopes that her classmates will be inspired by the senior class to voice their opinions on policy. “I would love to see us in one colored gown next year,” Sheridan said, indicating a desire for a return to unified gowns for future graduations.
A D11 spokesperson provided FOX21 with the following statement.
District 11 is proud of every member of the Class of 2026. Each graduate worked hard, contributed to their school community, and earned this moment of celebration. We are also proud to recognize students who demonstrated exceptional academic achievement. Academic excellence is central to the mission of public education, and it is worthy of celebration.
Some students continue to advocate for the district to honor academic achievement through cords. The next group of seniors is prepared to continue the advocacy initiated by the Class of 2026. However, it remains unclear if District 11 plans to revert to its former policy regarding academic recognition at graduation ceremonies.

A Fox News Digital investigation found that the nonprofit received $22.4 million from Singham.
Communism was a recurring theme at May Day in New York, with the Revolutionary Communists of America, the Revolutionary Communist Party and signs for the Communist Workers of America held by several demonstrators.
Pro-communism advocates were canvassing the crowd, hawking communist newspapers and encouraging participation in upcoming organization events.

Mamdani stood in front of billboards labeled “NO ICE, NO WAR” and “NO BILLIONAIRES,” and pushed his commitment to taxing the rich, and noted “faster buses” instead of his usual commitment to making bus transportation in the city free.

Crowds dispersed following Mamdani’s brief address, but some roads remained closed as demonstrators continued the march, and one ambulance with flashing lights was forced to turn around earlier in the day on the march from Union Square to Washington Square.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Environmental groups rallied at Polar Beverages’ headquarters on Tuesday, calling out the company’s influence in lobbying efforts they say are stalling updates to Massachusetts bottle recycling laws.
Environmental advocates stand outside Polar Beverages’ headquarters in Worcester, protesting the company’s opposition to updating Massachusetts’ “bottle bill” laws. The measure provides customers a refund for returning beverage containers for recycling.
Several environmental advocacy groups are calling for a statewide boycott of Polar Beverages, alleging the Worcester-based company is standing in the way of efforts to modernize Massachusetts’ bottle recycling laws. A coalition of environmentalist groups held signs as they rallied outside the company’s headquarters Tuesday to call for a two-month boycott, urging customers not to buy its products through the end of August.
Massachusetts was among the first states to adopt a so-called “bottle bill” in 1983. It requires customers to pay a 5-cent deposit fee when they buy certain beverages, though they get that money back if they return the empty bottle for recycling.
Advocates argue the law is long overdue for an update since so many bottles and cans are never returned, and they’ve pushed — unsuccessfully — for many years to increase the deposit fee to 10 cents and include more types of beverage containers. Part of the reason these efforts keep failing on Beacon Hill is that companies like Polar are fighting the change over fears it will increase costs for them, said Kirstie Pecci with national nonprofit Just Zero.
"Beverage companies don't want to pay their fair share for dealing with all these bottles and cans," Pecci said. Beverage companies like Polar are required to help oversee bottle recycling programs, and they pay a small handling fee for every returned container. They do not have to pay this fee when people recycle bottles on the curb. Advocates argue 5-cent returns are no longer enough to motivate people to return empty containers.
And they say a 10-cent bottle redemption law would put Massachusetts in line with many other states and encourage more people to return their empties. Pecci pointed to Connecticut and Oregon, states that saw a jump in bottle returns after refunds went from 5 cents to 10 cents. Beyond upping recycling, she said the change would reduce litter and lower curbside recycling costs for cities and towns.
"Governments adopt a bottle bill because it is the most climate-friendly, material-efficient, and cheapest way to refill or recycle your bottles and cans," she said, adding Massachusetts"should be expanding system and modernizing it. " Polar has manufacturing facilities in New York, Georgia and Texas. The company’s president and CEO, Ralph Crowley Jr., is treasurer of the American Beverage Association.in 2014 to defeat a ballot measure to increase the bottle bill refund in Massachusetts.
Like similar bills in recent years, Pecci said the legislation is unlikely to advance before the legislative session ends this summer. However, she said, proponents of the bill hope to bring Polar and other industry players to the table to improve their chances in the future.
"No one's trying to put any of these companies out of business,” she said, “and there's no reason that this will hurt their bottom line. ”

A protest hosted by the American Society for the Defense of Tradition, Family, and Property was recently held at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. in response to the pro-LBGT conference organized by Jesuit Fr. James Martin. If you aren’t a Catholic, brace yourself because this post is going to get a little niche.
Young Catholics gathered at the gates of Georgetown University to protest Fr. James Martin's pro-LGBT "Outreach 2026" conference.
— TFP Student Action (@tfpsa)
Not only are the event speakers at odds with the Bible, but also against natural law, papal documents, the Fathers of the Church, the Doctors of…[pic.twitter.com/KBzE2rvsIp][June 21, 2026]
The conference has widely been condemned by American Catholics, 31,000 of whom signed a petition of protest for the event. I’ve participated in a protest hosted by TFP during my college years after the city decided to allow a leader in the Satanic Temple to give the invocation for the council meeting. It almost entirely consisted of praying the rosary and attempting to fruitlessly evangelize some of the more odd individuals who came to support the Satanists.
This most recent protest is about combating something far more perverse, however.
I’ve always wanted to believe that Fr. Martin’s heart is in the right place, but his actions are so absurdly misguided that they almost cannot be explained by any good reason. A lot of his public statements make that belief harder. One panel at the conference being called “Celebrating the Transgender Catholic Experience” is an example. My conclusion has always been to pray for Fr. Martin and the complete conversions of all of those he ministers to.
Many believe that Fr. Martin is approaching those struggling with same-sex attraction with the heart and love of Christ. They would quickly criticize others for being too harsh on LGBT groups by dismissing things like Pride Month as demonic and destructive to Christian society. They would, correctly, say that the Church is a hospital for sinners and that everyone is welcome.
Many others believe that Fr. Martin is doing harm to the souls of the world’s troubled youth.
A problem arises when welcomeness prohibits a demand for repentance and change. We’re called to strive to live sinlessly like Christ. We are called to aid our brothers and sisters in faith to do the same. A watering down of the truth isn’t just uncharitable, it’s malicious.
The Catholic Church is one of the last institutions maintaining many moral and theological truths professed by Christians for thousands of years: that marriage (and as a byproduct, sex) is a bond only broken by death and only for a man and a woman, abortion in any circumstance is the equivalent of hiring a hitman for a murder, that contraception is illicit, and that ecclesial leadership is the duty of men.
Obviously many Protestants proclaim at least a few of these truths, but the number of sects that do grows smaller and smaller as the years go on. The number of politicians who would do the same, even privately, is far fewer. An unpopular reality is that some of the most socially conservative politicians in the U.S. are far more socially liberal than the average parish priest. But a rebirth in the traditional minded youth is at hand, and I’m blessed to have lived through it first-hand.
Before I became a Catholic missionary, I had converted to the faith in college. Sadly, my parents did not give me the gift of faith. I grew up with absolutely no concept of religion and couldn’t tell you the last time I was even inside of a church before I began my journey of opening the Bible and becoming a Catholic. MESSAGE_TEXT:
More than 50 U.S. cities will join a national protest against data centers tomorrow.

Protests are planned in more than 50 locations across the United States on July 18 as communities push back against the rapid expansion of the massive facilities.

The demonstrations are being organized by Humans First, a conservative advocacy group that says residents are being excluded from decisions about what gets built in their communities.

Organizers say the protests will focus on rising electricity bills, enormous water and energy demand, noise, pollution, land-use changes and concerns about the wider effects of artificial intelligence.

Events are planned in cities and rural communities across more than 20 states, including California, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas and Virginia.

The campaign reflects growing resistance to data centers across political lines.

A recent Gallup poll found that seven in 10 Americans oppose an AI data center being built near their home, with nearly half saying they strongly oppose one.

Resource use was the most commonly cited concern, including electricity consumption, water demand and the loss of farmland and wildlife habitat.

Others raised concerns about higher utility bills, declining property values, traffic, noise and air or water pollution.

Supporters argue that data centers are essential to expanding artificial intelligence and helping the United States compete with countries such as China.

But opponents say local communities should have more control over projects that could permanently reshape their surroundings.

Data Center Watch estimates that local opposition has already blocked or delayed roughly $64 billion in proposed projects.

Organizers say the July 18 demonstrations are intended to show elected officials that resistance to unchecked data center development is no longer isolated; it is becoming a national movement.

Learn more:
"National Day of Protest Against Data Centers on July 18—Map, List of Cities." Newsweek

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Approximately 40 shlichim (“Israeli emissaries”) from the Jewish Agency for Israel marched in New York City’s annual Israel Day on Fifth parade on May 31 as part of a joint float organized with the American Zionist Movement and World Zionist Organization.
They marched alongside Yaron Shavit, deputy chairman of the executive of the Jewish Agency; Yaakov Hagoel, chairman of the World Zionist Organization; and Herbert Block, executive director of the American Zionist Movement. Also marching with the float were Ronen and Orna Neutra, the parents of Omer Neutra, an Israeli-American IDF officer killed in the Hamas-led terrorist attacks in Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.
Bringing Israeli music, dancing, flags and enthusiasm to the parade, the emissaries helped energize the atmosphere while serving as a visible expression of the deep connection between Israel and Jewish communities across North America.
The parade’s theme this year, “Proud Americans, Proud Zionists,” reflected the enduring and inextricable bond between American Jewry and Israel—a message that resonated throughout the day’s celebrations and demonstrations of solidarity.
The shlichim, who serve in Jewish communities, schools, summer camps and on college campuses, traveled from across the country to participate alongside hundreds of supporters, community leaders and representatives from partner organizations. They serve as a living bridge between Israel and Jewish communities worldwide, helping strengthen Jewish identity, Hebrew and Israeli culture, and connections to Israel in communities throughout North America.
“Having our shlichim march in the Israel Day parade is a true reflection of our mutual responsibility and the deep sense of solidarity they foster in communities throughout America,” said Gal Atia, head of the Jewish Agency’s Delegation to North America.
“Just as the community here has stood by our side throughout the years, our shlichim are here to walk shoulder to shoulder with the community. This year’s parade and its theme powerfully captured the values of identity, unity and shared purpose that our emissaries work daily to strengthen across the nation,” he said.
The parade comes as Jewish communities around the world continue to demonstrate solidarity with Israel and support for communities impacted by the ongoing war. Since Oct. 7, the Jewish Agency has played a central role in emergency response efforts across Israel while also supporting Jewish communities worldwide.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Demonstrators donning the logo and insignia of Patriot Front, a white supremacist group, were seen protesting in the Eastern Market neighborhood and on Capitol Hill on the 250th anniversary of U.S. independence.
Sporting white masks, sunglasses and Patriot Front’s signature tan caps, the protesters carried Confederate, Patriot Front and upside-down U.S. flags as they marched through Capitol Hill. The group was also photographed riding public transit on Saturday morning.
Outside Union Station, demonstrators chanted phrases including “Life, liberty, victory!” and “Reclaim America!” — slogans regularly used by the group.
The demonstration unfolded as tourists and Americans alike flocked to the “Salute to America” celebration on the National Mall, which will culminate in a speech by President Donald Trump and a fireworks show expected to last for a record-breaking 40 minutes. The Trump administration has made the nation’s 250th anniversary a top priority over the past few months through high-profile initiatives like the Great American State Fair and restoration work at the Reflecting Pool.
Later, anti-Trump demonstrators were filmed walking toward the White House carrying a large Declaration of Independence banner and chanting “8647,” a slogan calling for Trump’s removal from the presidency.
Patriot Front was founded in 2017 by Thomas Ryan Rousseau, who split from the alt-right organization Vanguard America in the aftermath of the deadly Unite the Right rally in Charlottesville, Virginia. Patriot Front’s website describes the group as a “fraternal, nationalist, activist organization” and writes that “Our people, born to this nation of our European race, must reforge themselves as a new collective capable of asserting our right to cultural independence.”
The D.C. mayor’s office referred POLITICO to the Metropolitan police department for comment.
“The Metropolitan Police Department (MPD) is tracking First Amendment activities that occurred this morning in the Eastern Market neighborhood,” the department said in a statement Saturday. “MPD recognizes the rights of individuals to peacefully express their views and remains committed to maintaining public safety and security for DC residents and visitors.”
Gregory Svirnovskiy contributed to this report.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Entre 650.000 y 700.000 personas llegarán a DC este fin de semana para Capital Pride, el mayor evento LGBTQ+ de la capital. El desfile arranca mañana sábado a las 3 PM desde 14th Street y T Street NW, recorre Thomas Circle y baja por Pennsylvania Avenue hasta 9th Street NW, frente al Capitolio.
El tema de este año es "Exist. Resist. Have the Audacity!", una consigna que la Capital Pride Alliance describe como respuesta directa a los desafíos que enfrenta la comunidad LGBTQ+ en el contexto político actual. Es la edición número 51 del evento en Washington.
Cierres de calles y estacionamiento
Dupont Circle está completamente cerrado desde hoy viernes 19 hasta el lunes 22 de junio por la celebración. La policía metropolitana estableció restricciones de estacionamiento de emergencia a lo largo de toda la ruta del desfile.
Las calles cerradas al tráfico vehicular el sábado desde las 6 AM incluyen: 15th Street desde Rhode Island Avenue hasta U Street NW (zona de concentración del desfile), 14th Street hacia el sur, y Pennsylvania Avenue entre 14th y 9th Street NW. El domingo, Pennsylvania Avenue entre 7th y 9th Street y 7th Street entre D Street y Constitution Avenue pueden tener cierres intermitentes para el festival.
Los conductores que transiten por el centro de DC deben considerar rutas alternas. La policía metropolitana recomienda consultar las actualizaciones en tiempo real en la cuenta @DCPoliceTraffic.
Qué incluye el fin de semana
El viernes por la noche arranca con la fiesta RIOT en Echostage, con DJ set de BOB The Drag Queen y la ganadora de Rupaul's Drag Race Season 18, Myki Meeks. El sábado, además del desfile, hay un block party en 17th Street NW entre P y R Streets, en el histórico corredor de Dupont Circle, con música en vivo, jardines de bebidas y vista directa al desfile desde las 3 hasta las 8 PM.
El domingo es el día del festival y concierto gratuito en Pennsylvania Avenue y Constitution Avenue NW, con el escenario principal Monument Stage frente al Washington Monument de 12 a 7 PM. La programación completa está en capitalpride.org.
Impacto económico para la ciudad
El impacto económico directo de Capital Pride no se mide anualmente, pero el WorldPride de 2025 en DC atrajo a 1,2 millones de visitantes y generó $310 millones en actividad económica, incluyendo $25 millones en ingresos fiscales por ventas y hospedaje.
"Sabemos que cuando la gente se reúne para nuestros grandes festivales anuales en el Distrito, eso genera una cantidad significativa de actividad económica",[dijo Nina Albert, vicealcaldesa de Planificación y Desarrollo Económico de DC, en declaraciones a WTOP]
Los bares y negocios del corredor LGBTQ+ de Dupont Circle reportan que el fin de semana de Pride es su periodo más fuerte del año. Eli Downes, gerente general de JR's, uno de los bares gay más antiguos de DC, dijo a WTOP que "Pride literalmente nos mantiene a flote y nos sostiene los otros 364 días del año".
Cómo llegar en Metro
Las estaciones más cercanas a la ruta del desfile son Dupont Circle (línea roja), U Street/African-Amer Civil War Memorial/Cardozo (líneas verde y amarilla) y Metro Center (todas las líneas). Para el festival del domingo, las estaciones Archives-Navy Memorial y Federal Triangle están a corta distancia.
Este fin de semana también coincide con Juneteenth, la celebración del Smithsonian Solstice y los eventos del 250 aniversario de Estados Unidos, por lo que el tráfico peatonal y vehicular en el centro de DC será excepcionalmente alto.

Between 650,000 and 700,000 people are expected to arrive in Washington, D.C., this weekend for Capital Pride, the capital's largest LGBTQ+ event. The parade kicks off tomorrow, Saturday, at 3 p.m. from 14th Street and T Street NW, proceeds along Thomas Circle, and continues down Pennsylvania Avenue to 9th Street NW, in front of the Capitol.

This year's theme is "Exist. Resist. Have the Audacity!", a slogan the Capital Pride Alliance describes as a direct response to the challenges the LGBTQ+ community faces in the current political climate. This is the 51st annual event in Washington.

Street Closures and Parking Restrictions
Dupont Circle is completely closed from today, Friday, June 19, through Monday, June 22, for the celebration. The Metropolitan Police Department has implemented emergency parking restrictions along the entire parade route.

Streets closed to vehicular traffic on Saturday starting at 6 AM include: 15th Street from Rhode Island Avenue to U Street NW (parade assembly area), 14th Street southbound, and Pennsylvania Avenue between 14th and 9th Street NW. On Sunday, Pennsylvania Avenue between 7th and 9th Streets and 7th Street between D Street and Constitution Avenue may experience intermittent closures for the festival.

Drivers traveling through downtown DC should consider alternate routes. The Metropolitan Police Department recommends checking real-time updates on the @DCPoliceTraffic account.
What's on this weekend?
Friday night kicks off with the RIOT party at Echostage, featuring a DJ set by BOB The Drag Queen and RuPaul's Drag Race Season 18 winner Myki Meeks. On Saturday, in addition to the parade, there's a block party on 17th Street NW between P and R Streets, in the historic Dupont Circle corridor, with live music, beverage gardens, and a direct view of the parade from 3 to 8 PM.

Sunday is festival day with a free concert on Pennsylvania Avenue and Constitution Avenue NW, with the main stage, the Monument Stage, in front of the Washington Monument from 12 to 7 PM. The full schedule is available at capitalpride.org.

Economic Impact on the City
The direct economic impact of Capital Pride is not measured annually, but WorldPride 2025 in DC attracted 1.2 million visitors and generated $310 million in economic activity, including $25 million in tax revenue from sales and lodging.

“We know that when people come together for our big annual festivals in the District, it generates a significant amount of economic activity,” [D.C. Deputy Mayor for Planning and Economic Development Nina Albert told WTOP].
Bars and businesses along the Dupont Circle LGBTQ+ corridor report that Pride weekend is their busiest time of year. Eli Downes, general manager of JR’s, one of DC’s oldest gay bars, told WTOP, “Pride literally keeps us afloat and sustains us the other 364 days of the year.”

Getting there by Metro: The closest stations to the parade route are Dupont Circle (Red Line), U Street/African-American Civil War Memorial/Cardozo (Green and Yellow Lines), and Metro Center (all lines). For Sunday’s festival, the Archives-Navy Memorial and Federal Triangle stations are within easy reach. This weekend also coincides with Juneteenth, the Smithsonian Solstice celebration, and the United States' 250th anniversary events, so pedestrian and vehicular traffic in downtown DC will be exceptionally heavy.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Officials warned commuters to expect disruptions Monday after workers walked off the job following stalled contract talks, shutting down one of the nation’s busiest commuter rails.
LIRR employee Olivier Desinor leads striking workers in chants during a picket outside Jamaica Station in Queens, New York City, on Saturday. New York officials urged commuters to work from home Monday as a strike by Long Island Rail Road workers threatened to disrupt travel for hundreds of thousands of riders across the region.

Kathy Hochul said the state and the Metropolitan Transportation Authority were preparing emergency transportation alternatives, including shuttle buses from Long Island into Queens and additional subway service, after negotiations between the MTA and rail unions broke down this weekend, prompting workers to walk off the job and shutting down the railroad Saturday.
“Let’s face the facts: it’s impossible to fully replace LIRR service,” Hochul told reporters Sunday at a press conference. The strike — the LIRR’s first in roughly 30 years — has halted service on one of the nation’s busiest commuter rail systems, which carries hundreds of thousands of riders between Long Island and New York City.
Shuttle buses for essential workers were set begin operating at about 4:30 a.m. Monday from six locations across Nassau and Suffolk counties to subway connections in Queens. Adam Gray / Getty Images MTA officials blamed union leadership for walking away from negotiations, saying the transit agency remained willing to continue bargaining.
“We made it clear we are available if they want to come back and negotiate,” MTA CEO Janno Lieber said. “They walked out and they went on strike. ” The coalition of unions representing roughly 3,500 Long Island Rail Road workers accused Lieber and MTA leadership of forcing a shutdown by refusing to agree to wage increases after years without raises amid rising living costs.
In a statement Sunday, the unions said the two sides were separated by less than 1 percentage point before talks broke down Friday night and argued the strike was “completely avoidable. ” “Long Island Rail Road workers want to be doing what they’ve always done — serving the riding public and keeping LIRR moving safely and efficiently,” said IAM Union International President Brian Bryant.
“But after years without raises and with the cost of living continuing to climb across Long Island and the New York City area, workers deserve a fair contract that recognizes their contributions and sacrifices. This strike was completely avoidable, and the coalition remains ready to negotiate at any time if MTA leadership is finally prepared to bargain seriously. ” The unions pointed to recommendations from two presidential emergency boards that they said backed stronger wages increases for workers.
Hochul defended the MTA’s position Sunday, saying the agency could not agree to labor demands that would force steep fare hikes and higher taxes.
“New York is a pro labor state,” Hochul said. “We believe in working men and women receiving a fair wage and benefits, but the MTA cannot agree to a contract that would raise fares as much as 8% and risk hiking taxes for Long Islanders. ”

MESSAGE_TEXT:

News
Advocates held an election day rally today outside the New York City Board of Elections (BOE) headquarters, calling on the BOE and the New York City Department of Correction (DOC) to ensure that every eligible voter incarcerated in city jails can cast a ballot that is counted on this and all future election days.
At least 6,000 New Yorkers held at Rikers Island are potentially eligible to vote, and more than 92 percent of those detained are people of color, reflecting the deep racial disparities in the city’s criminal legal system. By neglecting to facilitate voting in jails, the BOE and DOC are effectively disenfranchising Black and Brown New Yorkers.
To achieve true voting equity, the BOE must establish polling sites in city jails. In-jail polling sites would ensure that ballots are not rejected, that voters can immediately correct any issues, and that all eligible voters can cast ballots during the full voting period. Similar programs have been successfully implemented in other jurisdictions across the country.
“For too long, incarcerated New Yorkers — the majority of whom are people of color — have been subjected to widespread disenfranchisement inside New York City jails,” said Takeasha Newton, Lead Community Organizer in the Community Justice Unit at Legal Aid. “This is an affront to democracy that must come to an end.”

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Officials join hundreds of protesters at 'No ICE' rally in Newburgh
NEWBURGH — Under an occasional faint drizzle, about 300 Hudson Valley residents and elected officials gathered in Algonquin Park on the evening of July 7 for a "No ICE in Newburgh" rally.
With a long line of vehicles parked along the grass perimeter, the protesters at 54 Powder Mill Road carried signs condemning U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, some featuring strong disapproval and mocking caricatures of President Donald Trump.
Messages on the posters included "No human is illegal," "No ICE, no Gestapo," "Warehouses are for pallets/products/packages not people" and "Abolish ICE now."
Those gathered chanted, "Show me what democracy looks like! This is what democracy looks like!" "Whose streets? Our streets!," "ICE out now!" and "Hey, hey, ho, ho! Donald Trump has got to go!"
Organized by a coalition of advocacy groups, the protest was attended by a large group of public officials, including U.S. Rep. Pat Ryan, Assemblymember Jonathan Jacobson, Orange County Legislator Genesis Ramos, Town of Chester Supervisor Brandon Holdridge and Orange County Democratic Party Chairman Zak Constantine.
The speakers touted their prior mobilization efforts and protests over canceled federal plans for an ICE detention site at a warehouse in Chester.
Ramos cited the fatal shooting of a Mexican immigrant, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, in Houston by ICE earlier in the day and called ICE a "rogue" agency in need of oversight. She called dissent patriotic and vowed to prevent the opening of a detention facility in Newburgh and asked the broader community to engage and consider the anti-immigrant rhetoric and animus.
"Has a single deportation made your life better?" Ramos said. "Has one inhumane detention center improved your circumstances and conditions? Has terrorizing our streets, tearing apart families, has any of it made your life easier, your wages higher, or your communities stronger? No, it hasn't and it won't."
Jacobson spoke of choosing compassion over fear and rejected the presence of a detention site in Newburgh — "Not now, not ever." Citing the recently passed "Dignity Not Detention" legislation he supported against civil detention, Jacobson said, "The state, counties and local governments cannot contract with ICE, including hosting detention facilities or renting out jails."
The implementation of the legislation remains unclear as the Department of Homeland Security sued New York, challenging the state's attempts to end long-standing 287(g) cooperation agreements and unmask federal enforcement officers.
Ryan said the possibility of a mass detention site conjured the darkest moments in human history and it was not a coincidence Orange County was targeted twice.
Advertisement
"Now twice here in our own backyard," Ryan said, "the very people elected by the American people have turned their backs on that declaration, on our Constitution, on our Bill of Rights, on our patriotic values as Americans that we care for everyone. And when we say liberty and justice for all, it means actually all."
A day earlier, Ryan's opponent in the upcoming November election for New York's 18th Congressional District, Jackie Auringer, also opposed a Newburgh ICE facility in an email statement, but attributed the possibility to the recent Albany legislation that limits cooperation with ICE.
"Albany Democrats did not make immigration enforcement more humane, they made it more chaotic," Auringer said. "They passed laws that defy federal immigration law and block cooperation with federal immigration enforcement which does nothing to reduce the need to process illegal immigrants. It only pushes Washington toward more costly options, away from existing local capacity, and into a system that makes life harder for those being detained."
The reaction comes after reports during the past week pointed to a possible detention site at a warehouse lease related to the U.S. General Services Administration, though the federal government has not announced anything.
Located near Stewart International Airport, the site in question is at 800 Corporate Blvd. off state Route 17K in the Town of Newburgh. It is a 60,143-square-foot, single-story building on 9.5 acres. The owner of the property is listed as 4.5 Associates on Liberty Street in New York City, according to county property records.
More: Amazon warehouse project dealt major setback in Orange County court
The possibility of using the site as a detention center likely stems from the use of "detainee buses and vans" and need for a secure sally port/garage in the procurement summary for a GSA solicitation in the area of Newburgh.
The Corporate Boulevard address is listed as "New lease - DHS ICE" in GSA's Inventory of Owned and Leased Properties dated July 3, with the location tag (NY7716).
ICE media representatives have not returned multiple requests for clarification.

When the crowd at Rockland Community College in Suffern started chanting “four more years,” Donald Trump didn’t just let the moment land. He grabbed it—then turned it into a merchandise pitch.
Standing at a campaign-style rally at the Eugene Levy Fieldhouse on May 22. 2026. Trump referred to himself as a “three-term president.” The chant that followed—“four more years”—quickly became part of his act. “We have a hat. The hat says ‘4 more years.’ It drives the radical left lunatics crazy. ” he told supporters. leaning into the crowd energy as they cheered.
Trump then doubled down on the “three-term” framing. “You know we’re a three-term president, we just don’t want the results,” he said. “We don’t want — we won three times, but we only want the results of the first and the third.”
The merch pitch wasn’t theoretical. Trump’s operation has been selling red “Trump 2028” hats for $50 since April 24, as he continued floating the idea of seeking a constitutionally barred third term.
The product listing on the Trump Store describes the hat in upbeat terms: “The future looks bright!. Rewrite the rules with the Trump 2028 high crown hat. Fully embroidered with a snap closure in the back. this will become your new go-to hat.” The store has also been selling T-shirts bearing the same phrase alongside the slogan “Rewrite the Rules.”.
Trump’s political operation then leaned into social proof. A photo on X shared by Trump’s operation showed Eric Trump wearing the hat; Eric reposted it describing the merchandise as “master trolling” and adding the caption “#NeverSayNever.”
The constitutional constraint remains clear. The 22nd Amendment states: “No person shall be elected to the office of the President more than twice.”
Even so, speculation around a path back to office has continued. Donald told NBC News it was one possible route to return by being elected vice president and then later ascending to the presidency if the sitting president resigned, adding “there are others, too,” without elaborating.
Inside the rally, the merchandise moment sat alongside familiar policy and politics. Trump’s May 22 appearance was aimed at supporting Republicans in a competitive House district ahead of the November midterms.
The event leaned heavily on federal tax cuts. Trump dubbed Congressman Mike Lawler “Mr. SALT,” pointing to Lawler’s role in securing a provision in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that raised the SALT deduction cap from $10,000 to $40,000.
Ahead of the event, White House spokesperson Liz Huston said, “The President will discuss how he and Republicans in Congress delivered the largest middle-class tax cuts in history — including quadrupling the State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction cap from $10,000 to $40,000.”

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Labor strike by Long Island Rail Road workers prompts disruption to commuter rail system in New York, NY
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Long Island Rail Road workers are on strike, union officials said early Saturday, paralyzing the busiest commuter rail system in North America.
Labor unions representing about half the system's workers announced the walkout after negotiations with the MTA ended Friday without a new contract.
What You Need To Know
- Long Island Rail Road workers are on strike, union officials said early Saturday
- Labor unions representing about half the system's workers announced the walkout after negotiations with the MTA ended Friday without a new contract
- The strike will force the roughly 250,000 people who ride the system each weekday to find alternative routes into New York City from its Long Island suburbs or to work from home
The five unions, which represent about half the system’s 7,000 workers, including locomotive engineers, machinists and signalmen, weren't legally allowed to go on strike until 12:01 a.m. Saturday.
Kevin Sexton of the National Vice President of the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen said no new negotiations have been scheduled.
“We’re far apart at this point," Sexton said. “We are truly sorry that we are in this situation.”
Janno Lieber, the MTA chairman, said the agency “gave the union everything they said they wanted in terms of pay” and that to him it was apparent the unions always intended to walk out.
The strike will force the roughly 250,000 people who ride the system each weekday to find alternative routes into New York City from its Long Island suburbs or to work from home. That means more cars on traffic-choked highways and longer work commutes.
The strike could make it challenging for some sports fans to get into Manhattan to watch the NBA’s New York Knicks playoff run or see the baseball rivals the New York Yankees battle the crosstown Mets this weekend.
Gov. Kathy Hochul has urged LIRR riders to work from during the walkout as the MTA plans to provide free but limited shuttle buses during the work day rush hours geared toward essential workers.
In a statement she blamed the strike on union leadership.
“Commuters are dealing with unnecessary dysfunction and thousands of union LIRR workers are being forced to go without a paycheck because of decisions made by a small group of union leaders," Hochul said. "I stand with LIRR riders and will fight to preserve the long term stability of the MTA.”
Both sides said the fight was over wage increases and health care premiums.
Details on exactly where each side stood late Friday weren't released, but the union had gone into the talks demanding a total raise of 16% over four years, saying it was needed to help workers keep up with inflation.
The MTA has argued that the union’s initial demands would lead to fare increases. Lieber said that while the MTA had met the pay demands, it had asked for new hires to the LIRR to pay higher health care premiums to offset some costs. The union rejected that idea.
A strike was temporarily averted in September when President Donald Trump’s administration agreed to help with negotiations. Those efforts ended without a deal, giving both sides 60 days — ending 12:01 a.m. Saturday — to again try to resolve their differences before the union is legally allowed to go on strike or the agency could lock out workers.
LIRR workers last went on strike in 1994, for about two days.
Workers on the commuter rail system connecting Manhattan to New Jersey, New Jersey Transit, went on strike last year. It lasted three days.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Houston, TX City Council to vote on proposal to clarify level of cooperation with ICE
MESSAGE_TEXT:
With less than 24 hours before a scheduled vote, several Houston City Council members say they are frustrated as they review a newly revised proposal spelling out HPD's level of cooperation with ICE.
Wednesday, April 22, 2026 3:19AMWith less than 24 hours before a scheduled vote, several Houston City Council members say they are frustrated as they review a newly revised proposal spelling out HPD's level of cooperation with ICE.
Protesters gathered outside City Hall on Tuesday, chanting against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement policies before filing into council chambers. Inside, the room was packed as community members voiced sharply divided opinions over public safety funding and the city's approach to immigration enforcement. Mayor John Whitmire unveiled proposed changes to an ordinance governing how Houston police interact with federal immigration authorities during routine stops. He said the revisions are intended to help the city avoid losing critical public safety funding from the state. Some council members criticized the timing, saying they had little opportunity to review the updated language. "I think we really need to look at the language, have a chance to digest it and be ready for tomorrow," Council Member Edward Pollard said. Two weeks ago, the council passed an ordinance that removed the requirement that Houston Police Department officers wait 30 minutes for ICE to respond after being notified of someone with an administrative warrant. The earlier version also stated that civil immigration warrants alone were not sufficient grounds for detention.Council Member Abbie Kamin said the issue stems from constitutional protections. "This is about the rights of Houstonians - rights enshrined in the Bill of Rights - and local law enforcement we entrust to enforce our laws regardless of immigration status," Kamin said. One amendment clarifies that nothing in the ordinance limits cooperation with federal immigration authorities when required by state law or agreements. Another provision allows officers to temporarily detain individuals for a "reasonably necessary" period to complete the purpose of the initial stop or to address a legitimate issue discovered during the detention. During the meeting, council member Alejandra Salinas asked whether the changes would effectively reinstate the prior 30-minute waiting policy for ICE response.The updated proposal also removes explicit language from the original ordinance stating that individuals must be released if there is no separate criminal justification for detention."The Constitution clearly states that during a stop, after the law enforcement officer has conducted the reason for the stop, you can't prolong or detain a person for something that has nothing to do with the stop," he said. Critics argue the revisions could infringe on constitutional rights, while supporters say the city must adopt the amendments to avoid losing state funding and to give officers more discretion. "By taking away an officer's discretion ... that's a problem," one speaker said during public comment.With the revised proposal now on the table, the Houston City Council is expected to vote on Wednesday.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
PORTLAND, Ore. — A student-led demonstration resulted in over one hundred students walking out of Central Catholic High School on Friday morning.
The walkout was orchestrated in protest after a player on the school's baseball team reportedly said a racial slur during a pre-game cheer. According to students at the school, varsity players hazed a freshman into saying what he did.
“Last week, we learned that racial hate speech was used by a member of our baseball team during a pre-game cheer," the Central Catholic administration said in statement when the incident first came to light. "This language is offensive, harmful, and in direct conflict with who we are as a school community.”
The school forfeited a couple baseball games, and also canceled in-person classes Monday and Tuesday to determine how to support students.
But the students who walked out Friday are asking for more from the Catholic school administration, and said what has been done thus far has not been effective.
“They hold these safe spaces for us where we can talk and freely share our opinions, but they create no real change, and want to change pretty much nothing," said Jalen Jackson, a senior at the school.
“Our Black students are obviously mortified by this happening, but I see too many people in this school walking up to them and talking like nothing has ever happened. It's really disgusting, to be honest, and we need to be better as a community," Jackson continued.
Students want the school to take greater accountability.
“We’re first asking for varsity baseball players (to be) kicked off the team," said Melissa Vargas, another senior at the school. “The varsity players essentially hazed a freshman into saying the racial slurs in the hate speech, and their season should be over and JV should be swung up instead."
They also want coaches to be held accountable.
“Our second ask is a mandatory training for coaches on anti-racism and anti-hazing," Vargas continued, "so the coaches need to have an understanding and awareness of what this looks like on their team. And we just ask that this doesn't happen again, and the coaches should be suspended until they become educated on this topic."
Their third ask is a revision of the student handbook, completed with student approval.
“I think the two games canceled wasn't enough. I think this has been going on even before those two games, and I think it's disgusting," Vargas said.
The school released an updated statement Friday, following the walkout:
"Today’s walkout was a powerful expression of the real hurt and urgency many of our Black students and community members are carrying. We support our student’s right to express themselves. Students have raised serious concerns about potential hazing, team culture, coaching oversight, and our response as a school. We are addressing each of these concerns directly and in alignment with our current policies."
"We have taken action consistent with our current policies and are continuing to hold students accountable in ways that reflect the seriousness of this situation. We are strengthening expectations for coaching through required training and support to ensure team culture, supervision, and leadership consistent with Central Catholic’s values.
"We have engaged culturally-responsive partners to conduct a comprehensive review of our school. Their findings and recommendations will be shared with our school community, including our Black Student Union, and will directly inform the actions we take moving forward. Our focus remains on supporting students and maintaining a safe and respectful environment."

CAPTION_ENDORSE: At least six nurses fired from Saint Mary of Nazareth Hospital in Chicago, IL after Prime Healthcare acquired hospital in March 2025
MESSAGE_TEXT:
When Saint Mary of Nazareth Hospital was acquired by Prime Healthcare in March 2025, nurse Karlie Thorn said she noticed conditions in the emergency department changed for the worse almost immediately.
A disproportionate number of inexperienced nurses, cheaper supplies and staffing shortages were among the concerning conditions Thorn and several other nurses allege, alarming them enough to prompt considering unionization.
As staffers launched an effort to hold an election to unionize with National Nurses Organizing Committee/National Nurses United last month, at least six nurses were fired in what the union calls a “troubling pattern of going after experienced nurses who are advocating for their patients and coworkers.”
“I think it sent a message to the nurses in our community that we’re expendable and when we speak up for each other, they’ll get rid of us with no just cause,” said Thorn, one of the fired nurses. “We want an election that’s fair and without interference from Prime, and we want our nurses back.”
“As nurses, we take care of everyone all day,” added Thorn, an emergency department nurse for the last four years. “We deserve to be taken care of as well.”
Registered nurses at Saint Mary’s plan to hold a one-day strike on June 11 to protest what they is retaliation for speaking out about unsafe conditions, calling it a strike for “patient safety and an end to union busting.” The fired nurses are also petitioning to get their jobs back.
In a statement to the Sun-Times, a Saint Mary’s spokesperson said, “we have not and will not retaliate against employees for exercising their rights and have consistently applied longstanding hospital policies that protect safety and patient care.”
“Saint Mary’s of Nazareth Hospital respects the right of nurses to make their own decisions regarding union representation and to engage in lawful protected activity,” the statement said. Saint Mary’s added that “comprehensive plans” were in place to ensure operations uninterrupted during the one-day strike.
Since Prime acquired Saint Mary’s, along with seven other area hospitals, nurses at the Ukrainian Village hospital say they have felt overworked, fearful for their jobs and greater concerned for their safety and for that of their patients.
“We have always had staffing issues in the ER, but they have gotten worse since Prime took over,” Thorn said. “It’s just not safe for us to have 25 people in the waiting room and each nurse already has four to five patients.”
Patient ratios for emergency room nurses are typically one-to-five, Thorn noted, though more recently it has been seven patients for every nurse because of staff members who left because of concerns about hospital conditions or were fired.
Jesus Hernandez, a behavioral health nurse for the seven years before he was fired, said his unit has lost monitors, making it more difficult to care for patients quickly and leaving patients at risk of harming each other or staff members who are responding to a crisis.
“[The monitors] are kind of our eyes and ears on the behavioral health floor to make sure the patients and staff are safe,” Hernandez said.
Some older patients are at more likely to fall, while others without a safety attendant have impulses that could lead to physical aggression, he said.
Amiee Bae worked for more than seven years in Saint Mary’s acute male psychiatric unit before she she says she was fired for speaking out about poor conditions in her unit. Bae said the changes after Prime took over were small at first.
Things like lower-quailty gloves, patient socks and towels gave way to bigger changes, Bae said, including the loss of addiction medication that in some instances was life-saving for patients in the hospital’s six psychiatric units.
“Alcohol withdrawal can kill somebody if you’re not treating them properly,” Bae said. “They can go into severe pain and distress.”
Though Bae has been a vocal critic of the changes she’s seen since Prime took over, she said she’s still willing to work with the California-based healthcare company because of her passion for nursing. She hopes the strike leads to the fired nurses getting reinstated.
“I gave 200% of my soul, my physical capacity to St. Mary’s for seven years,” Bae said.
“I’m still willing to work with Prime because I love my hospital. I love who I serve.”
Mohammad Samra
Chicago Sun-TimesNews reporter

MESSAGE_TEXT:
A group of eight protestors were arrested in Hoboken on Thursday after they were caught scaling a building to hang up a massive banner.
The protest was held near 111 River St., which houses the headquarters of Unilever, the parent company of personal care brand Dove. Greenpeace USA led the protest, which advocates for the removal of plastic packaging amid debates about its affect on men’s reproductive health.
Dove is an official sponsor of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Hoboken Police showed up at the protest on Thursday morning, following reports of demonstrators climbing poles near the Unilever headquarters. The eight protestors identified themselves as members of Greenpeace USA, Marci Rubin, a spokeswoman for the city said.
Of the eight arrested, five were charged with obstructing the administration of the law and three were charged with disorderly conduct and defiant trespassing.
At the protest, Greenpeace USA hung a 50-foot banner near the Unilever headquarters that reads: “Care for Men’s Health, Kick Plastic Out.”
The activist organization said Unilever ranks as one of the world’s top plastic polluters amid growing concerns about the role of plastics in men’s fertility.
“As an official sponsor of the World Cup, Dove has spent millions telling men it cares for their most sensitive parts. But its parent company, Unilever, is one of the world’s top plastic polluters — and now plastic pollution is showing up below the belt,“ said Lindsey Jurca, the senior oceans campaigner for Greenpeace USA. ”Dove can’t have it both ways. We’re asking Dove to put its money where its mouth is and kick plastic out."
The city did not name the protestors who were arrested. They were all charged by summons and released.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Protest blocks area outside courthouse in Morelia, Michoacan, Mexico
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Morelia, Michoacán.- Personal del Poder Judicial de la Federación (PJF) realizó una manifestación en las afueras de los tribunales ubicados en la capital del estado para exigir un alto al hostigamiento en las áreas administrativas y denunciar recortes de personal.
Las inconformes, encabezadas por Yetzgli Lorena y Araceli Aguiar, recordaron que desde septiembre del año pasado promovieron una queja formal ante las instancias de disciplina interna en contra de una juzgadora del circuito judicial. Las afectadas acusaron a la servidora pública de ejercer presuntas amenazas institucionales y maltrato laboral severo en perjuicio de los oficiales encargados de los juzgados federales.
Las empleadas manifestaron que las deficiencias técnicas de la titular entorpecían el desahogo ágil de los expedientes y juicios de amparo promovidos por la ciudadanía en la entidad. Tras varias horas de presión en el acceso principal, representantes sindicales confirmaron que el órgano supervisor ordenó el cese fulminante de la acusada de sus funciones jurisdiccionales.
Denuncian despidos masivos de trabajadores sociales en defensoría pública
La protesta también sirvió como plataforma para visibilizar la destitución injustificada de casi cincuenta trabajadores de la salud social adscritos al Instituto Federal de Defensoría Pública (IFDP) en el territorio nacional. En la delegación de Michoacán, el ajuste presupuestal alcanzó a una especialista con casi tres décadas de trayectoria en la elaboración de dictámenes socioeconómicos.
Nancy Ortiz, oficial de la dependencia, externó que la afectada se encontraba a las puertas de consolidar su jubilación de ley cuando le notificaron el término de su contrato sin mediar explicación alguna. Los líderes de la base trabajadora abrieron mesas de negociación con los mandos estatales para presionar a la sede central en la capital del país por una reinstalación inmediata.
Con información de Agencia de Comunicación Gráfica
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Morelia, Michoacán – Employees of the Federal Judiciary (PJF) held a demonstration outside the courts in the state capital to demand an end to harassment in administrative areas and to denounce staff cuts.

The protesters, led by Yetzgli Lorena and Araceli Aguiar, recalled that they filed a formal complaint with internal disciplinary bodies last September against a judge in the judicial circuit. The affected employees accused the public servant of making alleged institutional threats and committing severe workplace abuse against the officials in charge of the federal courts.

The employees stated that the judge's technical deficiencies hindered the efficient handling of cases and injunctions filed by citizens in the state. After several hours of pressure at the main entrance, union representatives confirmed that the supervisory body ordered the immediate dismissal of the accused from her judicial duties. Mass Layoffs of Social Workers at Public Defender's Office Denounced
The protest also served as a platform to highlight the unjustified dismissal of nearly fifty social workers assigned to the Federal Institute of Public Defenders (IFDP) nationwide. In the Michoacán delegation, the budget cuts affected a specialist with almost three decades of experience preparing socioeconomic reports.

Nancy Ortiz, an official with the agency, stated that the affected worker was about to receive her legally mandated retirement when she was notified of the termination of her contract without any explanation. Union leaders have opened negotiations with state officials to pressure the central office in Mexico City for her immediate reinstatement.

With information from Agencia de Comunicación Gráfica

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Protesters block road in Kodali area of Jayankondam, Tamil Nadu, India
MESSAGE_TEXT:
A group of students, wearing uniforms of the government schools at Kodali near Jayankondam staged a protest on Saturday along with the residents of the village, demanding the closure of a Tasmac outlet.
Claiming that the presence of the outlet had made several people addicted to liquor, the protesters blocked the traffic at Kodali on Anaikarai and Kodalikaruppur road. On information, the T. Palur police and the Tasmac officials rushed to the spot and began negotiation with the protesters.
While the officials sought two months to close the outlet, the protesters refused to budge. As a mark of registering their protest, the protesters, including boys and girls, ran towards the Tasmac outlet and vandalised the barrier. Some of them indulged in stone throwing on the outlet. A tussle ensued between the protesters and the police, when they tried to control them.
The officials thereafter resumed negotiations with the protesters who dispersed from the spot following a promise that the Tasmac outlet would be closed immediately.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
La protesta, convocada por la plataforma Galiza pola Paz y los movimientos sociales, coincidió con los actos del Día de las Fuerzas Armadas en Vigo y reunió a manifestantes llegados de toda Galicia bajo un grito unitario de ‘no a la guerra’.
Más abajo, noticia de El Salto en castellano: Galicia responde al desfile militar con una multitudinaria protesta por la paz
Milleiros de persoas percorreron este sábado as rúas de Vigo denunciando a propaganda militarista, o incremento do gasto público en armamento, o papel da OTAN e reclamando a fin das guerras e o imperialismo. Mentres, a poucos quilómetros, na praia de Samil, as Forzas Armadas españolas despregan os seus efectivos nun evento de exaltación militarista que conta coa presenza do rei e a raíña de España, Felipe VI e Letizia Ortiz, e da princesa Leonor de Borbón.
O Goberno español duplicou os fondos para armas e defensa en cinco anos até gastar 42.000 millóns en 2025
Rompe a bandeira española durante o izado no Día das Forzas Armadas en Vigo.
Redacción
Vigo viviu este sábado unha xornada marcada polo contraste entre o despregamento das Forzas Armadas españolas e a resposta antimilitarista nas rúas da cidade. Mentres a praia de Samil e o litoral vigués acollían os actos centrais do Día das Forzas Armadas, milleiros de persoas participaban na manifestación convocada por Galiza pola Paz baixo o lema «Paz e soberanía. Nin guerra, nin OTAN nin gastos militares. Non ao desfile militar».
A mobilización percorreu as rúas da cidade olívica en rexeitamento do que a plataforma define como unha «exaltación obscena do militarismo» nun contexto internacional marcado pola guerra en Palestina, Ucraína, Líbano ou Irán e polo aumento do gasto militar promovido desde a Unión Europea e a OTAN.
Durante varios días Vigo foi convertido nun grande escaparate militar. Exposicións de armamento, visitas a buques de guerra, demostracións operativas, concertos de bandas castrenses e o propio desfile conforman unha programación que os colectivos antimilitaristas interpretan como unha operación de normalización do discurso bélico.
Desde Galiza pola Paz denuncian que os investimentos destinados ao rearme se producen «en detrimento da calidade de vida» da poboación e defenden que eses recursos deberían dirixirse á sanidade pública, o ensino, a dependencia, as pensións ou as políticas sociais. A plataforma reúne organizacións sindicais, políticas, culturais e movementos sociais que reivindican unha saída pacífica aos conflitos internacionais e unha orde global baseada na soberanía dos pobos.
Durante a lectura do manifesto, a organización cualificou de «obscenidade» o despregamento do Exército español na cidade, denunciando tanto os seus custos económicos como o impacto sobre a vida diaria da veciñanza. «Non queremos tanques nas rúas, Galiza quere paz», resumiron.
O Goberno español duplicou os fondos para armas e defensa en cinco anos até gastar 42.000 millóns en 2025
A plataforma criticou a utilización de espazos públicos, os cortes de tráfico e a programación de actividades vinculadas ao Exército, cuestionando tamén a presenza de escolares en actos como o izado da bandeira española decorrido esta semana en Vigo. Galiza pola Paz denunciou igualmente o gasto público asociado ao Día das Forzas Armadas. Segundo indicaron, só a grada de autoridades instalada para o desfile custaría arredor de 400.000 euros. «Case medio millón para un día, unhas horas. Despois: desmontar e ao lixo. A pregunta é:por que é este o único gasto que coñecemos?».
No manifesto, a plataforma vinculou o desfile co proceso de militarización impulsado, ao seu xuízo, polo Goberno español, a OTAN e a Unión Europea. Criticou especialmente o plan europeo de rearme, os incrementos dos orzamentos militares e a compra de armamento, advertindo de que «cada euro que vai para a maquinaria de destrución é un euro que deixa de ir ao ensino, á sanidade ou aos servizos públicos».
Os colectivos convocantes tamén cuestionaron o papel internacional do Exército español, mencionando intervencións militares como as de Iraq, Afganistán ou a eventual participación en Ucraína, e acusaron os exércitos das potencias occidentais de actuar ao servizo de intereses imperialistas.
Nunha intervención de marcado ton antimilitarista e antiimperialista, a plataforma reivindicou a tradición pacifista da sociedade galega, desde a oposición á OTAN até as mobilizacións contra a guerra de Iraq ou o apoio actual a Palestina. «Fronte á súa militarización, paz e soberanía. Nin guerras, nin OTAN, nin gastos militares», concluíu o manifesto lido ao remate da mobilización.
Galicia responde al desfile militar con una multitudinaria protesta por la paz
Javier H. Rodríguez
Miles de personas llegadas de distintos puntos de Galicia se movilizaron este sábado en Vigo para mostrar su rechazo al desfile militar organizado con motivo del Día de las Fuerzas Armadas. Convocadas por la plataforma Galiza pola Paz y por decenas de colectivos sociales, antimilitaristas y organizaciones políticas, las manifestantes recorrieron las calles de la ciudad bajo consignas a favor de la paz y contra el aumento del gasto militar y el discurso belicista.
La protesta coincidió con los actos oficiales celebrados en la playa de Samil y reunió a participantes procedentes de las cuatro provincias gallegas. Durante la marcha pudieron verse pancartas con lemas en defensa de la resolución pacífica de los conflictos y críticas a la creciente militarización de la política internacional.
Entre las personas asistentes se encontraba el diputado del BNG en el Congreso, Néstor Rego, quien cargó contra el “inmenso” gasto destinado por el Gobierno central al desfile y a la movilización de material militar. El parlamentario calificó el acto de “una exaltación del militarismo absolutamente costosa e innecesaria” y consideró un “despropósito” dedicar recursos públicos a este tipo de celebraciones “en un momento de crisis social y económica”.
“En el BNG lo tenemos claro: escogemos entre militarismo y defensa de la democracia y de Galicia como nación. Frente al gasto militar, optamos por la inversión social; y, frente a la guerra imperialista, optamos por la paz y por la soberanía de los pueblos, incluido el pueblo gallego”, afirmó antes del inicio de la manifestación.
Las organizaciones convocantes denunciaron que la celebración del desfile contribuye a normalizar la cultura militar en un contexto marcado por el incremento de los presupuestos de defensa en numerosos países europeos. Asimismo, reclamaron que los recursos destinados al ámbito militar se orienten a reforzar los servicios públicos, la cooperación internacional, la vivienda y las políticas sociales.
En la misma línea, Rego responsabilizó al Ejecutivo de Pedro Sánchez de impulsar “el mayor incremento del gasto militar de las últimas décadas” y vinculó esta política a una “escalada armamentística que hipoteca recursos públicos” y que, según sostuvo, se realiza “al dictado de la OTAN y de los Estados Unidos”.
El diputado anunció además que el BNG llevará al próximo pleno del Congreso una moción para que los grupos parlamentarios se posicionen sobre el aumento del gasto militar y sobre la permanencia de España en la OTAN. “En época de crisis, ¿cuál debe ser la prioridad?”, planteó.
La movilización transcurrió sin incidentes y concluyó con la lectura de un manifiesto en el que se reivindicó una Galicia comprometida con la paz, el desarme y la solidaridad entre los pueblos. Los colectivos participantes defendieron que la seguridad debe construirse desde la justicia social y la diplomacia, y no mediante la exhibición de poder militar. Con cánticos, música y centenares de banderas y pancartas, la protesta convirtió el centro de Vigo en el principal escaparate del rechazo al desfile castrense celebrado simultáneamente en Samil.

The protest, called by the platform Galicia for Peace and social movements, coincided with the Armed Forces Day events in Vigo and brought together demonstrators from all over Galicia under a united cry of 'no to war'.
Below, news from El Salto in Spanish: Galicia responds to the military parade with a massive protest for peace
Thousands of people walked the streets of Vigo this Saturday denouncing militarist propaganda, the increase in public spending on armaments, the role of NATO and demanding an end to wars and imperialism. Meanwhile, a few kilometers away, on Samil beach, the Spanish Armed Forces are deploying their troops in an event of militaristic exaltation that is attended by the King and Queen of Spain, Felipe VI and Letizia Ortiz, and Princess Leonor de Borbón.
The Spanish Government has doubled funds for weapons and defense in five years to spend 42,000 million in 2025
The Spanish flag is torn during the raising on Armed Forces Day in Vigo.
Editorial
This Saturday, Vigo experienced a day marked by the contrast between the deployment of the Spanish Armed Forces and the anti-militarist response on the streets of the city. While Samil beach and the Vigo coastline hosted the central events of Armed Forces Day, thousands of people participated in the demonstration called by Galicia for Peace under the slogan "Peace and sovereignty. No war, no NATO or military spending. No to the military parade".
The mobilization traveled through the streets of the olive-growing city in rejection of what the platform defines as an "obscene glorification of militarism" in an international context marked by the war in Palestine, Ukraine, Lebanon or Iran and by the increase in military spending promoted by the European Union and NATO.
For several days, Vigo was turned into a large military showcase. Armament exhibitions, visits to warships, operational demonstrations, concerts by military bands and the parade itself make up a program that anti-militarist groups interpret as an operation to normalize the war discourse.
From Galicia for Peace they denounce that the investments destined for rearmament are produced "to the detriment of the quality of life" of the population and defend that these resources should be directed to public health, education, dependency, pensions or social policies. The platform brings together trade union, political, cultural organizations and social movements that demand a peaceful solution to international conflicts and a global order based on the sovereignty of peoples.
During the reading of the manifesto, the organization described the deployment of the Spanish Army in the city as "obscenity", denouncing both its economic costs and the impact on the daily life of the neighborhood. "We do not want tanks in the streets, Galicia wants peace", they summarized.
The Spanish Government has doubled its funds for weapons and defense in five years to spend 42 billion in 2025
The platform criticized the use of public spaces, traffic jams and the programming of activities linked to the Army, also questioning the presence of schoolchildren in events such as the raising of the Spanish flag that took place this week in Vigo. Galicia for Peace also denounced the public spending associated with Armed Forces Day. According to them, only the official stands installed for the parade would cost around 400,000 euros. "Almost half a million for a day, a few hours. Then: dismantle and throw in the trash. The question is: why is this the only expense we know about?"
In the manifesto, the platform linked the parade to the militarization process promoted, in their opinion, by the Spanish Government, NATO and the European Union. It particularly criticized the European rearmament plan, increases in military budgets and the purchase of weapons, warning that "every euro that goes to the machinery of destruction is a euro that stops going to education, health or public services".
The convening groups also questioned the international role of the Spanish Army, mentioning military interventions such as those in Iraq, Afghanistan or the eventual participation in Ukraine, and accused the armies of the Western powers of acting in the service of imperialist interests.
In an intervention with a marked anti-militarist and anti-imperialist tone, the platform vindicated the pacifist tradition of Galician society, from opposition to NATO to mobilizations against the Iraq war or current support for Palestine. "In the face of its militarization, peace and sovereignty. No wars, no NATO, no military spending", concluded the manifesto read at the end of the mobilization.
Galicia responds to the military parade with a massive protest for peace
Javier H. Rodríguez
Thousands of people from different parts of Galicia mobilized this Saturday in Vigo to show their rejection of the military parade organized on the occasion of Armed Forces Day. Called by the Galicia for Peace platform and dozens of social groups, anti-militarist and political organizations, the demonstrators walked the streets of the city under slogans in favor of peace and against the increase in military spending and warmongering discourse.
The protest coincided with the official events held on Samil beach and brought together participants from the four Galician provinces. During the march, banners with slogans in defense of the peaceful resolution of conflicts and criticism of the increasing militarization of international politics could be seen.
Among the people attending was the BNG deputy in Congress, Néstor Rego, who charged against the "immense" expenditure allocated by the central government to the parade and the mobilization of military equipment. The parliamentarian described the act as "an absolutely costly and unnecessary exaltation of militarism" and considered it a "nonsense" to devote public resources to this type of celebrations "at a time of social and economic crisis".
"In the BNG we are clear: we choose between militarism and the defense of democracy and of Galicia as a nation. In the face of military spending, we opt for social investment; and, in the face of imperialist war, we opt for peace and for the sovereignty of the peoples, including the Galician people", he said before the beginning of the demonstration.
The convening organizations denounced that the celebration of the parade contributes to the normalization of military culture in a context marked by the increase in defense budgets in many European countries. They also demanded that the resources allocated to the military be directed to strengthening public services, international cooperation, housing and social policies.
In the same line, Rego held Pedro Sánchez's Executive responsible for promoting "the largest increase in military spending in recent decades" and linked this policy to an "armament escalation that mortgages public resources" and which, he argued, is being carried out "at the behest of NATO and the United States".
The deputy also announced that the BNG will bring to the next full session of Congress a motion for the parliamentary groups to position themselves on the increase in military spending and on Spain's permanence in NATO. "In times of crisis, what should be the priority?" he asked.
The mobilization took place without incident and concluded with the reading of a manifesto in which a Galicia committed to peace, disarmament and solidarity between the peoples was claimed. The participating groups defended that security must be built from social justice and diplomacy, and not through the display of military power. With chants, music and hundreds of flags and banners, the protest turned the center of Vigo into the main showcase of the rejection of the military parade held simultaneously in Samil.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Σε συμμετοχή στην πανελλαδική απεργία των εργαζομένων στο εμπόριο, που έχει προκηρυχθεί για την Κυριακή 19 Ιουλίου, καλεί το Σωματείο Εμπορο...
Σε συμμετοχή στην πανελλαδική απεργία των εργαζομένων στο εμπόριο, που έχει προκηρυχθεί για την Κυριακή 19 Ιουλίου, καλεί το Σωματείο Εμποροϋπαλλήλων – Ιδιωτικών Υπαλλήλων Περιοχής Αλεξανδρούπολης – Φερών – Σουφλίου «Η Ενότητα».
Στην ανακοίνωσή του υποστηρίζει ότι οι εργαζόμενοι στον κλάδο αντιμετωπίζουν εντατικοποίηση της εργασίας, χαμηλές αμοιβές και ευέλικτες μορφές απασχόλησης, ενώ εκφράζει την αντίθεσή του στις σχεδιαζόμενες αλλαγές που –όπως αναφέρει– διευρύνουν τη δυνατότητα λειτουργίας των καταστημάτων τις Κυριακές.
Τα βασικά αιτήματα
Μεταξύ των βασικών διεκδικήσεων που προβάλλει το σωματείο είναι:
- Κατοχύρωση της κυριακάτικης αργίας και απόρριψη κάθε επέκτασης της εργασίας τις Κυριακές.
- Αυξήσεις στους μισθούς, με βασικό μισθό στα 1.000 ευρώ και προσαυξήσεις λόγω προϋπηρεσίας.
- Καθιέρωση 7ωρου – 5ήμερου – 35ωρου και κατάργηση του σπαστού ωραρίου.
- Σταθερό πρόγραμμα εργασίας και συγκεκριμένες βάρδιες.
- Κατοχύρωση επιδομάτων, όπως γάμου, παιδιών, πολυετίας και ταμειακών λαθών.
- Ενίσχυση των μέτρων υγείας και ασφάλειας στους χώρους εργασίας και σαφής καθορισμός των ειδικοτήτων.
Το σωματείο υποστηρίζει επίσης ότι η υπογραφή νέας Κλαδικής Συλλογικής Σύμβασης Εργασίας αποτελεί βασική προϋπόθεση για τη βελτίωση των όρων απασχόλησης στον κλάδο.
Στο κάλεσμά του επισημαίνει ότι η απεργία της 19ης Ιουλίου αποτελεί κινητοποίηση απέναντι στις εργασιακές αλλαγές που, σύμφωνα με την ανακοίνωση, πλήττουν τα δικαιώματα των εργαζομένων στο εμπόριο.
Παράλληλα, καλεί τους εργαζόμενους να συμμετάσχουν και στο παλλαϊκό συλλαλητήριο που έχει προγραμματιστεί στη Θεσσαλονίκη, στο πλαίσιο της ΔΕΘ, στις 5 Σεπτεμβρίου.

In participation in the nationwide strike of trade workers, which has been announced for Sunday, July 19, the Trade Union of Alexandroupolis - Fera - Soufli "The Unity" calls.
