Affaire Lyhanna : rassemblement de fonctionnaires de la justice à Avignon après les sanctions prises par le gouvernement
Par Paul GUIBAL
"Ici c'est Auch", ont tenu en main des fonctionnaires de la justice, ce mardi 23 juin, à Avignon, en soutient à leur consœur visée par une enquête administrative dans le cadre de l'affaire Lyhanna.
/ Photo Paul Guibal
Avignon
Des magistrats vauclusiens se sont mobilisés devant le tribunal judiciaire d'Avignon pour dénoncer les décisions et sanctions prises par le ministre de la Justice, Gérald Darmanin, après la publication d'un rapport déclenché par la mort de Lyhanna.
"Malheureusement, des affaires Lyhanna, il y en aura d'autres si aucun moyen n'est apporté pour la justice." La vingtaine de magistrats du siège et du parquet réunis ce mardi 23 juin dans la salle des pas perdus du tribunal judiciaire d'Avignon sont en colère contre leur ministère.
À l'appel de plusieurs syndicats de la magistrature, les robes noires sont d'abord là pour apporter leur soutien à leur consœur du parquet d’Auch (Gers), "jetée en pâture" par le garde des Sceaux, Gérald Darmanin, après la mort de la jeune collégienne Lyhanna, le 4 juin dernier. Tenant quelques lettres formant la phrase "Ici c'est Auch", les robes noires expliquent souffrir depuis des années, entre conditions de travail de plus en plus lourdes et un manque "cruel" de moyens humains et matériels. "Les politiques écartent toute problématique de moyens et préfèrent désigner des coupables", dénoncent-ils. Selon les professionnels, toute la chaîne serait concernée, de la plainte à la décision de justice, des enquêteurs aux juges.
Deux postes de magistrats non pourvus
Dans les colonnes de La Provence, en décembre 2025, "on se serre la ceinture" expliquait déjà un magistrat, concernant des coupes budgétaires ô combien impactantes sur la charge de travail des magistrats. Le bâtonnier des avocats avignonnais de l'époque, Philippe Cano, décrivait un "parquet en souffrance" et une situation "en état d'urgence absolue".
Et la plaie ne risque pas de se refermer : pour la rentrée de septembre, à Avignon, "deux postes ne seront pas pourvus", précise un professionnel. Ainsi, neuf magistrats sur onze feront tourner le parquet, avec le soutien temporaire du parquet général nîmois. À titre de comparaison, un syndicat de la magistrature rappelle que le parquet d’Auch fonctionne avec moins de quatre magistrats à temps plein "là où ils devraient être a minima 24 selon la moyenne européenne et six d'après la moyenne nationale".
216 plaintes à réexaminer à Avignon, 180 à Carpentras
"Qu'on nous demande sur un cours délai de reprendre les plaintes et les procédures, ça paraît normal, poursuit un responsable. Mais une fois de plus, il y a des choses dites par le politique qui pose des difficultés. Alors que l'enquête administrative (contre la substitut d’Auch, Ndlr) vient à peine de commencer, on tire déjà des conclusions en désignant un responsable, au lieu de s'attaquer aux causes structurelles et documentées qui conduisent à ce type de drame."
En début de carrière, plusieurs jeunes magistrates expliquent faire ce métier pour "protéger la société et les victimes" et sont mobilisées, comme leurs paires, dans le réexamen des quelque 70 000 plaintes concernant les agresssions sexuelles sur mineurs demandées par le ministre. "On met tout en stand-by, très bien. Mais on ne pourra clairement pas continuer comme ça tant que le problème n'est pas résolu."
Pour rappel, sur le ressort de la cour d'appel de Nîmes, 1 497 procédures sont enclenchées, dont 216 plaintes pour Avignon et 180 sur Carpentras.
Un système "déjà sur les rotules"
Le cri d'alarme sur tous ces dysfonctionnements avait déjà été sonné en novembre 2021, lors d'un appel à l'ampleur inédite dans l'histoire de la profession : 3 000 magistrats et une centaine de greffiers signaient alors une tribune publiée dans Le Monde, dénonçant une justice "déshumanisée", les obligeant à choisir entre "juger vite mais mal" ou "juger bien mais dans des délais inacceptables". Et les magistrats avignonnais de rappeler le suicide à l'origine de cette lettre : celui de Charlotte, 29 ans, qui s'était suicidée le 23 août, après "seulement" deux années d'exercice.
Revenant sur l'affaire Lyhanna, "ces successions de cas isolés sont ensuite échafaudées en "symboles" pour nous pondre des réformes qui n'en sont pas, estime un juge. On augmente les peines, les délais de prescription… C'est du travail supplémentaire à moyen constant qui sera toujours aussi difficilement géré et qui mettra encore plus les services à genoux. Tout cela est bon en politique, pour leur com', mais ne fait que détruire encore plus un système déjà sur les rotules."

By Paul Guibal
"This is Auch," held up signs held by judicial officials in Avignon on Tuesday, June 23, in support of their colleague targeted by an administrative inquiry in the Lyhanna case.

/ Photo Paul Guibal
Avignon
Magistrates from the Vaucluse region mobilized in front of the Avignon courthouse to denounce the decisions and sanctions imposed by the Minister of Justice, Gérald Darmanin, following the publication of a report triggered by Lyhanna's death.

"Unfortunately, there will be other Lyhanna cases if no resources are allocated to the justice system." The twenty or so judges and prosecutors gathered on Tuesday, June 23, in the main hall of the Avignon courthouse are angry with their ministry. At the call of several magistrates' unions, the lawyers were primarily there to show their support for their colleague from the Auch (Gers) prosecutor's office, "thrown to the wolves" by the Minister of Justice, Gérald Darmanin, after the death of the young schoolgirl Lyhanna on June 4th. Holding up letters spelling "This is Auch," the lawyers explained that they have been suffering for years, between increasingly difficult working conditions and a "cruel" lack of human and material resources. "Politicians dismiss any issue of resources and prefer to point the finger at scapegoats," they denounced. According to the professionals, the entire system is affected, from the initial complaint to the court decision, from investigators to judges.

Two magistrate positions remain unfilled. In the pages of La Provence, in December 2025, one magistrate explained, "We're tightening our belts," regarding budget cuts that are having a significant impact on the workload of magistrates. The head of the Avignon bar association at the time, Philippe Cano, described a "prosecutor's office in distress" and a situation "in a state of absolute emergency."

And the wound is unlikely to heal: for the start of the judicial year in September, in Avignon, "two positions will remain vacant," a professional explains. Thus, nine out of eleven magistrates will be working at the prosecutor's office, with temporary support from the Nîmes public prosecutor's office. By comparison, a magistrates' union points out that the Auch prosecutor's office operates with fewer than four full-time magistrates, "whereas there should be at least 24 according to the European average and six according to the national average."

216 complaints to be reviewed in Avignon, 180 in Carpentras
"It seems normal to be asked to take over complaints and procedures on short notice," continues an official. "But once again, there are things said by politicians that are causing problems. While the administrative inquiry (against the deputy prosecutor in Auch, Ed.) has barely begun, conclusions are already being drawn by pointing the finger at someone, instead of addressing the structural and documented causes that lead to this type of tragedy." Early in their careers, several young magistrates explain that they are in this profession to "protect society and victims" and are mobilized, like their colleagues, in the review of the approximately 70,000 complaints concerning sexual assaults on minors requested by the minister. "Everything is being put on hold, very well. But we clearly cannot continue like this until the problem is resolved."

As a reminder, within the jurisdiction of the Nîmes Court of Appeal, 1,497 proceedings are underway, including 216 complaints in Avignon and 180 in Carpentras.

A system "already on its last legs"
The alarm bells about all these dysfunctions had already been rung in November 2021, during an appeal of unprecedented scale in the history of the profession: 3,000 judges and around one hundred court clerks signed an open letter published in Le Monde, denouncing a "dehumanized" justice system, forcing them to choose between "judging quickly but poorly" or "judging well but within unacceptable timeframes." The Avignon judges also recalled the suicide that prompted this letter: that of Charlotte, 29, who took her own life on August 23, after "only" two years of practice.

Returning to the Lyhanna case, "these series of isolated cases are then constructed into 'symbols' to justify reforms that aren't really reforms at all," a judge believes. "They increase sentences, statutes of limitations… It's additional work with the same resources, which will be just as difficult to manage and will further cripple the services. All of this is good for politics, for their PR, but it only further destroys a system already on its knees."

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Rail passengers travelling with West Midlands Railway are facing disruption this week due to planned strike action.
Members of the Transport Salaried Staffs Association (TSSA) are in an ongoing dispute over pay and have confirmed the industrial action will go ahead as planned, after the Tube strikes in London were called off.
The walkout will affect services in Birmingham and the Black Country, Wolverhampton, Warwickshire, Shropshire, Herefordshire, Worcestershire and Staffordshire on Thursday, Friday and Saturday.
The strikes, involving roster clerks, duty train crew managers, and control staff, are expected to severely impact services across the network.
TSSA general secretary Maryam Eslamdoust said: “As things stand, these strikes will go ahead as planned because the company is simply refusing to give our members parity with those in other unions. That is an intolerable situation, especially given the fact these are modest demands.”
Ms Eslamdoust added the union’s representatives had consulted their membership, who “remain determined to proceed with their legitimate action”, adding the union “only takes strike action as a last resort”. The union is seeking parity with other unions on rest day pay.
West Midlands Railway has since advised customers to “only travel if necessary” on Friday and Saturday. The operator confirmed services on both days will be very limited, running on a small number of routes and adhering to a reduced timetable.
Passengers should note there will be no trains operating after 7pm on Friday, and services will not commence until 7am on Saturday.
It comes after strikes planned for Tuesday and Thursday by London Underground drivers in the capital were called off at the last minute.
The Rail, Maritime and Transport (RMT) union previously announced that its members were due to walk out for 24 hours from midday on Tuesday, and again on Thursday from midday.
A union spokesperson said: “At the 11th hour, the employer has shifted its position, allowing us to further explore our members’ concerns around the imposition of new rosters, fatigue and safety issues.
“The dispute is not over and more strike action will follow if we fail to make sufficient progress.”
Strikes scheduled for 16 and 18 June have also been called off, but the union announced new 24-hour strike dates on 2 and 4 June if the dispute remains unresolved.
The union says its members oppose a new four-day working week arrangement on the underground, but the Aslef train drivers’ union, which represents a slight majority of Tube drivers, has backed Transport for London proposal.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Sanlúcar de Barrameda vivió este fin de semana una multitudinaria manifestación contra los vertidos de las minas de Aznalcóllar y Gerena al río Guadalquivir, una protesta que reunió a vecinos de distintos municipios ribereños y que contó con el respaldo del Ayuntamiento. La marcha, convocada por la Cofradía de Pescadores de Sanlúcar, la Plataforma Ciudadana 'Salvemos el Guadalquivir', Ecologistas en Acción y Greenpeace, partió de la Capilla del Carmen de Bajo de Guía y recorrió buena parte de la ciudad pese a la intensa lluvia, hasta finalizar en la céntrica calle San Juan.
La alcaldesa, Carmen Álvarez, estuvo presente junto a otros alcaldes de localidades vecinas y cargos públicos de la comarca para expresar su "profunda preocupación por las repercusiones medioambientales, económicas y sociales" que la reapertura de estas minas podría provocar en la pesca y en la biodiversidad del río. "Tenemos que salir a defender nuestro río, que está sufriendo vertidos de las minas de Aznalcóllar y Gerena, y dada la pretensión de la Junta de Andalucía de reabrir esta mina, será un desastre", afirmó la regidora, que se mostró satisfecha "ante la masiva respuesta que ha dado el pueblo de Sanlúcar".
"Bonanza es el segundo puerto pesquero más importante de Andalucía y no lo podemos permitir
Las cifras del proyecto que preocupan a los manifestantes son contundentes. Las explotaciones mineras contemplan la extracción, a lo largo de 17 años, de cerca de 76 millones de toneladas de mineral —principalmente cobre, plomo, zinc y plata—, lo que supondría además el vertido de 120.000 millones de litros de aguas residuales al río Guadalquivir. Un impacto que los convocantes consideran inaceptable para un río que es fuente de vida y de sustento económico para decenas de municipios ribereños.
La alcaldesa ha recordado que los vertidos de Aznalcóllar ya provocaron un grave desastre ecológico en 1998, afectando seriamente a la pesca. "Bonanza es el segundo puerto pesquero más importante de Andalucía y no podemos permitir que vuelva a ocurrir algo así", ha subrayado Álvarez, que ha garantizado que el Ayuntamiento seguirá realizando "todas las gestiones y acciones necesarias para evitar cualquier vertido en el Guadalquivir".
El Ayuntamiento denuncia a la Junta ante la Fiscalía de Medio Ambiente
La posición del Ayuntamiento de Sanlúcar va más allá de la protesta en la calle. El consistorio presentó alegaciones al proyecto de las minas de Aznalcóllar que fueron desestimadas por la Junta de Andalucía, y ahora prepara un escrito de denuncia ante la Fiscalía de Medio Ambiente para solicitar que se investiguen posibles responsabilidades penales en el proceso de autorización.
Las reivindicaciones de las entidades convocantes, respaldadas por el Ayuntamiento, incluyen la paralización de las autorizaciones y prospecciones mineras mediante una moratoria y la constitución de un grupo técnico-científico de expertos independientes que evalúe en profundidad los efectos de las minas en el medio ambiente, la salud y la seguridad alimentaria.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Sanlúcar de Barrameda witnessed a massive demonstration this weekend against the dumping of waste from the Aznalcóllar and Gerena mines into the Guadalquivir River. The protest brought together residents from various riverside towns and was supported by the City Council. The march, organized by the Sanlúcar Fishermen's Guild, the citizens' platform "Save the Guadalquivir," Ecologists in Action, and Greenpeace, began at the Chapel of Carmen in Bajo de Guía and proceeded through much of the city despite the heavy rain, ending on the central San Juan Street.

Mayor Carmen Álvarez was present, along with other mayors from neighboring towns and local officials, to express her "deep concern about the environmental, economic, and social repercussions" that the reopening of these mines could have on fishing and the river's biodiversity. "We must come out and defend our river, which is suffering from spills from the Aznalcóllar and Gerena mines, and given the Andalusian Regional Government's intention to reopen this mine, it will be a disaster," stated the mayor, who expressed her satisfaction "with the massive response from the people of Sanlúcar."

"We have to go out and defend our river, which is suffering from spills from the Aznalcóllar and Gerena mines, and given the Andalusian Regional Government's intention to reopen this mine, it will be a disaster," she added. "Bonanza is the second most important fishing port in Andalusia, and we cannot allow this."
The figures for the project that are worrying the protesters are compelling. The mining operations envision the extraction, over 17 years, of nearly 76 million tons of ore—mainly copper, lead, zinc, and silver—which would also entail the discharge of 120 billion liters of wastewater into the Guadalquivir River. An impact that the organizers consider unacceptable for a river that is a source of life and economic sustenance for dozens of riverside municipalities.
The mayor recalled that the Aznalcóllar spills already caused a serious ecological disaster in 1998, severely affecting fishing. "Bonanza is the second most important fishing port in Andalusia, and we cannot allow something like that to happen again," Álvarez stressed, guaranteeing that the City Council will continue to carry out "all the necessary procedures and actions to prevent any discharge into the Guadalquivir."

The City Council files complaint against the Regional Government with the Environmental Prosecutor's Office
The Sanlúcar City Council's stance goes beyond street protests. The council submitted objections to the Aznalcóllar mining project, which were rejected by the Regional Government of Andalusia, and is now preparing a formal complaint to the Environmental Prosecutor's Office requesting an investigation into potential criminal liability in the authorization process.

The demands of the organizing groups, supported by the City Council, include a moratorium on mining authorizations and exploration, and the establishment of an independent technical and scientific panel of experts to thoroughly assess the effects of the mines on the environment, health, and food safety.

WDR erhält Gegenwind für geplante COSMO-Einstellung: Diese Promis unterstützen den Protest

Köln - Der Protest gegen die geplante Einstellung des interkulturellen Radiosenders COSMO durch den Westdeutschen Rundfunk (WDR) wird lauter.
Wie das Bündnis #SaveCOSMOradio mitteilte, hat eine Online-Petition für den Erhalt der Welle die Marke von 100.000 Unterschriften überschritten.
Zu den Unterzeichnern gehören demnach Prominente wie Herbert Grönemeyer (70), Peter Fox (54), Jan Delay (49), Fatih Akin (52), İlker Çatak (42) und die Band AnnenMayKantereit.
Der WDR-Rundfunkrat hatte die Neuausrichtung der jungen Radiowellen mit knapper Mehrheit gebilligt. Laut Beschluss des Gremiums soll COSMO im April 2027 eingestellt und durch das Format "1LIVE Street" ersetzt werden.
Außerdem wird die Welle "1LIVE Diggi" in "1LIVE Lounge" umbenannt. Kritiker warnen vor einem Verlust an inhaltlicher Tiefe und kultureller Vielfalt.
Der WDR verteidigte sich in einer Pressemitteilung damit, dass auch das neue Format "1LIVE Street" – genauso wie COSMO aktuell – eine kulturell diverse, urban orientierte Zielgruppe ansprechen solle.
"Passend zum im WDR-Gesetz festgelegten Auftrag zur Stärkung des interkulturellen Zusammenlebens bleibt kulturelle Vielfalt zentrales Thema des Senders", heißt es in der Mitteilung.
Mouse on Mars geben Preis aus Protest zurück
Besonders deutlich gegen die Veränderungen positioniert sich der Deutsche Musikrat. Generalsekretärin Antje Valentin (61) betonte, dass migrantische Stimmen und Perspektiven ein Anrecht auf Präsenz im öffentlich-rechtlichen Rundfunk hätten. Sie forderte einen "ARD-Schulterschluss für COSMO 2.0".
Für viele Menschen mit Migrationsgeschichte sei der Sender bisher der einzige Kanal, der ihre Lebenswirklichkeit in den Mittelpunkt stelle. Der Informations- und Kulturauftrag für den öffentlich-rechtlichen Rundfunk gelte allen Menschen in Deutschland.
Der Widerstand wird von einer recht breiten Allianz getragen. Mehr als 500 Organisationen aus Kultur, Wissenschaft und Medien wandten sich bereits in einem offenen Brief an die ARD-Intendanzen. WDR Faces Backlash for Planned COSMO Shutdown: These Celebrities Support the Protest

By Marco Rauch
Cologne – The protest against the planned shutdown of the intercultural radio station COSMO by West German Broadcasting (WDR) is growing louder.

As the #SaveCOSMOradio alliance announced, an online petition to save the station has surpassed 100,000 signatures.

According to the announcement, celebrities such as Herbert Grönemeyer (70), Peter Fox (54), Jan Delay (49), Fatih Akin (52), İlker Çatak (42), and the band AnnenMayKantereit are among the signatories.

The WDR Broadcasting Council approved the restructuring of the youth radio stations by a narrow majority. According to the council's decision, COSMO is to be shut down in April 2027 and replaced by the "1LIVE Street" format.

Furthermore, the radio station "1LIVE Diggi" will be renamed "1LIVE Lounge." Critics warn of a loss of in-depth content and cultural diversity.

In a press release, WDR defended itself by stating that the new format "1LIVE Street"—just like COSMO aktuell—is intended to appeal to a culturally diverse, urban-oriented audience.

"In line with the WDR's mandate to strengthen intercultural coexistence, as stipulated in the WDR Act, cultural diversity remains a central theme for the broadcaster," the statement reads.

Mouse on Mars return award in protest.

The German Music Council has taken a particularly strong stance against the changes. Secretary General Antje Valentin (61) emphasized that migrant voices and perspectives have a right to be represented on public broadcasting. She called for "ARD to stand united for COSMO 2.0."

For many people with a migration background, the station has been the only channel that focuses on their lived experiences. The public broadcasting mandate for information and culture applies to all people in Germany.

The resistance is supported by a fairly broad alliance. More than 500 organizations from the cultural, scientific, and media sectors have already addressed an open letter to the ARD directors. They oppose the cancellation of programs in native languages ​​and the associated loss of an important platform for "global pop" in Germany.

As a symbolic act of protest, the electronic duo Mouse on Mars returned their "1LIVE Krone" award, which they won in 2000, to WDR. The musicians described the closure of COSMO as a "devastating step backward in times of reactionary thinking" and as a sign against cosmopolitanism.

Education
Unions call for a "fill Barcelona" on Sunday in a new day of education protests
Unions demand a new law in Catalonia because public education "has hit rock bottom"
The unions USTEC, CGT, Intersindical, CNT, and COS have called for a "fill Barcelona again" this Sunday with a new demonstration. The march will depart from the Jardinets de Gràcia at 11:30 a.m. and end in Plaça Catalunya.

In a press conference at Plaça del Rei, the unions warned this Friday that the next school year will begin with more strikes and protests. David Caño, spokesperson for USTEC, demanded a new education law in Catalonia and stated that public education "has hit rock bottom." Ingrid Chavarría, a delegate from the CGT, called on society to take to the streets to "address the education emergency." From the Intersindical union, Marc Martorell emphasized that this is a “fight for the future of the country.”

From USTEC, Caño stated that it is “crucial” to “fill” the streets of Barcelona again this Sunday: “Education has hit rock bottom,” he warned, noting that the sector receives only 3%, half of the funding mandated by law (6% of GDP).

The USTEC spokesperson outlined the two “plans” prioritized by the unions: educational reform and labor improvements. The unions are committed, on the one hand, to placing the debate and transformation “at the forefront,” starting with the Catalan Education Assembly on June 20th and the faculty meetings.

In this way, they want to establish the “priorities” for the next academic year, in which they hope Catalan will become a “crucial and cross-cutting” element. “We are lagging behind in both results and investment. We must once again become an example of educational improvement, not of school failure,” Caño argued.

Meanwhile, the unions reiterated their call for mobilization this Sunday, but also warned of further strikes and actions at the start of the next school year in September. Their main demand is a new reform of the Catalan education law: “The current one is insufficient and powerless; it doesn't solve our problems,” Caño reiterated.

“Save Public Education”
For her part, Chavarría, from the CGT union, stated that teachers' demands are no longer just about working conditions or salaries, but about “saving public education.” The CGT representative called on “the entire population and all sectors” to support Sunday's demonstration.

“We need everyone to defend the society we deserve, because education is the future of the country,” she emphasized. Chavarría also reaffirmed that the unions will ask parliamentary groups for more investment in education to reach 6% of GDP, as established by the 2017 law.

“If there is money to expand the airport and train lines, for large-scale tourism projects, and for the Mossos d'Esquadra (Catalan police), there must also be money for public education,” said the CGT representative, who warned that next year “the fight will continue.”

“Fight for the future of the country”
Regarding the Intersindical (a trade union confederation), Martorell insisted that Sunday's demonstration should serve to show that the struggle of education workers has “broad social support.” “It's not just about our working conditions, but it's a fight for the future of the country,” she concluded. From the CNT (National Confederation of Labor), Raúl Ortega championed the “dignity” and “consistency” of the education sector.

Sunday's demonstration will depart at 11:30 a.m. from the Jardinets de Gràcia and end in Plaça Catalunya, where union representatives will deliver speeches to conclude the march. The mobilization comes 10 days after teachers rejected, in a consultation last week, the preliminary agreement between the Education Department and the unions CCOO, UGT, USTEC, and Secondary School Teachers.

Teachers resumed their strike on Tuesday with a demonstration that began in Plaça Espanya and drew 6,500 people according to the Barcelona City Police (Guardia Urbana) and 45,000 according to the unions. Also called by USTEC, CGT, Intersindical, CNT, and COS, they gathered at the Venetian Towers to begin a march that ended at the Catalan Parliament (Parlament), where the unions delivered a letter to parliamentary groups demanding increased investment in education.

The demonstration coincided with the arrival of Pope Leo XIV in Barcelona.

Warnstreik im WDR am Montag: Was das für Programme bedeutet
WDR-Warnstreik. Wer am Montag auf verlässliche Radio- und TV-Programme setzt, muss beim WDR mit Ausfällen oder Änderungen rechnen.
Die Mediengewerkschaft VRFF hat für Montag, 8. Juni, ab 2.00 Uhr zu einem 24-stündigen Warnstreik im Westdeutschen Rundfunk (WDR) aufgerufen. Als Grund nennt die VRFF die anstehende nächste Verhandlungsrunde mit dem WDR am darauffolgenden Dienstag. Weitere Details zur Programmlage oder zu möglichen Ersatzangeboten wurden in der Mitteilung nicht genannt.

- Zeitraum: ab 2.00 Uhr, Dauer 24 Stunden

Nach Angaben der VRFF ist die vierte Verhandlungsrunde Ende April ohne Ergebnis geblieben. Warning strike at WDR on Monday: What this means for programming

WDR warning strike. Anyone relying on dependable radio and TV programming on Monday should expect cancellations or changes at WDR.

The media union VRFF has called for a 24-hour warning strike at West German Broadcasting (WDR) on Monday, June 8, starting at 2:00 a.m. According to the announcement, the strike also applies to employees of the Broadcasting Fee Service (ZBS). The announcement does not specify which programs or services will be affected.

The VRFF cites the upcoming round of negotiations with WDR on the following Tuesday as the reason for the strike. Further details regarding programming or possible alternative services were not provided in the announcement.


VRFF What's certain as of Monday, June 8:

- Timeframe: from 2:00 a.m., duration 24 hours
- Location/Operator: Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR)

- Affected areas according to VRFF: WDR and the ZBS (Central Broadcasting Fee Service)

- Unclear: Which specific programs, channels, or online services are affected
Are there any exceptions or unaffected regions?

The announcement does not mention any exceptions or specific locations. Therefore, it remains unclear whether and to what extent individual editorial departments, studios, or services will operate normally.

Background: WDR collective bargaining negotiations
According to VRFF, the fourth round of negotiations ended without an agreement at the end of April. The union criticizes WDR's current offer, particularly regarding salary developments in the coming years. Matthias Kopatz, VRFF's chief negotiator at WDR and deputy chairman of the VRFF Federal Collective Bargaining Commission, refers to the KEF's (Commission for the Determination of Financial Requirements of Broadcasting Organizations) recommendation: Personnel cost increases of "2.46%" are, in their view, appropriate.

The next round of negotiations is scheduled for Tuesday, June 9th; according to VRFF, WDR has invited participants for an "open-ended" meeting. A rally is also planned for the day of the strike, from 9:00 a.m. to approximately 2:00 p.m. at the Mouse Monument in front of the WDR's Vierscheibenhaus (Four-Slab Building). [red]

“Bu kara düzenle uzlaşanlara teslim olanlara, aparat olanlara nefes tüketmeyeceğim”

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Intro
CPM demands drought declaration for Kalaburagi, urges immediate relief measures amid water shortages and agricultural distress across Kalyana Karnataka
Kalaburagi
Workers of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) staged a protest outside the Kalaburagi Zilla Panchayat office, demanding that the state government immediately declare Kalaburagi district and the entire Kalyana Karnataka region as drought-hit areas.
The protesters gathered at Jagat Circle and later took out a procession towards the Zilla Panchayat office, raising slogans against both the state and Central governments over their response to the emerging drought situation.
Addressing the gathering, CPI(M) district secretary K. Neela said that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar had already acknowledged drought-like conditions prevailing in several parts of the state. He said inadequate rainfall has affected water sources and agricultural activities in Kalaburagi district.
“Due to insufficient rainfall, many water bodies are drying up and sowing activities have reduced significantly. The government should immediately declare Kalaburagi and the Kalyana Karnataka region as drought-affected areas and announce relief measures,” he demanded.
The CPI(M) leaders urged the government to invoke provisions of the Disaster Management Act and provide immediate assistance to affected communities. They demanded arrangements for drinking water supply, cattle fodder, and employment opportunities for people facing difficulties due to drought conditions.
The protesters also called for expansion of employment opportunities under rural and urban employment guarantee schemes. They demanded implementation of a food-for-work programme to support vulnerable families struggling due to loss of livelihood.
The party alleged that drought situations often lead to exploitation by middlemen, who increase prices of essential commodities by taking advantage of shortages. They urged the government to take steps to control price rise and protect consumers.
The CPI(M) criticised the expenditure on large public events and political programmes while people were facing serious hardships due to drought conditions.
Several party leaders and workers participated in the protest, including Meenakshi Bali, Sudham Dhanni, Prabhu Pyarabuddi, Shrimant Biradar, Shivasharanappa Mulegaon, Shanta Ghanti, Chandamma Gola, and Pandurang Mavinkar.
The protesters submitted their demands to the district administration and urged immediate government action to address the growing concerns of farmers and rural communities.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Γιώργος Μανουσάκης στο «Πάμε Αέρα»: «Τα νοσοκομεία λειτουργούν από το φιλότιμο του προσωπικού – Ο κόσμος αναγκάζεται να πληρώνει ιδιωτικά»
Σοβαρή προειδοποίηση για την κατάσταση που επικρατεί στα δημόσια νοσοκομεία της Κρήτης απηύθυνε μέσα από την εκπομπή «Πάμε Αέρα» με τον Θάνο Κορομπύλια ο πρόεδρος των εργαζομένων του Γενικού Νοσοκομείου Αγίου Νικολάου, Γιώργος Μανουσάκης με αφορμή τη σημερινή παγκρήτια κινητοποίηση υγειονομικών στο Ηράκλειο.
Μιλώντας καθ’ οδόν προς το Ηράκλειο, όπου εργαζόμενοι από όλα τα νοσοκομεία της Κρήτης συμμετέχουν σε συγκέντρωση διαμαρτυρίας, ο κ. Μανουσάκης περιέγραψε μια ιδιαίτερα πιεστική εικόνα για το δημόσιο σύστημα υγείας στο νησί, τονίζοντας ότι «το ΕΣΥ πραγματικά είναι έτοιμο να γονατίσει».
Η κινητοποίηση ξεκίνησε από το Βενιζέλειο Νοσοκομείο, με πορεία μέσω της λεωφόρου Κνωσού και κατάληξη στην Πλατεία Ελευθερίας, έξω από το κτίριο της Περιφέρειας Κρήτης.
«Αν είχαν λυθεί τα προβλήματα, δεν θα ήμασταν κάθε λίγο και λιγάκι στους δρόμους», ανέφερε χαρακτηριστικά ο πρόεδρος των εργαζομένων του ΓΝΑΝ, σημειώνοντας πως οι ελλείψεις προσωπικού, οι δύσκολες συνθήκες εργασίας και η συνεχής υποστελέχωση παραμένουν άλυτα ζητήματα εδώ και χρόνια.
«Η κυβέρνηση επιχειρεί επικοινωνιακή διαχείριση»
Ο κ. Μανουσάκης άσκησε σκληρή κριτική στην κυβερνητική πολιτική για την υγεία, υποστηρίζοντας ότι επιχειρείται μια «πλασματική εικόνα» για την πραγματική κατάσταση των νοσοκομείων.
«Ο υπουργός Υγείας παρουσιάζει ένα ΕΣΥ πολύ διαφορετικό από αυτό που βιώνουμε καθημερινά στην Κρήτη. Στην πραγματικότητα έχουμε ένα από τα πιο επιβαρυμένα συστήματα υγείας της χώρας», είπε.
Παράλληλα, έκανε λόγο για συνεχή ενίσχυση του ιδιωτικού τομέα υγείας, την ώρα που – όπως υποστήριξε – οι δημόσιες δομές αποδυναμώνονται.
«Ο κόσμος δεν μπορεί να βρει ραντεβού, δεν μπορεί να εξυπηρετηθεί επειδή δεν υπάρχουν γιατροί, αναισθησιολόγοι και βασικές ειδικότητες. Αναγκάζεται είτε να περιμένει είτε να πληρώνει από την τσέπη του σε ιδιωτικά κέντρα», ανέφερε.
«Δεν παίρνουμε άδειες και ρεπό»
Ιδιαίτερη αναφορά έκανε και στις συνθήκες εργασίας των υγειονομικών, τονίζοντας ότι οι εργαζόμενοι στα νοσοκομεία λειτουργούν στα όρια της εξουθένωσης.
«Δεν παίρνουμε τις άδειές μας, δεν παίρνουμε τα ρεπό μας. Οι αναλογίες προσωπικού με ασθενείς είναι τραγικές και οι βάρδιες βγαίνουν με τεράστια δυσκολία. Τα νοσοκομεία λειτουργούν χάρη στο φιλότιμο του προσωπικού», υπογράμμισε.
Αλυσιδωτές επιπτώσεις στα νοσοκομεία της Κρήτης
Ο πρόεδρος των εργαζομένων του ΓΝΑΝ αναφέρθηκε και στην κατάσταση που επικρατεί στα υπόλοιπα νοσοκομεία του νομού Λασιθίου και της Κρήτης, σημειώνοντας ότι «η λειτουργία των νοσοκομείων είναι συγκοινωνούντα δοχεία».
Όπως είπε, η παθολογική κλινική του Νοσοκομείου Σητείας ουσιαστικά δεν λειτουργεί εδώ και περίπου ενάμιση χρόνο, με αποτέλεσμα τα περισσότερα περιστατικά να μεταφέρονται στον Άγιο Νικόλαο.
«Η πληρότητα της παθολογικής κλινικής του Νοσοκομείου Αγίου Νικολάου φτάνει συνεχώς στο 120% και 130%, με ασθενείς να νοσηλεύονται ακόμη και σε άλλες κλινικές», ανέφερε.
Παράλληλα, εξήγησε ότι όταν στο Νοσοκομείο Αγίου Νικολάου δεν υπάρχουν βασικές ειδικότητες, όπως ακτινολόγοι ή αναισθησιολόγοι, πολλά περιστατικά διακομίζονται στα νοσοκομεία του Ηρακλείου, επιβαρύνοντας περαιτέρω το Βενιζέλειο και το ΠΑΓΝΗ.
«Η κοινωνία είναι δίπλα μας»
Ο Γιώργος Μανουσάκηςστάθηκε ιδιαίτερα στη στήριξη που λαμβάνουν οι κινητοποιήσεις από την τοπική κοινωνία και φορείς της Κρήτης.
«Η κοινωνία είναι δίπλα μας. Το βλέπουμε από τα ψηφίσματα συμπαράστασης αλλά και από την καθημερινή επαφή με τους πολίτες. Η υγεία είναι ζήτημα που απασχολεί όλους», σημείωσε.
Κλείνοντας, ξεκαθάρισε ότι οι εργαζόμενοι θα συνεχίσουν τις κινητοποιήσεις όσο παραμένουν άλυτα τα προβλήματα στο δημόσιο σύστημα υγείας.
«Όσο υπάρχουν αυτά τα προβλήματα, θα συνεχίσουμε να είμαστε στον δρόμο και να πιέζουμε», τόνισε.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Georgos Manousakis on “Pame Aera”: “Hospitals operate on the dedication of the staff – People are forced to pay privately”
A serious warning about the situation prevailing in public hospitals in Crete was issued through the show “Pame Aera” with Thanos Korombilias by the president of the workers of the General Hospital of Agios Nikolaos, Giorgos Manousakis, on the occasion of today’s pan-Cretan mobilization of healthcare workers in Heraklion.
Speaking on the way to Heraklion, where workers from all hospitals in Crete are participating in a protest rally, Mr. Manousakis described a particularly depressing picture of the public health system on the island, emphasizing that “the National Health System is really ready to kneel.”
The mobilization started from Venizelio Hospital, with a march through Knossos Avenue and ending at Eleftherias Square, outside the building of the Region of Crete.
“If the problems had been solved, we would not be on the streets every now and then,” the president of the GNAN workers said characteristically, noting that staff shortages, difficult working conditions and constant understaffing have remained unresolved issues for years.
“The government is attempting communication management”
Mr. Manousakis harshly criticized the government’s health policy, claiming that an attempt is being made to present a “fictitious picture” of the real situation of hospitals.
“The Minister of Health presents a very different NHS from what we experience daily in Crete. In reality, we have one of the most burdened health systems in the country,” he said.
At the same time, he spoke of the continuous strengthening of the private health sector, while – as he argued – public structures are being weakened.
“People cannot find an appointment, they cannot be served because there are no doctors, anesthesiologists and basic specialties. They are forced to either wait or pay out of pocket in private centers,” he said.
“We do not take leave or days off”
He also made special reference to the working conditions of healthcare workers, emphasizing that hospital workers operate on the verge of exhaustion.
“We do not take our leave, we do not take our days off. The staff-patient ratios are tragic and shifts are coming out with enormous difficulty. Hospitals operate thanks to the dedication of the staff,” he emphasized.
Chain effects on hospitals in Crete
The president of the GNAN workers also referred to the situation prevailing in the other hospitals in the prefecture of Lasithi and Crete, noting that "the operation of hospitals is like communicating vessels".
As he said, the pathology clinic of Sitia Hospital has essentially not been operating for about a year and a half, as a result of which most cases are transferred to Agios Nikolaos.
"The occupancy rate of the pathology clinic of Agios Nikolaos Hospital constantly reaches 120% and 130%, with patients even being hospitalized in other clinics", he said.
At the same time, he explained that when Agios Nikolaos Hospital does not have basic specialties, such as radiologists or anesthesiologists, many cases are transferred to the hospitals of Heraklion, further burdening Venizelio and PAGNI.
“Society is with us”
Georgos Manousakis focused particularly on the support that the protests receive from the local community and institutions of Crete.
“Society is with us. We see this from the resolutions of support but also from the daily contact with citizens. Health is an issue that concerns everyone,” he noted.
In closing, he clarified that the workers will continue the protests as long as the problems in the public health system remain unresolved.
“As long as these problems exist, we will continue to be on the streets and press,” he stressed.

Lundi, avant une conférence sur la citoyenneté et la guerre à l’UBO, un rassemblement est prévu par trois syndicats étudiants, qui craignent « une propagande pour enrôler la jeunesse ».
La Ferc Sup CGT de l’UBO, Sud Éducation et l‘Union Pirate « appellent à un rassemblement ce lundi 18 mai 2026 à 18 h devant l’amphithéâtre Florence-Arthaud (20 avenue Le Gorgeu, arrêt tram Université), contre la propagande guerrière ». « Si l’hypothèse de la guerre ne doit jamais être considérée avec légèreté, nous nous devons d’agir là où nous vivons contre toute montée à la guerre, et donc contre toutes formes de propagande militariste. Ce n’est pas un hasard si une telle réunion se tient à l’université », estiment les syndicats étudiants. « L’objectif est de mener une propagande pour enrôler la jeunesse dans la défense nationale et l’armée ».

TRANSLATED_TEXT:
On Monday, before a conference on citizenship and war at the University of Western Brittany (UBO), a rally is planned by three student unions, who fear "propaganda to recruit young people." The UBO's Ferc Sup CGT, Sud Éducation, and the Pirate Union "are calling for a rally this Monday, May 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. in front of the Florence-Arthaud amphitheater (20 avenue Le Gorgeu, Université tram stop), against war propaganda." At 6:30 p.m., UBO will host a discussion entitled "The People of Finistère Facing War: Bringing Citizens Closer to Defense Issues in the Era of New Conflicts," moderated by Mélanie Thomin (Socialist Party MP for the sixth constituency of Châteaulin-Carhaix) and Nicolas Roche (Secretary General for Defense and National Security).

“While the possibility of war should never be taken lightly, we have a duty to act where we live against any escalation to war, and therefore against all forms of militaristic propaganda. It is no coincidence that such a meeting is being held at the university,” the student unions believe. “The objective is to conduct propaganda to enlist young people in national defense and the army.”

“The significant increase in the military budget brings a financial windfall to arms companies. Consequently, laboratories are being approached by these companies to collaborate… and develop research projects for these military companies. UBO, for example, has contracts with Thales, a company accused by various NGOs of complicity in war crimes. UBO recently established a partnership with the navy. MESSAGE_TEXT:
C’est la surprise de ce mouvement social national prévu mercredi 10 juin : malgré l’appel lancé par plusieurs organisations syndicales, la grève ne devrait, selon toute vraisemblance, pas être massivement suivie sur le réseau ferroviaire régional. D’après les prévisions communiquées par SNCF Voyageurs, près de deux circulations ferroviaires sur trois seront assurées en Bourgogne-Franche-Comté.
Dans le détail, la situation restera toutefois contrastée selon les territoires. En Bourgogne, le trafic s’annonce relativement préservé, avec près de quatre trains sur cinq en circulation. En Franche-Comté, les perturbations seront plus sensibles, même si plus d’un train sur deux devrait circuler. SNCF Voyageurs indique avoir mis en place un plan de transport adapté afin d’assurer le plus grand nombre possible de trajets sur le réseau des trains Mobigo.
Certaines lignes régionales ne devraient même pas être impactées par le mouvement social. C’est le cas des trains Mobigo entre Dijon et Nevers, entre Nevers et Cosne, ainsi que sur l’axe Chalon-sur-Saône – Montchanin – Paray-le-Monial. Sur les lignes les plus touchées, des substitutions routières seront mises en place.
Du côté des grandes lignes, des perturbations sont également attendues, mais là encore le trafic restera partiellement assuré. En moyenne, deux TGV sur trois devraient circuler pour les TGV INOUI et TGV Lyria. Les voyageurs concernés par une annulation seront recontactés et pourront bénéficier d’un remboursement ou d’un report sur un autre train. SNCF Voyageurs précise que, grâce aux places encore disponibles, l’ensemble des clients devrait pouvoir voyager dans la journée. Les billets prévus le 10 juin pourront par ailleurs être annulés ou échangés sans frais.
Les Intercités seront davantage touchés, notamment sur les lignes de jour et de nuit, dont l’axe Paris – Nevers – Clermont-Ferrand. Environ un train sur deux devrait circuler. Là aussi, les voyageurs concernés par une annulation seront informés et pourront demander un remboursement ou un échange sans frais.
SNCF Voyageurs invite les usagers à vérifier systématiquement les horaires de leur train avant tout déplacement. Les informations seront disponibles sur les canaux habituels : application Mobigo, SNCF Connect, site TER Bourgogne-Franche-Comté et affichage en gare. Les horaires actualisés seront publiés au plus tard la veille à partir de 17 heures.
Malgré le contexte social national, cette journée de grève pourrait donc se traduire, en Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, par des perturbations réelles mais contenues, loin d’un blocage généralisé du trafic ferroviaire.

The surprise of this national strike planned for Wednesday, June 10th, is that despite the call from several unions, it is not expected to be widely observed on the regional rail network. According to forecasts from SNCF Voyageurs, nearly two out of three trains will be running in the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté region. However, the situation will vary depending on the area. In Burgundy, service is expected to be relatively unaffected, with nearly four out of five trains running. In Franche-Comté, disruptions will be more significant, although more than half of the trains are expected to operate. SNCF Voyageurs indicates that it has implemented an adapted transport plan to ensure as many journeys as possible on the Mobigo train network. Some regional lines are not even expected to be impacted by the strike. This is the case for Mobigo trains between Dijon and Nevers, between Nevers and Cosne, as well as on the Chalon-sur-Saône – Montchanin – Paray-le-Monial line. On the most affected lines, bus replacements will be provided. Disruptions are also expected on long-distance lines, but service will again be partially maintained. On average, two out of three TGVs are expected to run for TGV INOUI and TGV Lyria trains. Passengers affected by a cancellation will be contacted and will be able to receive a refund or transfer to another train. SNCF Voyageurs specifies that, thanks to the seats still available, all customers should be able to travel on the same day. Tickets booked for June 10 can also be canceled or exchanged free of charge. Intercités trains will be more affected, particularly on day and night lines, including the Paris – Nevers – Clermont-Ferrand line. Approximately one out of two trains is expected to run. Here too, passengers affected by a cancellation will be informed and can request a refund or exchange free of charge. SNCF Voyageurs encourages users to always check their train schedules before traveling. Information will be available through the usual channels: the Mobigo app, SNCF Connect, the TER Bourgogne-Franche-Comté website, and station displays. Updated schedules will be published no later than 5:00 PM the day before departure.

Despite the national social climate, this strike day could therefore result in some real but limited disruptions in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, far from a widespread blockage of rail traffic.

Επ΄ αόριστον στη Ριζοελιά οι κτηνοτρόφοι – Καταγγέλλουν στοχοποίησή τους με εξώδικα
ΛΕΥΚΩΣΙΑ. Επ΄ αόριστον θα παραμείνουν στον κυκλικό κόμβο Ριζοελιάς οι κτηνοτρόφοι, που κατέρχονται σε νέα διαμαρτυρία την Παρασκευή στις 11 το πρωί, ενώ η Αστυνομία εκδίδει εξώδικα για παράνομη στάθμευση κατά τη διαμαρτυρία της 23ης Απριλίου, δηλώνει η εκπρόσωπος του συνδέσμου «Η Φωνή των Κτηνοτρόφων», Στέλλα Πέτρου, λέγοντας ότι πρόκειται για στοχοποίηση.
Έβγαλαν εξώδικα στον κόσμο για παράνομη στάθμευση στη διαμαρτυρία της 23ης Απριλίου, αλλά η Αστυνομία τους είχε υποδείξει να σταθμεύσουν εκεί, δήλωσε, κάνοντας λόγο για «σκοπιμότητα και στοχοποίηση», ενώ ανέφερε πως η ίδια κλήθηκε για κατάθεση για το κλείσιμο των δρόμων.
«Θέλω να μας απαντήσει κάποιος υπεύθυνος από την Αστυνομία σε ποια άλλη διαμαρτυρία στην Κύπρο έγινε αυτό το πράγμα, να βγάζουν εξώδικα. Αν είναι ποτέ δυνατόν», είπε.
Σε σχέση με την νέα προγραμματισμένη συγκέντρωση διαμαρτυρίας στον κυκλικό κόμβο Ριζοελιάς, η κ. Πέτρου ανέφερε πως αναμένουν την άδεια από την Αστυνομία. Όπως σημείωσε, «η διαμαρτυρία θα είναι ειρηνική».
«Θα κλείσουμε τη μια λωρίδα και θα διανυκτερεύσουμε εκεί. Θα παραμείνουμε στο σημείο επ’ αόριστον», πρόσθεσε.
Σχετικά με την προσέλευση που αναμένουν στη διαμαρτυρία, η κ. Πέτρου εκτίμησε ότι θα είναι ανάλογη με αυτήν της προηγούμενης διαμαρτυρίας, ίσως και λίγο μεγαλύτερη.
Η Στέλλα Πέτρου ανέφερε επίσης ότι κλήθηκε από την Αστυνομία για κατάθεση για το κλείσιμο των δρόμων στη διαμαρτυρία που πραγματοποιήθηκε στις 23 Απριλίου.
Εξάλλου, είπε ότι ο σύνδεσμος «Η Φωνή των Κτηνοτρόφων» δεν έλαβε κάποια πρόσκληση ή ενημέρωση για τη συνάντηση που προγραμματίστηκε για το πρωί της Πέμπτης στο Υπουργείο Γεωργίας, για τον αφθώδη πυρετό και τις αποζημιώσεις.
«Δεν μας υπολογίζουν. Όσο δεν μας υπολογίζουν, τόσο πιο πολύ πορωνόμαστε. Δεν έχουμε λάβει απάντηση από κανέναν, ούτε από την Υπουργό, ούτε από τον κ. Γρηγορίου», σημείωσε, ενώ ανέφερε ότι «Η Φωνή των Κτηνοτρόφων» δεν έχει καμία επαφή με τον Παναγροτικό και την ΕΚΑ.
«Έχουμε θυμώσει γιατί οι πιο πολλοί δεν είναι κτηνοτρόφοι και κάθονται στο τραπέζι και συζητούν για τους κτηνοτρόφους», είπε.
«Θέλουμε ο κόσμος να είναι δίπλα μας και να μας σταθεί γιατί παλεύουμε για όλους», σημείωσε καταληκτικά η κ. Πέτρου.

Livestock farmers to remain indefinitely in Rizoelia – They denounce their targeting with citations
NICOSIA. Livestock farmers, who are staging a new protest on Friday at 11 am, will remain indefinitely at the Rizoelia roundabout, while the Police are issuing citations for illegal parking during the protest on April 23, says Stella Petrou, the spokesperson for the association “The Voice of Livestock Farmers”, saying that this is targeting.
They issued citations to people for illegal parking at the April 23 protest, but the Police had instructed them to park there, she said, citing “purposefulness and targeting,” while mentioning that she herself was summoned to testify about the road closures.

Stella Petrou also reported that she was summoned by the Police to testify about the road closures during the protest that took place on April 23.
Furthermore, she said that the association “The Voice of Livestock Breeders” did not receive any invitation or information about the meeting scheduled for Thursday morning at the Ministry of Agriculture, about foot-and-mouth disease and compensation.
“They do not count on us. The more they do not count on us, the more we suffer. We have not received a response from anyone, neither from the Minister nor from Mr. Grigoriou,” she noted, while stating that “The Voice of Livestock Breeders” has no contact with Panagrotikos and the EKA.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Demonstration planned for June 22 at 16:45 in front of Mulhouse Alsace Agglomeration Council in Petit-Landau, France
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Crédit photo : Jorge Franganillo / Pixabay Des organisations citoyennes réunies derrière le collectif « IA pas moyen ! » (dont Alsace Nature, Eau en danger, la Confédération paysanne d’Alsace, Extinction Rebellion Alsace, Les Soulèvements de la Terre, Stop Fessenheim, Attac 68, Le chaudron des alternatives, le MAN. ..), appellent à se rassembler contre l’implantation d’un data center Microsoft à Petit-Landau, lors du conseil de Mulhouse Alsace agglomération du 22 juin, à partir de 16h45.
Derrière la manifestation, c’est un débat local et national essentiel sur l’énergie, la démocratie environnementale et la souveraineté numérique qui se joue.
Un projet industriel hors norme Annoncé en mai 2024 lors du sommet « Choose France », le projet (à propos duquel on impute au député Olivier Becht un rôle déterminant) représente un investissement supérieur à 2 milliards d’euros , avec une mise en service envisagée à l’horizon 2027 ( alterpresse68.info ).
Le site prévu s’étend sur environ 36 hectares de terres agricoles , dont un tiers cultivées en bio, le long du Rhin , à cheval sur Petit-Landau et Hombourg ( channelnews.fr ).
Selon la Mission régionale d’autorité environnementale (MRAe), la consommation électrique du futur centre pourrait représenter 80 % de celle de l’ensemble des ménages du Haut-Rhin . Le média ChannelNews évoque une fourchette de 1 500 à 1 750 GWh par an , principalement pour alimenter des serveurs dédiés à l’IA générative.
Pour les opposants, ces chiffres suffisent à qualifier le projet « d’ogre énergétique » , après un avis sévère de la MRAe rendu en mars 2026.
Une enquête publique sous haute surveillance L’enquête publique unique est ouverte du 1er juin au 3 juillet 2026 . Elle porte à la fois sur l’autorisation environnementale, les permis de construire et la déclaration de projet emportant mise en compatibilité du PLU de Petit-Landau.
Or, la MRAe Grand Est a jugé le dossier incomplet et a recommandé au préfet de surseoir à la poursuite de l’instruction , estimant que l’étude des dangers et l’évaluation des risques sanitaires devaient être approfondies .
En cause notamment : la présence prévue de 111 groupes électrogènes de secours , susceptibles d’émettre des oxydes d’azote (NOx) en cas de fonctionnement dégradé.
Plus préoccupant encore pour les collectifs citoyens : une évolution réglementaire européenne, révélée en avril 2026, classe comme « secret des affaires » une grande partie des données environnementales site par site.
Cette disposition, obtenue après des interventions de Microsoft et du lobby Digital Europe, limite l’accès public aux indicateurs détaillés. Des juristes interrogés estiment qu’une telle opacité pourrait entrer en tension avec la convention d’Aarhus sur l’accès à l’information environnementale.
Terres agricoles amputées et artificialisation substantielle Dans son analyse du bilan de concertation publié par m2A, nous avons souligné le déséquilibre entre l’argumentaire promotionnel de Microsoft et la restitution des préoccupations citoyennes .
La consommation de 35 à 36 hectares de terres nourricières y est identifiée comme un point noir majeur. La MRAe évoque une perte importante de fonctionnalités écosystémiques et s’interroge sur le respect effectif de la séquence « Éviter, Réduire, Compenser » .
Pour un territoire engagé dans des objectifs de sobriété foncière et de transition écologique, le signal envoyé interroge : comment concilier artificialisation massive, double ligne haute tension 225 kV et discours sur la neutralité carbone ?
Emplois promis, bénéfices discutés Microsoft met en avant la création de 200 emplois en France . Les collectifs, eux, relativisent : combien d’emplois directs réellement localisés ? Quelle qualification ? Quel effet net sur l’emploi local face à l’automatisation et à l’IA générative ?
Au-delà de la promesse industrielle, la question posée aux élus de m2A est celle de l’équilibre coût-bénéfice : pression sur le réseau électrique régional, mobilisation foncière irréversible, dépendance accrue à un acteur extra-européen, contre retombées fiscales et emplois encore incertains.
Des citoyens exigent débat et transparence Le 22 juin à 16h45, devant le Parc Expo de Mulhouse, les opposants entendent rappeler aux conseillers communautaires que leur décision ne relève pas d’une simple formalité administrative. La procédure de mise en compatibilité du PLU de Petit-Landau, portée par m2A, constitue un levier déterminant.
À l’heure où l’enquête publique est en cours (jusqu’au 3 juillet 2026), la mobilisation vise à peser sur un calendrier institutionnel jugé trop favorable au porteur de projet.
Le débat dépasse largement les 800 habitants de Petit-Landau. Et il pose une question de fond : l’Alsace veut-elle devenir un hub énergétique pour l’IA des géants du numérique, au prix d’une consommation électrique équivalente à celle de la quasi-totalité des ménages d’un département ?
Quoi qu’il en soit, lundi, devant le Parc Expo, les manifestants comptent affirmer que la modernité ne saurait s’imposer sans transparence, exercice effectif de la démocratie locale.

(including Alsace Nature, Eau en danger, the Confédération paysanne d’Alsace, Extinction Rebellion Alsace, Les Soulèvements de la Terre, Stop Fessenheim, Attac 68, Le chaudron des alternatives, the MAN, etc.) are calling for a demonstration against the construction of a Microsoft data center in Petit-Landau, during the Mulhouse Alsace Agglomeration council meeting on June 22, starting at 4:45 p.m.

Behind the demonstration lies a crucial local and national debate on energy, environmental democracy, and digital sovereignty.

An extraordinary industrial project. Announced in May 2024 at the "Choose France" summit, the project (for which MP Olivier Becht is credited with playing a key role) represents an investment exceeding €2 billion, with commissioning planned for 2027 (alterpresse68.info).
The planned site covers approximately 36 hectares of farmland, a third of which is organically farmed, along the Rhine River, straddling the towns of Petit-Landau and Hombourg (channelnews.fr).
According to the Regional Environmental Authority (MRAe), the future center's electricity consumption could represent 80% of that of all households in the Haut-Rhin department. ChannelNews reports a range of 1,500 to 1,750 GWh per year, primarily to power servers dedicated to generative AI.

For opponents, these figures are enough to label the project an "energy monster," following a scathing opinion issued by the Regional Environmental Authority (MRAe) in March 2026.

A closely monitored public inquiry: The single public inquiry is open from June 1st to July 3rd, 2026. It covers the environmental authorization, building permits, and the project declaration, which entails amending the Local Urban Development Plan (PLU) of Petit-Landau.

However, the MRAe Grand Est deemed the file incomplete and recommended that the prefect suspend further investigation, believing that the hazard study and health risk assessment needed to be more thorough. At issue, in particular, is the planned presence of 111 emergency generators, which could emit nitrogen oxides (NOx) in the event of malfunction.

Even more concerning for citizen groups: a European regulatory change, revealed in April 2026, classifies a large portion of site-by-site environmental data as "trade secrets."

This provision, obtained after interventions by Microsoft and the Digital Europe lobby, limits public access to detailed indicators. Legal experts consulted believe that such opacity could conflict with the Aarhus Convention on access to environmental information.

The consumption of 35 to 36 hectares of arable land is identified as a major problem. The Regional Environmental Authority (MRAe) mentions a significant loss of ecosystem functions and questions the actual implementation of the "Avoid, Reduce, Compensate" sequence.

The procedure for bringing the Petit-Landau Local Urban Development Plan (PLU), led by m2A, into compliance is a crucial lever.
With the public inquiry currently underway (until July 3, 2026), the mobilization aims to influence an institutional timeline deemed too favorable to the project proponent.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Indian Prime Minister Modi to address public meeting and "Chalo Parade Ground" rally on May 10 at Parade Ground in Secunderabad, Telangana
MESSAGE_TEXT:
From welding work on giant metal barricades to police teams checking rooftops overlooking the venue, preparations continued late into Thursday (May 7, 2026) night at the sprawling Parade Ground in Secunderabad ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public meeting and ‘Chalo Parade Ground’ rally scheduled for Sunday (May 10, 2026).
With an estimated crowd of nearly 70,000 people expected to converge in the heart of Hyderabad and around 2,000 buses set to ferry supporters from across Telangana, the city police have mounted an extensive security and traffic operation around the venue, the Begumpet airport route and adjoining stretches.
Workers could be seen racing against time at the Parade Ground through the day, setting up tents, fixing lighting systems and preparing galleries for attendees, while police officers supervised the layout of entry points, parking zones and surveillance arrangements. Senior officials said nearly 80 to 90% of the preparations, including the stage, seating for 80,000 people and galleries for people to stand, would be completed by Friday night.
“Special teams including anti-sabotage teams, sniper teams, bomb disposal squads and dog squads will be deployed for the bandobast. Around 2,000 police personnel across all ranks will be involved in the security arrangements,” said Begumpet ACP P. Gopala Krishna Murthy.
Modi to launch ₹7,823-crore projects in Telangana on May 10, address public meeting at Parade Grounds: BJP The police have established a temporary command and control centre inside the Parade Ground, with surveillance being carried out through nearly 150 CCTV cameras covering the venue, gates, surrounding roads and nearby Metro stations.
Police officials said portions of Hyderabad Metro stations and other elevated structures overlooking the Parade Ground may be screened off or covered to prevent people from viewing the event through binoculars or other devices from above.
Security deployment has intensified even before the Prime Minister’s arrival, with patrolling teams, check-posts and pickets stationed across key junctions in Secunderabad and Begumpet.
The Prime Minister is expected to arrive at Begumpet airport on Sunday morning before proceeding to programmes in Hitec City. He is later scheduled to return to Begumpet airport in the evening and leave for the Parade Ground around 5.40 p.m., reaching the venue by 6 p.m.
To manage the expected influx , the traffic police have identified 10 major parking locations, including Bison Polo Grounds and Wesley Grounds, where buses carrying supporters from various districts will be stationed.
“We are expecting around 60,000 to 70,000 people at the venue and nearly 2,000 buses. Four special trains have also been arranged, so a large number of people will be moving from Secunderabad railway station towards the Parade Ground,” said Malkajgiri DCP (Traffic-I) Rahul Reddy.
QR codes will be installed along approach routes so that visitors arriving from different districts can quickly identify their designated parking areas. Separate alighting points have also been planned close to the venue to minimise walking distances for attendees in the summer heat.
“Because of the heat, we have specifically planned drop points so people do not have to walk long distances,” the DCP said.
Nearly 500 traffic personnel will be deployed exclusively for traffic regulation and crowd movement around the event. While temporary diversions are expected during the Prime Minister’s movement between Begumpet airport and the Parade Ground, police officials maintained that major arterial roads would remain functional.
The police are also experimenting with a dedicated emergency vehicle corridor along parts of the route. A test run will be carried out on Thursday afternoon for the Telangana Chief Minister’s convoy. Barricades, ropes and traffic cones will be used to carve out a segregated lane from Begumpet Airport till the Lifestyle store in Begumpet to ensure uninterrupted movement for emergency services and VIP convoys while allowing regular traffic to continue moving.
“If this works successfully, other commissionerates may also replicate the model during future large-scale events,” the officer said.
Police officials also indicated that Metro Rail timings and operations near the venue could be adjusted on Sunday evening depending on crowd movement and security requirements. The police are also exploring permission to deploy drones for controlled aerial surveillance, even though airspace restrictions are typically enforced during such high-security events.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Verdi ruft Telekom-Beschäftigte zu Streik auf
Die Gewerkschaft Verdi hat die rund 500 Telekom-Beschäftigten am Standort Saarbrücken für heute zum Warnstreik aufgerufen. Beim Kundenservice sei mit erheblichen Beeinträchtigungen zu rechnen. Hintergrund sind die stockenden Tarifverhandlungen mit dem Telekommunikationskonzern.
An insgesamt acht Standorten in Rheinland-Pfalz und im Saarland sind die Beschäftigten der Telekom heute zum Streik aufgerufen.
Nach Verdi-Angaben betrifft der Ausstand die Standorte der Telekom in Saarbrücken, Kaiserslautern, Trier, Neustadt an der Weinstraße, Ludwigshafen sowie Mainz, Koblenz und Bad Kreuznach.
Kundendienst bei Telekom von Streik betroffen
Alles was am Telekom-Standort in Saarbrücken mit Kundendienst zu tun habe, wird wegen des Streiks nicht stattfinden, sagte Verdi-Gewerkschaftssekretär Andreas Wiese dem SR. Wiese geht davon aus, dass ein Fünftel der rund 500 Beschäftigten am Warnstreik in der Großwaldhalle in Eiweiler teilnehmen wird.
Der Standort Saarbrücken ist unter anderem zuständig für den Telefon-Service, den Außendienst bei Störungen sowie den Glasfaserausbau und -service.
Verdi fordert 6,6 Prozent mehr Entgelt für Telekombeschäftigte
Mit dem Streik will Verdi nach eigenen Angaben den Druck auf die Arbeitgeber vor der dritten Tarifverhandlungsrunde in zwei Wochen erhöhen. Bisher hatte die Telekom kein Angebot vorgelegt.
Verdi verlangt unter anderem 6,6 Prozent mehr Lohn bei einer Laufzeit des Tarifvertrags von einem Jahr. Eine weitere Forderung: Gewerkschaftsmitglieder sollen einen jährlichen Bonus in Höhe von 660 Euro erhalten.
Die dritte Tarifverhandlungsrunde ist für den 11. und 12. Mai angesetzt
Über dieses Thema haben auch die SR info-Nachrichten im Radio am 30.04.2026 berichtet.

Verdi calls on Telekom employees to strike
The Verdi union has called on the approximately 500 Telekom employees at the Saarbrücken location to stage a warning strike today. Significant disruptions to customer service are expected. The strike stems from stalled wage negotiations with the telecommunications company.

Telekom employees at a total of eight locations in Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland are called to strike today.

According to Verdi, the strike affects Telekom locations in Saarbrücken, Kaiserslautern, Trier, Neustadt an der Weinstraße, Ludwigshafen, as well as Mainz, Koblenz, and Bad Kreuznach.

Telekom customer service affected by strike
"All customer service activities at the Telekom location in Saarbrücken will be suspended due to the strike," Verdi union secretary Andreas Wiese told SR. Wiese expects that one-fifth of the approximately 500 employees will participate in the warning strike at the Großwaldhalle in Eiweiler.

The Saarbrücken location is responsible for, among other things, telephone service, field service for malfunctions, and fiber optic expansion and maintenance.

Verdi demands a 6.6 percent pay increase for Telekom employees.

With the strike, Verdi aims to increase pressure on employers ahead of the third round of collective bargaining negotiations in two weeks. Telekom has not yet submitted an offer.

Verdi is demanding, among other things, a 6.6 percent pay increase with a one-year contract term. Another demand: Union members should receive an annual bonus of 660 euros.

The third round of negotiations is scheduled for May 11 and 12.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Kwara, Nigeria Magistrates to begin indefinite strike on July 2 over unpaid allowances and poor welfare
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Kwara Magistrates Declare Indefinite Strike Over Poor Welfare, Unpaid Allowances
Magistrates in Kwara State have announced plans to embark on an indefinite strike over unresolved welfare concerns, unpaid allowances, and what they described as unfair treatment by the state government.
The industrial action is scheduled to begin on Thursday, July 2, 2026, if authorities fail to address their demands before the deadline.
The decision was reached by members of the Magistrates’ Association of Nigeria during a congress held in the state, where members expressed dissatisfaction over what they called years of neglect and worsening working conditions.
In an official communiqué issued after the meeting, the association said magistrates had grown increasingly frustrated over issues relating to salary structure, unpaid statutory entitlements, and poor welfare support.
The communiqué, signed by the chairman of the association in Kwara, revealed that members unanimously agreed that industrial action had become necessary after repeated concerns failed to attract meaningful intervention.
One of the major concerns raised by the magistrates is the salary structure currently in place. According to the association, the situation has become deeply discouraging, especially as magistrates now earn less than court registrars on the same grade level.
The association described the development as both unfair and embarrassing for judicial officers who carry significant responsibilities within the justice system.
Another key issue raised was the non-payment of furniture allowance, which the magistrates said is a statutory entitlement expected every four years.
According to them, the allowance has not been paid since the administration of Abdulfatah Ahmed, leaving many judicial officers without benefits that are due to them by law.
The magistrates also complained about unpaid allowances and what they described as unequal distribution of official vehicles.
They alleged that while some magistrates were provided with official vehicles, many others were left out entirely, creating what they see as unfair treatment among officers within the same judicial structure.
The association disclosed that many members initially pushed for the strike to begin within 48 hours after the congress due to growing frustration.
However, the intervention of the Chief Judge of Kwara State reportedly changed the timeline.
According to the communiqué, the Chief Judge advised that due process required a minimum notice period of seven days before any industrial action could commence.
“Today, we held a crucial Congress where the voice of the Magistrates was heard loud, clear and resolute. There was palpable frustration and righteous anger over the challenges we face, and the overwhelming sentiment was a call to action that a strike must commence within 48 hours,” the communiqué stated.
Following further consultations, the magistrates agreed to issue a seven-day ultimatum, counting both Saturday and Sunday as part of the notice period.
“This strike shall commence on Thursday, the 2nd day of July, 2026,” they said.
The association urged its members to remain united and disciplined as the planned action draws closer.
It also assured members that the leadership would continue engaging relevant authorities while pressing for immediate solutions to the issues raised.
The demands of the magistrates include: “Immediate salary review to address the disparity in pay between magistrates and court registrars on the same grade level.
“Payment of furniture allowance, last paid during the administration of former Governor Abdulfatah Ahmed, Payment of other outstanding allowances; and Fair distribution of official vehicles among magistrates in the state.”
If no resolution is reached before the deadline, court activities across magistrates’ courts in Kwara State are expected to face major disruption.
The planned strike could significantly affect judicial proceedings, legal filings, and access to justice for residents across the state.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
A worker from the city government’s Department of Environment and Public Services helps clean up Liwasang Bonifacio ahead of a rally by the Iglesia ni Cristo on July 2, 2026. — Photo from Manila Public Information Office/Facebook MANILA, Philippines – Protesters at the Iglesia ni Cristo (INC)-led rally in Manila are prepared to camp at Liwasang Bonifacio and stay there “for as long as it takes,” Batangas 1st District Rep. Leandro Leviste said on Thursday, signaling that the demonstration could continue beyond the weekend.
Leviste joined protesters who traveled from Batangas to the rally, saying demonstrators intend to stay until their demands are met.
“This won’t end in the next few days. Because, of course, our demands here cannot be achieved immediately,” Leviste told reporters in a mix of English and Filipino.
Article continues after this advertisement The lawmaker said more protesters from different provinces are expected to arrive in the coming days.
“It would be good for the government to show that it stands for true justice and accountability,” he said.
The dayslong mobilization came after the Office of the Ombudsman announced it would file nonbailable plunder charges against Sen. Rodante Marcoleta, an active member of the religious sect.
The INC-led rally began on Tuesday near the People Power Monument in Quezon City before relocating to Liwasang Bonifacio after the Quezon City government revoked the group’s rally permit, citing traffic gridlock and public order concerns.
The Manila city government, meanwhile, reiterated that Liwasang Bonifacio is a designated freedom park where public assemblies may be held without a permit.
Article continues after this advertisement Most of the rallyists arrived on Wednesday and spent the night at the plaza, where volunteers distributed food and water as protesters prepared for an extended stay.
The Manila Police District estimated the crowd at about 2,800 as of 4 p.m. Thursday.
Article continues after this advertisement READ: Manila gov’t: Liwasang Bonifacio is freedom park, no permit needed
Aside from Leviste, no other prominent political figures were seen at the rally during the morning and afternoon program.
Some participants wore matching shirts bearing the slogan, “Transparency for a better democracy,” while a few attended the program barefoot. Others rested under tents and makeshift shelters set up around the plaza.
Food provided
Ally Ismael, a 46-year-old INC member, has been handing out free food packs and bottled water since early Thursday morning.
“We really need to do this. This is for the people. We are fighting for our rights, especially against our corrupt government. This is necessary for the welfare of the entire Philippines,” Ismael told the Inquirer in Filipino.
He said food is available to everyone, including non-INC members, adding that volunteers were instructed to continue distributing meals until at least Sunday.
Not all there for Marcoleta
Some protesters, however, said they were not attending the rally primarily to support Marcoleta.
Ronald Gadayan, a janitor who carried a handwritten placard calling for honesty and patriotism in government, said he is not an INC member but decided to join the gathering because of his frustration over corruption.
“I am here because I want honest and patriotic leaders,” Gadayan told the Inquirer in Filipino.

New Delhi: Lakhs of members from various tribal communities from across the nation gathered at Delhi's Red Fort grounds on Sunday and called for the de-listing of converted tribals from the Scheduled Tribe category.

"This cultural programme is aimed at giving a major push to our long-pending demand for de-listing converted tribals from the Scheduled Tribe category. This issue goes back to the time of tribal leader Kartik Oraon ji, who raised it before the then prime minister Indira Gandhi in the late 1960s," Maalaya Jigdung of the Janjati Suraksha Manch, Assam prant, said.
Jigdung asserted that the mobilisation will help build wider national support for a constitutional amendment under Article 342.
ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Organisers claimed that nearly 1.5 lakh people from over 500 tribal communities across the country participated in the event.
"This has been one of our oldest demands and the core objective behind the formation of the Janjati Suraksha Manch. Through this programme, we have showcased tribal cultural identity while also strengthening our movement for de-listing," Jigdung told PTI .
The event began with cultural processions from five locations in the national capital -- Rajghat Chowk, Ramlila Maidan, Ajmeri Gate Chowk, Qudsia Bagh near Kashmiri Gate and Shyamgiri Temple near Shastri Park Bus Depot. The rallies, covering around 2.5 to 3.5 kilometres, converged at the Red Fort grounds.
Participants dressed in traditional attire carried tribal flags, beat drums and performed folk dances as they marched through Delhi's streets.
Groups from Assam, Tripura, Bihar, Jharkhand , Odisha, Andaman and Nicobar and several other states took part in the event, which organisers described as the "largest tribal cultural mobilisation of its kind".
Kartik Oraon, a prominent tribal leader from Bihar and former Congress MP, had submitted memoranda signed by hundreds of MPs in 1967 and 1970 seeking the removal of Scheduled Tribe benefits for tribals who had converted to Christianity or Islam.
Balaram Phangcho, organising secretary of the North East Janajati Dharm Sanskriti Suraksha Manch from Assam's Karbi Anglong district, said around 2,000 to 2,500 people had travelled from his district alone.
"This kind of programme is being organised for the first time. We have to protect the very existence of tribal communities. Those who have converted, especially to Islam or Christianity, should be removed from the Scheduled Tribe category. De-listing should be done through an amendment under Article 342," he said.
Phangcho mentioned that people had travelled from remote villages because they believed the issue is linked to the survival of tribal identity and traditions.
Stressing the link between identity and culture, he said, "My identity is my culture -- if my culture does not survive, neither will I." Shanti Bikas Chakma from Tripura said the gathering will help protect tribal religion, culture and traditions.
"This is the first time we are seeing such a programme organised at this scale. People from so many tribal communities have come together with one message," Chakma said.
Chakma also thanked the Delhi government and volunteers for arrangements related to accommodation, food and transport for participants arriving in special trains and buses from different states.
Janajati Suraksha Manch was formed in 2006 to campaign for the removal of ST benefits for tribals who had converted to other religions.
