Life
The strike's failure knocks out Metges de Catalunya in its crusade against the Generalitat
The tactics denounced by the sector and the low turnout for doctors' protests put Xavier Lleonart's union in a bind
Other stories: Mataró Hospital quells a doctors' mutiny, but falls into deficit
The chances of success for Metges de Catalunya (MC) in its crusade against the Generalitat are dwindling. The union has significantly strained negotiations for improved working conditions for the professional group and for the cancellation of the doctors' strike, with a very limited capacity for mobilization.

This week's demonstration only managed to bring around 5% of the medical staff to the streets, according to the Ministry of Health; the organizers put the turnout at 31%. A setback that dashes the aspirations of the general secretary, Xavier Lleonart, who desperately needs a way out of this impasse.

A new meeting is scheduled for this Thursday at the Labor Inspectorate, where the parties will try to find a way out of this predicament.

They appeal to Illa
Sources familiar with the state of the negotiations acknowledge in conversation with this publication that there is "desperation" within the organization led by Xavier Lleonart. Other voices elaborate on the union's profound difficulties in rallying its members to the cause. Moreover, they are now "asking for help to get out of this absurd situation."

In fact, the latest move by the union platform has been to formally address President Salvador Illa, asking him to intervene in the negotiations. In a letter sent to the head of the Catalan government, Lleonart has asked him to initiate a process of "listening and negotiation," threatening that the group "remains stubbornly steadfast."

This will not back down, reads the letter addressed to the Socialist leader, with whom they had already met once, before the conflict became entrenched. They have met twice with Health Minister Olga Pané, and with representatives of the department on 32 occasions since January 2025, through the various established dialogue forums.

The Catalan Medical Association (Metges de Catalunya) split from the State Confederation of Medical Unions (CESM) at the height of the independence movement, a few days after the October 1, 2017 referendum and the King's speech, which was criticized by the separatists. Now, it has allied itself with national organizations to oppose the Framework Statute promoted by the Ministry of Health.

Mónica García's office—now poised to challenge Isabel Díaz Ayuso (PP) for the presidency of the Community of Madrid—reached an agreement with the major unions in January to improve the basic collective bargaining agreement for healthcare workers. Neither CESM nor Metges de Catalunya signed the agreement, even though the text "includes many of their demands," according to other sources.

Far from "accepting the rules of the democratic game," according to other union sources, the Catalan doctors' platform has held ten consecutive days of strikes, and the protests—wearing Pané masks, which have not gone down well within the Health Department—have now lasted more than six months.

The Supreme Court precedent
The official call for the strikes, however, makes no mention of the Framework Statute. And of the nine demands it does include, two fall under the jurisdiction of the central government—early retirement and the reclassification of statutory staff—and therefore the Catalan government cannot assume responsibility for them. Nor of the remaining seven.

These refer to working conditions, such as 24-hour shifts, breaks, and working hours. However, Metges is already negotiating these as part of the new collective agreement for publicly funded healthcare, and the Supreme Court overturned previous agreements reached with employers' associations precisely because of the involvement of the regional health ministry and because these agreements were forged outside the negotiating table.
The Parliament's Setback
Despite this, Lleonart's organization insists on creating its own forum to engage with the Catalan government. It has adopted a motion passed by the Catalan Parliament on March 12, in which the political parties asked the government to enter into negotiations, despite the aforementioned ruling and the fact that the Catalan Health Institute (ICS) and the Catalan Health Service (SISCAT) are the only entities authorized to do so, as providers of the staff.
The Catalan Parliament's setback, forced by Metges, prompted criticism from the employers' associations. In a joint letter, the Catalan Health and Social Consortium (CSC) and the Catalan Hospital Union called for respect for "the legally established mechanisms for social dialogue and negotiation between trade unions and legitimate employer representatives."

"Neither the president, nor the minister, nor the Parliament can interfere," sources in the sector summarized.

Turning their backs on the Catalan Health Institute (ICS)
These maneuvers by the largest doctors' union in Catalonia—denied by the Confederation of Medical Unions (CESM), which maintains that "everyone is free to make their own demands within their community"—have generated disdain from the sections of other workers' organizations.
The secretary of the UGT Catalonia, José Manuel Domínguez, expressed his incomprehension of the particular battle waged by the MC. "We deeply respect the right to strike, but we believe they are not following the rules and that this is not the appropriate course of action. We agree with the signed agreement and will defend it," he explained to this publication.

Catalan healthcare officials agree with the union representative and are inviting doctors to participate in the "negotiating sessions" to discuss their specific conditions. While they are formally participating in talks with SISCAT (the Catalan Health Service) for the new agreement for private hospitals, they are reluctant to do so with the Catalan Health Institute (ICS) and the public healthcare network.
At this point, the options for resolving the situation are minimal for the largest doctors' union. "We want this to end; we have no desire for it to drag on," sources within the department explain. At the Travessera de les Corts (the Catalan government headquarters), they are in favor of "getting out of this mess as soon as possible" because, "although minor, it is having an impact on the population."

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Gremiales | 17 may 2026
En conferencia de prensa
PAMI y Remediar: FESINTRAS denunció recortes y llamó a una marcha federal
Denunció "fuertes recortes en medicamentos esenciales, reducción en la entrega de vacunas, vaciamiento del PAMI y ajuste en programas claves".
Con la consigna “El ajuste de Milei mata”, la Federación Sindical Nacional de Trabajadores y Trabajadoras de la Salud (FESINTRAS) realizó este viernes una conferencia de prensa en la sede del SUTEPA, donde ratificó la convocatoria al Paro Nacional de Salud del próximo miércoles 20 de mayo.
La medida de fuerza tendrá como acción central una Marcha Federal que partirá a las 13 horas desde el Ministerio de Salud de la Nación hacia Plaza de Mayo, en la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, y estará acompañada por actos y movilizaciones en distintas provincias del país, entre ellas Jujuy, Santa Fe, Córdoba y Chaco.
Desde FESINTRAS señalaron que “la jornada tiene carácter federal” y se realizará “en repudio a las políticas sanitarias impulsadas por el Gobierno Nacional, basadas en el ajuste, la desinversión y el recorte de programas esenciales como el REMEDIAR, el desfinanciamiento del PAMI y el ahogo presupuestario a provincias y municipios. Esta situación se traduce en atraso salarial, precarización y un escenario cada vez más crítico e insostenible para todo el sistema sanitario argentino”.
En línea con ello, el secretario General de FESINTRAS y CICOP, Pablo Maciel, sostuvo que “estas decisiones temerarias responden al avance del Gobierno de Javier Milei en la eliminación del principio de la salud como derecho, en donde ya no existe un sistema solidario o una responsabilidad del Estado, sino que la salud es concebida como un servicio y habrá usuarios que puedan consumir en tanto y en cuanto puedan pagar”.
Ademáso, Maciel precisó que los hospitales públicos bonaerenses registran un incremento de la demanda superior al 23%. “La crisis económica, el desempleo, el cierre prácticamente del REMEDIAR, la quiebra de obras sociales y la situación dramática del PAMI empujan a miles de personas al sistema público para resolver desde consultas hasta cirugías”, explicó al respecto.
“El resultado es un sistema sanitario saturado, con equipos de salud sobrecargados y recursos insuficientes para responder a una demanda creciente. A este cuadro se suma una situación interna cada vez más grave: las trabajadoras y los trabajadores del sector público nacional enfrentan un deterioro salarial inaudito, con falta de respuestas paritarias y aumento de la conflictividad en la atención”, agregó Maciel.
Por su parte Nicolás Fernández, secretario General de APUAP, fue contundente al decir que “Se está viviendo un retroceso de más de 30 años en políticas sanitarias” y remarcó que “uno de los aspectos más críticos del ajuste, es el vaciamiento del Plan Remediar, programa que durante más de dos décadas garantizó el acceso a medicamentos esenciales para 20 millones de personas a través de 8000 centros de salud de todo el país”.
“El impacto es inmediato y grave: pacientes con enfermedades crónicas, autoinmunes o inflamatorias están descontinuando tratamientos porque no pueden costearlos, lo que genera complicaciones severas y, en los casos más extremos, muertes evitables”, precisó Fernández.
Por su parte, el secretario General del SUTEPA, Hernán Corredoira, manifestó que “la situación del PAMI expresa con crudeza el deterioro de las políticas públicas de salud y previsión social”. En ese sentido, indicaron que, según datos de la Oficina de Presupuesto del Congreso, las transferencias de recursos nacionales al PAMI registraron una caída real del 54,4% durante el primer cuatrimestre de 2026 en comparación con el mismo período del año anterior”.
“Ese ajuste se traduce en una caída concreta de prestaciones, demoras en la atención, dificultades en el acceso a medicamentos y una creciente deuda con prestadores, médicos de cabecera y odontólogos, que compromete el funcionamiento cotidiano del sistema y profundiza la incertidumbre de millones de afiliadas y afiliados”, aseguró Corredoira y añadió que “los trabajadores del PAMI llevan dos años sin actualización salarial adecuada”.
Durante la conferencia, el Secretario General Adjunto de APHEC, Hospital El Cruce de Florencio Varela, Damián Zamorano, alertó que “en este establecimiento de alta complejidad la lógica de privatización y mercantilización ya está sucediendo, mediante políticas de productividad que incrementan la atención y profundizan la sobrecarga laboral del personal de salud”.
También fue parte de la mesa Pedro Lynn, Secretario Gremial de ATE Capital y delegado de ATE Salud. En su intervención, sentenció que “el Gobierno Nacional tiene una política deliberada de que no haya salud pública y de que quien quiera atención médica deba pagarla”.
La actividad cerró con la participación especial del Secretario General de la CTA-T Nacional, Hugo Yasky, quien subrayó que “el pueblo en la calle va a poner un límite” y abogó por el compromiso de profundizar la Unidad para detener la destrucción de Milei y “ser un solo puño peleando”.
Finalmente, FESINTRAS convocó a toda la sociedad a sumarse a la jornada nacional de lucha del 20 de mayo. “El desafío es aunar fuerzas y articular luchas para exigirle al gobierno que recapacite y detenga las políticas de ajuste en salud, porque lo que está en juego es la vida de millones de personas”, concluyeron.
La conferencia contó con el acompañamiento del secretario General de la CTA-T Provincia de Buenos Aires, Roberto Baradel y el secretario General de FOETRA, Claudio Marín.
FESINTRAS está integrada por: CICOP (Asociación Sindical de Profesionales de la Salud de la Provincia de Buenos Aires), APUAP (Asociación de Profesionales Universitarios de la Administración Pública de Jujuy), APHEC (Asociación de Personal del Hospital El Cruce), SUTEPA (Sindicato Unido de Trabajadores y Empleados de PAMI) y UTRASACH (Unión de Trabajadores de la Salud del Chaco).

Les syndicats CGT et SUD, aux côtés du collectif Hébergement en danger, annoncent un rassemblement ce mardi 19 mai à 17h30 place Guichard, à Lyon, afin de protester contre les contrats d’hébergement d’urgence limités à trois mois mis en place dans le Rhône.
Selon les organisateurs, ce dispositif aurait été instauré par la préfecture du Rhône, via la Direction départementale de l’emploi, du travail et des solidarités (DDETS), depuis octobre dernier dans les structures d’hébergement d’urgence du département.
Les collectifs dénoncent une politique visant à "fluidifier" les places disponibles, qu’ils accusent de se traduire par des remises à la rue de personnes hébergées, y compris des familles et des enfants. Ils estiment que ces pratiques contreviennent au principe de continuité de l’hébergement d’urgence prévu par le Code de l’action sociale et des familles.
"Ces nouveaux contrats sont illégaux et inhumains !", dénoncent-ils.
Dans leur communiqué, les syndicats avancent le chiffre de plus de 14 000 personnes en attente d’un hébergement dans le Rhône et de 84 000 demandes de logement social. Ils critiquent également l’application de critères de "vulnérabilité" pour le renouvellement des contrats, affirmant qu’ils excluraient une partie des personnes sans-abri de l’accès aux dispositifs d’urgence.
Les organisateurs réclament notamment la fin des contrats de trois mois, davantage de places d’hébergement, un arrêt des remises à la rue ainsi qu’une augmentation de l’offre de logements abordables et la réquisition de bâtiments vacants.
Un préavis de grève a également été déposé dans le secteur de l’hébergement d’urgence.

The CGT and SUD unions, along with the "Housing in Danger" collective, are announcing a rally this Tuesday, May 19, at 5:30 p.m. in Place Guichard, Lyon, to protest against the three-month emergency housing contracts implemented in the Rhône department.

According to the organizers, this system was introduced by the Rhône prefecture, via the Departmental Directorate of Employment, Labor, and Solidarity (DDETS), last October in the department's emergency housing facilities.
The collectives denounce a policy aimed at "streamlining" available spaces, which they accuse of resulting in the eviction of people housed there, including families and children. They believe these practices violate the principle of continuity of emergency housing as stipulated by the Social Action and Families Code.

"These new contracts are illegal and inhumane!" they declare. In their press release, the unions cite figures of over 14,000 people awaiting emergency accommodation in the Rhône department and 84,000 applications for social housing. They also criticize the application of "vulnerability" criteria for contract renewals, arguing that these criteria exclude some homeless people from accessing emergency services.

The organizers are demanding, in particular, an end to three-month contracts, more emergency accommodation places, a halt to evictions, an increase in the supply of affordable housing, and the requisitioning of vacant buildings.

A strike notice has also been filed in the emergency accommodation sector.

Mehrere Versammlungen sind für den Maifeiertag am Freitag, 1. Mai, in Gera angemeldet. Neben der Gewerkschaftsveranstaltung am Vormittag und einem Neonazi-Aufmarsch am Nachmittag wurde gegen letzteren nun auch eine Gegenprotest-Veranstaltung angemeldet. Gewerkschaften informieren auf dem Marktplatz
Traditionell lädt zum Tag der Arbeit der Deutsche Gewerkschaftsbund (DGB) zur Kundgebung auf dem Geraer Marktplatz ein. Die Veranstaltung der DGB-Kreisverbände Gera und Greiz am Freitag, 1. Mai, ab 10 Uhr steht unter dem Motto „Erst unsere Jobs, dann eure Profite“. Die Besucher der Veranstaltung erwartet eine Rede von Gewerkschaftssekretärin Julia Langhammer vom DGB Bezirk Hessen-Thüringen, mit Kernforderungen der Gewerkschaften zum 1. Mai und Grußworten. Statt weiterer Reden werden wieder Interviews mit verschiedenen Akteuren an den Informationsständen geführt, die von Gewerkschaften, Vereinen und Parteien wieder zahlreich vertreten sind. Verkehrseinschränkungen wegen Demo am Nachmittag
Am Nachmittag muss in Gera mit Verkehrseinschränkungen durch einen Neonazi-Aufmarsch gerechnet werden. Die rechtsextreme Kleinstpartei „III. Weg“ hat relativ kurzfristig eine Demonstration in Gera mit bis zu 100 Teilnehmern angemeldet, teilte die Geraer Stadtverwaltung zu Beginn der Woche mit. Zur Aufzugstrecke wurde inzwischen konkretisiert, dass diese vom Gleisdreieck die Wiesestraße stadteinwärts bis zur Straße des Friedens, über die Heinrichsbrücke und Heinrichstraße bis zum Kreisverkehr und dann in Richtung Reichsstraße gelaufen wird. Über die Breitscheidstraße und Ernst-Toller-Straße endet der Aufzug am Hauptbahnhof.
Auf der Demostrecke kann es demnach ab 14 Uhr zu zeitweisen Verkehrseinschränkungen kommen. Die Polizei bereitet sich auf einen entsprechenden Einsatz vor. Die Versammlungsanmelder kommen laut Stadtverwaltung nicht aus Gera.

Several assemblies are registered for May Day on Friday, May 1st, in Gera. In addition to the union event in the morning and a neo-Nazi march in the afternoon, a counter-protest has now also been registered against the latter. According to the Thuringian State Police, the assembly situation in Gera represents a police priority.

Unions provide information at the market square
Traditionally, the German Trade Union Confederation (DGB) invites people to a rally at the Gera market square for Labor Day. The event, organized by the DGB district associations of Gera and Greiz, will take place on Friday, May 1st, starting at 10:00 a.m., under the motto "Our jobs first, then your profits." Attendees can expect a speech by union secretary Julia Langhammer from the DGB district of Hesse-Thuringia, outlining the unions' key demands for May Day and offering greetings. Instead of further speeches, interviews will again be conducted with various representatives at the information booths, which are once again numerous and staffed by unions, associations, and political parties. Musician Heinz Ratz and the children's dance group "Step by Step" from Gera will provide entertainment. There will be games and activities for children of all ages. Food and drinks will also be available.

Traffic disruptions expected this afternoon due to a neo-Nazi march in Gera. The far-right micro-party "III. Weg" (Third Way) registered a demonstration in Gera with up to 100 participants at relatively short notice, the Gera city administration announced at the beginning of the week. The route has now been specified: it will proceed from Gleisdreieck (railway triangle) along Wiesestraße towards the city center to Straße des Friedens (Street of Peace), across the Heinrichsbrücke (Heinrich Bridge) and along Heinrichstraße to the roundabout, and then towards Reichsstraße. The march will continue via Breitscheidstraße and Ernst-Toller-Straße, ending at the main train station.

Traffic disruptions are expected along the demonstration route starting at 2 p.m. The police are preparing for a possible deployment. According to the city administration, the organizers of the demonstration are not from Gera.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Solicitan más iluminación y cámaras de seguridad
Pobladores de Agua del Ajial de Punitaqui protestan por ola de robos
Su tercera protesta de la semana llevaron a cabo este viernes los pobladores del sector Agua del Ajial, de Las Ramadas de Punitaqui, cansados dicen, de los constantes robos que han sufrido sus viviendas en el último tiempo, situación que los tiene viviendo en la más completa inseguridad.
María Canivilo Rodríguez, dirigente de la localidad, manifiesta que “el otro día fue la gota que rebalsó el vaso. Yo creo que en el sector como el 70% de las viviendas han sufrido robos. Hay casas que han entrado dos veces, y ahora se pasaron para la parte más abajo. Nuestra principal preocupación es que ahí hay adultos mayores y estos ladrones no van a mirar, ellos simplemente si la señora va a salir la van a matar o a cualquiera”, enfatiza.
Señala que en varias oportunidades se han acercado al municipio a exponer esta inquietud, además de las denuncias que se habían hecho anteriormente, pero nada. Con posterioridad, lograron sostener una reunión con el edil y se les dijo que como comunidad podían comprar cámaras y que la casa edilicia ponía los técnicos para su instalación. “Y les consultamos cuánto valdría una cámara, nos dijeron que 10 millones y yo les dije ¿y ustedes creen que una junta de vecinos va a tener 10 millones de pesos para poner una cámara?”, cuestionó.
Ante esta situación, llevaron a cabo una primera manifestación el domingo pasado, la que repitieron el miércoles y este viernes. “Qué es lo que tiene que hacer el municipio con sus autoridades, los carabineros, cuando pasan estas cosas, aunque sea un solo robo. Ellos tenían que haber notificado inmediatamente a Ovalle, para ver si ponían más refuerzos, pero nosotros verdaderamente estamos en un pueblo totalmente olvidado. Es como que se ríen de nosotros las autoridades, de los que somos afectados”, acusó.
Plantea que esta situación se está produciendo desde el año pasado, pero que en el último tiempo se han incrementado los hechos delictuales. Por eso, han tomado algunas medidas por su cuenta, pero han sido infructuosas. “Con el esfuerzo de todo el sector se pusieron focos solares, pero se los robaron todos. Se luchó para que se pusieran luminarias, pero solo pusieron una en el paradero”, dice.
En este sentido, agrega que “lo que pasa es que ellos como que olfatean, ven que las personas se van a trabajar y es como que marcan la casa, como que viven pendientes, como que le saben los turnos. La gente no puede dejar de trabajar para cuidar sus casas. ¿Cómo viven? Roban de todo, incluso televisores, han dejado las casas peladas. Sobre el último robo, hay un joven que trabaja en Copiapó, y él cuando llegó todas sus herramientas, todo se lo habían llevado; el gas, la tele, todo lo que pillan roban, o sea, lo que ellos puedan sustraer lo hacen”.
Lo que piden, indica la vecina, es que se puedan atender las denuncias que ellos realizan y junto con ello, mejorar las condiciones de iluminación e incrementar las rondas de la policía para dar mayor seguridad. Les plantearon que no había recursos para poner cámaras “pero si no los tienen podemos postular a proyectos, hay otras formas en que pueden colaborar”, puntualiza.
La versión de las autoridades
Consultado respecto a la demanda de los vecinos de Agua del Ajial, el alcalde de Punitaqui, Pedro Araya Zepeda, manifestó que “como municipio conocemos la preocupación que existe en este sector, donde los vecinos y vecinas nos han manifestado su inquietud por la falta de iluminación y la necesidad de reforzar las medidas de seguridad”.
La autoridad recalca que no quieren quedar ajenos a esa realidad, “por eso asumimos el compromiso con la directiva de que nuestros equipos municipales realizarán una evaluación en terreno para analizar la factibilidad de instalar cámaras de televigilancia y reforzar la iluminación”.
En este sentido, enfatiza que “nuestro trabajo es escuchar a los vecinos y vecinas y responder a sus necesidades con acciones responsables. Queremos avanzar en iniciativas que entreguen mayor tranquilidad a la comunidad, fortalecer la seguridad del sector y contribuir a disminuir la sensación de inseguridad en nuestra comuna”.
Por su parte, la seremi de la seremi de Seguridad, María José Duarte, plantea que durante este año 2026 se registran en el lugar solo dos denuncias, uno por robo en bienes nacionales de uso público o sitios no determinados y otra por robo en lugar habitado o destinado a la habitación.
En este sentido, sostiene que, si bien pueden existir requerimientos o manifestaciones de preocupación por parte de la comunidad, estos no se han traducido en denuncias ingresadas por los canales formales “lo que dificulta la planificación de intervenciones focalizadas. En este período solo se registran dos denuncias, las cuales corresponden a hechos distintos de aquellos consultados”.
En este contexto, agrega, resulta fundamental realizar un llamado a la comunidad a denunciar oportunamente cualquier hecho constitutivo de delito. “La denuncia constituye una herramienta esencial para orientar la acción de las instituciones, fortalecer el análisis delictual y generar respuestas e intervenciones preventivas acordes a la realidad del territorio. Asimismo, se recuerda a la ciudadanía que puede realizar denuncias de manera completamente anónima a través del programa Denuncia Seguro (*4242), disponible las 24 horas del día, los siete días de la semana, garantizando la reserva de la identidad de quien entrega la información”, puntualizó.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Residents of Agua del Ajial, Punitaqui, protest wave of robberies, request more lighting and security cameras.
Residents of Agua del Ajial, Punitaqui, held their third protest of the week this Friday, fed up, they say, with the constant robberies their homes have suffered recently, a situation that has left them living in complete insecurity.

María Canivilo Rodríguez, a community leader, stated, “The other day was the last straw. I think about 70% of the homes in the area have been robbed. Some houses have been broken into twice, and now they've moved to the lower part of town. Our main concern is that there are elderly people there, and these thieves won't hesitate; if the woman goes out, they'll kill her or anyone else,” she emphasized.

She noted that they have approached the municipality on several occasions to express their concerns, in addition to the complaints they had filed previously, but nothing has been done. Later, they managed to meet with the mayor and were told that the community could purchase security cameras and that the town hall would provide the technicians for installation. “We asked them how much a camera would cost, and they told us 10 million pesos. I said, ‘Do you really think a neighborhood association is going to have 10 million pesos to install a camera?’” he questioned.

Faced with this situation, they held their first protest last Sunday, which they repeated on Wednesday and this Friday. “What should the municipality and its authorities, the police, do when these things happen, even if it’s just one robbery? They should have immediately notified Ovalle to see if they could send more reinforcements, but we are truly in a completely forgotten town. It’s like the authorities are laughing at us, at those of us who are affected,” he accused.

He states that this situation has been occurring since last year, but that criminal activity has increased recently. That's why they've taken some measures on their own, but they've been unsuccessful. "With the effort of the entire community, solar lights were installed, but they were all stolen. We fought to get streetlights installed, but they only put one at the bus stop," he says.

In this regard, he adds, "What happens is that they seem to have a nose for it; they see when people go to work and it's like they mark the house, like they're keeping an eye on them, like they know their shifts. People can't stop working to protect their homes. How do they live? They steal everything, even televisions; they've left the houses completely bare. Regarding the last robbery, there's a young man who works in Copiapó, and when he got home, all his tools were gone; the gas, the TV, everything they can get their hands on, they steal whatever they can."

What they are asking for, the neighbor indicates, is that their complaints be addressed, and along with that, improved lighting and increased police patrols to provide greater security. They were told there were no resources to install cameras, “but if they don't have them, we can apply for projects; there are other ways they can collaborate,” she points out.

The authorities' version
When asked about the demands of the residents of Agua del Ajial, the mayor of Punitaqui, Pedro Araya Zepeda, stated that “as a municipality, we are aware of the concerns in this area, where residents have expressed their unease about the lack of lighting and the need to reinforce security measures.”

The mayor emphasizes that they do not want to remain indifferent to this situation, “which is why we have committed to the residents' association that our municipal teams will conduct an on-site assessment to analyze the feasibility of installing surveillance cameras and improving lighting.” In this regard, she emphasizes that “our job is to listen to the residents and respond to their needs with responsible actions. We want to move forward with initiatives that provide greater peace of mind to the community, strengthen security in the area, and help reduce the feeling of insecurity in our municipality.”

For her part, the Regional Secretary of Security, María José Duarte, states that only two reports have been filed in the area this year, 2026: one for theft from public property or unspecified locations, and another for theft from an inhabited dwelling.

She maintains that, while there may be concerns or requests from the community, these have not resulted in formal complaints filed through official channels, “which hinders the planning of targeted interventions. Only two complaints have been filed during this period, and these correspond to incidents different from those reported.”

In this context, she adds, it is essential to urge the community to promptly report any criminal activity. “Reporting crimes is an essential tool for guiding institutional action, strengthening crime analysis, and generating preventive responses and interventions tailored to the realities of the area. Citizens are also reminded that they can report crimes completely anonymously through the Safe Reporting program (*4242), available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, guaranteeing the confidentiality of the person providing the information,” he stated.

This action was part of the national strike called by the National Coordinating Committee of Education Workers (CNTE), with which the dissident teachers' movement reactivated its mobilizations after a weekend of inactivity.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Argentine Confederation of Education Workers announces new national strike
MESSAGE_TEXT:
En el marco del conflicto salarial y de financiamiento que mantiene el sector docente con el Gobierno de Javier Milei, la Confederación de Trabajadores de la Educación de la República Argentina (CTERA) anunció un nuevo paro nacional docente y advirtió que profundizará las medidas de fuerza.
La decisión se comunicó este miércoles durante una Jornada Nacional de Lucha que sitió los accesos al Palacio Pizzurno, sede central de la Secretaría de Educación de la Nación.
Según explicaron las autoridades del gremio, la paralización del dictado de clases en las escuelas públicas responde a la “total ausencia” de canales de diálogo con el Gobierno y a la falta de respuestas institucionales ante el pliego de reclamos presentado por las organizaciones docentes.
Cuatro reclamos centrales al Gobierno nacional
La movilización en la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires nucleó a miembros de la Junta Ejecutiva de CTERA, secretarios generales de los sindicatos de base de distintas provincias, cuerpos de delegados y militantes de base.
Frente a las puertas del Palacio Pizzurno, los docentes ratificaron un pliego estructurado en cuatro demandas urgentes:
– Recomposición salarial: exigencia de un aumento presupuestario urgente que detenga la licuación de los sueldos básicos del sector.
– Restitución del FONID: reclamo por la devolución inmediata del Fondo Nacional de Incentivo Docente, una partida nacional recortada que golpea directamente el sueldo de bolsillo de los maestros de todas las jurisdicciones.
– Paritaria nacional: convocatoria perentoria a la Paritaria Nacional Docente para fijar un piso salarial de referencia obligatoria en todo el país.
– Previsión social: defensa irrestricta de la jubilación docente y de las cajas móviles ante los intentos de modificación de los regímenes especiales.
“No vamos a resignar ninguno de los derechos conquistados”
Durante el acto central montado sobre la vía pública, tomaron la palabra los principales referentes de las entidades que componen la confederación, quienes unificaron sus discursos para denunciar las consecuencias educativas del plan económico nacional.
El cierre del encuentro estuvo a cargo de la secretaria general de CTERA, Sonia Alesso, quien ratificó que las bases docentes no retrocederán frente al actual esquema de recortes presupuestarios.
“No vamos a resignar ninguno de los derechos conquistados por la docencia. Exigimos la inmediata convocatoria a la Paritaria Nacional Docente, la restitución del FONID y una recomposición salarial que permita a las y los trabajadores de la educación vivir con dignidad. Vamos a seguir en las calles y profundizando las medidas de fuerza hasta obtener respuestas concretas”, apuntó.
Unidad sindical y advertencia sobre la continuidad del plan de lucha
Además de la titular de CTERA, hicieron uso de la palabra Rodrigo Alonso (secretario general de AMSAFE Santa Fe), María Laura Torre (secretaria general de SUTEBA Buenos Aires) y Abel “Pachi” Antivero (secretario general de AGMER Entre Ríos).
Los secretarios generales coincidieron en que la actual coyuntura fiscal obliga a deponer diferencias sectoriales para estructurar una resistencia unificada que blinde el financiamiento de la escuela pública.
Desde el sindicato remarcaron que la masiva presencia de delegaciones provinciales en Buenos Aires consolida el compromiso del magisterio en la defensa integral de las condiciones de enseñanza y aprendizaje.
Alesso advirtió que la fecha y la modalidad del paro nacional se notificarán de forma orgánica en las próximas horas, y anticipó que las acciones gremiales continuarán escalando de manera sistemática hasta que las carteras ministeriales expidan soluciones reales para el sistema educativo.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Amid the ongoing wage and funding dispute between teachers and the government of Javier Milei, the Confederation of Education Workers of the Argentine Republic (CTERA) announced a new national teachers' strike and warned that it will escalate its actions.

The decision was announced this Wednesday during a National Day of Action that surrounded the entrances to the Pizzurno Palace, the headquarters of the National Ministry of Education.

According to union officials, the work stoppage in public schools is due to the "total absence" of dialogue with the government and the lack of institutional responses to the list of demands presented by teachers' organizations.

Four key demands of the national government
The mobilization in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires brought together members of CTERA's Executive Board, general secretaries of local unions from various provinces, delegates, and grassroots activists.

In front of the Pizzurno Palace, teachers ratified a list of demands structured around four urgent points:

– Salary Restructuring: an urgent budget increase to halt the erosion of basic salaries in the sector.

– Reinstatement of the National Teacher Incentive Fund (FONID): a demand for the immediate return of the National Teacher Incentive Fund, a cut national allocation that directly impacts the take-home pay of teachers in all jurisdictions.

– National Collective Bargaining: an urgent call for a National Teacher Collective Bargaining Committee to establish a mandatory minimum salary reference point throughout the country.

– Social Security: unwavering defense of teachers' pensions and the mobile pension funds against attempts to modify special pension schemes.

"We will not relinquish any of the rights we have won."
During the main event held in the street, the leading figures of the organizations that make up the confederation spoke, uniting their speeches to denounce the educational consequences of the national economic plan.

The closing remarks were delivered by CTERA General Secretary Sonia Alesso, who reaffirmed that teachers will not back down in the face of the current budget cuts.

“We will not relinquish any of the rights won by teachers. We demand the immediate convening of the National Teachers' Collective Bargaining Committee, the reinstatement of the National Teacher Incentive Fund (FONID), and a salary increase that allows education workers to live with dignity. We will continue taking to the streets and escalating our actions until we obtain concrete responses,” she stated.

Union unity and a warning about the continuation of the struggle
In addition to the CTERA leader, Rodrigo Alonso (General Secretary of AMSAFE Santa Fe), María Laura Torre (General Secretary of SUTEBA Buenos Aires), and Abel “Pachi” Antivero (General Secretary of AGMER Entre Ríos) also spoke.

The general secretaries agreed that the current fiscal situation compels them to set aside sectoral differences in order to structure a unified resistance that safeguards public school funding.

The union emphasized that the massive presence of provincial delegations in Buenos Aires reinforces teachers' commitment to the comprehensive defense of teaching and learning conditions.

Alesso warned that the date and details of the national strike will be officially announced in the coming hours, and anticipated that union actions will continue to escalate systematically until the ministries issue real solutions for the education system.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
À l’occasion de la Journée mondiale de lutte contre la désertification et la sécheresse, la Compagnie Sucrière du Tchad (CST) et les habitants du canton Banda se sont mobilisés ce mercredi 17 juin 2026 à Maïbo. Cette initiative collective, qui a rassemblé les employés de l’entreprise et les forces vives locales, vise à sensibiliser les communautés à la protection de la nature et à la préservation des ressources naturelles face aux défis climatiques de la province.
Le parcours a débuté à l’usine de la CST pour s’achever au marché central de Maïbo, transformant la trajectoire en une action de nettoyage citoyen. Les volontaires ont collecté les sachets plastiques, les détritus logés dans les eaux stagnantes et divers macro-déchets encombrant les espaces publics, avant de les acheminer directement vers des bacs de regroupement pour redonner au centre-bourg un aspect propre et sain.
En marge de cette collecte, le chef du département Développement Durable et Conformité de la CST, Alladoum Djimta Vincent, a rappelé que la désertification représente l’un des défis environnementaux majeurs pour le Moyen-Chari et d’autres provinces du pays, insistant sur le fait que cette journée constitue une opportunité d’agir concrètement. Le responsable a également alerté sur les conséquences de l’abattage abusif des arbres, qualifiant la sauvegarde des forêts de rempart essentiel pour la protection des sols et la pérennité des ressources en eau, tout en pointant du doigt les risques sanitaires liés à la prolifération des déchets plastiques.
Saluant l’engagement des participants en fin de parcours, il a invité les citoyens à intégrer ces gestes de propreté dans leur quotidien et a encouragé les médias à relayer ces actions d’intérêt public. Cette démarche a été saluée par les habitants du canton Banda, qui se sont dits prêts à promouvoir la préservation de leur environnement au sein de leurs foyers.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
On the occasion of World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought, the Chad Sugar Company (CST) and the residents of the Banda canton mobilized this Wednesday, June 17, 2026, in Maïbo. This collective initiative, which brought together company employees and local community leaders, aimed to raise awareness among the community about protecting nature and preserving natural resources in the face of the province's climate challenges.
The route began at the CST factory and ended at the Maïbo central market, transforming the journey into a community cleanup. Volunteers collected plastic bags, debris from stagnant water, and various types of macro-waste cluttering public spaces, before taking them directly to collection bins to restore a clean and healthy appearance to the town center.

Alongside this cleanup, the head of the Sustainable Development and Compliance Department at CST, Alladoum Djimta Vincent, reiterated that desertification represents one of the major environmental challenges for Moyen-Chari and other provinces in the country, emphasizing that this day presents an opportunity for concrete action. He also warned of the consequences of excessive logging, describing forest conservation as an essential safeguard for soil protection and the sustainability of water resources, while highlighting the health risks associated with the proliferation of plastic waste.
Commending the participants' commitment at the end of the cleanup, he encouraged citizens to incorporate these clean-up practices into their daily lives and urged the media to publicize these initiatives of public interest. This approach was welcomed by the residents of the Banda canton, who expressed their readiness to promote environmental preservation within their own homes.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Ustec se compromete a convocar huelga indefinida si los docentes votan no al preacuerdo
Profesores en huelga
Los profesores podrá contestar si o “no, y me comprometo a hacer las huelgas necesarias hasta acabar el curso”
El principal sindicato educativo, Ustec, junto a CGT, Intersindical y COS,ha puesto en marcha la consulta dirigida a todos los profesores de Catalunya sobre ratificación del preacuerdo educativo firmado con el Govern el pasado viernes.
La pregunta es: “¿Aceptas el preacuerdo por el personal docente del 29 de mayo?”. Se incorporan dos posibles respuestas. “Sí”, en caso afirmativo. O “No, y me comprometo a hacer las huelgas necesarias hasta acabar el curso”.
Ustec, que defiende el pacto, se compromete a convocar huelga indefinida a partir del 8 de junio, un paro que ya está registrado oficialmente.
La consulta estará abierta desde el lunes y hasta el jueves
Esta consulta estará abierta a partir de mañana lunes y hasta el jueves al mediodía. Con el resultado, se movilizará a la base para que participe en las huelga del viernes 5 de junio.
Ustec y Professors de Secundària, que también está consultando a sus afiliados, han desconvocado las huelgas territoriales de lunes a jueves, pero mantienen la del viernes por si acaso.
En cambio, CGT, Intersindical y COS, sindicatos minoritarios, mantienen la convocatoria de huelga toda la semana porque entienden que el personal no ha votado.
El preacuerdo, de 2.700 millones, fue firmado el pasado viernes entre el Departament de Educació y cuatro de los cinco sindicatos: Ustec, CC.OO., Professors de Secundària y UGT. el sindicato anarcosindicalista CGT se descolgó en el último momento al considerar que no se recogían muchas de las medidas de los manifestantes.
El acuerdo supone la contratación de 6.400 profesionales para la inclusiva y una subida del sueldo adicional de 400 euros en cuatro años.

The main teachers' union, Ustec, along with CGT, Intersindical, and COS, has launched a consultation for all teachers in Catalonia regarding the ratification of the preliminary education agreement signed with the Catalan government last Friday.

The question is: “Do you accept the preliminary agreement for teaching staff of May 29th?” Two possible answers are provided: “Yes,” if affirmative, or “No, and I pledge to participate in the necessary strikes until the end of the school year.”
Ustec, which supports the agreement, pledges to call an indefinite strike starting June 8th, a strike that has already been officially registered.

The consultation will be open from Monday until Thursday.
This consultation will be open from tomorrow, Monday, until noon on Thursday. With this result, the rank and file will be mobilized to participate in the strike on Friday, June 5th.

Ustec and Professors de Secundària, which is also consulting its members, have called off the regional strikes from Monday to Thursday, but are maintaining the Friday strike as a precaution.
In contrast, CGT, Intersindical, and COS, minority unions, are maintaining their call for a strike all week because they believe the staff did not vote.
The preliminary agreement, worth 2.7 billion euros, was signed last Friday between the Department of Education and four of the five unions: Ustec, CC.OO., Professors de Secundària, and UGT. The anarcho-syndicalist union CGT withdrew at the last minute, arguing that many of the protesters' demands were not included.

The agreement entails the hiring of 6,400 professionals for inclusive education and an additional salary increase of 400 euros over four years.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
La sanidad pública valenciana afronta una nueva semana de movilizaciones. Los médicos y facultativos de la Comunitat Valenciana han iniciado la quinta semana de huelga intermitente para reclamar mejoras laborales, más recursos humanos y la creación de un Estatuto Marco específico para la profesión médica. Las protestas, que se desarrollarán durante varios días, incluirán concentraciones en hospitales y centros de salud, manifestaciones en València y Alicante y nuevas acciones informativas dirigidas a la ciudadanía.
El conflicto sanitario se ha convertido en uno de los más relevantes del año dentro del sistema público de salud. Según los sindicatos convocantes, las movilizaciones responden a una situación que consideran insostenible debido a la sobrecarga asistencial, la escasez de profesionales y las dificultades para garantizar una atención de calidad en consultas, hospitales y servicios de urgencias.
Desde la Confederación Estatal de Sindicatos Médicos de la Comunitat Valenciana (CESM-CV) insisten en que sus reivindicaciones no se limitan a cuestiones laborales. La organización sostiene que la falta de médicos y el aumento constante de la presión asistencial repercuten directamente en la atención que reciben los pacientes. Por ello, defienden que la huelga busca también proteger la calidad del sistema sanitario público y mejorar las condiciones en las que se presta la asistencia sanitaria.
El acto central de esta nueva semana de protestas tendrá lugar el miércoles con manifestaciones simultáneas en València y Alicante. En la capital valenciana, la marcha partirá a las 18.30 horas desde la Conselleria de Sanidad, recorrerá varios puntos del centro de la ciudad y finalizará frente al Palau de la Generalitat. En Alicante, la movilización comenzará en el Mercado Central y concluirá en la Casa de las Brujas, sede de la Delegación del Consell en la provincia.
Además de las manifestaciones, se han convocado concentraciones en diferentes hospitales y centros sanitarios de las tres provincias. En València, los profesionales están llamados a concentrarse en hospitales como La Fe, el Clínico, el General y el Doctor Peset. En Alicante también habrá protestas en los hospitales de Alicante y San Juan, mientras que en Castellón se han previsto concentraciones en los principales centros sanitarios de la provincia.
Entre las iniciativas previstas destaca también el denominado “Autobús del Cambio”, una acción itinerante que recorrerá varios hospitales de Alicante y San Juan para acercar las reivindicaciones del colectivo médico tanto a los profesionales sanitarios como a los ciudadanos. La campaña pretende explicar las consecuencias que tiene la escasez de personal sobre el funcionamiento diario de los servicios sanitarios y concienciar sobre la situación que atraviesa el sistema público de salud.
Las cifras reflejan la dimensión del conflicto. Los sindicatos aseguran que las jornadas de huelga han provocado ya la suspensión de más de 280.000 actos médicos en la Comunitat Valenciana. Aunque la actividad urgente y los servicios mínimos continúan garantizados, las movilizaciones han afectado especialmente a consultas, revisiones, pruebas diagnósticas y otras actividades programadas, generando retrasos que preocupan tanto a profesionales como a pacientes.
La última huelga antes del verano
Esta convocatoria supone la quinta semana de huelga desde que comenzó el paro indefinido contra el Ministerio de Sanidad y la tercera dirigida específicamente contra la Conselleria de Sanidad valenciana. Sin embargo, los sindicatos han anunciado que esta será la última movilización antes del verano. Argumentan que los meses estivales representan un periodo especialmente delicado para el sistema sanitario debido a las vacaciones del personal, la reducción de plantillas y el incremento de la presión asistencial en determinadas zonas.
Las organizaciones médicas han señalado que, por responsabilidad, no promoverán nuevas jornadas de protesta durante los meses de julio y agosto para evitar un mayor impacto en un momento especialmente complejo para hospitales y centros de salud. No obstante, ya han advertido de que las movilizaciones podrían retomarse a partir de septiembre si no se producen avances significativos en las negociaciones con las administraciones sanitarias.
La nueva semana de huelga llega además pocas semanas después de que el Consejo de Ministros aprobara el anteproyecto de reforma del Estatuto Marco del personal estatutario de los servicios de salud. El texto, impulsado por el Ministerio de Sanidad tras un acuerdo alcanzado con varias organizaciones sindicales representadas en la mesa de negociación, se encuentra actualmente en fase de consulta pública.
Tras la aprobación del anteproyecto, la ministra de Sanidad, Mónica García, convocó una reunión del Consejo Interterritorial del Sistema Nacional de Salud para abordar la reforma y analizar el conflicto abierto con los médicos. Sin embargo, el encuentro concluyó sin acuerdos después de que varias comunidades autónomas rechazaran votar los puntos incluidos en el orden del día relacionados con las reivindicaciones de los profesionales sanitarios.
Mientras tanto, miles de médicos valencianos mantienen sus reivindicaciones y reclaman soluciones que permitan reducir la presión asistencial, reforzar las plantillas y garantizar la sostenibilidad futura de la sanidad pública. El desarrollo de esta nueva semana de protestas será clave para medir el alcance de un conflicto que continúa abierto y que afecta a uno de los servicios públicos más sensibles para la ciudadanía.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
The Valencian public healthcare system faces another week of protests. Doctors and medical professionals in the Valencian Community have begun their fifth week of intermittent strikes to demand improved working conditions, more staff, and the creation of a specific Framework Statute for the medical profession. The protests, which will continue for several days, will include demonstrations at hospitals and health centers, marches in Valencia and Alicante, and new information campaigns aimed at the public.

The healthcare conflict has become one of the most significant of the year within the public health system. According to the organizing unions, the protests are a response to a situation they consider unsustainable due to excessive workloads, staff shortages, and difficulties in guaranteeing quality care in clinics, hospitals, and emergency services.
The State Confederation of Medical Unions of the Valencian Community (CESM-CV) insists that their demands are not limited to labor issues. The organization maintains that the shortage of doctors and the constant increase in pressure on healthcare services directly impact the care patients receive. Therefore, they argue that the strike also aims to protect the quality of the public healthcare system and improve the conditions under which healthcare is provided.

The main event of this new week of protests will take place on Wednesday with simultaneous demonstrations in Valencia and Alicante. In Valencia, the march will begin at 6:30 p.m. from the Ministry of Health, proceed through several points in the city center, and end in front of the Palau de la Generalitat (the seat of the Valencian government). In Alicante, the demonstration will begin at the Central Market and conclude at the Casa de las Brujas (House of the Witches), the headquarters of the Valencian Government Delegation in the province.

In addition to the demonstrations, gatherings have been called at various hospitals and healthcare centers in the three provinces. In Valencia, healthcare professionals are expected to gather at hospitals such as La Fe, Clínico, General, and Doctor Peset. In Alicante, protests will also take place at the hospitals in Alicante and San Juan, while in Castellón, demonstrations are planned at the province's main healthcare centers.

Among the planned initiatives is the "Change Bus," a mobile campaign that will travel to several hospitals in Alicante and San Juan to bring the demands of the medical community closer to both healthcare professionals and the public. The campaign aims to explain the consequences of staff shortages on the daily operation of healthcare services and raise awareness of the situation facing the public health system.

The figures reflect the scale of the conflict. Unions assert that the strike days have already led to the cancellation of more than 280,000 medical procedures in the Valencian Community. Although urgent care and minimum services remain guaranteed, the mobilizations have particularly affected appointments, check-ups, diagnostic tests, and other scheduled activities, generating delays that are a concern for both professionals and patients.

The Last Strike Before Summer
This strike marks the fifth week of action since the indefinite strike against the Ministry of Health began, and the third specifically targeting the Valencian Health Department. However, the unions have announced that this will be the last mobilization before summer. They argue that the summer months represent a particularly delicate period for the healthcare system due to staff vacations, staff reductions, and increased pressure on services in certain areas.

Medical organizations have indicated that, out of a sense of responsibility, they will not promote further days of protest during July and August to avoid a greater impact at a particularly complex time for hospitals and health centers. Nevertheless, they have already warned that mobilizations could resume in September if significant progress is not made in negotiations with the health authorities.
This new week of strike action also comes just weeks after the Council of Ministers approved the draft bill to reform the Framework Statute for Statutory Personnel of the Health Services. The text, promoted by the Ministry of Health after an agreement reached with several labor unions represented at the negotiating table, is currently in the public consultation phase.

Following the approval of the draft bill, the Minister of Health, Mónica García, convened a meeting of the Interterritorial Council of the National Health System to address the reform and analyze the ongoing conflict with doctors. However, the meeting concluded without agreements after several autonomous communities refused to vote on the agenda items related to the demands of healthcare professionals.

Meanwhile, thousands of doctors in the Valencian Community are maintaining their demands and calling for solutions that will reduce the pressure on healthcare services, reinforce staffing levels, and guarantee the future sustainability of the public healthcare system. The development of this new week of protests will be key to gauging the scope of a conflict that remains unresolved and affects one of the most vital public services for citizens.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
La Asociación Bancaria llevó adelante este miércoles una jornada de protesta en Rosario con interrupción de actividades en el Banco Hipotecario. La medida se realizó en rechazo al cierre de sucursales y a la reducción de personal que afecta a distintas provincias del país.
En la ciudad, la atención al público en el Banco Hipotecario permanecerá totalmente paralizada entre las 10:15 y las 13:15. La protesta se llevó a cabo en la sede de calle Santa Fe y contó con el acompañamiento de delegados de otras entidades bancarias.
Desde el sindicato explicaron que la medida forma parte de una acción coordinada a nivel nacional impulsada por La Bancaria. Según detalló Sergio Rivolta, secretario general del gremio en Rosario, el reclamo apunta a frenar el cierre de oficinas y los despidos que comenzaron a aplicarse en distintas sucursales del Banco Hipotecario en el país.
El dirigente sostuvo que en Rosario todavía no se anunciaron cierres ni reducción de personal, aunque advirtió que existe preocupación por la posibilidad de que las medidas también alcancen a la ciudad. En ese sentido, consideró que la protesta busca anticiparse a un eventual ajuste local y defender las fuentes de trabajo.
Rivolta además vinculó las decisiones empresariales con la política económica nacional y aseguró que, según el análisis del gremio, varias de las sucursales afectadas eran rentables. Por eso, desde el sindicato interpretan que el proceso responde más a una estrategia política que a una necesidad financiera.
El reclamo también incluyó críticas al cierre de tesoros regionales del Banco Central. La Bancaria denunció que el Gobierno nacional dispuso la clausura de 12 de los 21 centros operativos existentes en el país, una situación que, aseguran, no solo perjudica a los trabajadores, sino también a las comunidades que dependían de esos servicios.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:

In Rosario, customer service at Banco Hipotecario will be completely paralyzed between 10:15 AM and 1:15 PM. The protest took place at the branch on Santa Fe Street and was supported by delegates from other banks.

The union explained that the action is part of a coordinated nationwide effort led by La Bancaria. According to Sergio Rivolta, the union's general secretary in Rosario, the protest aims to halt the branch closures and layoffs that have begun at various Banco Hipotecario branches nationwide.

The union leader stated that no closures or staff reductions have yet been announced in Rosario, but warned of concerns that these measures could also affect the city. In that sense, he considered that the protest seeks to anticipate a possible local restructuring and defend jobs.

Rivolta also linked the business decisions to national economic policy and asserted that, according to the union's analysis, several of the affected branches were profitable. Therefore, the union interprets the process as a political strategy rather than a financial necessity.

The protest also included criticism of the closure of the Central Bank's regional branches. The Banking Union denounced that the national government ordered the closure of 12 of the 21 existing operational centers in the country, a situation that, they claim, not only harms the workers but also the communities that depended on those services.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Greenpeace to take legal action against JBS for expansion plans in Netherlands
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Een groep van 48 Greenpeace-actievoerders heeft de eerste aandeelhoudersvergadering van vleesgigant JBS in Nederland verstoord. De actievoerders hingen een spandoek met druipend nepbloed en de tekst: ‘JBS: Keep your bloody business out of Africa’ aan het Sheraton hotel op Schiphol, waar de vergadering plaatsvond. In de hal van het hotel wordt ook een metershoog spandoek met dezelfde tekst opgehangen. De actievoerders betraden de vergaderzaal en Greenpeace directeur Marieke Vellekoop bood het informatieverzoek aan de aandeelhouders van JBS aan, wat de eerste stap is naar juridische actie tegen de uitbreidingsplannen van JBS. Greenpeace wil dat JBS van de destructieve groeiplannen afziet. De aandeelhoudersvergadering is stilgelegd.
Isabel Willemsen, campagneleider biodiversiteit Greenpeace Nederland: ‘Wij zijn hier vandaag om de wereldwijde verwoesting van JBS te stoppen. Terwijl het Amazonewoud verdwijnt en de aarde opwarmt, wil deze vleesgigant verder uitbreiden en nog meer natuur verwoesten – ten koste van mensen en een leefbare aarde. Met hun verhuizing naar Nederland hebben zij zich ook aan de Nederlandse wet te houden. Dat geeft ons de kans nu juridische stappen te zetten. Met deze actie kondigen we die stappen aan en zetten we de spotlight op de bloody business van deze vleesmiljardairs.’’
Ontbossing en natuurverwoesting
Vleesgigant JBS is het grootste en een van de meest vervuilende vleesbedrijven ter wereld. Het bedrijf draagt bij aan ontbossing en natuurverwoesting in de Amazone en uit onderzoek blijkt dat de methaanuitstoot van het bedrijf hoger is dan die van Shell en ExxonMobil samen. JBS is in staat om elke dag 14 miljoen dieren te slachten. De multinational is daarnaast ook in verband gebracht met corruptieschandalen en mensenrechtenschendingen. JBS is van oorsprong een Braziliaanse multinational, maar sinds vorig jaar is het hoofdkantoor (op papier) in Nederland gevestigd.
Destructieve groeiplannen
JBS heeft aangekondigd tussen de 5 en 6 miljard dollar te investeren in nieuwe projecten wereldwijd. Het grootste gedeelte daarvan wordt geïnvesteerd in Nigeria, om nieuwe vleesverwerkingsfabrieken en infrastructuur te realiseren. Op dit moment bestaat er nog geen intensieve veehouderij in Nigeria en wordt vee door lokale boeren op kleine schaal gehouden en verkregen uit buurlanden. Het grootste deel van het vlees dat JBS in Nigeria gaat produceren is bestemd voor export naar het Midden-Oosten en dus niet voor de Nigeriaanse bevolking zelf.
Elizabeth Atieno, campaigner bij Greenpeace Afrika: “De groei van het vleesimperium van JBS gaat hand in hand met milieuvernietiging, enorme uitstoot, mensenrechtenschendingen, corruptie en een totaal gebrek aan transparantie. Nu is het bedrijf van plan dit bedrijfsmodel naar Sub-Sahara Afrika te exporteren. De roofzuchtige expansie van JBS in Nigeria zorgt er niet alleen voor dat de uitstoot de komende decennia blijft stijgen, maar dreigt ook onomkeerbare milieuschade te veroorzaken en kleine boeren te verdrijven om de zakken van rijke internationale elites te vullen.”
Juridische stap tegen JBS
JBS en de Nigeriaanse overheid geven, ondanks verzoeken van lokale groepen, geen openheid van zaken over de deal die zij gesloten hebben en de impact die dat heeft op de lokale bevolking. A group of 48 Greenpeace activists disrupted the first shareholders' meeting of meat giant JBS in the Netherlands. The activists hung a banner featuring dripping fake blood and the text: ‘JBS: Keep your bloody business out of Africa’ at the Sheraton Hotel at Schiphol, where the meeting was taking place. A banner several meters high with the same text is also being hung in the hotel lobby. The activists entered the meeting room, and Greenpeace Director Marieke Vellekoop presented the request for information to JBS shareholders, which is the first step toward legal action against JBS’s expansion plans. Greenpeace wants JBS to abandon the destructive growth plans. The shareholders' meeting has been suspended.

Isabel Willemsen, Biodiversity Campaign Leader Greenpeace Netherlands: ‘We are here today to stop the global destruction caused by JBS. While the Amazon rainforest is disappearing and the earth is warming, this meat giant wants to expand further and destroy even more nature – at the expense of people and a livable earth.’ With their move to the Netherlands, they are also required to comply with Dutch law. This gives us the opportunity to take legal action now. With this action, we are announcing those steps and shining a spotlight on the bloody business of these meat billionaires.

Deforestation and environmental destruction
Meat giant JBS is the largest and one of the most polluting meat companies in the world. The company contributes to deforestation and environmental destruction in the Amazon, and research shows that the company's methane emissions are higher than those of Shell and ExxonMobil combined. JBS is capable of slaughtering 14 million animals every day. The multinational has also been linked to corruption scandals and human rights violations. JBS is originally a Brazilian multinational, but since last year, its headquarters have been (on paper) based in the Netherlands.

Destructive growth plans
JBS has announced it will invest between 5 and 6 billion dollars in new projects worldwide. The largest portion of this will be invested in Nigeria to realize new meat processing plants and infrastructure. Currently, there is no intensive livestock farming in Nigeria, and cattle are kept on a small scale by local farmers and sourced from neighboring countries. The majority of the meat that JBS will produce in Nigeria is destined for export to the Middle East and therefore not for the Nigerian population itself.

Elizabeth Atieno, campaigner at Greenpeace Africa: “The growth of the JBS meat empire goes hand in hand with environmental destruction, massive emissions, human rights violations, corruption, and a total lack of transparency. Now the company plans to export this business model to Sub-Saharan Africa. The predatory expansion of JBS in Nigeria not only ensures that emissions continue to rise over the coming decades but also threatens to cause irreversible environmental damage and displace small farmers to fill the pockets of wealthy international elites.”

Legal action against JBS
Despite requests from local groups, JBS and the Nigerian government are not providing any transparency regarding the deal they have concluded and the impact this has on the local population. Civil society organizations in Nigeria have expressed serious concerns regarding the environmental, health, and social risks associated with the expansion plans.

Greenpeace and local civil society organizations are demanding transparency from JBS regarding its growth plans. Therefore, Greenpeace Netherlands is taking legal action and has sent an official letter requesting JBS to release more information regarding the environmental impact of its activities. If JBS does not comply with this request, Greenpeace Netherlands will file a petition with the court to obtain the requested information. Greenpeace argues that the environmental damage and methane emissions caused by JBS's activities violate the Dutch duty of care, and that JBS's expansion plans in Nigeria and beyond will exacerbate this damage.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Severe overcrowding at a primary school in Alexandra has prompted protests by parents and raised concerns about conditions in Gauteng schools.
Parents of children at Bovet Primary School recently staged a protest, saying conditions were not suitable for learning because some children were forced to sit on the floor due to a lack of desks and space.
General secretary of the National Association of School Governing Bodies, Matakanye Matakanya, said the situation is a “very serious matter” that does not make educational sense. He questioned how pupils were expected to write and concentrate in such conditions.
“It is unacceptable,” he said.
Matakanya said the issue has been raised with the basic education department, but little progress has been made.
“We said let’s come together and see how best we can solve this matter,” he said, adding the situation was worsened by the closure of some schools that could be used to ease overcrowding.
“Overcrowding makes classroom management more difficult and often forces teachers into “survival-based teaching.”
— Prof Veronica Dwarika
He said expecting teachers to perform under such conditions was unrealistic, especially with classes of up to 90 pupils, and he defended parents’ right to protest.
“Somebody must hear them,” he said.
The South African Democratic Teachers Union said overcrowded classrooms are placing a strain on pupils and teachers. Spokesperson Nomusa Cembi said large class sizes made it difficult for teachers to give individual attention, meaning some pupils are left behind.
“One teacher cannot give individual attention if there are too many pupils,” she said.
She said the situation is stressful for teachers and makes effective teaching difficult. “It is unhealthy, it is hazardous and it does not benefit education at all,” she said, raising concerns about safety and limited movement in overcrowded classrooms.
Cembi said teachers receive little support in such conditions and called for urgent intervention, including building more classrooms and hiring more teachers.
An education expert from the University of Johannesburg said the crisis went beyond a lack of infrastructure and posed serious risks to learning and child development.
Prof Veronica Dwarika, head of department and educational psychologist in the faculty of education, said overcrowded classrooms are a major barrier to academic achievement, especially in the early years when individual attention is critical. In such environments, teachers are unable to give feedback, support struggling pupils or identify learning difficulties, meaning many pupils “fall through the cracks”.
She said large class sizes also reduced the quality of teaching as teachers cannot adapt lessons to meet different learning needs or use interactive teaching methods.
The impact is not only academic. Dwarika said overcrowded classrooms are linked to stress, frustration and reduced participation among pupils, with noise and distraction making it harder to concentrate.
“For young children, learning is relational and interactive,” she said, warning cramped conditions and sitting on the floor can affect pupils’ motivation, self-esteem and sense of belonging.
I am a resident of that community. I’m fully aware of the matter and am part of co-ordinating the solutions
— Onwabile Lubhelwana, Gauteng education MEC spokesperson
She said overcrowding makes classroom management more difficult and often forces teachers into “survival-based teaching”, where the focus shifts to maintaining order rather than meaningful learning. This places a heavy emotional burden on teachers, contributing to stress, fatigue and burnout over time.
Dwarika said a class of more than 90 pupils is far beyond acceptable norms and highlights deep inequalities in the education system, particularly in under-resourced communities.
Gauteng education MEC spokesperson Onwabile Lubhelwana said the department is aware of the situation and working on solutions. “I am a resident of that community. I’m fully aware of the matter and am part of co-ordinating the solutions,” he said.
He said Alexandra is densely populated and lacks land for new schools, but the department is exploring options to identify new sites. In the meantime, mobile classrooms and additional furniture are being arranged.
“We urge parents not to disrupt teaching and learning,” he added.
The situation at Bovet reflects wider challenges facing the province’s education system. Gauteng education MEC Lebogang Maile recently said pupil enrolment has more than doubled from about 1.4-million in 1995 to more than 2.8-million in 2026, driven by urbanisation and migration.
He said overcrowding remains a major issue, particularly in township and inner-city schools, where classes can reach between 60 and 70 pupils per teacher. About 723 schools across Gauteng were affected by overcrowding, with a shortage of more than 5,500 classrooms.
The province needs at least 200 new schools, but delays in infrastructure projects continue to put pressure on the system.

"Meanwhile, other healthcare professionals, such as physiotherapists, speech therapists, occupational therapists, podiatrists, and home health care services, have joined the protests. Nationwide, resistance is forming against the planned cuts in both outpatient and inpatient care."

If the other proposals from Berlin are taken into account, many practices will hardly be economically viable anymore. "The dissatisfaction among most of our medical colleagues is growing because, given the extreme time and economic pressure, we are being forced to provide 'poor' medicine that doesn't meet our standards," complain the doctors in Leichlingen.

They plan to draw attention to these problems on Wednesday. A rally will be held at 10 a.m. at the Leichlingen weekly market near Postwiese/Wupperbrücke, where the practice of a general practitioner covered by public health insurance will be symbolically buried. Citizens can also sign a petition against the austerity measures.
