Fridays for Future Demonstrates Against "Wrong Turns" on Bicycles

The "Fridays for Future" bicycle demonstration criticized the energy policy of the Berlin coalition. Economics Minister Reiche was a particular target.

By Manfred Ofer
Mannheim. As part of the nationwide climate strikes by the "Fridays for Future" movement, a demonstration was also called for in Mannheim last Friday. In the end, around 200 participants set off on bicycles for a protest march through the city center. Key demands included a complete phase-out of gas and a rapid and just energy transition. Criticism was also leveled at Federal Economics Minister Katherina Reiche.

"We are here, we are loud, because you are stealing our future!": This slogan was heard repeatedly in Mannheim on Friday. In front of the water tower, the activists mounted their bicycles and set off to emphasize their demands.

Linus Wöllner, spokesperson for the local "Fridays for Future" group, subsequently gave a positive assessment of the event. "We hadn't expected this," he said, pleased with the large turnout. "Today in Mannheim, we sent a strong message in support of the energy transition and against the current government policies." He added that they had succeeded in giving voice to the anger shared by many and channeling it constructively. The protest was directed particularly at the wealthy, especially regarding the need for a rapid and equitable energy and transportation transition. It was repeatedly stated that they and the CDU were well on their way to sabotaging the progress already made. The accusation: lobbying for fossil fuel companies. Instead, they argued, what was needed was an expansion of renewable energies, storage capacities, and a sustainable heat supply.

The activists and their supporters expected the federal government to actively promote socially just climate protection. They saw the SPD, as the CDU's coalition partner, as having a particular responsibility in this regard. Speakers addressing participants at the stops along the bike demonstration at Paradeplatz and Alter Messplatz spoke out against the promotion of fossil fuels and in favor of subsidizing renewable energy and heat pumps.

Also of interest:

"Fridays for Future" demonstration in Heidelberg: For the winegrowers, the protest against the South German natural gas pipeline comes too late.

Martin (45) was one of those who joined the demonstrators in front of the water tower on Friday. The mechanical engineer had traveled from Mühlhausen in the Kraichgau region to advocate for adhering to climate goals instead of, as he emphasized, further fueling the climate crisis. He brought a sign he had made with his children. "The government is setting the wrong course," he declared. He shared the frequently cited accusation on Friday that those politically responsible were giving a platform to the fossil fuel lobby.

Kijaron (18) and Matthäus (17) attend the Bach Gymnasium in Mannheim and are active in "Fridays for Future." “If I have children, I want them to grow up in the same beautiful world I did,” said Kijaron. They were aware that interest in their cause had noticeably declined recently. That's why actions like the one in Mannheim were so important. The unexpectedly high number of participants encouraged them to continue working for a better future. A future that Matthäus also viewed with concern. “I see our government's energy policy as more of a step backward,” he remarked before setting off by bicycle to Paradeplatz.

At this first stop, Wöllner and Nicky Franz from “Fridays for Future” took the floor, using a staged conversation to explore the positive energy of anger. Anger that they were witnessing the energy transition, which they consider so crucial for their future, being reversed by current attitudes in politics and society. Resignation, however, was not an option. They would and must continue to work for the common good.

Clemens Fiebig of the "Parents for Future" network initiative warned of a political and strategic reversal that would lead society toward climate catastrophe. At the Old Fairground, Manfred Stindl of the German Transport Club (VCD) was among those who spoke, advocating for environmentally friendly, safe, and healthy mobility. Sinan (18), a high school graduate from the Waldorf School in Mannheim, criticized the German government for pursuing an energy policy that would benefit future generations.

The activists felt encouraged by the turnout over the weekend. Further actions are planned.

TGSRTC Resume Bus Services after 3-Day Strike, Relief for Passengers Telangana M Srinivas 25 April 2026 8:31 AM IST 25 April 2026 8:31 AM IST The MGBS, JBS and other busy bus stations in twin cities teemed with passengers since morning to reach their destinations x Three days after observing strike in support of their demands, the employees of TGSRTC started operating buses from Saturday morning bringing much needed relief for passengers especially women and students. (File Photo) Hyderabad: Three days after observing strike in support of their demands, the employees of TGSRTC started operating buses from Saturday morning bringing much needed relief for passengers especially women and students.
The ever-busy Mahatma Gandhi Bus Station (MGBS) in Afzalgunj, Jubilee Bus Station (JBS), and Ranigunj I and II depots in Secunderabad, among others wore a deserted look for the last three days due to the strike.
As the employees called off their strike after the State government conceded to their demands, the drivers started operating the buses. The MGBS, JBS and other busy bus stations in twin cities teemed with passengers since morning to reach their destinations.
As many weddings were scheduled on Sunday, several families utilized RTC bus services to reach relatives’ houses. Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka held discussions with the RTC JAC unions till late night on Friday at Secretariat.
After discussions were concluded successfully, the JAC leaders announced that they were calling off the strike. The government agreed to all the 32 demands of the JAC including 11 per cent PRC and willingness for merger of RTC into the government apart from giving its nod to hold elections.
For the last three days, private transport operators fleeced passengers charging exorbitant prices. Left with no other option, the passengers had to shell out more to these operators.
( Source : Deccan Chronicle )

Σε συγκέντρωση διαμαρτυρίας έξω από το κτίριο του υπουργείου Παιδείας, Θρησκευμάτων και Αθλητισμού στις 13:00 καλεί η Διδασκαλική Ομοσπονδία Ελλάδος (ΔΟΕ), αντιδρώντας στις «δραστικές περικοπές στους διορισμούς μόνιμων εκπαιδευτικών και αναπληρωτών», καθώς επίσης και την επιλογή διδακτικών βιβλίων εν όψει εφαρμογής του πολλαπλού βιβλίου.
Με επιστολή της χθες η ΔΟΕΑ ζήτησε να πραγματοποιηθεί συνάντηση με την ηγεσία του υπουργείου Παιδείας, στο πλαίσιο της παρουσίας των εκπαιδευτικών έξω από το κτίριο του υπουργείου.

Ειδικότερα, στην επιστολή εκφράστηκε η ανησυχία της ΔΟΕ σχετικά με τη διαδικασία και το χρονοδιάγραμμα της επιλογής σχολικών εγχειριδίων. «Εντός 10 εργάσιμων ημερών και μάλιστα στο τέλος της σχολικής χρονιάς, χιλιάδες εκπαιδευτικοί καλούνται να επιλέξουν, χωρίς καμία προετοιμασία και χωρίς να έχουν λάβει επαρκή γνώση του περιεχομένου των εγχειριδίων, τα βιβλία που θα διδαχτούν οι μαθητές για το σχολικό έτος 2027-2028», ανέφερε η ΔΟΕ, σημειώνοντας ότι «η επιλογή σχολικών εγχειριδίων αποτελεί μια εξαιρετικά σημαντική, παιδαγωγική απόφαση».

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Fahrraddemo auf zwei Autobahnen: Unter dem Motto «Zukunft statt Beton» haben in Frankfurt Tausende Radler und Radlerinnen gegen einen zehnspurigen Ausbau der A5 protestiert. Ihre Route führt unter anderem über die A648 und die A66, eine Abschlusskundgebung mit Redebeträgen und Diskussionsrunde war auf dem Frankfurter Opernplatz geplant.
Dort war auch der Start der Demo, zu der rund 2.500 Menschen erwartet wurden, die auf mehreren Zubringerrouten zum Opernplatz gelangten. «Wir wehren uns gehen die Pläne, die Autobahn A5 von heute sechs auf zehn Spuren zu erweitern», hieß es im Aufruf zur Demo.
Nicht die erste Demo gegen den Ausbau
«Mehr Fahrstreifen lösen aus wissenschaftlicher Sicht keine Verkehrsprobleme, da durch ein verbessertes Angebot auch mehr Menschen aufs Auto umsteigen», erklärte das Bündnis «Stopp A5-Ausbau», dem auch Parteien und Verbände angehören.
Schon im September 2024 gab es eine Fahrraddemonstration auf der Autobahn gegen den Ausbau. Die Polizei schätzte die Teilnehmerzahl damals auf 4.000. Bereits damals sollte die Demonstration auch über die A5 führen, dies wurde jedoch von der Stadt Frankfurt untersagt. Die Entscheidung hatte vor Gericht Bestand.
Im Juni 2024 waren Ergebnisse einer Untersuchung veröffentlicht worden, die die technische Machbarkeit des Ausbaus vom Frankfurter Kreuz bis zur Anschlussstelle Friedberg auf bis zu zehn Streifen ergab. Weitere Untersuchungen seien aber erforderlich, hieß es von der Autobahn GmbH.

TRANSLATED_TEXT:
A bicycle demonstration took place on two highways: Under the motto "Future instead of concrete," thousands of cyclists protested in Frankfurt against the planned ten-lane expansion of the A5 motorway. Their route led them along the A648 and A66 motorways, among others. A final rally with speeches and a panel discussion was planned at Frankfurt's Opera Square.

The demonstration, which was expected to draw around 2,500 people, started there, with several feeder routes leading to the square. "We are resisting the plans to expand the A5 motorway from its current six lanes to ten," stated the call to action.

This is not the first demonstration against the expansion.

"From a scientific perspective, more lanes do not solve traffic problems, as an improved infrastructure simply leads to more people switching to cars," explained the "Stop A5 Expansion" alliance, which includes political parties and associations.

A bicycle demonstration against the expansion already took place on the motorway in September 2024. Police estimated the number of participants at 4,000 at the time. The demonstration was also planned to proceed along the A5 motorway, but this was prohibited by the city of Frankfurt. The decision was upheld in court.

In June 2024, the results of a study were published, which determined the technical feasibility of expanding the motorway from the Frankfurter Kreuz interchange to the Friedberg exit to up to ten lanes. MESSAGE_TEXT:
Brenner-Blockade: Acht Stunden kein Transit möglich
Damit ist die wichtigste Nord-Süd-Verbindung der Alpen zeitweise unpassierbar. Initiiert hat den Protest der Bürgermeister der Gemeinde Gries am Brenner, Karl Mühlsteiger.
Was ist der Grund der Demonstration?
Die Verkehrsflut am Brenner. Die 15.000 Bewohner des Wipptales, von denen viele in unmittelbarer Nähe von Autobahn und Bundesstraße leben, leiden unter Lärm, Feinstaub und vielen Beeinträchtigungen im täglichen Leben durch häufige Staus auf allen Strecken. Fast elf Millionen Autos und rund 2,5 Millionen Lastwagen haben 2025 laut Autobahnbetreiber Asfinag die mautpflichtige Autobahn benutzt. Bei den Lkw beträgt der Zuwachs seit 2010 rund 40 Prozent. Seit Inbetriebnahme der Brennerautobahn in den 1960er Jahren hat sich das Verkehrsaufkommen laut Asfinag fast versiebenfacht.
Warum lässt die Justiz die Demonstration zu?
Während bisherige Demonstrations-Versuche wegen eines drohenden Verkehrskollapses nicht genehmigt wurden, weicht das Landesverwaltungsgericht Tirol in seinem Urteil ab. „Eine Untersagung der Demonstration gegen eine hohe Verkehrsbelastung mit einer hohen Verkehrsbelastung zu begründen, führt im Grunde die Versammlungsfreiheit ad absurdum“, heißt es in dem Richterspruch. Es sei Sinn der Versammlungs- und Meinungsfreiheit aufzurütteln und zu provozieren, was auch für die Allgemeinheit unangenehm sein könne.
Mit welchen Behinderungen ist zu rechnen?
In dem achtstündigen Zeitraum passieren normalerweise Zehntausende Fahrzeuge den Brenner. Die Blockade fällt mitten in den Pfingstferien von Bayern und Baden-Württemberg sowie ans Ferienende in Sachsen-Anhalt. Die Polizei rechnet mit einer sehr schwierigen Situation auf den Straßen.
Bereits an den Landesgrenzen – also weit vor dem Brenner – werden Fahrzeuge kontrolliert und Fahrer informiert. Sollte es zu einem Verkehrskollaps kommen, droht eine Dosierung des Verkehrs. Auch vor und nach der Sperre dürfte es zu erheblichen Staus kommen.
Kommt wirklich niemand durch?
In der betroffenen Region ist jeglicher Transitverkehr in dem Zeitraum verboten. Erlaubt ist Ziel- und Quellverkehr. Wer also in einem Ort zum Beispiel im Stubaital ein Hotel gebucht hat und das nachweisen kann, darf die Sperre passieren. Radfahrer dürfen die Landstraße zum Brenner benutzen.
Warum ist der Brenner so wichtig?
Seit Tausenden Jahren nutzen Reisende und Geschäftsleute den mit 1.370 Metern niedrigsten Übergang zwischen Österreich und Italien. In den 1960er Jahren wurde die Brennerautobahn gebaut. Die 1963 eröffnete Europabrücke nahe der Mautstelle Schönberg war mit ihren 190 Metern über Grund zeitweise die höchste Brücke Europas. Gerade für Lastwagen ist der Pass attraktiv – sowohl wegen seiner geringen Steigung als auch der im Vergleich zu anderen Übergängen niedrigeren Maut.
Welche Alternativen gibt es?
Für den 30. Mai und auch sonst gibt es auf der Fahrt nach Südtirol und anderen Zielen in Italien zumindest auf dem Papier Alternativen zum Brenner. Dazu zählen der Reschenpass, das Timmelsjoch in Österreich, der Gotthardtunnel und der San-Bernadino-Tunnel in der Schweiz. Der Nachteil: Fast alle diese Routen sind deutlich mühsamer und zeitaufwendiger.
Eine elegante Alternative könnte der Zug sein. Der braucht von Innsbruck bis nach Franzensfeste auf der italienischen Seite heute 80 Minuten. Wenn der Brenner-Basistunnel im Jahr 2032 in Betrieb geht, rauschen die Züge für den Personen- und Güterverkehr mit Tempo 200 durch die rund 64 Kilometer lange Röhre. Die Fahrtzeit für die Strecke beträgt dann nur noch 25 Minuten.

TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Brenner Pass Blockade: Eight Hours of Transit Impossible

This means the most important north-south connection in the Alps is temporarily impassable. The protest was initiated by the mayor of the municipality of Gries am Brenner, Karl Mühlsteiger.

What is the reason for the demonstration?

The flood of traffic at the Brenner Pass. The 15,000 residents of the Wipptal valley, many of whom live in the immediate vicinity of the motorway and main road, suffer from noise, particulate matter, and numerous disruptions to their daily lives due to frequent traffic jams on all routes. According to motorway operator Asfinag, almost eleven million cars and around 2.5 million trucks used the toll motorway in 2025. The increase in truck traffic since 2010 is around 40 percent. Since the Brenner motorway opened in the 1960s, traffic volume has increased almost sevenfold, according to Asfinag.

Why is the court allowing the demonstration?

While previous attempts to hold demonstrations were not permitted due to the threat of a traffic collapse, the Tyrolean Administrative Court has deviated from this ruling. "To justify prohibiting a demonstration against heavy traffic with heavy traffic is essentially a mockery of freedom of assembly," the court ruling states. The purpose of freedom of assembly and expression is to provoke and challenge, even if it might be unpleasant for the general public.

What disruptions can be expected?
Tens of thousands of vehicles normally cross the Brenner Pass during the eight-hour period. The blockade coincides with the Pentecost holidays in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, as well as the end of the holidays in Saxony-Anhalt. Police anticipate a very difficult situation on the roads.

Vehicles will be checked and drivers informed well before the Brenner Pass, even at the state borders. If a traffic collapse occurs, traffic flow will be regulated. Significant traffic jams are also expected before and after the closure.

Will no one be able to get through?
All transit traffic is prohibited in the affected region during this period. Local traffic is permitted. Anyone who has booked a hotel in a town, for example in the Stubai Valley, and can prove it, is allowed to pass through the closure. Cyclists are permitted to use the country road to the Brenner Pass.

Why is the Brenner Pass so important?
For thousands of years, travelers and businesspeople have used the lowest crossing between Austria and Italy, at 1,370 meters. The Brenner motorway was built in the 1960s. The Europa Bridge, opened in 1963 near the Schönberg toll station, was, at 190 meters above ground, temporarily the highest bridge in Europe. The pass is particularly attractive for trucks – both because of its gentle gradient and the lower toll compared to other crossings.

What alternatives are there? For May 30th and at other times, there are, at least on paper, alternatives to the Brenner Pass for traveling to South Tyrol and other destinations in Italy. These include the Reschen Pass, the Timmelsjoch Pass in Austria, the Gotthard Tunnel, and the San Bernardino Tunnel in Switzerland. The downside: Almost all of these routes are significantly more arduous and time-consuming.

An elegant alternative could be the train. Currently, it takes 80 minutes to travel from Innsbruck to Franzensfeste on the Italian side. When the Brenner Base Tunnel opens in 2032, passenger and freight trains will speed through the approximately 64-kilometer-long tunnel at 200 km/h. The journey time will then be just 25 minutes.

(dpa/KO)

راجوری//گورنمنٹ میڈیکل کالج راجوری کے نان گزیٹڈ ملازمین نے پیر کے روز سروس ریکروٹمنٹ رولز کی تشکیل اور حتمی منظوری میں طویل تاخیر کے خلاف دو روزہ پُرامن احتجاج شروع کیا۔ یہ قواعد 2019 سے زیر التوا ہیں۔احتجاج میں نرسنگ، پیرا میڈیکل، منسٹریل اور ملٹی ٹاسکنگ اسٹاف (ایم ٹی ایس) زمرے سے تعلق رکھنے والے ملازمین نے شرکت کی۔ مظاہرین نے سات سالہ تاخیر کو ان کی پیشہ ورانہ ترقی اور ملازمت کے تحفظ کے لیے ایک سنگین دھچکہ قرار دیا۔
احتجاج کی قیادت جی ایم سی راجوری کے نان گزیٹڈ ملازمین کی نمائندگی کرتے ہوئے سندیپ نارنیا، سومیش سودن، وشو شرما اور ابھیشیک شرما نے کی۔اجتماع سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے احتجاجی ملازمین نے کہا کہ سروس ریکروٹمنٹ رولز کو حتمی شکل نہ دیے جانے سے جموں و کشمیر کے نئے قائم شدہ میڈیکل کالجوں میں کام کر رہے ہزاروں ملازمین کی ترقیوں، تنخواہی ڈھانچے، کیریئر میں پیش رفت اور دیگر سروس فوائد پر منفی اثر پڑا ہے۔ملازمین نے وزیر صحت اور محکمہ صحت و طبی تعلیم سے اپیل کی کہ وہ فوری مداخلت کرتے ہوئے اس طویل عرصے سے زیر التوا مسئلے کو بلا تاخیر حل کریں۔احتجاج کے باوجود ایمرجنسی خدمات، آؤٹ پیشنٹ ڈیپارٹمنٹس (او پی ڈیز) اور معمول کی اختیاری آپریشن تھیٹر خدمات مکمل طور پر فعال رہیں، جس سے مریضوں کی دیکھ بھال اور عوامی فلاح کے تئیں ملازمین کے عزم کا اظہار ہوا۔احتجاج پُرامن طور پر اختتام پذیر ہوا، تاہم ملازمین نے خبردار کیا کہ اگر ان کے مطالبات پورے نہ کیے گئے تو احتجاج دوسرے دن بھی جاری رہے گا۔

Uzma News Service
RAJOURI//Non-gazetted employees of Government Medical College Rajouri on Monday began a two-day peaceful protest against the long delay in the formulation and final approval of the service recruitment rules. The rules have been pending since 2019. The protest was attended by employees belonging to the nursing, paramedical, ministerial and multi-tasking staff (MTS) categories. The protesters termed the seven-year delay as a serious setback to their professional development and job security.
The protest was led by Sandeep Narnia, Somesh Sudan, Vishwa Sharma and Abhishek Sharma, representing the non-gazetted employees of GMC Rajouri. Addressing the gathering, the protesting employees said that the non-finalization of the service recruitment rules has adversely affected the promotions, pay structure, career progression and other service benefits of thousands of employees working in the newly established medical colleges of Jammu and Kashmir. The employees appealed to the Health Minister and the Department of Health and Medical Education to intervene immediately and resolve this long-pending issue without delay. Despite the protest, emergency services, outpatient departments (OPDs) and routine elective operation theatre services remained fully functional, demonstrating the employees’ commitment to patient care and public welfare. The protest ended peacefully, however, the employees warned that the protest would continue for the second day if their demands were not met.

Demonstrations this Saturday, May 2, 2026, in Mexico City: Where and when will there be marches and blockades?

This is the schedule of mobilizations for this Saturday in Mexico City: there will be marches, blockades, and bike rides, as well as cultural, artistic, and sporting events. Mexico City will experience a day of high social, cultural, and recreational activity this May 2, 2026, headlined by the 26th World Marijuana Liberation Day March, which is expected to gather approximately 900 people in the city center, according to the mobilization schedule of the Secretariat of Citizen Security (SSC).

In addition to this march, Mexico City authorities have registered four gatherings, six bike rides (motorcycles and bicycles), and 28 recreational events, which could cause traffic disruptions in various parts of the city. Marches Today in Mexico City
- Cannabis March to Depart from the Palace of Fine Arts towards Reforma Avenue
The main event of the day will be the march organized by the Mexican Cannabis Movement, scheduled for 2:00 p.m. at the esplanade of the Palace of Fine Arts, in the Cuauhtémoc borough.

The group will proceed to the Angel of Independence monument along Paseo de la Reforma. Organizers are demanding free access to cannabis, the right to home cultivation, and respect for its various uses, as well as an end to discrimination against cannabis users.
Political and cultural activities will take place at the beginning and end of the march. The participation of other groups in favor of decriminalization is also possible.

Throughout the day, several gatherings will also take place in the capital:
- At 12:00 PM, the Plataforma 4:20 collective will meet at the Monumento a la Madre (Monument to the Mother) to hold cultural activities and promote rights related to cannabis use (estimated attendance: 50 people).

- At 2:00 PM, the Laboratorio 4:20 group will hold an information session at the Glorieta de los Insurgentes (Insurgentes Roundabout), with workshops and a petition drive (30 attendees).

- In the Cuauhtémoc borough, the Unión Revolucionaria de Trabajadores del Arte (Revolutionary Union of Art Workers) will hold a political-cultural event at 12:00 PM at the Museo Panteón de San Fernando (San Fernando Pantheon Museum), commemorating the birth of Karl Marx (25 people).

- Meanwhile, the Ecos del Río collective will hold a cultural activity at 11:30 AM at the Mercado Turístico Magdalena Atlitic (Magdalena Atlitic Tourist Market) in Magdalena Contreras, focused on environmental defense (15 attendees). Motorcycle and Bicycle Rides in Mexico City
The schedule also includes rides that could impact traffic:
- At 8:00 p.m., a motorcycle group will depart from the Dr. Enrique Cabrera General Hospital in Álvaro Obregón for its third anniversary (50 participants).

- At 9:00 p.m., the Maniacos Biker’s collective will depart from Galerías Coapa in Tlalpan for a friendly ride (50 people).

- Another ride, organized by Arrancones Tláhuac, will begin at 8:30 a.m. from San Ángel heading towards Ajusco, with an estimated 150 motorcyclists.

- Regarding cyclists:
- At 1:30 p.m., a group will depart from the Guerrero neighborhood in support of the cannabis march (50 participants). - At 7:00 a.m., cyclists will depart from the Torre del Caballito (Little Horse Tower) towards Texcoco (30 people).

- At 8:00 a.m., the 4th Annual Children's Bike Ride 2026 will take place, starting from the Monument to the Revolution, with an estimated 1,500 participants.

Cultural, sporting, and entertainment events in Mexico City
The day also includes numerous recreational and cultural activities with high attendance:
- At the Arena Ciudad de México, Laura Pausini will perform at 9:00 p.m., with a capacity of 12,500 people.

- The National Auditorium will host the opera Eugene Onegin at 11:00 a.m., while the musical The Lion King will be performed at the Telcel Theater.

- Large-scale events such as the 2026 Flowers and Gardens Festival in Polanco (up to 10,000 attendees) and the Carnivals in Milpa Alta (up to 25,000 people) will take place throughout the day.

- In the sports arena, the América vs. Juárez match of the Liga MX Femenil at the Ciudad de los Deportes Stadium at 4:00 p.m. stands out, with a capacity of 25,000 spectators.

- There will also be activities at the Hermanos Rodríguez Racetrack, the Alfredo Harp Helú Stadium, and various cultural and religious venues in boroughs such as Iztapalapa, Tlalpan, and Xochimilco.

Recommendations for the day of demonstrations in Mexico City
Due to the concentration of activities, authorities anticipate traffic disruptions, mainly in the city center and on major avenues such as Paseo de la Reforma and Insurgentes. Citizens are advised to plan their trips in advance and consider alternate routes.

The SSC indicated that it will maintain constant monitoring to guarantee mobility and security during these activities.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
'What kind of democracy is this?': Assam activist Pranab Doley detained over Kaziranga protest
India TodayNE
- Jul 12, 2026,
- Updated Jul 12, 2026, 1:25 PM IST
Dispur Police on Sunday, July 12, detained activist Pranab Doley, who has been spearheading protests against the proposed construction of luxury hotels near Assam's Kaziranga National Park, and brought him to Dispur Police Station for interrogation.
Videos circulating on social media showed Doley shouting as he was being escorted by police personnel. "We can't even be the voice of the people. What kind of democracy is this? I was arrested without any papers and brought here. What kind of democracy is this?" he said while being taken away.
Sources said Doley has been booked under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Sections 61(2), 191(2), 191(3), 190, 329(3), 324(2), 221, 132, 121, 121(1), 121(2), 351(3), 74, 326(g), and 62.
The case has been registered at Bokakhat Police Station, and officials said he will be handed over to Bokakhat Police for further legal proceedings.
Doley, a member of Assam's indigenous Mising community, has been at the forefront of opposition to the proposed hospitality projects near Kaziranga, raising concerns over their potential environmental impact and the rights of local communities.
An MSW graduate from the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), Doley has founded and co-founded several organisations, including the Centre for North East Studies and Policy Advocacy (CNAPA), the All Kaziranga Affected Communities' Rights Committee, the People Ecology Network, and the Jyoti Bishnu Cultural and Research Centre. Through these organisations, he has worked on issues related to indigenous rights, sustainable development, environmental conservation, and community welfare.
Assam Police sources said Bokakhat Police were on their way to take Doley into custody at the time of filing this report, as the case had been registered at Bokakhat Police Station.

A march from Las Plassas to Barumini is planned to protest the wind turbines near Su Nuraxi. "From today until Saturday, May 30th, we will maintain a permanent garrison in Barumini day and night to protect one of Sardinia's most symbolic locations from further attacks on its territory," said spokesperson Davide Fadda on behalf of the garrison.

We invite citizens, committees, associations, administrators, movements, and all free Sardinians to participate, to be present, and to take a stand.”

MESSAGE_TEXT:
A section of private bus operators in Kozhikode district has resumed their protest against the State government’s Priyadarshini free travel scheme for women in KSRTC buses, alleging that the scheme will derail their business and push hundreds of bus owners and workers into acute financial distress.
The protesters, owing allegiance to the Kerala Private Bus Operators Association, staged a hunger strike in front of the Collectorate on Thursday (July 2, 2026). They alleged that the State government had been deliberately ignoring the survival issues raised by bus operators since the scheme’s launch.
They claimed that the surge in women passengers availing themselves of free travel on KSRTC buses had already disrupted the regular service schedules of many private bus operators. They said the sharp decline in the number of regular passengers on several village and urban routes had come as an unexpected blow to private operators already walking a tightrope financially.
A senior leader of the association, addressing the hunger strike, said the government’s failure to identify the most deserving beneficiaries through a sensible screening mechanism had dealt a blow to the ailing private bus sector. The scheme could have been accepted by all if it had been limited to eligible categories of passengers, such as women from lower-income groups, the unemployed, senior citizens, or those with serious ailments, the leader added.
“The government failed to initiate any practical measures to compensate private bus operators for their losses. Instead, it shifted the entire burden onto helpless private bus owners, asking them to devise their own measures to overcome the crisis,” said C. Baburaj, a private bus owner. He added private bus operators would not be able to come up with independent measures to attract passengers, particularly at a time of steep fuel price hikes and rising taxes, without adequate support from the State government.
Association leaders, including district president K.T. Vasudevan and secretary Beeran Koya, said the financial burden of implementing welfare schemes aimed at winning public support and political mileage should not be placed on private bus owners and workers. They said local bus operators were already facing an acute financial crisis, and the recent hike in fuel prices, coupled with rising maintenance costs and higher wages, had forced many operators to quit the sector in search of other viable livelihoods..

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Antorchistas exigen al INVI agilizar trámite para construcción de vivienda en Xochimilco
Una comisión de integrantes del Movimiento Antorchista se manifestó en las oficinas del Instituto de Vivienda de la Ciudad de México (INVI) para exigir la entrega inmediata de un documento indispensable para dar continuidad al proyecto habitacional del predio ubicado en Tepepan, alcaldía Xochimilco.
Previamente, una representación de los solicitantes acudió a la Secretaría de Planeación, Ordenamiento Territorial y Coordinación Metropolitana (SPOTMET) para dar seguimiento al proceso relacionado con dicho proyecto de vivienda. Durante la reunión se informó que la dependencia aún no había recibido el oficio correspondiente por parte del INVI, documento necesario para continuar con el trámite.
Ante esta situación, los antorchistas se trasladaron a las oficinas centrales del Instituto, ubicadas en la calle Canela, en la alcaldía Iztacalco, para exigir una explicación y demandar una pronta solución.
Ya en el INVI, funcionarios reconocieron que la nueva documentación fue ingresada desde el pasado 14 de abril, pero admitieron que el oficio no había sido elaborado ni enviado a la SPOTMET. Asimismo, señalaron que la elaboración del documento no representa un proceso complejo y que podría realizarse en poco tiempo.
Ante la demora de más de dos meses para emitir un trámite que, según las propias autoridades, no requiere mayor tiempo para su elaboración, los manifestantes decidieron intensificar su protesta, con el objetivo de presionar a las autoridades para que atendieran la demanda de manera inmediata.
Como resultado de la movilización, funcionarios del INVI se comprometieron a elaborar y entregar el oficio a la brevedad para remitir a la SPOTMET y permitir que continúe el procedimiento relacionado con el proyecto habitacional de Tepepan.
Los inconformes advirtieron que, en caso de que el compromiso no sea cumplido, regresarán a las instalaciones del Instituto para continuar con las acciones de protesta hasta que el documento sea entregado y el trámite avance sin más retrasos.
Por su parte, Oliver Saavedra, miembro del Comité Estatal del Movimiento Antorchista en la Ciudad de México, señaló que la movilización fue necesaria ante la falta de respuesta de las autoridades.
“Las familias solicitantes han esperado durante años una solución a su necesidad de vivienda y no es justo que el avance de un proyecto se vea frenado por la burocracia y la negligencia administrativa. Si las propias autoridades reconocen que este trámite puede resolverse en poco tiempo, no existe justificación para mantenerlo detenido durante más de dos meses. La movilización fue necesaria para que se atendiera una demanda legítima y estaremos pendientes de que se cumpla el compromiso adquirido; de lo contrario, continuaremos con las acciones necesarias hasta que el documento sea entregado y el proyecto siga avanzando”, afirmó.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Antorcha Campesina members demand INVI expedite housing construction permit in Xochimilco
A delegation of members of the Antorcha Campesina movement demonstrated at the offices of the Mexico City Housing Institute (INVI) to demand the immediate delivery of a document essential for continuing the housing project on the property located in Tepepan, Xochimilco borough.

Previously, a group of applicants went to the Secretariat of Planning, Territorial Organization, and Metropolitan Coordination (SPOTMET) to follow up on the process related to the housing project. During the meeting, they were informed that the agency had not yet received the corresponding official document from INVI, a document necessary to continue the process.

Given this situation, the Antorcha Campesina members went to the Institute's headquarters, located on Canela Street in the Iztacalco borough, to demand an explanation and a prompt solution. At the INVI (Housing Institute of Veracruz), officials acknowledged that the new documentation had been submitted on April 14th, but admitted that the official document had not yet been drafted or sent to SPOTMET (State Secretariat for Territorial Planning and Housing). They also indicated that drafting the document was not a complex process and could be completed quickly.

Given the delay of more than two months in processing a document that, according to the authorities themselves, should not require much time, the protesters decided to intensify their demonstration to pressure the authorities to address their demand immediately.

As a result of the mobilization, INVI officials committed to drafting and delivering the document as soon as possible to SPOTMET, thus allowing the process related to the Tepepan housing project to continue.

The protesters warned that if this commitment is not fulfilled, they will return to the Institute's facilities to continue their protests until the document is delivered and the process moves forward without further delays. For his part, Oliver Saavedra, a member of the State Committee of the Antorcha Campesina Movement in Mexico City, stated that the mobilization was necessary due to the lack of response from the authorities.

“The families applying for housing have waited for years for a solution to their housing needs, and it is not fair that the progress of a project is being stalled by bureaucracy and administrative negligence. If the authorities themselves acknowledge that this process can be resolved quickly, there is no justification for keeping it stalled for more than two months. The mobilization was necessary to ensure that a legitimate demand was addressed, and we will be monitoring the situation to ensure that the commitment made is fulfilled; otherwise, we will continue with the necessary actions until the document is delivered and the project moves forward,” he affirmed.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
VANCOUVER — Unionized workers in Metro Vancouver who oversee drinking water, wastewater treatment, air quality and other important jobs across more than 20 municipalities are taking full-scale strike action starting Monday.
The union representing more than 700 Metro Vancouver outside workers says all non-essential staff will walk off their jobs, although those who are designated as essential service will remain at work.
Jesse Medeiros, the president of the Greater Vancouver Regional District Employees’ Union, said in a news release Friday that members are "angry and frustrated" after 17 months without a contract, and Metro Vancouver's management is ignoring their concerns.
"GVRDEU members are the front line workers that keep Metro Vancouver running and we are sick and tired of management incompetence and disrespect,” Medeiros said.
"Taxpayers and the elected mayors and councillors on Metro Vancouver’s Board should be demanding better — starting with getting a new contract with our members and then fixing the problems management has created.”
The union accuses the regional district of setting preconditions before contract talks can resume, which Metro Vancouver has denied.
The district has said that it has offered several dates for restarting talks, without preconditions, and has proposed the help of a mediator.
Rotating pickets have been set up by the union over the last few weeks.
Medeiros said the public will notice the full-scale strike immediately, with unionized staff walking off their jobs in regional parks, at water and wastewater treatment plants, construction sites, and elsewhere.
“We regret the inconvenience to the public and appreciate their support in this dispute but we can’t wait forever to get a new contract for our members,” Medeiros said.
The union also said workers will rally at the Metro Vancouver headquarters in Burnaby on Monday.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published June 12, 2026.
Chuck Chiang, The Canadian Press

Las personas manifestantes, en su mayoría mujeres, llegaron al inmueble antes de las 9 de la mañana con cartulinas en las que pidieron justicia y la liberación de sus familiares y seres queridos.
La detención ocurrió el pasado 29 de mayo, cuando elementos de la Guardia Nacional, las FSPE y el Ejército Mexicano participaron en un operativo realizado en la colonia Fermín Montenegro, de Cortazar, e ingresaron al domicilio de Isabel Gallegos para detener a sus dos hijos y a su esposo, quienes estaban durmiendo.
Huachicol, detención y protesta en Celaya
A mi hijo menor de edad lo dejaron salir hasta el día siguiente. Ellos siempre se han dedicado a trabajar, trabajan en una empresa”, mencionó.
Los familiares de Aarón “N” y Cristóbal “N” aseguraron que hubo varias irregularidades en su detención, ya que no presentaron una orden de presentación y ambos fueron golpeados.
Cuando ingresaron no presentaron ningún papel, nunca nadie se acercó a decirme de qué los estaban acusando, nada más se los llevaron. Hasta después, cuando tuvimos una asesoría legal, fue cuando el licenciado nos comentó que por
[extracción de hidrocarburo los]estaban imputando”, señaló.
Tanto Aarón como Cristóbal trabajan en una fábrica y, en sus tiempos libres, hacen trabajos de albañilería y electricidad.
Ellos están cerca de un ducto de Pemex y ahora es delito vivir cerca de donde viven. No es justo que gente inocente esté pagando por algo que hace otra gente.
Desgraciadamente nos pueden llamar ignorantes, pero exigimos justicia. No es justo que el Gobierno agarre gente por agarrar para levantarse el cuello y decir que están trabajando”, señaló una de sus familiares.
Los dos detenidos continúan recluidos en el Cereso de Celaya y sus familiares no han podido verlos.
“Queremos ser escuchados en todos los lugares que nos puedan escuchar, queremos justicia, los queremos libres porque son inocentes, son gente trabajadora, honrada, nunca se meten con nadie. Mi hermano no es de fiestas ni de andar en la calle, se dedica a su trabajo y a su familia”, señaló.
El presidente municipal, Juan Miguel Ramírez Sánchez, salió al patio de la Presidencia para escuchar a los manifestantes y mostrarles su apoyo.
El pasado 11 de junio, la Secretaría de Seguridad y Paz emitió un comunicado de prensa en el que informó que entre las Fuerzas de Seguridad Pública del Estado (FSPE), la Guardia Nacional y la Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional se asegurararon aproximadamente 46 mil litros de hidrocarburo, además de equipo presuntamente utilizado para su almacenamiento y transferencia irregular.
“En dos intervenciones distintas fueron localizados contenedores con combustible, motobombas, mangueras especializadas y un vehículo. Además, tres personas fueron puestas a disposición de la autoridad federal competente para las investigaciones correspondientes”, señala el boletín.
AM solicitó una postura a la dependencia estatal sobre esta manifestación e informó, a través de su área de Comunicación Social, que la Secretaría de Seguridad y Paz emitió un boletín en el que se dio a conocer la acción con los resultados, y que todo lo demás corresponde al seguimiento en la Fiscalía General de la República.

The protesters, mostly women, arrived at the building before 9:00 a.m. with signs demanding justice and the release of their relatives and loved ones.

The arrests occurred on May 29, when members of the National Guard, the State Police (FSPE), and the Mexican Army participated in an operation in the Fermín Montenegro neighborhood of Cortazar. They entered the home of Isabel Gallegos and arrested her two sons and her husband, who were asleep.

Huachicol, arrest, and protest in Celaya
"My minor son wasn't released until the next day." “They’ve always been hard workers, they work for a company,” he said.
The families of Aarón “N” and Cristóbal “N” asserted that there were several irregularities in their arrest, as no warrant was presented and both were beaten. “When they were taken in, they didn’t present any paperwork, no one ever approached me to tell me what they were being accused of, they were just taken away. It wasn’t until later, when we had legal counsel, that the lawyer told us they were being charged with
[hydrocarbon extraction],” he stated.
Both Aarón and Cristóbal work in a factory and, in their free time, do construction and electrical work.
They live near a Pemex pipeline, and now it’s a crime to live near where they live. It’s not fair that innocent people are paying for something other people do.
Unfortunately, they can call us ignorant, but we demand justice. “It’s not fair that the government arrests people just to make themselves look good and say they’re doing their job,” said one of their relatives.
The two detainees remain incarcerated at the Celaya prison, and their families have not been able to see them.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
À l’occasion de la Journée mondiale des réfugiés, une cinquantaine de membres de la diaspora touareg et sahélienne se sont réunis, le 20 juin, devant l’ambassade de Russie à Paris. Un rassemblement à la tonalité essentiellement humanitaire, destiné à alerter sur le sort des populations civiles victimes du conflit qui ravage le nord du Mali depuis la dénonciation des accords de paix.
Par Rania Hadjer
Paris, Place de la Colombie, XVIe arrondissement. Sous un ciel caniculaire et à quelques mètres de l’ambassade de la Fédération de Russie, une cinquantaine de personnes se sont réunies dans le calme. Des Touaregs et Maures originaires de l’Azawad (nord du Mali), du Niger, d’Algérie et de Libye ont répondu à l’appel de l’Organisation de la Diaspora des Touaregs d’Europe (ODTE) et de plusieurs associations de la diaspora sahélienne.
Les organisateurs ont profité de la Journée mondiale des réfugiés pour attirer l’attention sur le sort des centaines de milliers de déplacés et de réfugiés ayant fui les violences qui secouent le nord du Mali depuis la dénonciation des accords d’Alger et la reprise du conflit entre Bamako et les mouvements indépendantistes de l’Azawad (nom donné par ces mouvements aux régions du nord du Mali), en 2023. À côté des banderoles et affiches accusant la Russie de soutenir les opérations militaires menées dans la région du nord du Mali et dénonçant le silence de la communauté internationale, des photographies d’enfants blessés, de victimes de bombardements et de familles déplacées rappellent la dimension humaine du conflit.
Frappes aériennes indiscriminées
Plusieurs pancartes font référence aux frappes aériennes qui se sont multipliées dans le nord du pays ces dernières années. Pour les organisateurs, ces opérations militaires se traduisent par un ciblage indiscriminé des populations civiles et alimentent l’exode de milliers de familles vers les pays voisins.
À partir de 15 heures, les participants prennent progressivement place. Les discussions se déroulent en français, en tamasheq et en arabe. Beaucoup se connaissent déjà : militants associatifs, journalistes, membres de la diaspora, réfugiés politiques ou proches de familles toujours présentes dans les camps. Vers 15h30, Abdoulahi Attayoub, président de l’ODTE, ouvre officiellement le rassemblement : « Nous remercions toutes les personnes qui se sont déplacées pour nous soutenir à ce rassemblement et exprimer leur opposition au soutien apporté par la Fédération de Russie à l’armée malienne et aux armées du Sahel qui perpétuent des massacres contre les populations civiles touarègues, peules et arabes, essentiellement en Azawad, nord-Mali, mais également au Burkina Faso et au Niger.»
Dans son intervention, il rappelle les objectifs de la journée : attirer l’attention de l’opinion publique sur la situation des civils dans l’Azawad et plus largement dans le Sahel central, tout en exprimant une solidarité avec les réfugiés dispersés entre la Mauritanie, l’Algérie et l’Europe. La question des réfugiés est au cœur des préoccupations des organisateurs. Les autorités mauritaniennes et plusieurs agences internationales évoquent désormais près de 300 000 réfugiés installés dans les zones frontalières du pays. Dans les camps de Mbera et dans les localités environnantes, les infrastructures peinent à suivre. Les besoins en eau, en alimentation, en santé et en éducation augmentent tandis que l’aide internationale tend à diminuer.
Le discours du président de l’ODTE est ensuite traduit en tamasheq par Tohima ag Libnina, représentante d’Azawad Solidarity, puis en arabe par Ayoub ag Chamad, président de l’ONG Imouhagh International. L’animation des différentes prises de parole est assurée par Mohamed Ag Ahmedou, de l’Amicale des Touaregs de Rennes. L’atmosphère demeure recueillie. Pas de slogans scandés en continu ni de démonstration de force. Les organisateurs ont manifestement privilégié les témoignages.
La Russie sur le banc des accusés
Au fil de l’après-midi, les récits se succèdent. Plusieurs témoignages décrivent les difficultés de l’exil : la vie dans les camps, la séparation familiale, l’incertitude permanente. D’autres évoquent des proches tués ou blessés lors de frappes aériennes dans les régions de Kidal, Tombouctou, Gao ou Menaka. Les intervenants dénoncent ce qu’ils qualifient de politique de « la terre brûlée » menée par les Forces armées maliennes (FAMa) avec l’appui de leurs partenaires russes.
Plusieurs associations accusent également Bamako de mener une politique de persécution visant spécifiquement les populations touarègues, arabes et peules, accusations rejetées par les autorités maliennes. Depuis le remplacement officiel du groupe Wagner par l’Africa Corps, unité placée directement sous le commandement du ministère russe de la Défense, la présence russe au Mali demeure au cœur des critiques formulées par les organisations de défense des droits humains et par les populations déplacées. Face à l’ambassade de Russie, plusieurs intervenants appellent Moscou à mettre fin à son implication militaire dans le conflit malien.
L’affiche diffusée avant l’événement dénonçait explicitement le soutien de l’Africa Corps aux opérations militaires dans l’Azawad et le Sahel central. Pour les organisateurs, la Russie porte une part de responsabilité dans les souffrances des populations civiles.
Drones, déplacements forcés et accusations de nettoyage ethnique
Au-delà de la dénonciation de l’implication russe, les organisateurs ont voulu attirer l’attention sur ce qu’ils considèrent comme une aggravation des méthodes de guerre employées dans le nord du Mali. Les intervenants ont multiplié les témoignages sur les frappes de drones visant des localités, des campements nomades ou des convois civils. Plusieurs participants ont affirmé avoir perdu des proches lors de bombardements qu’ils estiment dépourvus d’objectifs militaires clairement identifiables.
De nombreuses prises de parole ont également dénoncé ce qui est présenté comme une politique de déplacement forcé des populations et de destruction systématique des moyens de subsistance. Villages abandonnés, puits détruits, cheptels décimés et marchés désertés composent un tableau régulièrement évoqué au cours de l’après-midi. Les responsables associatifs présents parlent d’une stratégie de « nettoyage ethnique » destinée à modifier durablement l’équilibre démographique de certaines zones.
Des armes controversées au cœur des inquiétudes
Plusieurs orateurs ont également alerté sur l’utilisation d’armes à sous-munitions dans le nord du Mali. Depuis plusieurs semaines, des organisations internationales spécialisées dans le désarmement examinent des images diffusées après certaines frappes aériennes dans l’Azawad. Selon ces organisations, ces images pourraient montrer des sous-munitions issues de bombes de type RBK-500, d’origine russe. Aucune enquête indépendante n’a toutefois permis, à ce stade, d’établir définitivement les circonstances de leur utilisation.
La question suscite une inquiétude particulière en raison des effets de ces armes sur les populations civiles. Les sous-munitions dispersent de nombreux petits explosifs sur une large surface et certaines demeurent actives après l’impact, représentant un danger durable pour les habitants longtemps après la fin des combats. Pour les participants au rassemblement parisien, ces soupçons illustrent l’escalade du conflit et la vulnérabilité croissante des populations civiles.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
On the occasion of World Refugee Day, around fifty members of the Tuareg and Sahelian diaspora gathered on June 20 in front of the Russian Embassy in Paris. The gathering, primarily humanitarian in nature, aimed to raise awareness of the plight of civilians affected by the conflict that has ravaged northern Mali since the collapse of the peace agreements.

By Rania Hadjer
Paris, Place de la Colombie, 16th arrondissement. Under a scorching sun and just a few meters from the Embassy of the Russian Federation, about fifty people gathered peacefully. Tuaregs and Moors from Azawad (northern Mali), Niger, Algeria, and Libya responded to the call from the Organization of the Tuareg Diaspora in Europe (ODTE) and several Sahelian diaspora associations.

The organizers used World Refugee Day to draw attention to the plight of the hundreds of thousands of displaced persons and refugees who have fled the violence that has plagued northern Mali since the denunciation of the Algiers Accords and the resumption of the conflict between Bamako and the Azawad separatist movements (the name given by these movements to the northern regions of Mali) in 2023. Alongside banners and posters accusing Russia of supporting military operations in northern Mali and denouncing the silence of the international community, photographs of wounded children, bombing victims, and displaced families serve as reminders of the human dimension of the conflict.

Indiscriminate Airstrikes
Several signs refer to the airstrikes that have increased in the north of the country in recent years. For the organizers, these military operations amount to the indiscriminate targeting of civilian populations and fuel the exodus of thousands of families to neighboring countries.

From 3 p.m. onwards, participants gradually took their seats. Discussions were conducted in French, Tamasheq, and Arabic. Many already knew each other: activists, journalists, members of the diaspora, political refugees, or relatives of families still living in the camps. Around 3:30 p.m., Abdoulahi Attayoub, president of the ODTE, officially opened the gathering: “We thank all those who have come to support us at this gathering and to express their opposition to the support provided by the Russian Federation to the Malian army and the armies of the Sahel, which are perpetrating massacres against Tuareg, Fulani, and Arab civilian populations, primarily in Azawad, northern Mali, but also in Burkina Faso and Niger.”

In his address, he reiterated the day's objectives: to draw public attention to the situation of civilians in Azawad and more broadly in the central Sahel, while expressing solidarity with the refugees scattered between Mauritania, Algeria, and Europe. The refugee issue is at the heart of the organizers' concerns. Mauritanian authorities and several international agencies now report nearly 300,000 refugees living in the country's border areas. In the Mbera camps and surrounding towns, infrastructure is struggling to keep up. The needs for water, food, healthcare, and education are increasing while international aid is dwindling.
The speech by the president of the ODTE (Organization for the Defense of the Environment and Tourism) was then translated into Tamasheq by Tohima ag Libnina, representative of Azawad Solidarity, and then into Arabic by Ayoub ag Chamad, president of the NGO Imouhagh International. The various presentations were moderated by Mohamed Ag Ahmedou of the Rennes Tuareg Association. The atmosphere remained somber. There were no continuous chants or displays of force. The organizers clearly prioritized personal accounts. Russia in the Dock
As the afternoon wore on, stories unfolded. Several testimonies described the hardships of exile: life in camps, family separation, and constant uncertainty. Others spoke of relatives killed or wounded in airstrikes in the regions of Kidal, Timbuktu, Gao, and Menaka. The speakers denounced what they called a "scorched earth" policy pursued by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) with the support of their Russian partners.
Several associations also accused Bamako of conducting a policy of persecution specifically targeting the Tuareg, Arab, and Fulani populations, accusations rejected by the Malian authorities. Since the official replacement of the Wagner Group by the Africa Corps, a unit placed directly under the command of the Russian Ministry of Defense, the Russian presence in Mali remains at the heart of criticism voiced by human rights organizations and displaced populations. In front of the Russian embassy, ​​several speakers called on Moscow to end its military involvement in the Malian conflict. The poster distributed before the event explicitly denounced the Africa Corps' support for military operations in Azawad and the central Sahel. According to the organizers, Russia bears some responsibility for the suffering of civilian populations.

Drones, forced displacement, and accusations of ethnic cleansing
Beyond denouncing Russian involvement, the organizers wanted to draw attention to what they consider an escalation of the warfare employed in northern Mali. Speakers shared numerous accounts of drone strikes targeting towns, nomadic camps, and civilian convoys. Several participants stated that they had lost relatives in bombings they believe lacked clearly identifiable military objectives.
Many speakers also denounced what is presented as a policy of forced displacement of populations and systematic destruction of livelihoods. Abandoned villages, destroyed wells, decimated livestock, and deserted markets formed a picture regularly evoked throughout the afternoon. Representatives of NGOs present spoke of a strategy of “ethnic cleansing” intended to permanently alter the demographic balance of certain areas.

Controversial weapons at the heart of concerns
Several speakers also raised concerns about the use of cluster munitions in northern Mali. For several weeks, international organizations specializing in disarmament have been examining images released after certain airstrikes in Azawad. According to these organizations, these images could show submunitions from Russian-made RBK-500 bombs. However, no independent investigation has yet definitively established the circumstances of their use.
The issue is of particular concern because of the effects of these weapons on civilian populations. Cluster munitions disperse numerous small explosives over a wide area, and some remain active after impact, posing a lasting danger to residents long after the fighting has ended. For those attending the Paris rally, these suspicions illustrate the escalation of the conflict and the growing vulnerability of civilian populations.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Political protest planned for April 22 at Vattiyoorkavu Police Station in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India
MESSAGE_TEXT:
BJP to take out 'mass march' to Commissioner's office on April 23 after clash with CPM in TVM
Mail This Article
The BJP will take out a protest march to the Police Commissioner's office on April 22, demanding the removal of the Vattiyoorkavu Station House Officer, CI Vipin A C, who, according to the party, was acting like a henchman of the CPM and had used third-degree methods against innocent BJP workers.
“If this CI Vipin continues in his job, we fear that even murders could take place in the area. To avoid this, either he should be transferred or placed on leave,” BJP district president Karamana Jayan said on Tuesday.
He said that the party had placed this demand before the Commissioner, K Karthik. “The Commissioner had said that he would consider our request favourably, but no action has still been taken. This means that the CPM has strongly intervened in the issue,” Jayan said.
Later in the day, BJP's women councillors took out a 'mahila march' to the Vattiyoorkavu Police Station as a warning measure before a “mass protest march” to the City Police Commissioner's office on April 22. The mass march will be led by BJP state vice president and former DGP R Sreelekha.
“If our demand is not met even after these two protests, we will intensify our agitation,” Jayan said.
The BJP's demand for the removal of the CI comes after two consecutive days of bloody and prolonged BJP-CPM clash in the Malamukal area of Thiruvananthapuram Corporation. The issue began as a dispute between neighbours. It was alleged that a man verbally abused and indulged in indecent exposure before the lady of the other house.
The incident flared up into a major political clash after a group of people, allegedly CPM workers, roughed up the husband, a local BJP leader named Binu, who was returning after filing a police complaint against the neighbour. Binu had to be rushed to the Peroorkada District hospital.
When things escalated into a gang war of sorts at Malamukal junction, the Vattiyoorkavu police intervened. The charge was that CI Vipin behaved in an impartial manner, lathi-charging only the BJP workers. In retaliation, stones were pelted at the police, and the police fought back with materials collected from a nearby shop. Civil police officer Deepu was injured in the stone-throwing.
The BJP says that the stones were thrown by the CPM workers, with the intention of implicating the BJP. “We have video proof showing the direction from which the stones were coming. We have shown this to the Commissioner and he was convinced,” Jayan, the BJP district president, said.
On April 20, next day, a police team barged into the first floor of the Balasubramaniam Temple office, forced open the entrance door, and took six BJP-RSS workers into custody and, on the way to the Armed Reserve Camp at Nandavanam, was allegedly violently beaten up by the police. “Some of them were not even involved in the case,” BJP vice president R Sreelekha said.
BJP's Nettayam area secretary Binu, who had initially filed a complaint with the police, had his face punched near the eye. Photographs show him bleeding profusely from under his right eye. Sreelekha said that Binu was attacked only because he filed a complaint against a CPM worker. “The CPM somehow could not stomach the fact that someone had dared to complain against a party man,” she said.
After the news of the alleged police violence spread, BJP workers collected in large numbers before the AR camp. Until Mayor V V Rajesh arrived on the spot, the police did not allow any BJP leader to enter the camp premises to talk to the arrested workers.
Later, the police removed Binu and another local BJP leader Ayyappan from the list of the accused.
The former DGP also said that the police had no authority to step into the premises of a temple without taking the permission of the temple authorities. She said there were Supreme Court guidelines and central and state government orders that prohibited the entry of police into places of worship.

El Ayuntamiento de València prepara un dispositivo de tráfico para la manifestación este sábado del Orgullo LGTBIAQ+, convocada por el colectivo Lambda, que tendrá lugar de 19.30 a 22 horas y que empezará en el paseo de L'Albereda y circulará por el Pont de L'Exposició, Justícia, Porta de la Mar, Colón, Xàtiva, Marqués de Sotelo y finalizará en la plaza del consistorio.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Police officers pelted with stones and chairs, cans, and flares during protest in Portswood area of Southampton, UK
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Protesters have pelted police with missiles in clashes close to where Henry Nowak was stabbed to death.
Hundreds gathered outside Southampton Central Police Station on Tuesday where activist Tommy Robinson and Laurence Fox were among those who spoke to the crowd.
Violent scenes broke out after a large group walked across town to the area of Portswood.
A police helicopter hovered overhead as officers were pelted with stones.
Demonstrators chanted “Henry, Henry” as the line of police were pelted with bricks.
Chairs, cans and flares were thrown at police in riot gear, eventually forcing officers and three police vans back from the line they had been holding.
The killer of finance student Mr Nowak, 23-year-old Vickrum Digwa, told police attending the scene of the stabbing in Southampton on December 3 2025 that he had been the victim of a racist attack.
In body-worn camera footage from the incident, Mr Nowak can be heard repeatedly saying: “I’ve been stabbed”, to which an officer replies: “Don’t think you have, mate.”
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood later condemned the scenes in Portswood as “completely unacceptable” and accused the demonstrators of “hijacking this tragedy to stir up violence and disorder” in defiance of a plea by the Nowak family not to use the murder to feed division and hatred.
The clashes with police come amid growing tensions and scrutiny over how officers dealt with the incident which included arresting and handcuffing Mr Nowak as he lay dying.
Ms Mahmood said: “The Nowak family made a powerful call to us all yesterday to not let Henry’s death be used to create further division, hatred or tension.
“There can be no justification for hijacking this tragedy to stir up violence and disorder. Those responsible can expect to face the full force of the law.
“I thank the police who have tonight shown great bravery and calm in the face of disgraceful violence directed at them.”
Digwa was given a life sentence with a minimum of 21 years in prison for stabbing Mr Nowak with a ceremonial knife with a 21cm blade prosecutors said was a kirpan, which he carried as part of his Sikh religion.
He had previously been investigated by police in 2023 on suspicion of stealing ceremonial blades from a Sikh temple in Southampton but no further action was taken.
The National Police Chiefs’ Council (NPCC) announced it would review anti-racism guidance – called the Race Action Plan – that some have blamed for the actions of the officers who arrested Mr Nowak.
NPCC chairman Gavin Stephens said: “We are listening to legitimate concerns about how some of these commitments are worded or phrased, and where needed we can and will make changes, but this should not detract from the intent, which is to improve the quality of policing.”
Earlier on Tuesday Hampshire Police said an officer not connected to the case has faced death threats after being misidentified in online posts.
In a post on X, the force said: “We recognise the desire for answers about the police response that night” and warned people not to indulge in “harmful online speculation”.
Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer has said he “felt sick” watching “harrowing” footage of police handcuffing Mr Nowak and said there are “serious questions” to answer about the case.
There needs to be an examination into how “accusations of racism” informed the police’s decision-making in the case, he added.
The police watchdog is expected to report on the case within the next three months.
The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said investigators are examining a large amount of body-worn video as well as material presented during Digwa’s trial.
Hampshire Police confirmed that one of the officers involved in the case has resigned, while the other three are still serving. All of them are being treated as witnesses.
Mr Nowak’s father Mark Nowak, speaking after Digwa was sentenced on Monday, said: “We do not want his death to be used to create further division, hatred or tension.”
But Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said people should respond with “pure cold rage” to Mr Nowak’s treatment, which he said was evidence of a “two-tier culture”.
Mr Nowak was “actually treated in a way that meant an accusation of a racial slur was treated more seriously than an act of murder”, Mr Farage said.
In other developments:
– Attorney General Lord Hermer has received “multiple requests” to consider whether Digwa’s sentence should be reviewed as unduly lenient.
– Digwa, his father Moga Singh, 52, and brother Gurpreet Digwa, 27, appeared at Southampton Magistrates’ Court to face multiple weapons charges.
– A statement issued by the killer’s family apologised “for the pain and suffering the Nowak family has had to endure”, and for bringing the Sikh community into “disrepute”.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Aquaculture farmers protest in front of Fisheries Department office in Ongole, Andhra Pradesh, India
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Aquaculture farmers staged a protest in front of the Fisheries Department office in Ongole on Tuesday (May 12, 2026) against the rise in shrimp feed prices. They demanded strict action against the feed manufacturing companies that have increased prices without the permission of the Andhra Pradesh State Aquaculture Development Authority (APSADA).
Prakasam Shrimp Farmers Association president Duggineni Gopinath said that the shrimp feed companies have unilaterally increased tiger shrimp feed by ₹10-70 per kg and Vannamei shrimp feed by ₹8-40 per kg without the permission of the State government, citing that the prices of raw materials used in feed manufacturing have gone up.
He said, “As per the increased feed prices, the additional cost of production will increase by ₹35 to 40 per kg for farmers cultivating tiger shrimp and by ₹15 to 20 per kg for farmers cultivating Vannamei shrimp. This will be a heavy burden on the farmers who have been suffering due to non-remunerative prices in the export market.”

O katliamın planlayıcısını kırmızı halılarda ağırlıyorlar. Ne yapacaklarını bilmiyorlar. Ankara’yı yurttaşlarımıza zindan ettiler, onları saraylarda ağırlayacaklar. Kim? Filistin’in katilleri!
Filistin’deki katliam sürüyor. İran’daki savaşın, İran’a dönük saldırganlığın nereye evrildiğini bile bilmiyoruz. Şu anda hala bir çatışma var orada, yanı başımızda, komşumuzdur. Ondan sonra gelmişler, gencecik bir arkadaşımızı “kutsal değerlere hakaret etti” diye tutukladılar. Bu olacak iş mi?

O yüzden biz NATO ile işimizi bugün ve yarın da bırakmayacağız. Takipçisi olacağız bu zirvenin. Bu zirvede aldıkları uluslararası kararların takipçisi olacağız ve mücadeleye devam edecek.
Edeceğiz ki bu ülke, sevgili ülkemiz; bağımsız, egemen, sömürüsüz, özgür, sosyalist bir ülke haline gelsin. O güne kadar mücadeleye devam. Üslere el konsun, NATO defolsun.
İzmir’de yurttaşlar NATO üssüne yürüdü

İnam şunları söyledi:
NATO sermaye sınıfının, patronların, tarikatların, ülkemizi karanlığa sürükleyen sömürücü haydutların temsilcisidir. Onların silahlı kuvvetidir. Ülkemizde her türlü kötülüğü NATO eliyle hayata geçirdiler. Aydınlarımıza, gençlerimize, emekçi halkımıza doğrulttular o silahları. Cinayetler, katliamlar, darbeler yaptılar. Kurduğumuz Cumhuriyet’e başından beri düşmanlar, Cumhuriyet’i ortadan kaldırabilmek için ellerinden geleni ardına koymadılar. Bağımsızlık ve egemenliğimizi ayaklar altına aldılar.
AKP iktidarı, NATO’nun ülkemizdeki ve bölgedeki karanlığını sürdürmesi için önemli bir aktördür ve suçludur. ‘Ülkemize ve onurumuza sahip çıkıyoruz’
Küstah işbirlikçi iktidara da işgalci, katil NATO’ya da boyun eğmeyeceğiz. Ülkemize, onurumuza sahip çıkıyoruz. Türkiye’nin NATO’dan çıkması, NATO’nun ülkemizdeki varlığının son bulması, Türkiye’nin sokulmaya çalışıldığı yeni Osmanlıcı savaş politikalarının boşa düşürülmesi için halkın örgütlülüğünü sağlayacağız. Bu oyunu bozacağız.
Bu kavga yeni başlamıyor. Ama bu kavgayı çok daha fazla güçlendireceğimize, ülkemizi bu barbarlardan, sömürücülerden kurtaracağımıza söz veriyoruz. İnsanlığın, iyiliğin, eşitliğin, özgürlüğün, bağımsızlığın kazandığı bir ülke ve dünya yaratacağımıza söz veriyoruz.”

‘Yerli ve milliyiz diyenler yalan söylüyor
Ateşli konuşmasında ayrıca şunları söyledi:

Türkiye Cumhuriyeti dünyanın dört yanından gelen işgalcilere karşı bağımsızlığını kan ve can bedeli olarak kazanmıştır. 1922’de Samsun kıyılarından kentimize bombalar yağdıranları, insanlarımızı öldürenleri bugün elbette çiçeklerle karşılamayacağız. Chakhroma body stages protest, seeks action on Maova land dispute
Chakhroma Public Organisation stages protest, demanding government action over the Maova land dispute and enforcement of longstanding administrative orders
DIMAPUR — Declaring that they were defending the ancestral land and customary rights of the Chakhro people, hundreds of members of the Chakhroma Public Organisation (CPO) on Friday staged a protest rally at Dzümha Rü Bridge Junction in New Medziphema village, demanding that Nagaland government implement decades-old administrative orders and resolve the long-running land dispute with Maova village.
Carrying placards calling on the government to enforce its own directives, protesters marched before submitting an eight-point charter of demands to the chief secretary through the additional deputy commissioner (ADC) of Medziphema.
The CPO maintained that successive administrative authorities had recognised Tsüüma village as the traditional landowner in the disputed area but alleged that the government's failure to enforce those directives had allowed the dispute to persist. It urged the state to acknowledge what it described as the customary ownership rights of the Chakhro people and ensure compliance with earlier official orders.
Among its demands, the organisation called for enforcement of administrative orders issued between 1979 and 2001, payment of the customary annual token tax by Maova Village to Tsüüma Village in recognition of traditional land ownership, a review of the status of the Maova Village Council, and the immediate derecognition of Maova village.
The memorandum also sought the removal of the Head GB of Maova village, suspension of the issuance of official documents to the village pending verification based on the 1963 Electoral Roll, and implementation of the Chakhroma Youth Organisation's customary expulsion order against three Maova Village leaders.
Addressing the gathering, CPO president Zhato Kimho said the protest was aimed at protecting what the organisation described as the ancestral land and customary rights of the Chakhro people. He alleged that despite repeated representations and administrative directives spanning several decades, the government had failed to implement its own decisions.
Referring to Article 371A of the Constitution, Kimho alleged that recognition of Maova village had been granted without the consent of the traditional landowners and urged the government to immediately derecognise the village.
He also appealed to Naga political groups not to provide shelter or training to Kuki youths, alleging that such support could undermine the interests of the Naga community. Referring to the ongoing ethnic conflict in neighbouring Manipur, Kimho claimed that similar attempts were being made to create divisions among Nagas in Nagaland and urged the community to remain united in safeguarding its customary land rights.
Kimho further alleged that attempts had been made to prevent Friday's protest after representatives of Maova village met government officials ahead of the rally. He added that the CPO had pursued a peaceful resolution since February but claimed continued government inaction had compelled the organisation to intensify its agitation.
Speaking at the rally, Angami Public Organisation (APO) president Thejao Vihienuo claimed that Kukis first entered Naga areas about 170 years ago as mercenaries and later settled in Naga territory with the consent of Naga landowners. He alleged that the settlements were established on the understanding of peaceful coexistence, but contended that the trust extended by the Naga community had since been repeatedly violated.
He urged the government to examine historical records and review the legal status of such settlements, contending that the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873, and Article 371A were intended to safeguard the customary rights of indigenous Nagas.
Chakhroma Youth Organisation (CYO) president Medochüzo Medoze maintained that the youth had exercised restraint at the request of community leaders but warned that patience was wearing thin due to what he described as the government's failure to act. He urged the authorities to resolve the dispute without further delay.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
People gathered near the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar statue at Necklace Road in Hyderabad on Thursday evening, July 16, to hold a candlelight vigil in solidarity with activist Sonam Wangchuk and to demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak. The gathering was held as activist Sonam Wangshuk’s hunger strike entered its 19th day.
Organised by a coalition of civil society organisations, the protest began around 7 p.m. with participants lighting candles and raising slogans. As the evening progressed, more people joined the gathering. People carried placards reading ‘Save Sonam Wangchuk’, ‘Protect Student Rights’ and ‘Sack Dharmendra Pradhan’. Slogans demanding the resignation of the Union Education Minister echoed through the venue.
A poster displayed at the protest listed three demands: protect student rights, scrap the National Testing Agency (NTA), and remove Dharmendra Pradhan as Union Education Minister.
Among those participating was Dinesh, a working professional, who criticised the handling of national entrance examinations. “We work day and night, pay taxes to the government, and yet it is unable to conduct an examination properly. What is even worse is that the government is not even willing to have a dialogue with those who are protesting, especially Sonam Wangchuk, who has been on a hunger strike for 19 days,” he said.
Sandhya, a teacher who joined the vigil, said broader public participation was needed. “Students are coming out and participating in these protests, but things will not change unless parents of lakhs of children also join the movement,” she said.
Former chairman of the Telangana Education Commission, Akunuri Murali, who also participated in the protest, expressed concern over Wangchuk’s health and criticised the Union government’s response. “The silence of the Government of India is unacceptable. It appears as though they are waiting for something unfortunate to happen. Our demands are to protect Sonam Wangchuk, seek the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and call for an investigation into theNTA,” he said.
Mr. Murali also questioned the centralisation of entrance examinations under the NTA. He argued that States were capable of conducting their own entrance tests and said the Centre should limit itself to examinations for institutions under its jurisdiction. “The present system is overly centralised and goes against the spirit of federalism. State governments have the capacity to conduct their own examinations. The Centre need not take over that responsibility except for admissions to Central institutions,” he said.
