MESSAGE_TEXT:
Por.- Mariano Bolaños Montañez
Morelia, Mich., a 16 de julio del 2026.- Vecinos de la Colonia Jacarandas, en la ciudad de Morelia, se manifestaron la tarde de este miércoles en exigencia de la construcción de un puente para el cruce a pie durante el paso del tren por la zona, concentración que tuvo lugar sobre la avenida Michoacán casi en su cruce con el Río Grande.
La enérgica consigna se da luego del lamentable accidente donde el pasado martes perdiera la vida el pequeño Tadeo, de tan solo 6 años de edad, quién falleció arrollado tras intentar cruzar con su madre por encima de los vagones detenidos que obstruían el tránsito, momento en que el convoy comenzó a avanzar, provocando la caída del menor.
De acuerdo con vecinos de la zona, son varios los incidentes parecidos a este los que se han reportado en este cruce, mismos que han dejado personas con extremidades amputadas y víctimas mortales.
En este sentido, revelaron que ya se habían hecho solicitudes previas desde hace varios meses para la instalación de un cruce seguro, gestiones que han sido ignoradas por autoridades estatales y municipales, según denunciaron.
Durante la nutrida manifestación, habitantes de la zona recolectaron firmas de conductores y peatones para respaldar los oficios; tras varios minutos de circulación intermitente, finalmente el paso vehicular fue bloqueado en su totalidad.
Ante esta situación, elementos de la Secretaría de Seguridad Pública (SSP) de Michoacán arribaron al lugar, alineados en formación y con escudo en mano con miras a disolver la protesta que se realizaba de manera pacífica.
Tras una tensa negociación, algunos intercambios de palabras, incertidumbre y consignas por parte de los vecinos, se llegó a un acuerdo en el que autoridades de los gobiernos de Morelia y Michoacán, recibirán a representantes de la colonia la mañana de este jueves.
Sin embargo, de acuerdo a lo que informó Sergio Morales, encargado del orden de la Colonia Jacarandas, de no cumplirse este compromiso volverán a tomar la zona de manera indefinida, incluso pese a la presión e intimidación de los granaderos, hasta que se cumplan las demandas de la ciudadanía.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
By Mariano Bolaños Montañez
Morelia, Michoacán, July 16, 2026 - Residents of the Jacarandas neighborhood in Morelia protested Wednesday afternoon, demanding the construction of a pedestrian bridge to cross the train tracks. The demonstration took place on Michoacán Avenue near its intersection with the Río Grande.

This forceful protest comes after the tragic accident on Tuesday in which six-year-old Tadeo lost his life. He was struck and killed while attempting to cross with his mother over the stopped train cars that were blocking traffic. As the train began to move, the child fell.

According to local residents, several similar incidents have been reported at this crossing, resulting in amputations and fatalities. In this regard, they revealed that they had already submitted requests several months ago for the installation of a safe crossing, requests that have been ignored by state and municipal authorities, they denounced.

During the large demonstration, residents of the area collected signatures from drivers and pedestrians to support the petitions; after several minutes of intermittent traffic, the road was finally completely blocked.
Faced with this situation, officers from the Michoacán Public Security Secretariat (SSP) arrived at the scene, lined up in formation and with shields in hand, intending to disperse the peaceful protest.
After tense negotiations, some heated exchanges, uncertainty, and chants from the residents, an agreement was reached in which authorities from the Morelia and Michoacán governments will meet with representatives of the neighborhood on Thursday morning. However, according to Sergio Morales, the community leader in the Jacarandas neighborhood, if this commitment is not fulfilled, they will reoccupy the area indefinitely, even despite pressure and intimidation from the riot police, until the citizens' demands are met.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Doctors at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), Ghana’s second-largest teaching hospital, began a total withdrawal of services on Saturday (6 June), after condemning the suspension of the hospital’s chief executive officer and raising concerns about chronic overcrowding at its Emergency Department.
The industrial action, announced by the Komfo Anokye Doctors Association (KADA) in a notice dated 5 June, follows what the group described as recent developments involving the hospital’s management and worsening pressure on healthcare services.
In the notice signed by KADA Chairman Dr. Michael Leat, the doctors said members unanimously supported the strike after reviewing conditions at the hospital and the circumstances surrounding the CEO’s suspension.
The association said the CEO’s decision to temporarily halt new emergency admissions and coordinate patient referrals with nearby health facilities was a necessary measure to protect patients and staff amid severe congestion.
“KADA views the suspension as unjustified and counterproductive to ongoing efforts to address systemic challenges confronting the hospital,” the doctors said.
The association demanded the immediate review and reversal of the CEO’s suspension as a condition for ending the strike.
It also called on the KATH Board to establish clear policies for managing situations where emergency facilities exceed capacity, including guidelines on restricting admissions when patient safety is at risk.
In addition, the doctors urged the Ministry of Health to provide timelines for the operationalisation of Sewua Hospital and Afari Military Hospital, as well as the retooling of KATH and other hospitals in the Ashanti Region to ease pressure on the facility.
KADA said KATH serves as the main tertiary referral centre for Ghana’s middle and northern sectors but continues to operate under significant infrastructure constraints despite rising patient numbers.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
SRINAGAR: Scores of lawyers on Saturday staged a protest and blocked the High Court road in the Janipur area of Jammu, alleging that a police team from Srinagar attempted to arrest a practising advocate from within the High Court premises, triggering strong opposition from the legal fraternity.
According to Jammu newspaper Excelsior, a team from Sherghari Police Station, Srinagar, had reached the High Court premises on Friday to execute an arrest warrant issued by the Passenger Tax Court, Srinagar, against Advocate Ranjodh Singh.
The protesting lawyers raised slogans and condemned the alleged attempt to arrest the advocate inside the court complex, claiming it violated the sanctity of the court and established legal norms governing court premises.
Sources said lawyers present at the High Court prevented the police team from carrying out the arrest. Subsequently, a team from Janipur Police Station, led by the Station House Officer (SHO), reached the spot and defused the situation amicably.
The protesting lawyers alleged that senior officials of the Jammu and Kashmir Sports Department were behind the complaint registered against Advocate Ranjodh Singh at Sherghari Police Station and the subsequent court proceedings.
They claimed that the case was aimed at silencing the advocate, who had been questioning the alleged appointment of ineligible candidates under the sports quota. The lawyers demanded an inquiry into the recent appointments made in the Sports Department and extended full support to their colleague.
Meanwhile, the Jammu and Kashmir High Court Bar Association, Jammu (JKHCBAJ), also condemned the alleged attempt to arrest one of its members from inside the court premises.
In a statement, Association President Nirmal Kotwal described the incident as a serious breach of legal norms and court decorum.
“The Association views the attempted arrest as a serious breach of established legal norms and court decorum. Interference with advocates while they are performing their professional duties inside the court precincts compromises the independence of the legal profession and creates an atmosphere of intimidation that is detrimental to the administration of justice,” he said.
Kotwal also stressed the need for mutual respect between law enforcement agencies and the legal fraternity and urged the authorities to adhere to proper legal procedures while dealing with members of the Bar.

"Sans stockage de l'eau on ne pourra pas survivre": des éleveurs approuvent le projet d'un lac artificiel aux Angles
Publié le
Alors qu'une vingtaine d'associations dénoncent une grave atteinte à l'environnement et appellent à manifester ce dimanche 28 juin contre la retenue d'eau du Roc d'Aude, le projet est soutenu par la présidente du groupement pastoral Balcère Lladure qui réunit une trentaine d'éleveurs locaux.
C'est un projet à à 5,5 millions d'euros qui suscite la polémique et une forte opposition en Cerdagne/Capcir: porté par la mairie des Angles, la retenue d'eau du Roc d'Aude doit permettre de stocker jusqu'à 113.000 m³ d'eau, l'équivalent de 45 piscines olympiques, à plus de 2.000m d'altitude. Inacceptable pour de nombreuses associations et collectifs tels que Frene 66, Alternatiba, Bien Vivre en Pyrénées catalanes, la Ligue de Protection des Oiseaux ou encore Mountain Wilderness France qui dénoncent "un projet inutile et destructeur pour alimenter les canons à neige de la station de ski des Angles" et appellent donc à un rassemblement de contestation ce dimanche 28 juin à 11 heures, au niveau des télécabines de la station.
Un projet perçu très différemment selon les acteurs
Cependant, cette retenue collinaire compte également des soutiens, parmi lesquels celui de certains éleveurs locaux qui y voit au contraire une véritable planche de salut pour sauver l'avenir de leurs métiers. C'est notamment le cas de Mathilde Perarnaud, éleveuse à Formiguères et présidente du groupement Pastoral Balcère Lladure qui réunit une trentaine d'éleveurs favorables à la création de ce lac artificiel du Roc d'Aude:
"Nous sommes clairement un territoire où l'eau est un sujet de préoccupation majeure depuis de nombreuses années. Il faut donc parvenir à réinventer sa gestion et notamment son stockage pour l'agriculture et réussir à avoir de l'eau à disposition, surtout pour l'abreuvement de nos bêtes en été. On a déjà des secteurs ici sur la coll del Palm, à plus de 2. 000 mètres d'altitude où on ne peut pas rester aussi longtemps qu'avant parce qu'on n'a pas d'eau pour abreuver les brebis. Les sources sont taries et on a du mal à avoir de l 'eau pour abreuver nos troupeaux. Pour l'instant, on ne se sent pas encore directement menacés, on gère différemment. Mais on se dit que si ce projet de retenue du Roc d'Aude n'aboutit jamais, dans quelques années peut être, on ne pourra plus abreuver nos troupeaux, arroser nos prairies pour faire du foin pour l'hiver. Sans gestion de l'eau et sans stockage de l eau, on ne pourra pas survivre."
Un argument également mis en avant par la mairie des Angles qui affirme que la nouvelle retenue d'eau servirait aussi à sécuriser l'approvisionnement des éleveurs locaux et constituera un réservoir utile par les sapeurs-pompiers en cas d'incendie.
Face à la polémique, la mairie des Angles se défend
Alors que les nombreux détracteurs du lac artificiel du Roc d'Aude dénoncent un chantier lancé "sans étude d'impact, sans enquête publique et dans une logique de fait accompli lamentable" et demandent au Parc naturel régional des Pyrénées catalanes de faire respecter sa charte de protection de l'environnement tout en soulignant le contexte de réchauffement climatique et de raréfaction de la ressource en eau, la commune des Angles se défend bec et ongles.
Dans un communiqué publié sur ses réseaux sociaux, elle évoque "un projet de développement durable et d’utilité publique"(...) "fondamental pour l’avenir du territoire", "à faible impact environnemental" et qui "fera l’objet d’un suivi environnemental et écologique après sa réalisation". (...) L’eau sera prélevée pendant les périodes où les besoins naturels seront les plus faibles, afin de préserver la ressource et d’en garantir une gestion responsable ; transformée en neige elle retournera au printemps dans son milieu naturel, sur le même bassin versant, au moment où les sols, la végétation et les nappes en auront le plus besoin. (...) Il ne s’agit pas d’utiliser plus d’eau qu’actuellement, mais de mieux l’exploiter."
Une lecture diamétralement opposé donc à celle faite par une vingtaine d'associations écologistes et collectifs citoyens qui dénoncent au contraire "une atteinte à l’environnement sans précédent à l’échelle des Pyrénées et même à l’échelle de toutes les montagnes françaises" et annoncent avoir déposé un pourvoi en cassation au conseil d'Etat pour stopper le chantier de construction en cours. En attendant, le degré d'amplitude de la mobilisation de ce dimanche aux Angles aura valeur de test populaire pour tous les opposants au lac artificiel du Roc d'Aude.

"Without water storage, we won't be able to survive": Farmers approve the artificial lake project in Les Angles
Published on
While some twenty associations denounce a serious threat to the environment and are calling for a demonstration this Sunday, June 28, against the Roc d'Aude reservoir, the project is supported by the president of the Balcère Lladure pastoral group, which brings together about thirty local farmers.
This €5.5 million project is sparking controversy and strong opposition in Cerdagne/Capcir: spearheaded by the Les Angles town hall, the Roc d'Aude reservoir is intended to store up to 113,000 m³ of water, the equivalent of 45 Olympic-sized swimming pools, at an altitude of over 2,000 meters. Unacceptable to numerous associations and groups such as Frene 66, Alternatiba, Bien Vivre en Pyrénées catalanes, the League for the Protection of Birds, and Mountain Wilderness France, who denounce "a useless and destructive project to supply the snow cannons at the Les Angles ski resort" and are therefore calling for a protest rally this Sunday, June 28, at 11:00 a.m., at the resort's gondola lifts.

A project perceived very differently by different stakeholders.
However, this reservoir also has its supporters, including some local farmers who see it as a real lifeline to save the future of their livelihoods. This is particularly true for Mathilde Perarnaud, a livestock farmer in Formiguères and president of the Pastoral Balcère Lladure group, which brings together some thirty farmers in favor of creating this artificial lake at Roc d'Aude:

"We are clearly a region where water has been a major concern for many years. We therefore need to reinvent its management, especially its storage for agriculture, and ensure we have water available, particularly for watering our livestock in the summer. We already have areas here on the Coll del Palm, at over 2,000 meters altitude, where we can't stay as long as before because we don't have enough water for the sheep. The springs have dried up, and we struggle to get water for our flocks. For now, we don't feel directly threatened; we're managing things differently. But we're thinking that if this reservoir project goes ahead..." The Roc d'Aude project will never be completed. In a few years, perhaps, we won't be able to water our herds or irrigate our meadows to make hay for the winter. Without water management and storage, we won't be able to survive." This argument is also put forward by the Les Angles town hall, which asserts that the new reservoir will also serve to secure the water supply for local farmers and will constitute a useful reservoir for firefighters in case of fire.
Faced with the controversy, the Les Angles town hall defends itself.
While the many detractors of the Roc d'Aude artificial lake denounce a project launched "without an impact study, without a public inquiry, and in a lamentable fait accompli" and demand that the Catalan Pyrenees Regional Natural Park enforce its environmental protection charter, while emphasizing the context of climate change and water scarcity, the municipality of Les Angles is defending itself tooth and nail. In a statement published on its social media, it refers to "a sustainable development and public utility project" (...) "fundamental to the future of the region," "with a low environmental impact," and which "will be subject to environmental and ecological monitoring after its completion." (...) Water will be drawn during periods of lowest natural demand, in order to preserve the resource and ensure responsible management; transformed into snow, it will return to its natural environment in the spring, within the same watershed, at the time when the soil, vegetation, and groundwater need it most. (...) It's not about using more water than we currently do, but about using it more efficiently." This interpretation is diametrically opposed to that of some twenty environmental associations and citizen groups who, on the contrary, denounce "an unprecedented attack on the environment in the Pyrenees and even in all of France's mountain ranges" and announce that they have filed an appeal with the Council of State to halt the ongoing construction. Meanwhile, the scale of the mobilization this Sunday in Les Angles will serve as a popular test for all those opposed to the artificial lake at Roc d'Aude.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
SAFTU general secretary Zwelinzima Vavi addressed Sapo workers outside the department offices.
Image: Oupa Mokoena/Independent Newspapers
Highlighting their plight of working for nine years without salary increases, disgruntled SA Post Office (Sapo) workers took to the street in Pretoria on Wednesday.
Joined by various workers' unions affiliated to the SA Federation of Trade Unions (SAFTU) and Cosatu, workers marched from the Union Buildings to the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies to hand over a memorandum of demands.
They demanded that Minister Solly Malatsi intervene in their labour disputes and provide an update regarding Sapo's business rescue process.
SAFTU secretary general Zwelinzima Vavi, addressing marchers outside the department offices, hailed the demonstration as a show of unity among workers' unions.
He said it was not the first time workers had come to the department to make a plea for their issues to be addressed, but to no avail.
He painted a bleak picture of the Post Office entity, noting that a mere 5 700 workers remain after successive retrenchments.
He further accused the government of "deliberately killing one of the most important sectors. They are leaving it to collapse so that they can give to their comrades".
Vavi claimed “comrades” looted the Post Office while serving on its board.
He alleged Sapo deducted provident fund contributions from salaries but failed to pay them over to the relevant authorities.
"They deducted money for medical aid and when you become sick you discover that you have no cent," he said.
Their memorandum also demanded an immediate R5 000 across-the-board salary increase and that 30% of government business be allocated to Sapo.
They also demanded answers on the R3.8 billion funding intervention meant to stabilise operations, along with full job security and a moratorium on retrenchments.
The business rescue practitioners recently confirmed that the R3.8bn is in Sapo’s approved rescue plan and government submissions.
Of that, R2.4 bn has been released to cover operating costs and creditor payments, and they said a turnaround plan exists to stabilise the entity.
Workers further called for the immediate appointment of a functional Sapo board and a time-bound exit strategy for business rescue practitioners that avoids liquidation.
The South African Postal Workers said: "We want the government to address the issue of outstanding money for the completion of the business rescue plan which is R3.8 billion."
National Organiser for Communication Workers Union, Moffat Seutlwadi, said the government needs to transform Sapo to be technologically competitive instead of requesting the private sector to invest in it and privatise the entity.
"The post office is not for sale to be privatised," he said.
A department representative, who received the memorandum, promised to give feedback to workers leaders within the stipulated timeframe.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Taux d’occupation de 250 %, dégradation des conditions de travail : pourquoi la maison d’arrêt de Carcassonne sera-t-elle bloquée par un mouvement syndical ?
Lundi 27 avril, c’est dans le cadre d’un mouvement national que la section locale du syndicat Ufap-Unsa Justice participera au blocage de la maison d’arrêt de Carcassonne, dans un contexte de dégradation des conditions de travail. Explications.
À l’appel du bureau national Ufap-Unsa Justice, la section locale de Carcassonne fait savoir qu’elle participera au mouvement national prévu ce lundi 27 avril, avec le blocage de la maison d’arrêt départemental de l’avenue du Général Leclerc, à partir de 6 h 30. Cette mobilisation s’inscrit dans un contexte de dégradation continue des conditions de travail des personnels pénitentiaire, avec une situation particulièrement préoccupante au niveau national faisant aujourd’hui état de 88 000 détenus, pour 66 000 places. À Carcassonne, on peut désormais parler "d’une surpopulation carcérale chronique, où rien ne roule !"
Nous sommes aujourd’hui à un taux d’occupation de 250 % avec 155 détenus
Secrétaire local Ufap-Unsa, Pierre Journet ne se fait plus d’illusion : "A la maison d’arrêt de Carcassonne, nous sommes aujourd’hui à un taux d’occupation de 250 % avec 155 détenus pour 64 places effectives. Ici, c’est devenu une moyenne et c’est ça le pire. Ça engendre bien évidemment des bagarres, car on a pas mal de narcotrafiquants venus de régions différentes. Nous manquons de moyens humains et financiers…"
Sur le plan national, ce sont 5 000 postes qui restent vacants, dont 4 000 chez les personnels pénitentiaires. En région Occitanie, les besoins restent tout aussi importants, avec un manque estimé à 400 postes tous corps confondus, dont 250 pour les personnels de surveillance. "Dans ce contexte, l’annonce de la création de onze postes apparaît largement insuffisante au regard de la réalité du terrain qui est ignorée !", souligne le syndicat Ufap-Unsa Justice. Sur ces onze postes, Pierre Journet se réjouit tout de même, même s’il ne saute pas au plafond, "car nous devrions en avoir quatre à Carcassonne. Un moindre mal, par rapport à la dizaine de départs à la retraite dont nous avons à faire face…"
Ce n’est pas en agitant le chiffon rouge que la situation va se débloquer
Ce lundi 27 avril dès 6 h 30, c’est pour cela que la section locale de l’Ufap-Unsa Justice de la maison d’arrêt de Carcassonne bloquera l’entrée de l’établissement pénitentiaire, avec pour conséquences d’empêcher notamment de rentrer "les personnels non indispensables, ainsi que les livraisons". Cette situation de blocage est prévue pour durer toute la matinée… S’il se dit solidaire du mouvement porté par l’Ufap-Unsa Justice, le syndicat FO pénitentiaire de la maison d’arrêt n’y participera pas : "Nous partageons bien évidemment le triste constat de la double problématique actuelle que sont la densité carcérale et les vacances de postes… Mais ce n’est pas en agitant le chiffon rouge que la situation va se débloquer. L’urgence mérite de vraies solutions, pas un enfumage électoral !" N’y auraient pas des élections professionnelles à venir bientôt ?

MESSAGE_TEXT:
MADRID (EP). Los sindicatos Rstic, UGT, Intersindical, USO y Co.Bas han convocado para la semana que viene tres jornadas de huelga para la plantilla de la consultora tecnológica francesa Capgemini en España, en el marco del Expediente de Regulación de Empleo (ERE) que afecta a 717 trabajadores en el país, en Valencia y otros seis centros de trabajo.
Según ha informado UGT en un comunicado, las secciones sindicales en Capgemini España irán a la huelga los próximos días 20, 21 y 22 de mayo, tras constatar el "bloqueo" de la negociación del despido colectivo planteado por la dirección de la compañía, que afecta al 6,5% de la plantilla.
Los sindicatos han denunciado, después de varias reuniones de negociación, que la empresa "no ha mostrado una voluntad real de reducir o evitar los despidos", ni tampoco de acordar medidas de voluntariedad "suficientes" que minimicen las salidas forzosas.
Las organizaciones sindicales han considerado "inaceptables" las propuestas trasladadas hasta la fecha por la empresa, al entender que los avances en aspectos "esenciales" como el número de personas afectadas, las indemnizaciones o la voluntariedad han sido "mínimos insuficientes, pese a que el grupo Capgemini obtuvo en el pasado ejercicio un beneficio neto de 1.061 millones de euros".
Los sindicatos convocantes han señalado que el objetivo de las movilizaciones es "exigir alternativas menos traumáticas al despido, entre ellas, fórmulas de voluntariedad real, prejubilaciones, recolocaciones efectivas y planes de formación y reciclaje profesional".
En este contexto, han insistido que su voluntad es seguir afrontando las próximas reuniones "con responsabilidad y voluntad de negociación", pero han reclamado a la dirección un cambio de actitud que permita avanzar hacia un acuerdo que proteja a las personas afectadas.
Reduce en 31 personas la afectación del ERE
Capgemini redujo la semana pasada en 31 trabajadores la afectación del ERE en España, que ahora alcanzará a un máximo de 717 personas, frente a las 748 salidas iniciales, lo que supone una reducción aproximada del 4,1% y una incidencia cercana al 6,5% de la plantilla, compuesta por alrededor de 11.000 personas.
El proceso, que afectará a siete centros de trabajo (Madrid, Barcelona, Asturias, Valencia, Sevilla, Málaga y Cádiz), se centra mayoritariamente en trabajadores sin proyecto.
Según informó en un comunicado la sección sindical de CCOO-Capgemini, la quinta jornada de negociación del despido colectivo concluyó con avances "parciales" en las condiciones para la plantilla.
En este contexto, la empresa planteó una indemnización de entre 20 y 30 días por año trabajado, con un tope de 12 mensualidades según el tramo, una propuesta que el sindicato rechazó por considerarla "insuficiente".
Así, el sindicato consideró que la propuesta actual de la dirección todavía dista de los objetivos mínimos necesarios para garantizar una protección adecuada.
En este sentido, la sección sindical sostuvo que cualquier acuerdo debe partir, como mínimo, de las indemnizaciones equivalentes al despido improcedente, esto es, entre 33 y 45 días por año trabajado y un máximo de entre 24 y 42 mensualidades.
En cuanto al escudo social, CCOO consiguió ampliar los colectivos excluidos del ERE al incorporar, a los supuestos ya aceptados, la protección de parejas --para evitar que el despido afecte a ambos miembros-- y de personas trabajadoras con una discapacidad igual o superior al 33%.
En cuanto a la voluntariedad, la dirección mantuvo el derecho de veto y ofreció primas de adhesión por tramo de edad que oscilan entre 5.000 y 8.000 euros, cuantías que CCOO consideró también "insuficientes" para reducir las salidas forzosas.
No obstante, el sindicato mantuvo su firme posición de excluir también a quienes tengan a su cargo menores con una discapacidad superior al 50%.
Entre los compromisos alcanzados destacaron el cómputo de la edad actuarial con la edad cumplida durante todo 2026; la ampliación del convenio especial con la Seguridad Social, extendiendo la cotización hasta los 63 años para el tramo de 55 a 62 años; y beneficios adicionales como la prórroga del seguro médico durante tres meses, la inoperatividad de los pactos de no competencia y un servicio 'premium' de 'outplacement'.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
MADRID (EP). The unions Rstic, UGT, Intersindical, USO, and Co.Bas have called for three days of strike action next week for the workforce of the French technology consulting firm Capgemini in Spain, as part of the Employment Regulation File (ERE) affecting 717 workers in the country, in Valencia, and at six other work centers.

According to a statement released by UGT, the union sections at Capgemini Spain will strike on May 20, 21, and 22, after observing the "blockage" in negotiations regarding the collective dismissal proposed by the company's management, which affects 6.5% of the workforce.

The unions denounced, after several negotiation meetings, that the company "has not shown a real willingness to reduce or avoid layoffs," nor to agree on "sufficient" voluntary measures to minimize forced departures.

The unions have deemed the proposals put forward by the company to date "unacceptable," arguing that progress on "essential" issues such as the number of affected employees, compensation, and voluntary redundancy has been "minimal and insufficient, despite the fact that the Capgemini group posted a net profit of €1.061 billion last year."

The unions organizing the protests stated that the aim is "to demand less traumatic alternatives to layoffs, including genuine voluntary redundancy options, early retirement, effective job placement, and training and retraining programs."

In this context, they emphasized their commitment to approaching upcoming meetings "responsibly and with a willingness to negotiate," but called on management to change its approach to reach an agreement that protects those affected.

Capgemini Reduces the Impact of Layoff Plan by 31 Employees
Last week, Capgemini reduced the number of employees affected by its planned layoff plan in Spain by 31, bringing the maximum number of job losses to 717, down from the initial 748. This represents a reduction of approximately 4.1% and an impact of around 6.5% of the workforce, which comprises approximately 11,000 people.

The process, which will affect seven work centers (Madrid, Barcelona, ​​Asturias, Valencia, Seville, Malaga, and Cadiz), focuses primarily on employees without specific projects.

According to a statement from the CCOO-Capgemini union, the fifth day of collective dismissal negotiations concluded with "partial" progress on the terms for the workforce.

In this context, the company proposed severance pay of between 20 and 30 days per year of service, capped at 12 months' salary depending on the seniority bracket. The union rejected this proposal as "insufficient." Thus, the union considered that management's current proposal still falls short of the minimum objectives necessary to guarantee adequate protection.

In this regard, the union branch maintained that any agreement must begin, at a minimum, with compensation equivalent to that for unfair dismissal, that is, between 33 and 45 days per year of service and a maximum of between 24 and 42 months' salary.

Regarding the social safety net, CCOO managed to expand the groups excluded from the workforce reduction plan by adding, to the already accepted cases, protection for couples—to prevent the dismissal from affecting both partners—and for workers with a disability of 33% or more.

As for voluntary participation, management maintained its right of veto and offered commitment bonuses based on age brackets, ranging from 5,000 to 8,000 euros, amounts that CCOO also considered "insufficient" to reduce forced layoffs.

However, the union maintained its firm position of also excluding those with dependent children with a disability exceeding 50%.

Among the commitments reached were the calculation of actuarial age based on the age reached throughout 2026; the extension of the special agreement with Social Security, extending contributions until age 63 for the 55-62 age bracket; and additional benefits such as a three-month extension of health insurance, the suspension of non-compete agreements, and a premium outplacement service.

Malda: Crores missing from over 100 CSP bank accounts
MPost25 Jun 2026 12:50 AM IST
MPost25 Jun 2026 12:50 AM IST
Malda: Tension prevailed at the main branch of a nationalised bank near Netaji More in English Bazar municipal area on Wednesday after hundreds of customers staged a protest alleging that crores of rupees had been siphoned off from more than 100 accounts linked to a Customer Service Point (CSP) at Nityanandapur under the Kazigram region of English Bazar block.
According to the protesters, the CSP was operated by Satyajit Lala and Nipa Das, who allegedly misappropriated customers’ deposits worth almost 4 crores over several years. Most of the affected account holders are daily wage earners and villagers who regularly deposit their savings through the CSP. Customers alleged that whenever someone withdrew Rs 10,000, additional amounts ranging from Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000 were withdrawn from their accounts without their knowledge. They further claimed that passbooks were updated with manipulated entries, concealing the unauthorised transactions. Several customers alleged that the money was withdrawn through the bank’s main branch and accused certain officials of ignoring repeated complaints.
“We trusted the CSP with our hard-earned savings. When we checked our accounts, we found huge amounts missing. Despite informing the authorities several times, no action was taken,” alleged customer Sumon Ghosh.
Another customer, Jaya Das, said: “Some people have lost Rs 50,000, while others have lost lakhs. One customer reportedly found nearly Rs 15 lakh missing from the account. We want a proper investigation and our money returned.”
As the CSP has remained closed for the past week, angry customers gathered at the main branch and demonstrated for several hours. The situation became tense, prompting the deployment of police from English Bazar Police Station to maintain order. The protesters demanded immediate intervention by bank authorities and warned of a larger agitation if the missing funds are not recovered. Neither Satyajit Lala nor bank officials issued any official statement regarding the allegations.

La huelga indefinida en la educación valenciana que comenzó el pasado 11 de mayo entra en la cuarta semana entre denuncias de agresión y encierros. La Generalitat rechaza «ceder a presiones que bloquean el diálogo, recuerda que la Ley de Libertad Educativa la aprobaron las Cortes» y recalca que «ha realizado la mejor oferta de la historia».
La novena reunión entre los sindicatos y Educación terminó sin acuerdo y con los representantes del Stepv, UGT y CCOO encerrados durante horas en la Conselleria. Los representantes de CSIF lamentaron haberse quedado bloqueados en el edificio de Educación en contra de su voluntad.
Antes, los sindicatos denunciaron una «brutal agresión» de un agente de la Policía Nacional a una docente que protestaba en la calle. La Delegación del Gobierno anunció una «investigación para depurar responsabilidades».
El debate entre los sindicatos y la Generalitat había encallado en el punto de retribuciones, una cuestión sobre la cual ya hay un acuerdo firmado por dos organizaciones sindicales: ANPE y CSIF. Sin embargo, los otros tres sindicatos han reclamado que se vuelva a ponerse sobre la mesa argumentando que es precisamente esta cuestión la más rechazada en la consulta que han realizado este fin de semana a los docentes. Defienden que «se tiene que reabrir para facilitar la firma de un acuerdo de bases, necesario para poder ir cerrando el conflicto y que necesariamente requerirá de posteriores desarrollos».
Por ello, los sindicatos han propuesto a la consellera de Educación, Carmen Ortí, que consultara a su homólogo de Hacienda, José Antonio Rovira, para incorporar la propuesta, y han aseverado que iban a permanecer en la sala «a la espera» de que se les diera una respuesta a sus dos principales peticiones: un documento base sobre un posible «acuerdo global» y que se reabran las conversaciones sobre la subida salarial al profesorado.
Ortí ha lamentado el bloqueo al que ha llegado la negociación con las organizaciones sindicales después de que STEPV, UGT y CCOO decidieron encerrarse en las dependencias de la Conselleria y hayan exigido reivindicaciones que no corresponden a la mesa de negociación.
Ortí ha recordado que durante las últimas semanas se han acercado posturas relativas a la reducción de ratios, eliminación de burocracia, mejora de infraestructuras educativas, inclusión y Formación Profesional. Todas ellas, ha destacado, acompañadas de calendarios concretos y dotación presupuestaria.
La consellera de Educación ha señalado que el principal obstáculo para cerrar un acuerdo ya no reside en cuestiones educativas, sino en la exigencia de algunos sindicatos de reabrir el acuerdo salarial alcanzado previamente con otras organizaciones sindicales.
«Lo que no vamos a hacer es romper de manera unilateral un acuerdo que ya tenemos cerrado con una parte de las organizaciones sindicales. No hablaría bien de nosotros si nos sometiésemos ahora a presiones y rompiésemos un acuerdo que ya hemos firmado previamente», ha afirmado.
En este sentido, la consellera ha insistido en que está dispuesta a seguir dialogando sobre todos los aspectos que continúan abiertos, pero considera que cualquier negociación seria debe respetar los acuerdos ya alcanzados.
Asimismo, ha defendido que la propuesta retributiva presentada por la Generalitat Valenciana sitúa al profesorado en condiciones equiparables a las acordadas recientemente en Cataluña.
Según ha explicado, la Comunidad Valenciana adelanta la aplicación de las mejoras salariales y permite que el profesorado empiece a percibir el incremento ya desde septiembre de este año.
Por otra parte, Ortí también ha trasladado el rechazo a la derogación de la Ley de Libertad Educativa, una exigencia planteada por STEPV, UGT y CCOO.
«No podemos derogar una ley aprobada por Les Corts mediante una mesa de negociación. Si tienen una propuesta legislativa, ese es otro ámbito. Exigir la derogación de una ley no es negociar, implica romper las negociaciones», han señalado desde el departamento autonómico.
Respecto al encierro protagonizado por representantes sindicales en dependencias de la Conselleria, la consellera ha apelado a la responsabilidad de todas las partes y ha pedido que la situación se resuelva sin aumentar la tensión.

The indefinite strike in Valencian education enters its fourth week amid allegations of assault and sit-ins.
The indefinite strike in Valencian education, which began on May 11, enters its fourth week amid allegations of assault and sit-ins. The Valencian government (Generalitat) refuses to "give in to pressures that are blocking dialogue," recalling that the Law on Educational Freedom was approved by the Valencian Parliament (Cortes) and emphasizing that it "has made the best offer in history."

The ninth meeting between the unions and the Education Department ended without an agreement, with representatives from STEPV, UGT, and CCOO locked inside the Ministry for hours. CSIF representatives lamented being trapped in the Education building against their will.

Earlier, the unions denounced a "brutal assault" by a National Police officer on a teacher protesting in the street. The Government Delegation announced an "investigation to determine responsibility."

The debate between the unions and the Generalitat (Valencian regional government) had stalled on the issue of salaries, a matter on which two unions, ANPE and CSIF, had already signed an agreement. However, the other three unions demanded that the issue be reopened, arguing that it was precisely this issue that received the most rejection in the consultation they conducted with teachers this past weekend. They maintain that "it must be reopened to facilitate the signing of a framework agreement, necessary to begin resolving the conflict and which will necessarily require further developments."

Therefore, the unions proposed to the Minister of Education, Carmen Ortí, that she consult with her counterpart in Finance, José Antonio Rovira, to incorporate the proposal, and asserted that they would remain in the room "waiting" for a response to their two main demands: a framework document outlining a possible "comprehensive agreement" and the reopening of talks on the salary increase for teachers.

Ortí lamented the deadlock in negotiations with the unions after STEPV, UGT, and CCOO staged a sit-in at the Ministry of Education and demanded concessions that were not within the scope of the negotiation table.

Ortí noted that in recent weeks, positions had been narrowing regarding reduced class sizes, streamlined bureaucracy, improved educational infrastructure, inclusion, and Vocational Training. She emphasized that all of these issues were accompanied by specific timelines and budget allocations.

The Minister of Education pointed out that the main obstacle to reaching an agreement no longer lies in educational matters, but rather in the demands of some unions to reopen the salary agreement previously reached with other unions.

"What we will not do is unilaterally break an agreement that we have already reached with some of the unions. It would reflect poorly on us if we were to succumb to pressure now and break an agreement that we have already signed," she stated. In this regard, the regional minister insisted that she is willing to continue dialogue on all outstanding issues, but believes that any serious negotiation must respect the agreements already reached.

She also defended the salary proposal presented by the Valencian Regional Government, stating that it places teachers on a level playing field with those recently agreed upon in Catalonia.

As she explained, the Valencian Community is bringing forward the implementation of salary increases, allowing teachers to begin receiving the raise as early as September of this year.

Furthermore, Ortí also conveyed her rejection of the repeal of the Law on Educational Freedom, a demand put forward by the STEPV, UGT, and CCOO unions.

"We cannot repeal a law approved by the Valencian Parliament through a negotiation table. If they have a legislative proposal, that is a different matter. Demanding the repeal of a law is not negotiation; it implies breaking off negotiations," the regional department stated. Regarding the sit-in staged by union representatives at the Ministry's offices, the Minister appealed to the responsibility of all parties and asked that the situation be resolved without escalating tensions.

"They are adults, and above all else is their own will. Our position is that negotiations can continue, and it is not necessary to make any unilateral and concrete decisions that would block dialogue," she stated.

New meetings this Monday
The Minister of Education reiterated that she is keeping the lines of communication open and insisted that her objective remains to reach a comprehensive agreement that benefits teachers and the Valencian education system. However, she warned that she will not accept conditions that exceed her authority, nor the reopening of agreements already signed while other issues remain unresolved.
The unions have been invited to sectoral negotiation meetings to discuss each point of the proposal and move forward in finalizing agreements. A panel discussion on Educational Inclusion is scheduled for Monday at 9:00 a.m., and another at 1:00 p.m. on Staffing.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
OTTAWA — Security officers at the Bank of Canada began a job action today after talks failed to secure a new collective agreement between the central bank and the union.
The Public Service Alliance of Canada says 63 security officers at the Bank of Canada's Ottawa and Montreal offices are on strike and the Montreal workers are also locked out by the employer.
A statement from the union claims officials at the central bank are pushing for changes that would undermine how seniority affects overtime and vacation for workers, as well as proposing a rollback in maternity leave.
The union also alleges that the Bank of Canada has been contacting workers to work through the legal strike and plans to contract a third-party for security services during the labour disruption.
The Bank of Canada would not comment on the labour action or negotiations but says in a statement that management needs to ensure all critical operations can continue during the dispute while honouring its obligations under the Labour Code.
The union says workers are looking for fair wages, stable schedules and "basic respect" from one of Canada's most powerful financial institutions.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published June 23, 2026.
Craig Lord, The Canadian Press

MESSAGE_TEXT:
شهد محيط مركب جمعية تحدي الإعاقة بمدينة تيزنيت، مساء أمس الجمعة، وقفة احتجاجية غاضبة خاضتها مجموعة من أمهات وآباء الأطفال المستفيدين من خدمات المركز، تنديداً بما وصفنه بـ”الإقصاء الممنهج” والتمويه المتعمّد لحرمانهن من المشاركة في أشغال الجمع العام الاستثنائي المخصص لتجديد المكتب المسير للجمعية .
وحسب تصريحات متطابقة للمحتجات، فإن إدارة الجمعية وجّهت دعوات للأمهات والمنخرطين لحضور الجمع العام الاستثنائي حددت فيها الموعد مساء يوم الجمعة في تمام الساعة الرابعة والنصف بعد الزوال . كما أكدت إحدى الأمهات المنخرطات منذ سنة 2011 أن مديرة المركز أرسلت تسجيلاً صوتياً عبر تطبيق “واتساب” صبيحة يوم الخميس تؤكد فيه صراحة انعقاد الجمع في “الفترة المسائية” دون أي إشارة للفترة الصباحية .
إلا أنه وبمجرد وصول الأمهات والآباء إلى مقر المركب في الوقت المحدد، تفاجأ الجميع بإبلاغهم من طرف الإدارة بأن عملية التصويت قد انتهت بالفعل وأن أشغال الجمع العام قد أُغلقت ، بدعوى أن الاجتماع انعقد في الساعة العاشرة صباحاً، وهو ما اعتبره المحتجون “طبخة جاهزة” وتمويهاً مقصوداً لإبعاد الأصوات الناقدة وتمرير لائحة المكتب الجديد دون نصاب قانوني حقيقي منخرط .
وأفادت شهادات استقتها ” تيزبريس ” من أمهات منخرطات أن محاولتهن الولوج إلى القاعة ومطالبتهن بفتح باب النقاش أسفرت عن مشادات كلامية حادة وتلاسن بين المحتجات وبعض العاملين بالمركز، تطورت إلى إغلاق الأبواب في وجه الأمهات والاعتداء اللفظي عليهن وفق تصريحاتهن، وسط حالة من الفوضى استدعت حضور ممثلي السلطة المحلية وعناصر من القوات المساعدة والوقاية المدنية لتأمين المكان.
وفي هذا السياق، صرحت إحدى الأمهات الغاضبات قائلة: «نحن منخرطات منذ سنوات طويلة وبطاقاتنا تثبت ذلك، ولدينا كامل الحق في اختيار من يمثل مصلحة أبنائنا. ما حدث اليوم هو التفاف على القانون واستبداد بالمسؤولية، حيث تم إدخال بعض المؤطرين فقط للتصويت وإقصاء الأسر» .
وأمام هذا الوضع، طالبت الأسر المحتجة بإلغاء مخرجات هذا الجمع العام الاستثنائي نظراً لـما اعتبرته المحتجات “خروقات”، داعية إلى إعادة تنظيمه في ظروف تطبعها الشفافية والديمقراطية وبحضور كافة المنخرطين الفعليين .
كما وجّهت الأمهات نداءً عاجلاً إلى عامل إقليم تيزنيت للتدخل الفوري لفتح تحقيق في تدبير شؤون هذه الجمعية التي تستفيد من منائح ودعم عمومي موجه أساساً لرعاية الأطفال ذوي الإعاقة، معبرات عن تخوفهن من انعكاس هذه الصراعات الإدارية على جودة الخدمات والرعاية المقدمة لأبنائهن داخل المركز .
ويُذكر في هذا السياق، أن الجمعية كانت قد وزعت ونشرت سابقاً، بمناسبة حفل تأسيسها، برنامجاً رسمياً يتضمن في فقرته الأخيرة بنداً واضحاً يتعلق بعقد “الجمع العام الاستثنائي” يوم الجمعة 26 يونيو الجاري على الساعة الرابعة و النصف بعد الزوال .

The area surrounding the Challenge of Disability Association complex in Tiznit witnessed an angry protest on Friday evening by a group of mothers and fathers of children benefiting from the center's services. They were protesting what they described as "systematic exclusion" and deliberate obfuscation to prevent them from participating in the extraordinary general assembly scheduled to elect a new board for the association.

According to statements from the protesters, the association's administration had sent invitations to mothers and members to attend the extraordinary general assembly, specifying the meeting time as Friday afternoon at 4:30 PM. One mother, a member since 2011, confirmed that the center's director had sent a voice recording via WhatsApp on Thursday morning explicitly stating that the assembly would be held in the "afternoon," without any mention of the morning.

However, upon the arrival of the mothers and fathers at the center on time, they were surprised to be informed by the administration that the voting process had already concluded and the general assembly meeting had been adjourned. The administration claimed the meeting had begun at 10:00 AM, a claim the protesters considered a pre-arranged scheme and a deliberate attempt to silence dissenting voices and pass the new board without a genuine quorum.

According to testimonies gathered by "Tizpress" from mothers who were members, their attempts to enter the hall and demand a discussion led to heated verbal exchanges and arguments between the protesters and some center staff. These escalated to the point where the doors were locked against the mothers, and they were verbally abused, according to their statements. The resulting chaos necessitated the intervention of local authorities, auxiliary forces, and civil protection personnel to secure the area.

In this context, one of the angry mothers stated, "We have been members for many years, and our membership cards prove it. We have every right to choose who represents the best interests of our children." What happened today is a circumvention of the law and an abuse of power, as only a few supervisors were allowed to vote, excluding the families.

Faced with this situation, the protesting families demanded the annulment of the outcomes of this extraordinary general assembly, citing what they considered "violations." They called for its reorganization under conditions of transparency and democracy, with the participation of all active members.

The mothers also issued an urgent appeal to the governor of the Tiznit region, requesting his immediate intervention to launch an investigation into the management of this association, which benefits from grants and public support primarily intended for the care of children with disabilities. They expressed their concern that these administrative conflicts would negatively impact the quality of services and care provided to their children at the center.

It is worth noting that the association had previously distributed and published, on the occasion of its founding ceremony, an official program that included, in its final section, a clear clause regarding the convening of an "extraordinary general assembly" on Friday, June 26, at 4:30 PM.

Srinagar, May 7: The students and teachers of an educational institution in Jammu and Kashmir’s Shopian district on Thursday staged a protest march against the government’s decision to declare it an unlawful entity under the UAPA, officials said.

Political parties have criticised the government’s decision and demanded a withdrawal of the notification.–(PTI)

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Tension rises in Mhalaunda, Mzimba District, Malawi ahead of planned demonstration by Mhalaunda Citizens Forum
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Tension is rising in Mhalaunda, Mzimba District, following reports that the management of Embangweni Mission Hospital recently held a meeting with officers from Embangweni Police ahead of a planned demonstration by the Mhalaunda Citizens Forum.
The forum has vowed to close Mhalaunda Health Centre on July 13, 2026, following the expiry of a 90-day ultimatum it gave Embangweni Mission Hospital.
The group is demanding that the hospital hand over the facility to the Malawi Government so that residents can access free public healthcare services.
According to a source who claimed to have attended the meeting, the discussions were held on Wednesday at Embangweni Mission Hospital and involved officers from Embangweni Police Station.
“I can confirm that Embangweni Mission Hospital plans to use the police to stop people from closing Mhalaunda Health Centre. I attended the meeting, and there are also plans to arrest some leaders of the Mhalaunda Citizens Forum,” the source alleged.
Efforts to obtain comments from Embangweni Mission Hospital and Embangweni Police were unsuccessful by the time this article was published. The dispute centres on the ownership and management of Mhalaunda Health Centre.
Residents say the facility was built by the Mhalaunda community with support from World Vision and is currently managed by Embangweni Mission Hospital under the Livingstonia Synod of the CCAP.
Although under-five children’s services and maternity care are provided free of charge, patients are required to pay for most other medical services.
Community members claim and Malawi24 independently verified through an undercover visit by a reporter posing as a patient that consultation fees range from K2,500 to K5,000, while treatment for illnesses such as malaria, including medication, can cost up to K25,000.
They argue that these charges make healthcare unaffordable for many families.The Mhalaunda Citizens Forum maintains that the health centre should be handed over to the Malawi Government so that all residents can access free public healthcare services.
In a previously meeting held at M’mbelwa district council chamber Livingstonia Synod General Secretary William Tembo and the M’Mbelwa District Council reportedly acknowledged that Mhalaunda Health Centre belongs to the people of Mhalaunda and not to the Synod or Embangweni Mission Hospital.
Despite the reported plans to stop the taking over of the hospital leaders of the Mhalaunda Citizens Forum say they remain committed to pursuing what they describe as the community’s legitimate demand for accessible, affordable, and free public healthcare.
Malawi24 is following the matter, as the July 13 deadline approaches.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Σε απεργία κατέρχονται οι βοθροκαθαριστές της επαρχίας Λεμεσού. Οι επαγγελματίες του κλάδου διαμαρτύρονται για τα χρόνια προβλήματα στη διαχείριση και την απόρριψη των λυμάτων.
Αυτή την ώρα πραγματοποιούν εκδήλωση διαμαρτυρίας έξω από το Προεδρικό Μέγαρο.
Τα προβλήματα που προέκυψαν λόγω της μειωμένης δυναμικότητας του σταθμού Βατί είναι προσωρινά, λαμβάνονται μέτρα για την ορθή και απρόσκοπτη διαχείριση των λυμάτων και εξετάζονται πρόσθετες λύσεις προς διευκόλυνση των επαγγελματιών βοθροκαθαριστών της Λεμεσού, αναφέρει το Τμήμα Αναπτύξεως Υδάτων και το Τμήμα Περιβάλλοντος.
Σε ανακοίνωση, με αφορμή τις απεργιακές κινητοποιήσεις των βοθροκαθαριστών της Λεμεσού, ΤΑΥ και Τμήμα Περιβάλλοντος ενημερώνουν ότι, λόγω της αναβάθμισης του Σταθμού Επεξεργασίας Λυμάτων στο Βατί, έχουν ήδη τεθεί σε εφαρμογή συγκεκριμένες διευθετήσεις ώστε να διασφαλιστεί η συνεχής εξυπηρέτηση των επαγγελματιών του χώρου.
Κατά τη διάρκεια των εργασιών, προστίθεται, ο σταθμός λειτουργεί με μειωμένη δυναμικότητα, γεγονός που περιορίζει προσωρινά την ποσότητα λυμάτων που μπορεί να παραλαμβάνει και, ως εκ τούτου, «το ΤΑΥ και ο Επαρχιακός Οργανισμός Αυτοδιοίκησης (ΕΟΑ) Λεμεσού έχουν προχωρήσει σε συντονισμένες ενέργειες, ώστε να καλυφθούν οι ανάγκες της περιοχής μέχρι την ολοκλήρωση της αναβάθμισης».
Στο πλαίσιο αυτό, σημειώνει η ανακοίνωση, ο Σταθμός Επεξεργασίας Λυμάτων στη Μονή παραλαμβάνει επιπλέον ποσότητες λυμάτων, συγκεκριμένες μέρες της εβδομάδας, ώστε να απορροφηθεί σημαντικό μέρος του φορτίου, ενώ ο σταθμός της Βαθιάς Γωνιάς παραμένει διαθέσιμος για τους μεταφορείς και παράλληλα εξετάζονται και άλλες εναλλακτικές λύσεις για την περαιτέρω ενίσχυση της δυναμικότητας. The sewer cleaners of the Limassol district are on strike. The professionals in the sector are protesting the chronic problems in the management and disposal of sewage.
They are currently holding a protest outside the Presidential Palace.
The problems that arose due to the reduced capacity of the Vati station are temporary, measures are being taken for the proper and uninterrupted management of sewage and additional solutions are being examined to facilitate the professional sewer cleaners of Limassol, the Department of Water Development and the Department of the Environment report.
In an announcement, on the occasion of the strike of the sewer cleaners of Limassol, the WDD and the Department of Environment inform that, due to the upgrade of the Wastewater Treatment Plant in Vati, specific arrangements have already been put into place to ensure the continuous service of professionals in the field.
During the works, it is added, the plant operates at reduced capacity, which temporarily limits the amount of wastewater it can receive and, therefore, "the WDD and the Limassol District Government Organization (DGO) have taken coordinated actions to cover the needs of the area until the upgrade is completed".
In this context, the announcement notes, the Wastewater Treatment Plant in Moni receives additional quantities of wastewater on specific days of the week, in order to absorb a significant part of the load, while the Vathia Gonia station remains available for transporters and other alternative solutions are being examined to further enhance capacity. Furthermore, it is underlined that clear instructions have been given to professionals for coordinated and planned discharges into the EOA network, in order to ensure the rational management of quantities and the smooth operation of the stations.
“The problems that arose due to the reduced capacity of the Vati station are temporary, but are being closely monitored by the WDD and the Department of Environment, which are taking all necessary measures for the environmentally sound and uninterrupted management of wastewater,” the announcement continues and indicates that the upgrade of the station is expected to be completed in December, when its operation will be fully restored.
In the meantime, in addition to the above actions, additional solutions are being studied to facilitate professionals and all relevant departments remain in constant consultation with professional sewer cleaners and the Limassol Municipal Authority, with the aim of finding the most applicable solutions for the overall response to the situation, the announcement concludes.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Klimacamp, Demo, Aktionen
Großprotest: Klimabewegung macht mobil gegen Gaskraftwerke
Hamm (dpa/lnw)
Tausende Aktivisten und Demonstranten wollen in Hamm ein Zeichen gegen den geplanten Gaskraftwerksausbau setzen - und deutlich machen, dass mit der Klimabewegung noch zu rechnen ist.
Ein großes Camp von Klimaaktivisten, eine geplante Großdemo und angekündigte Aktionen zivilen Ungehorsams: Aus Protest gegen den Bau neuer Gaskraftwerke kommen viele Gruppen der Klimabewegung in der kommenden Woche in Hamm im Ruhrgebiet zusammen.
Allein für das Klimacamp rechnet die Polizei mit einer vierstelligen Teilnehmerzahl ab Mittwoch. Der Aufbau einer großen Zeltstadt beginnt an diesem Sonntag. Am 27. Mai beginnt dann das Programm des Klimacamps aus Vorträgen und Workshops.
Riesige Zeltstadt auf ehemaligem Zechengelände geplant
Vor allem am Samstag dürften die Gaskraftwerksgegner dann noch einmal mehr werden: Ein breites Bündnis verschiedener Umwelt- und Klimaorganisationen mobilisiert für eine große Kundgebung an der Lippe. Laut Polizei gehen die Verantwortlichen auch hier von mehreren tausend Demonstranten aus.
Für die Polizei beginnt der groß anlegte Einsatz bereits früher: Im Lippepark, einem ehemaligen Zechengelände, ziehen im Wochenverlauf mehr und mehr Klimaaktivisten ein. Die Polizei geht von mindestens 1.000 Teilnehmern ab Mittwoch aus, es könnten aber auch mehr werden, hieß es. Anreisen sollen sie aus dem ganz Deutschland und dem benachbarten Ausland.
Die Ruhrgebietsstadt Hamm als einstiger Standort eines Atomreaktors und lange Zeit wichtigem Kohlekraftwerksstandort ist nicht zufällig gewählt: «Kaum eine Stadt erzählt die Geschichte deutscher Energiepolitik so deutlich wie Hamm», teilen die Klimaaktivisten mit. Das Camp richte sich nun gegen den von Bundeswirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche geplanten Ausbau neuer Gaskraftwerke, erklären die Aktivisten - ein Ziel, hinter dem sich weite Teile der Klimabewegung zu vereinen scheinen.
Gemeinsam gegen die Gaspolitik der Bundesregierung
Mitte Mai hatte das Kabinett der Bundesregierung einen Gesetzentwurf zum Bau neuer Gaskraftwerke auf den Weg gebracht. Neue Gaskraftwerke sollen im Zuge des bis 2038 geplanten schrittweisen Kohleausstiegs die Versorgungssicherheit mit Strom gewährleisten und künftig als Backups einspringen - in «Dunkelflauten» mit einer geringen Erzeugung aus Solar- und Windenergie.
Für die Klimaaktivisten und Umweltorganisationen ist dies ein Ausdruck einer «rückwärtsgewandten Energiepolitik», Reiche bremse damit die Energiewende aus, heißt es in den Protestaufrufen. Zahlreiche lokale Klimabündnisse und Initiativen unterstützen das Camp, das Wert darauflegt, von keiner politischen Organisation, sondern von ehrenamtlichen Klimaaktivistinnen und -aktivisten getragen zu sein.
Seit Wochen Vorbereitungen für Aktionen zivilen Ungehorsams
Auch das Aktionsbündnis Ende Gelände mobilisiert seit Wochen für Aktionen zivilen Ungehorsams im gesamten Ruhrgebiet - und zwar «angelehnt an die Aktionen, die wir auch im Kohletagebau gemacht haben», wie Sprecherin Tomke Jansen sagt. Geplant seien diese von 28. bis 30. Mai. Es werden mehrere hundert Aktivisten erwartet. «Wir als Ende Gelände gehen an die Orte der Zerstörung und erzeugen dadurch Gegenmacht», erklärt sie. Bekannt wurde das Bündnis durch seine Blockaden im Rheinischen Braunkohlerevier und bei der Räumung des Dorfes Lützerath 2023.
Die Polizei bereitet sich auf verschiedene Einsatzszenarien vor und appellierte in einer Mitteilung: «Personen, die Straftaten begehen, Störungen verursachen oder kritische Infrastruktur gefährden wollen, müssen mit einer klaren polizeilichen Antwort rechnen». Friedlichen Protest unterstütze man dagegen.
Windrad-Weltrekord zum Abschluss einer Großdemo geplant
Seinen Abschluss finden soll der Anti-Gas-Protest in der Demo mit dem Motto «Zukunft statt Gas-Energiewende verteidigen», zu der Fridays for Future, Greenpeace, der BUND sowie Campact aufgerufen haben. Über die genaue Route des Aufzugs, der um 12 Uhr starten soll, sei man noch in Abstimmung, hieß es vom Demobündnis. Plan sei es, in der Nähe des Gersteinwerks, einem Gas- und Dampfturbinenkraftwerk von RWE auf dem angrenzenden Stadtgebiet von Werne, zu starten und auf der Halde Nord Ost in Hamm. Dort wollen die Demonstranten ein riesiges Windrad bilden und so einen Weltrekord aufstellen.
«Wir wollen gemeinsam zeigen, dass die Klimabewegung zurück ist», erklärte eine Sprecherin des Demobündnisses und kritisierte: «Während saubere und sichere Technologien längst bereitstehen, bereitet die Bundesregierung einen fossilen Roll-Back vor und heizt die Klimakrise weiter an.»

Climate Camp, Demonstration, Actions
Major Protest: Climate Movement Mobilizes Against Gas-Fired Power Plants
Hamm (dpa/lnw)
Thousands of activists and demonstrators plan to make a stand against the planned expansion of gas-fired power plants in Hamm – and to demonstrate that the climate movement is still a force to be reckoned with.

A large camp of climate activists, a planned major demonstration, and announced acts of civil disobedience: Many groups within the climate movement will gather in Hamm in the Ruhr region next week to protest the construction of new gas-fired power plants.

Police expect a four-figure number of participants at the climate camp alone, starting Wednesday. Construction of a large tent city begins this Sunday. The climate camp program, consisting of lectures and workshops, will then begin on May 27.

Huge Tent City Planned on Former Mine Site
The number of opponents of the gas-fired power plants is expected to increase even further, especially on Saturday: A broad alliance of various environmental and climate organizations is mobilizing for a large rally on the banks of the Lippe River. According to police, organizers anticipate several thousand demonstrators there as well.

For the police, the large-scale operation begins even earlier: More and more climate activists will be moving into Lippepark, a former coal mine site, throughout the week. Police expect at least 1,000 participants from Wednesday onwards, but the number could be higher, they said. They are expected to arrive from all over Germany and neighboring countries.

The Ruhr region city of Hamm, a former site of a nuclear reactor and for a long time an important coal-fired power plant location, was not chosen by chance: "Hardly any other city tells the story of German energy policy as clearly as Hamm," the climate activists stated. The camp is now directed against the expansion of new gas-fired power plants planned by Federal Minister of Economics Katherina Reiche, the activists explained – a goal that seems to unite large parts of the climate movement.

Together against the Federal Government's Gas Policy
In mid-May, the Federal Cabinet introduced a draft law for the construction of new gas-fired power plants. New gas-fired power plants are intended to guarantee security of electricity supply as part of the planned phase-out of coal by 2038 and will serve as backups during periods of low solar and wind power generation.

Climate activists and environmental organizations see this as an expression of a "backward-looking energy policy," claiming that Reiche is hindering the energy transition, according to their calls to protest. Numerous local climate alliances and initiatives support the camp, which emphasizes that it is run not by any political organization, but by volunteer climate activists.

Weeks of preparation for civil disobedience actions

The Ende Gelände action alliance has also been mobilizing for weeks for civil disobedience actions throughout the Ruhr region – "based on the actions we carried out in the open-cast coal mines," as spokesperson Tomke Jansen explains. These actions are planned for May 28-30, with several hundred activists expected to participate. “We at Ende Gelände go to the sites of destruction and thereby generate counter-power,” she explains. The alliance became known for its blockades in the Rhenish lignite mining region and during the eviction of the village of Lützerath in 2023.

The police are preparing for various operational scenarios and appealed in a statement: “Individuals who commit crimes, cause disturbances, or endanger critical infrastructure must expect a clear police response.” Peaceful protest, on the other hand, will be supported.

Wind turbine world record planned to conclude major demonstration

The anti-gas protest is to culminate in the demonstration with the motto “Future instead of gas – Defend the energy transition,” which was called for by Fridays for Future, Greenpeace, BUND (Friends of the Earth Germany), and Campact. The demonstration alliance stated that they are still coordinating the exact route of the march, which is scheduled to start at noon. The plan is to start near the Gersteinwerk, a gas and steam turbine power plant operated by RWE in the adjacent town of Werne, and then on the Halde Nord Ost spoil heap in Hamm. There, the demonstrators intend to form a giant wind turbine and thus set a world record.

"Together, we want to show that the climate movement is back," explained a spokesperson for the demonstration alliance, adding: "While clean and safe technologies have long been available, the German government is preparing a fossil fuel rollback and further fueling the climate crisis."

Η διοίκηση της Τροχαίας Ορεστιάδας επιβεβαίωσε στο ΡΑΔΙΟ ΕΒΡΟΣ ότι ο αποκλεισμός πραγματοποιήθηκε χθες, Δευτέρα 6 Ιουλίου, και η συνολική διάρκειά του ήταν περίπου μία ώρα.
Οι Βούλγαροι διαμαρτυρόμενοι υποστηρίζουν ακόμη ότι μετά την πλήρη ένταξη της Βουλγαρίας στη ζώνη Σένγκεν ανέμεναν την κατάργηση των συγκεκριμένων περιορισμών. Farmers and residents of the Ivaylovgrad region in Bulgaria mobilized yesterday, Monday, July 6, 2026, blocking the Ivaylovgrad-Kyprin border crossing, protesting the ban on the passage of vehicles over 3.5 tons.
According to the Bulgarian News Agency (BTA), the demonstrators carried out three consecutive traffic blockades, each lasting up to 30 minutes, with the main demand of their protest being to allow heavy vehicles to pass through the specific border crossing. As the organizer of the mobilization, Hristo Parasarev, told the agency, the restriction creates serious problems for Bulgarian farmers during the harvest season, as it makes it difficult to transport their products to Greece, while it also negatively affects tourism, since it also affects tourist buses, as the vehicles are forced to follow detours through the interior of Bulgaria, increasing the route by approximately 60 kilometers, according to a report by nova.bg.
The administration of the Orestiada Traffic Police confirmed to RADIO EVROS that the blockade took place yesterday, Monday, July 6, and its total duration was approximately one hour.
The Bulgarian protesters also claim that after Bulgaria's full integration into the Schengen zone, they expected the lifting of these restrictions. They say they have collected more than 500 signatures and have submitted repeated requests to the relevant authorities, without any result to date. According to Bulgarian publications, the relevant services are citing a bilateral agreement between Greece and Bulgaria from 2007, which provides for the restriction of the passage of heavy trucks through the specific crossing for reasons of infrastructure protection.
After the conclusion of yesterday's mobilization, the alleged organizer of the protest, Hristo Parasarev, stated in a Facebook post that the participants unanimously decided to hold a new mobilization on Sunday, July 12, with the aim of blocking the road for many hours and stopping the passage of all vehicles. In the same post, he claimed that yesterday's protest was also supported by Greek farmers, who - as he states - pledged to participate in the new mobilization, as the restrictions affect them as well.
The organizers are calling for mass participation in the new protest, warning that if there is no solution to the issue, the mobilizations will escalate.

Vecinos y organizaciones de Necochea convocaron a una movilización para repudiar la agresión que sufrieron varias mascotas en la vía pública pública. Se trata de una marcha en pedido de justicia por el maltrato animal a los perros, la cual se convirtió en el principal reclamo de la comunidad tras conocerse las imágenes del ataque. Los organizadores detallaron que el encuentro se realizará este viernes a las 12 del mediodía en la intersección de las calles 87 y 8, señalando que el punto de encuentro es frente a la vivienda de la persona acusada.

A partir de ese registro visual, los operadores del área de seguridad dieron el aviso correspondiente a las autoridades competentes, quienes iniciaron de forma urgente las tareas destinadas a buscar e identificar a la persona que aparecía en las filmaciones. MESSAGE_TEXT:
Transportes
Última oportunidad para evitar la huelga del transporte público de la Región de Murcia en julio
Sindicatos y patronal volverán a reunirse este viernes en la OMAL en otro intento por desbloquear la negociación del convenio colectivo y evitar los paros de los próximos días
El conflicto del transporte público de viajeros de la Región de Murcia, que irá a la huelga el próximo 1 y 2 de julio tal y como adelantó La Opinión, vuelve a afrontar esta semana un momento decisivo con la última oportunidad de negociación antes de que lleguen los días del anunciado paro. Tras meses de negociaciones sin avances y después de que los trabajadores anunciaran dejar parados tanto los autobuses urbanos, interurbanos y el tranvía de Murcia para ambos días, los representantes de los sindicatos y de la patronal volverán a verse las caras este próximo viernes en un último intento por alcanzar un acuerdo que evite el plante. Un last chance en toda regla, que dirían los británicos...
La reunión de mediación, convocada de nuevo en la Oficina de Mediación y Arbitraje Laboral (OMAL), llega después de que el enésimo encuentro entre las federaciones de Transportes de UGT, Comisiones Obreras y USO y la patronal regional Froet, junto a las empresas Monbus, Interbus, Grupo Ruiz y Tranvía de Murcia, concluyera nuevamente sin acuerdo para renovar el convenio el pasado viernes 12 de junio.
Ese bloqueo llevó a los representantes de los trabajadores a dar por "agotada la vía del diálogo" y a convocar una asamblea en la que se ratificó la huelga prevista para los días 1 y 2 de julio, una movilización que afectaría a los servicios urbanos e interurbanos de toda la Región -con excepción de las líneas de largo recorrido superiores a 20 kilómetros- y que podría dejar sin servicio a miles de usuarios de toda la Comunidad.
Los sindicatos mantienen como prioridad un calendario anual de descansos que garantice la conciliación familiar
Los sindicatos sostienen que el conflicto no responde a una cuestión salarial, sino a la necesidad de garantizar unas condiciones laborales que permitan la conciliación de la vida laboral y familiar. La principal "línea roja" de la negociación pasa por la elaboración de un calendario anual de descansos que permita a las plantillas conocer con antelación cuándo librarán y "poder organizar su vida personal".
Actualmente, denuncian, los conductores permanecen disponibles prácticamente durante todo el año para cubrir refuerzos e incidencias, con turnos variables y sin descansos planificados. Según explican, el incremento de servicios en periodos de mayor demanda, como la temporada estival o el inicio del curso universitario, se cubre con la misma plantilla, suprimiendo descansos en lugar de incorporar nuevos trabajadores. Además de esa reivindicación, los representantes sindicales reclaman una subida salarial del 2,9% para 2026 y una actualización de las tablas retributivas para 2027 y 2028 conforme a la evolución del IPC nacional.
"Voluntad" para lograr el desbloqueo
Pese a la convocatoria de huelga, las federaciones de Transportes de UGT, CCOO y USO aseguran que acudirán a la reunión del día 26 de junio con "voluntad de alcanzar un entendimiento". Los comités de empresa reconocen que desconocen "cuáles serán las propuestas que presentará la patronal ni la actitud con la que afrontará la mediación", aunque recuerdan que durante toda la negociación han demostrado disposición al acuerdo presentando alternativas y ofreciendo flexibilidad para su aplicación.
No obstante, advierten de que la conciliación laboral y familiar mediante un calendario anual de descansos continúa siendo una reivindicación "urgente e innegociable". "Nuestro objetivo prioritario es llegar a buen término el viernes para evitar la huelga de los días 1 y 2 de julio", explicaron fuentes de las organizaciones sindicales a este periódico, que sitúan ahora en la parte empresarial la responsabilidad de hacer posible un acuerdo.
Si la reunión en el OMAL vuelve a terminar sin consenso, la huelga seguirá adelante y podría ir acompañada de una manifestación prevista en Murcia el 2 de julio, coincidiendo con el inicio del periodo de rebajas comerciales, una fecha de gran afluencia de público en el centro de la ciudad.

Transport
Last chance to avoid the public transport strike in the Region of Murcia in July
Unions and employers will meet again this Friday at the OMAL (Murcia Regional Labor Observatory) in another attempt to unblock collective bargaining negotiations and avoid the upcoming strikes.
The public transport conflict in the Region of Murcia, which will go on strike on July 1st and 2nd, as reported by La Opinión, faces another crucial moment this week with the last opportunity for negotiation before the announced strike. After months of negotiations without progress, and after workers announced they would halt all urban and intercity buses and the Murcia tram on both days, representatives of the unions and employers will meet again this Friday in a final attempt to reach an agreement and avert the strike. A real last chance, as the British would say... The mediation meeting, convened once again at the Labor Mediation and Arbitration Office (OMAL), comes after yet another meeting between the transport federations of UGT, Comisiones Obreras, and USO and the regional employers' association Froet, along with the companies Monbus, Interbus, Grupo Ruiz, and Tranvía de Murcia, concluded again without an agreement to renew the collective bargaining agreement last Friday, June 12.

This deadlock led the workers' representatives to declare "the path of dialogue exhausted" and to call an assembly in which the strike planned for July 1 and 2 was ratified. This mobilization would affect urban and interurban services throughout the Region—with the exception of long-distance lines exceeding 20 kilometers—and could leave thousands of users across the Community without service.

Unions prioritize an annual rest schedule that guarantees work-life balance.
The unions maintain that the conflict is not about wages, but rather about the need to guarantee working conditions that allow for a balance between work and family life. The main "red line" in the negotiations is the creation of an annual rest schedule that allows staff to know in advance when they will have time off and "be able to organize their personal lives."

Currently, they denounce, drivers are on call practically year-round to cover extra shifts and incidents, with variable shifts and no planned rest periods. They explain that the increase in services during peak demand periods, such as the summer season or the start of the university term, is covered by the same staff, eliminating rest days instead of hiring new workers. In addition to this demand, union representatives are calling for a 2.9% salary increase by 2026 and an update of the pay scales for 2027 and 2028 in line with the national Consumer Price Index (CPI).

"Will" to Break the Deadlock
Despite the strike call, the Transport Federations of UGT, CCOO, and USO affirm that they will attend the meeting on June 26 with "a willingness to reach an agreement." The works councils acknowledge that they do not know "what proposals the employers will present or what attitude they will adopt toward the mediation," although they reiterate that throughout the negotiations they have demonstrated a willingness to reach an agreement by presenting alternatives and offering flexibility for their implementation.

However, they warn that work-life balance through an annual rest schedule remains an "urgent and non-negotiable" demand. "Our priority is to reach a successful conclusion on Friday to avoid the strike on July 1 and 2," explained sources from the unions to this newspaper, who now place the responsibility for making an agreement possible on the employers' side.

If the meeting at the OMAL (Labor Mediation and Arbitration Board) ends again without consensus, the strike will go ahead and could be accompanied by a planned demonstration in Murcia on July 2nd, coinciding with the start of the retail sales period, a time of high foot traffic in the city center.
