Striking Teachers Disrupt Mexico City Ahead of World Cup Opening
Striking teachers from the CNTE union blocked major roads and set football mannequins on fire in downtown Mexico City on Tuesday, disrupting the capital just days before it hosts its first 2026 World Cup match.
As reported by The Guardian, the protesters are demanding salary increases and the reversal of pension laws, threatening continued disruptions during the tournament if their demands remain unaddressed.
The demonstrations forced President Claudia Sheinbaum to hold a scheduled meeting with a top Spanish official via Zoom rather than in person, as protesters blocked access to the Zócalo and National Palace.
The unrest followed clashes on Monday where riot police allegedly used tear gas and rubber bullets against marching teachers, resulting in five injuries, including a teacher who lost an eye.
City authorities denied using rubber bullets or tear gas during the confrontation, which occurred near the historic Zócalo plaza where the World Cup Fan Fest is scheduled to take place.
Protesters later gathered outside the interior ministry to condemn the police actions and criticize officials for blocking access to the main plaza.
"This shows that the spaces of the people can be privatised at the whim and for the benefit of the large corporations behind this World Cup, minimising the fight for workers’ rights," said Filiberto Frausto, one of the union leaders.
The current violence follows similar altercations between protesting educators and police officers in the city of Oaxaca last month.
Government officials maintained that they are working toward a resolution with the union members.
"Through dialogue, we will try to address the problems that are feasible to address," said Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's president.
The president noted that while budgetary constraints prevent the government from fulfilling every demand, officials are actively addressing feasible requests.
Union members expressed skepticism regarding the government's efforts and vowed to continue their mobilization.
"All the government has done is hold meetings for dialogue, but there’s no progress," told Sergio Cruz, one of the protesting teachers.
He emphasized that the educators are demanding justice through their ongoing demonstrations.
"The protests will go on," said Cruz.
He added that the international sporting event serves as a platform for the global community to see the nature of their government.
The ongoing blockades and encampments have raised significant concerns among local business owners who anticipated an economic windfall from incoming tournament tourists.
"All the businesses around the main square were saying it was going to be great, that lots of people, lots of tourists, would come," said Gerardo López Becerra, head of the Concomercio business group.
Becerra estimated that the presence of protest tents across the historic center could negatively impact as many as 10,000 local businesses.

Continuation of the “No Execution Tuesdays” campaign in the 125th week in 56 different prisons
In the critical conditions of Iranian society, while the Velayat-e-Faqih government and its repressive and judicial apparatus have hanged more than 177 prisoners since the beginning of 1405, we continue to witness the issuance and execution of inhuman death sentences. A desperate attempt to contain the explosion of anger of the people who are fed up with oppression and high prices.
According to news published last week, in addition to hundreds of prisoners for general crimes who are sentenced to death in ignorance and a large number of their sentences are being carried out, at least the death sentences of political prisoners Ali Fattah and Mohammad Naghizadeh have been confirmed by the Supreme Court and transferred to solitary confinement in Qezl-e-Hsar Prison. Two other political prisoners, Ali Kamali and Peyman Ganji, have also been transferred from Greater Tehran Prison to Qezl-e-Hsar Prison. Peyman Ganji is a 23-year-old young man who was arrested during the uprising in January 1404 and sentenced to death by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court.
As we have mentioned many times before, Qezl-Hesar Prison is the main execution center in Tehran province and one of the government killing grounds, housing many death row inmates, and prisoners sentenced to death are at risk of execution after being transferred to this prison.
In response to the wave of executions of political prisoners and the threat to the lives of five prisoners (Alireza Mordasi, Masoud Jamei, Reza Abdoli, Farshad Etemadifar, and Hassan Moslavy), Amnesty International has called for a halt to the executions of these five and other prisoners in Iran.
We, the members of the “No to Execution Tuesdays” campaign, call for a swift halt to the executions, and we call on all conscious individuals and political, human rights, civil, trade union, and other activists to condemn the executions in every possible way and take serious action to stop them.
The realization of freedom, equality, and the preservation of human dignity is not possible without the realization of the right to life of human beings. We call on all opponents of the death penalty to unite and act in solidarity to break the authoritarian structure and the cycle of taking human life.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
La Plataforma por la conversión de la N-430 en la A-43 ha celebrado este martes una reunión de trabajo con representantes municipales de la comarca para coordinar la manifestación convocada el próximo 10 de junio, a las 19.30 horas en Piedrabuena, en defensa de una carretera digna y segura y para reclamar medidas efectivas contra el despoblamiento que afecta a esta zona de la provincia.
El encuentro, que ha tenido lugar en el Ayuntamiento de Piedrabuena, ha contado con la participación del alcalde del municipio, José Luis Cabezas, y de la teniente de alcalde de la localidad y presidenta de la Plataforma por la conversión de la N-430 en la A-43, Isabel Herrera. También han asistido el alcalde de Alcolea de Calatrava, Eduardo Plaza; la alcaldesa de Puebla de Don Rodrigo, Eva Gutiérrez; la alcaldesa de Agudo, María Isabel Mansilla; y la alcaldesa de Luciana, Josefa Navas, quienes han mostrado una vez más la unidad institucional existente en torno a esta reivindicación histórica.
Durante la reunión se abordaron los detalles organizativos de la manifestación, que partirá desde Los Jardincillos de Piedrabuena y recorrerá la travesía con el objetivo de trasladar a las administraciones competentes el malestar de vecinos, empresas, autónomos y ayuntamientos ante la situación que presenta actualmente la N-430.
La presidenta de la Plataforma, Isabel Herrera, valoró positivamente los trabajos de mejora que se están desarrollando en algunos tramos de la vía, aunque insistió en que las actuaciones actuales no resuelven el problema de fondo. “A pesar de los arreglos que se están acometiendo en la N-430 seguimos pidiendo una solución definitiva, porque los parches son parches y al final no tenemos una carretera digna”, afirmó.
Herrera recordó que la N-430 continúa siendo una de las principales vías de comunicación para miles de vecinos de la comarca, así como para el transporte de mercancías y la actividad económica de numerosos municipios. Por ello, reiteró la necesidad de acometer inversiones estructurales que garanticen la seguridad vial y mejoren la conectividad del territorio. “Solicitamos la adecuación completa del firme y la construcción de las variantes de Piedrabuena y Luciana cuanto antes. Son actuaciones necesarias para mejorar la seguridad, reducir riesgos y ofrecer a nuestros vecinos las infraestructuras que merecen”, señaló la presidenta de la Plataforma.
Los responsables municipales coincidieron en destacar que la situación de la N-430 trasciende el ámbito de la movilidad y afecta directamente al desarrollo económico, social y demográfico de la comarca. En este sentido, defendieron que disponer de infraestructuras modernas y seguras es un elemento fundamental para fijar población, atraer inversiones y garantizar la igualdad de oportunidades entre el medio rural y las grandes áreas urbanas.
La Plataforma ha mantenido durante más de veinte años una reivindicación constante para mejorar la seguridad de esta infraestructura, alertando de manera reiterada sobre los riesgos derivados de sus deficiencias. Durante este tiempo, numerosos accidentes han puesto de manifiesto la necesidad de actuar con urgencia, con un balance de víctimas mortales y heridos que ha marcado profundamente a las familias afectadas y al conjunto de la sociedad. La mejora de la seguridad vial ha sido, desde el inicio, uno de los principales argumentos de una demanda que trasciende las infraestructuras y se centra en la protección de las personas y en la prevención de nuevas tragedias.
Durante el encuentro también se puso de manifiesto la importancia de mantener la unidad institucional y social en torno a esta reivindicación, que viene siendo defendida desde hace años por ayuntamientos, colectivos ciudadanos, empresas y asociaciones del territorio. “Esta es una reivindicación justa, necesaria y compartida por toda la comarca. No estamos pidiendo privilegios, sino infraestructuras seguras y acordes a las necesidades reales de nuestros municipios”, destacó Isabel Herrera.
Llamamiento
La presidenta de la Plataforma hizo además un llamamiento a la participación ciudadana en la manifestación del próximo 10 de junio, subrayando que la implicación de los vecinos será clave para trasladar un mensaje claro y contundente a las administraciones responsables. “Animamos a todos los vecinos de Piedrabuena y de los municipios de nuestro entorno a sumarse a esta movilización. Cuantas más personas participen, más fuerza tendrá nuestra voz para reclamar una solución inmediata a una demanda que llevamos años exigiendo”, afirmó.
Herrera añadió que la seguridad de quienes utilizan diariamente esta carretera debe ser una prioridad y defendió que la comarca no puede seguir esperando indefinidamente soluciones definitivas. “Tenemos la obligación de seguir reivindicando mejoras para nuestro territorio. Queremos una carretera segura, moderna y preparada para el futuro. La ciudadanía ha demostrado su compromiso y ahora es el momento de que las administraciones respondan con hechos”, concluyó.
Desde el Ayuntamiento de Piedrabuena y el resto de municipios participantes se ha reiterado la invitación a vecinos, colectivos, asociaciones y tejido empresarial para que respalden esta movilización, convocada bajo el lema de conseguir una carretera digna y segura ya, una reivindicación que consideran fundamental para garantizar el futuro y el desarrollo de toda la comarca.

During the meeting, the organizational details of the demonstration were discussed. The march will begin in Los Jardincillos de Piedrabuena and proceed along the main road, aiming to convey to the relevant authorities the discontent of residents, businesses, the self-employed, and local councils regarding the current state of the N-430 highway.

The president of the Platform, Isabel Herrera, welcomed the improvement work being carried out on some sections of the road, although she insisted that the current actions do not resolve the underlying problem. “Despite the repairs being made to the N-430, we continue to demand a permanent solution, because temporary fixes are just temporary fixes, and in the end, we don't have a decent road,” she stated.

Herrera noted that the N-430 remains one of the main communication routes for thousands of residents in the region, as well as for the transport of goods and the economic activity of numerous municipalities. Therefore, she reiterated the need for structural investments that guarantee road safety and improve connectivity in the area. “We are requesting the complete resurfacing of the road and the construction of the Piedrabuena and Luciana bypasses as soon as possible. These actions are necessary to improve safety, reduce risks, and provide our residents with the infrastructure they deserve,” stated the president of the Platform.

Municipal officials agreed that the condition of the N-430 extends beyond mobility and directly affects the economic, social, and demographic development of the region. In this regard, they argued that having modern and safe infrastructure is fundamental to retaining population, attracting investment, and guaranteeing equal opportunities between rural areas and large urban centers.

For over twenty years, the Platform has consistently advocated for improved safety on this road, repeatedly warning of the risks stemming from its deficiencies. During this time, numerous accidents have highlighted the urgent need for action, with a toll of fatalities and injuries that has deeply affected the families involved and the community as a whole. Improving road safety has been, from the outset, one of the main arguments behind a demand that goes beyond infrastructure and focuses on protecting people and preventing future tragedies.

During the meeting, the importance of maintaining institutional and social unity around this demand was also highlighted. This demand has been championed for years by local councils, citizen groups, businesses, and associations in the region. “This is a fair and necessary demand, shared by the entire region. We are not asking for privileges, but for safe infrastructure that meets the real needs of our municipalities,” emphasized Isabel Herrera.

Call to Action
The Platform's president also called for citizen participation in the demonstration on June 10th, stressing that the involvement of residents will be key to conveying a clear and forceful message to the responsible authorities. “We encourage all residents of Piedrabuena and the surrounding municipalities to join this mobilization. The more people who participate, the stronger our voice will be in demanding an immediate solution to a demand we have been making for years,” he stated.

Herrera added that the safety of those who use this road daily must be a priority and argued that the region cannot continue waiting indefinitely for definitive solutions. “We have an obligation to continue demanding improvements for our territory. We want a safe, modern road, ready for the future. The citizens have demonstrated their commitment, and now it is time for the authorities to respond with action,” he concluded.
The Piedrabuena Town Hall and the other participating municipalities have reiterated their invitation to residents, community groups, associations, and businesses to support this mobilization, convened under the slogan “Achieve a decent and safe road now,” a demand they consider fundamental to guaranteeing the future and development of the entire region.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Families of victims of the 2018 Offa bank robbery and supporters of former Senate President, Bukola Saraki, have staged a rally in Ilorin, the Kwara State capital, rejecting renewed allegations seeking to link him to the deadly incident.
The protesters, including members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) youth wing and relatives of some victims, marched through major streets.
They later converged at the forecourt of the palace of the Emir of Ilorin, where they accused political actors of reviving an issue they said had been investigated and concluded.
Some bereaved relatives who joined the protest said they could not remain silent while, in their view, their pain was being dragged into political controversy.
A widow who lost her husband in the attack, Habeebat Sanni, said Saraki had no connection with the robbery and urged the government to focus on governance rather than reopening old wounds.
“We know Saraki and we know he knows nothing about this incident. The government should stop politicising our pains because it is something we also remember with tears. God will give us a government that will put food on our table. We are tired”, she said.
Another victim, Hussein Aditu, who said he lost his 27-year-old son in the robbery, described attempts to associate Saraki with the attack as painful and unjustified.
“The same Saraki they are trying to accuse was the person that came to Offa, identified with us and took steps that contributed to the arrest of the criminals,” he said.
“How would he now be the accused? Do they always want to renew our pain every four years? That is why I came to tell the world Saraki knows nothing about it”, he added.
He said victims had not been drawn into similar debates by previous administrations and questioned why the issue was resurfacing years after the incident.
Addressing protesters at the rally, Kwara PDP Youth Leader, Adio Odunjo, said the renewed narratives around the Offa robbery were politically motivated and should be withdrawn in the interest of peace.
According to him, the matter had passed through investigation and legal processes, leaving no basis for renewed accusations.
“The Offa robbery case was thoroughly investigated by the police. Legal advice made it clear there was no evidence linking Dr Bukola Saraki to the incident directly or indirectly,” he said.
“Suspects were charged, trials were conducted and judgments were delivered and upheld on appeal. So what exactly is this government trying to achieve now?”, he queried.
Odunjo said the protest was not about shielding anyone from scrutiny, but resisting an attempt to weaponise a painful tragedy for political ends.
“This is not about justice. This is about politics. You may oppose Saraki politically, that is democracy. But to attempt to smear his name with matters he has been legally cleared of is unacceptable”, he said.
He urged Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq to tread carefully, warning against actions capable of escalating tension in the state.
“Leadership demands responsibility, restraint and respect for institutions and heritage,” he said.
The April 2018 robbery in Offa left scores dead, including police personnel, and remains one of the most traumatic security incidents in the state.

Odunjo said the protest was not about shielding anyone from scrutiny, but resisting an attempt to weaponise a painful tragedy for political ends.
“This is not about justice. This is about politics. You may oppose Saraki politically, that is democracy. But to attempt to smear his name with matters he has been legally cleared of is unacceptable”, he said.
He urged Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq to tread carefully, warning against actions capable of escalating tension in the state.
“Leadership demands responsibility, restraint and respect for institutions and heritage,” he said.
The April 2018 robbery in Offa left scores dead, including police personnel, and remains one of the most traumatic security incidents in the state.

Sin acuerdos en la UAEMéx; rectora deja mesa de diálogo por protesta en Rectoría
Ambas partes mantuvieron diferencias sobre la aplicación de la gratuidad, los descuentos a colegiaturas, becas y el servicio de Potrobús
La mesa de diálogo entre autoridades y estudiantes de la Universidad Autónoma del Estado de México (UAEMéx) para discutir el proceso de gratuidad concluyó sin acuerdos y con la salida de la rectora Patricia Zarza, quien se trasladó al edificio de Rectoría tras una manifestación.
Durante el encuentro, que duró más de tres horas, las partes mantuvieron diferencias sobre la aplicación de la gratuidad, los descuentos a colegiaturas, becas y el servicio de Potrobús. Autoridades universitarias insistieron que han realizado acciones para avanzar hacia la gratuidad, pero que debe ser gradual por el tema presupuestal, mientras que los representantes estudiantiles pidieron transparencia y apertura a la participacion activa.
Demandan descuentos y trámites
Los estudiantes también demandaron que se respete el descuento del 12 por ciento en las cuotas escolares, que no se limite al periodo 2026-A y que trámites como constancias y trayectorias académicas sean gratuitos.
De manera paralela, alrededor de 20 estudiantes se manifestaron frente a Rectoría, donde denunciaron que la convocatoria para participar en las mesas de diálogo no fue difundida en todos los espacios universitarios, lo que, aseguraron, limitó la representación estudiantil.
Además, informaron que analizan una eventual toma del edificio, aunque precisaron que cualquier decisión será sometida a consulta entre la comunidad. Ante la protesta, trabajadores universitarios colocaron cadenas y candados en los accesos principales del edificio. En ese contexto, la rectora Patricia Zarza abandonó la mesa de trabajo para acudir a Rectoría, donde informó que un grupo de personas encapuchadas intentó ingresar de manera violenta a las instalaciones mientras se desarrollaba el diálogo.
"Quiero informarles que me encuentro ya en el edificio de Rectoría, donde hace unos minutos un grupo de personas encapuchadas intentaron ingresar de manera violenta e ilegítima a nuestras instalaciones”, expresó.
La rectora señaló que acudió para garantizar la seguridad de las y los trabajadores, rechazó cualquier acto de violencia.
“Resulta inadmisible que realicen estas acciones cuando paralelamente se realizaba un ejercicio de diálogo", compartió en sus redes sociales.
Finalmente reiteró que la universidad mantendrá abiertas las mesas de diálogo para continuar la búsqueda de acuerdos sobre el proceso de gratuidad.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
No agreements reached at UAEMéx; Rector leaves dialogue table due to protest at the Rector's Office
Both sides maintained differences regarding the implementation of free tuition, tuition discounts, scholarships, and the Potrobús bus service
The dialogue table between authorities and students of the Autonomous University of the State of Mexico (UAEMéx) to discuss the free tuition process concluded without agreements and with the departure of Rector Patricia Zarza, who went to the Rector's Office building after a protest.

During the meeting, which lasted more than three hours, the parties maintained differences regarding the implementation of free tuition, tuition discounts, scholarships, and the Potrobús bus service. University authorities insisted that they have taken steps to move toward free tuition, but that it must be gradual due to budgetary constraints, while student representatives asked for transparency and openness to active participation.

Students Demand Discounts and Streamlined Procedures
Students also demanded that the 12 percent discount on tuition fees be honored, that it not be limited to the 2026-A semester, and that procedures such as transcripts and academic records be free of charge.

Simultaneously, around 20 students demonstrated in front of the Rector's Office, where they denounced the fact that the call to participate in the dialogue sessions was not disseminated throughout the university, which, they asserted, limited student representation.

They also reported that they are considering a possible occupation of the building, although they specified that any decision will be subject to consultation with the university community. In response to the protest, university employees placed chains and padlocks on the main entrances of the building. In this context, Rector Patricia Zarza left the working group to go to the Rector's Office, where she reported that a group of hooded individuals attempted to violently enter the facilities while the dialogue was underway. “I want to inform you that I am now at the Rector's Office building, where a few minutes ago a group of hooded individuals attempted to violently and illegally enter our facilities,” she stated.

The rector indicated that she came to ensure the safety of the staff and rejected any act of violence.

“It is unacceptable that they carry out these actions while a dialogue was underway,” she shared on her social media.

Finally, she reiterated that the university will keep the dialogue tables open to continue seeking agreements on the tuition-free process.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
La Confederación Geneal del Trabajo (CGT), las dos CTA (de los Trabajadores y Autónoma) y la Unión de Trabajadores de la Economía Popular (UTEP), junto con las principales confederaciones sindicales, cerraron este martes en la sede de Azopardo un cronograma de movilizaciones que arranca el miércoles 22 de julio y se extiende hasta noviembre. El esquema, que los propios dirigentes comparan con el modelo que usó el sindicalismo francés para resistir a la reforma laboral de Macron, apuesta por paros escalonados y sectoriales que mantengan la presión durante meses, sin concentrar todo el conflicto en una sola medida. La reunión estuvo encabezada por los cosecretarios generales de la CGT Jorge Sola y Octavio Argüello, y contó con la participación de Juan Carlos Schmid, Rodolfo Daer, Hugo Godoy, Alejandro Gramajo, Roberto Baradel y Sergio Romero, entre otros dirigentes.
El primer hito del plan es la movilización al Congreso del próximo miércoles 22 de julio, convocada para potenciar el reclamo semanal de los jubilados. Le sigue la marcha del 7 de agosto, Día de San Cayetano, organizada junto a la UTEP y los movimientos sociales, que coincidirá con la reunión del Consejo del Salario Mínimo, Vital y Móvil (aunque seguramente sea virtual, las centrales convocaron a concentrarse frente a la Secretaría de Trabajo). La tercera semana de agosto está reservada para una movilización al Ministerio de Economía para denunciar el plan de endeudamiento del gobierno, con convocatoria extendida a pequeños y medianos empresarios y familias afectadas por las deudas. Para el 2 de septiembre, Día de la Industria, está prevista una jornada nacional de protesta para visibilizar la recesión, las suspensiones y los cierres de plantas, con movilizaciones hacia las sedes de la UIA y la AEA. También en agosto está confirmado un paro nacional docente impulsado por la UDA con adhesión de CTERA y el resto de las federaciones de educación.
Las centrales también acordaron participar de la Semana Social convocada por la Comisión Episcopal del 4 al 6 de septiembre en Córdoba, y darle continuidad al plan de lucha durante la visita del papa León XIV a la Argentina en noviembre. En ese marco, Hugo Godoy propuso una gran marcha federal con cese total de actividades en la previa de la llegada del Sumo Pontífice. El horizonte más ambicioso del plan es un paro general de 24 o 36 horas con concentración en Plaza de Mayo, proyectado para la primera quincena de diciembre. Fuentes gremiales remarcaron la necesidad de «crear músculo para una huelga nacional» y explicaron que el cronograma escalonado apunta exactamente a eso.
La estrategia de las centrales contempla también una presencia activa en cada conflicto sectorial, sin esperar que escalen para intervenir. Sola propuso garantizar la presencia permanente de entre 15 y 20 dirigentes de primera línea para acompañar físicamente cada disputa laboral, tanto en el AMBA como en las provincias. Se acordó además intensificar los contactos con las regionales de la CGT para realizar marchas provinciales que visibilicen conflictos puntuales. Las asambleas informativas en fábricas y la distribución masiva de folletos en estaciones y terminales también forman parte del esquema, diseñado para evitar el descuento del día no trabajado a quienes adhieran a las medidas. La Ley de Modernización Laboral y las millonarias multas aplicadas a la UTA y La Fraternidad funcionan como advertencia, por lo que los sindicatos decidieron priorizar la acción directa sectorial para eludir las restricciones al derecho de huelga que impone la nueva normativa.
El plan se lanza en un contexto de deterioro sostenido del empleo, los salarios y las condiciones de vida. Incluso la Organización Internacional del Trabajo (OIT) se pronunció contra las políticas de Milei, advirtiendo una marcada pérdida de derechos laborales. Las centrales estiman que el segundo semestre estará cargado de conflictos en la industria textil, la metalmecánica y otros sectores, y que el plan económico no generará ni reactivación ni mejora del empleo. El comunicado conjunto de las organizaciones reafirmó la voluntad de «profundizar los espacios de diálogo, coordinación y construcción colectiva» frente al «deterioro de las condiciones económicas, sociales, laborales y productivas que afectan a millones de argentinos». El movimiento obrero unificado apuesta a que la acumulación de fuerza en las calles durante los próximos meses construya las condiciones para la huelga general que varios sectores vienen reclamando desde hace tiempo.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
The General Confederation of Labor (CGT), the two CTAs (Workers' and Autonomous), and the Union of Workers of the Popular Economy (UTEP), along with the main labor confederations, finalized a schedule of mobilizations this Tuesday at their headquarters on Azopardo Street. The mobilizations will begin on Wednesday, July 22, and extend until November. The plan, which the leaders themselves compare to the model used by French unions to resist Macron's labor reforms, focuses on staggered, sector-specific strikes to maintain pressure for months, without concentrating the entire conflict in a single action. The meeting was chaired by CGT co-general secretaries Jorge Sola and Octavio Argüello, and included the participation of Juan Carlos Schmid, Rodolfo Daer, Hugo Godoy, Alejandro Gramajo, Roberto Baradel, and Sergio Romero, among other leaders.

The first milestone of the plan is the mobilization to Congress next Wednesday, July 22, called to amplify the weekly demands of retirees. This is followed by the march on August 7, Saint Cajetan's Day, organized in conjunction with the UTEP (Union of Workers of the Popular Economy) and social movements, which will coincide with the meeting of the Minimum Wage Council (although it will likely be virtual, the unions have called for a gathering in front of the Ministry of Labor). The third week of August is reserved for a mobilization to the Ministry of Economy to denounce the government's debt plan, with an invitation extended to small and medium-sized business owners and families affected by the debt. On September 2, Industry Day, a national day of protest is planned to highlight the recession, layoffs, and plant closures, with marches to the headquarters of the UIA (Argentine Industrial Union) and the AEA (Argentine Business Association). Also in August, a national teachers' strike called by the UDA (Argentine Teachers' Union) with the support of CTERA (Confederation of Education Workers of the Argentine Republic) and the other education federations is confirmed.

The labor unions also agreed to participate in the Social Week convened by the Episcopal Commission from September 4th to 6th in Córdoba, and to continue their plan of action during Pope Leo XIV's visit to Argentina in November. In this context, Hugo Godoy proposed a large-scale national march with a complete work stoppage prior to the Pope's arrival. The plan's most ambitious goal is a 24- or 36-hour general strike with a rally in Plaza de Mayo, projected for the first half of December. Union sources emphasized the need to "build strength for a national strike" and explained that the staggered schedule is precisely aimed at that.

The unions' strategy also includes an active presence in each sectoral conflict, without waiting for them to escalate before intervening. Sola proposed ensuring the permanent presence of 15 to 20 top-level leaders to physically accompany each labor dispute, both in the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Area (AMBA) and in the provinces. It was also agreed to intensify contacts with the CGT's regional branches to organize provincial marches that highlight specific conflicts. Informational meetings in factories and the mass distribution of leaflets at stations and terminals are also part of the plan, designed to prevent workers who participate in the measures from having their pay docked for the day they don't work. The Labor Modernization Law and the hefty fines levied against the UTA and La Fraternidad unions serve as a warning, so the unions decided to prioritize sectoral direct action to circumvent the restrictions on the right to strike imposed by the new legislation.

The plan is being launched against a backdrop of sustained deterioration in employment, wages, and living conditions. Even the International Labour Organization (ILO) has spoken out against Milei's policies, warning of a marked erosion of labor rights. The unions estimate that the second half of the year will be fraught with conflicts in the textile, metalworking, and other sectors, and that the economic plan will generate neither economic recovery nor job creation. The joint statement from the organizations reaffirmed their commitment to "deepen spaces for dialogue, coordination, and collective action" in the face of "the deteriorating economic, social, labor, and productive conditions affecting millions of Argentinians." The unified labor movement is betting that the accumulation of strength in the streets over the coming months will create the conditions for the general strike that various sectors have been demanding for some time.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Estalla huelga en CICE Veracruz por presuntas violaciones contractuales y laborales
-
Más de mil trabajadores resultan afectados tras el rompimiento de negociaciones entre sindicato y empresa
Irineo Pérez Melo
Veracruz, Ver., 1 de junio de 2026.- Trabajadores sindicalizados de la empresa Corporación Integral de Comercio Exterior (CICE) estallaron la huelga la madrugada de este lunes, luego de que fracasaran las negociaciones para la renovación del Contrato Colectivo de Trabajo y ante presuntas violaciones a sus derechos laborales e incumplimientos por parte de la empresa.
De acuerdo con Javier Gómez Figueroa, secretario general del sindicato, las banderas rojinegras fueron colocadas en las instalaciones de la operadora portuaria en punto de las 00:00 horas, tras agotarse las instancias de diálogo sin alcanzar acuerdos.
El dirigente sindical señaló que la empresa desatendió las demandas relacionadas con mejoras salariales, condiciones laborales y el pago del reparto de utilidades (PTU), situación que derivó en el estallamiento de la huelga.
Indicó que la suspensión de labores impacta directamente a unos mil 200 trabajadores, de los cuales aproximadamente 600 son sindicalizados y el resto pertenece al personal administrativo y de confianza.
Gómez Figueroa aseguró que el sindicato mantuvo disposición para resolver el conflicto mediante los mecanismos legales y ante los tribunales laborales; sin embargo, acusó que la empresa se negó a atender las principales exigencias de los trabajadores.
Entre los reclamos destaca el pago de utilidades. Según explicó, la empresa destinó únicamente 3 millones de pesos para este concepto, lo que representaría alrededor de 400 pesos por trabajador, cantidad que consideraron insuficiente y alejada de lo establecido por la legislación laboral.
Asimismo, el sindicato planteó un incremento salarial del 20 por ciento, mientras que la empresa habría ofrecido un aumento del 0.01 por ciento, propuesta que los trabajadores calificaron como inaceptable.
Además del aumento salarial y el reparto de utilidades, los sindicalizados exigen la atención de ocho presuntas violaciones al Contrato Colectivo de Trabajo y otros beneficios que impactan directamente en sus ingresos y condiciones laborales.
El líder sindical informó que la última audiencia de negociación se realizó el pasado jueves y que fue suspendida por los representantes de la empresa, por lo que posteriormente un juez federal reconoció el derecho de huelga de los trabajadores.
Finalmente, señaló que la suspensión de maniobras ya genera afectaciones en la actividad portuaria, incluida la salida de un buque con carga de Tubos y Aceros de México (Tamsa). También denunció que la empresa bloqueó 599 tarjetas de acceso al recinto portuario y que al menos 30 trabajadores quedaron al interior de las instalaciones al momento de iniciar el movimiento huelguístico.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Strike erupts at CICE Veracruz over alleged contract and labor violations
- More than a thousand workers affected after negotiations between union and company break down
Irineo Pérez Melo
Veracruz, Ver., June 1, 2026 - Unionized workers at the company Corporación Integral de Comercio Exterior (CICE) went on strike early Monday morning after negotiations to renew their Collective Bargaining Agreement failed, citing alleged violations of their labor rights and breaches of contract by the company.

According to Javier Gómez Figueroa, the union's general secretary, the red and black strike flags were raised at the port operator's facilities at midnight, after all avenues of dialogue were exhausted without reaching an agreement.

The union leader stated that the company ignored demands related to salary increases, improved working conditions, and profit-sharing payments, a situation that led to the strike.

He indicated that the work stoppage directly impacts approximately 1,200 workers, of whom about 600 are union members, while the rest are administrative and management staff.

Gómez Figueroa asserted that the union remained willing to resolve the conflict through legal channels and in labor courts; however, he accused the company of refusing to address the workers' main demands.

Among the demands, the most prominent is the payment of profit sharing. He explained that the company allocated only 3 million pesos for this purpose, which would represent approximately 400 pesos per worker, an amount they considered insufficient and far from what is stipulated by labor law. The union also proposed a 20 percent salary increase, while the company reportedly offered a mere 0.01 percent, a proposal the workers deemed unacceptable.

In addition to the salary increase and profit sharing, the union members are demanding attention to eight alleged violations of the Collective Bargaining Agreement and other benefits that directly impact their income and working conditions.

The union leader reported that the last negotiation hearing was held last Thursday and was suspended by company representatives. Subsequently, a federal judge recognized the workers' right to strike.

TORREVIEJA 10 MAY 2026 15:43 Updated 10 MAY 2026 15:45 Clavel Street in Torrevieja hosted a demonstration this Sunday to demand "justice" for "Nola," a cat brutally kicked to death in the street by a man seeking revenge against his ex-partner, the animal's owner. There was a moment of tension when the gathering turned into a demonstration, moving to the parallel street of Ramón Gallud and continuing to chant slogans on the other side of the same building. At this point, local police intervened to prevent traffic from being blocked by the large crowd, and the Civil Guard established a security cordon in front of the building's entrance to prevent the demonstrators from approaching.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Protest blocks Ring Road in Hatpada area of Sambalpur, Odisha, India
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Public dissatisfaction over prolonged drinking water crisis in Sambalpur spilled onto the streets on Tuesday as local residents staged a major road blockade in the Ring Road Hatpada area.
Amid the severe summer, the demonstration brought traffic movement to a complete standstill, leaving hundreds of vehicles stranded in long queues on both sides of the road. While administrative officials rushed to the location to negotiate with the agitators, the situation remained tense for several hours as residents demanded an immediate and permanent solution to the water scarcity.
Traffic Disruption And Local Demands
The ongoing shortage of drinking water emerged as a primary concern for the people. Protesters initially refused to withdraw their agitation, demanding the direct intervention of the district administration before clearing the highway.
Highlighting the structural challenges and the daily struggles faced by the community, a local resident said, "We will not remove the road blockade unless the Collector comes here and we meet him. We are suffering a lot due to the shortage of water. We are unable to perform daily activities due to a shortage of water."
Another protesting resident added, "In recent days, we went to the lower area of Hirakud Dam with the officials to figure out a way so that water from there can be directly sent to people's homes, but nothing was done regarding that."
Administrative Intervention
The deadlock was eventually broken when the Sambalpur Water Corporation of Odisha (WATCO) General Manager (GM) arrived at the spot to pacify the crowd. The GM provided a formal written assurance to the protesters promising that drinking water would be made systematically available to every household.
Commenting on the immediate steps taken to resolve the dispute, the WATCO General Manager said, "I have spoken to the people and have assured them that water would definitely be made available."
Following the written assurance, the GM reported that supply was initiated, leading to the official call-off of the road blockade. However, to verify the claim, residents escorted the official into the residential quarters to inspect the utility taps. The joint inspection revealed that the water supply had still not been restored to the household.
The GM attributed the localised failure to a choked pipe and assured the gathered community members that the technical glitch would be resolved soon.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Iranian opposition politician Reza Pahlavi reportedly attacked with tomato sauce during press conference in Berlin, Germany
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Exilpolitiker Reza Pahlavi will bei seinem Berlin-Besuch den Stimmen seiner Landsleute Gehör verschaffen. Anhänger und Gegner demonstrieren. Die Ereignisse im Live-Blog.
Von Lionel Kreglinger Marie Nadler Lisa Röther Stand: heute, 12:39 Uhr
Der iranische Exilpolitiker Reza Pahlavi, Sohn des 1979 gestürzten Schahs, ist seit dem späten Mittwochnachmittag in Berlin als Privatperson zu Besuch. Pahlavi will in der Hauptstadt Bundestagsabgeordnete treffen. Am Donnerstagvormittag gab er eine Pressekonferenz im Haus der Bundespressekonferenz am Spreeufer.
„Während die Iraner weiter für ihre Befreiung kämpfen, bin ich nach Berlin gekommen, um dafür zu sorgen, dass ihre Stimmen gehört werden“, schrieb er am Mittwoch auf X.
Rund um das Regierungsviertel gibt es mehrere Demonstrationen – von Unterstützern Pahlavis ebenso wie von Gegnern: Im Regierungsviertel am Reichstagsgebäude begannen bereits am Morgen Demonstrationen mit den Titeln „Freiheit für Iran“ und „Unterstützung Prinz Reza Pahlavi von EU und Deutschland“.
Die Entwicklungen in unserem Live-Blog: 12.30 Uhr: Pahlavi mit Tomatensoße beworfen – Festnahme Pahlavi ist im Anschluss an eine Pressekonferenz mit Tomatensoße beworfen worden. Danach wurde ein Mann festgenommen , wie die Polizei mitteilte. Der Zwischenfall ereignete sich, nachdem der Exilpolitiker in der Bundespressekonferenz zu Gast war. Weitere Details nannte die Polizei nicht. Die soßenartige Flüssigkeit war auf der Schulter und am Hals Pahlavis zu sehen.
11.54 Uhr: Polizei mit 800 Einsatzkräften im Regierungsviertel Die Polizei ist bei den Pro-Pahlavi-Demonstrationen im Regierungsviertel am heutigen Donnerstag mit 800 Kräften im Einsatz . Ein Pressesprecher sagte dem Tagesspiegel außerdem, dass es keine konkreten Hinweise gäbe, „dass es unfriedlich werden kann“. Vor Ort sind aktuell etwa 250 Demonstrierende.
Eine IT-Ingenieurin aus Den Haag sagt: „Unser Ziel ist, dass der Iran frei ist“. Farrokh Ajdadi schwenkt neben einer iranischen auch eine historische, persische Flagge in den Farben rot, lila und gelb. Sie stehe für Freiheit, Gerechtigkeit, Einigkeit und Liebe , sagt Ajdadi.
Farrokh Ajdadi, IT-Ingenieurin aus Den Haag. © Marie Nadler
11.29 Uhr: Eine Stimme für den ermordeten Bruder Erisa Heydari sagt auf Englisch, er demonstriere, um die Stimme seines Bruders zu sein, der vom iranischen Regime getötet worden sei. Er trägt ein Plakat mit einem Foto von ihm in der Hand und eine blaue Flagge, die für die „Pahlavi-Dynastie“ steht. „Ich bin hier, damit Pahlavi Demokratie in den Iran bringt.“ Heydari sagt, er habe neben seinem Bruder vier Freunde verloren.
Demo von Pahlavi-Unterstützern in Berlin-Mitte © Marie Nadler
10.57 Uhr: Kritik an Pahlavi von der Gesellschaft von Deutsch-Iranern Die Sprecherin der Gesellschaft von Deutsch-Iranern (GDI), Sahar Sanaie, warnt eindringlich davor, Reza Pahlavi politisch aufzuwerten. Dem Tagesspiegel sagte sie, die Legitimierung einer solchen Figur sei „ eine Ohrfeige für all jene, die im Iran für Freiheit kämpfen “. Das gelte insbesondere für die Demonstrierenden, die „Tod dem Unterdrücker, ob Schah oder Führer“ gerufen hätten, sowie für die 17 kürzlich hingerichteten politischen Gefangenen. Diese hätten sich in ihren letzten Botschaften sowohl gegen die Mullah-Diktatur als auch gegen eine Rückkehr zur Monarchie ausgesprochen.
Pahlavi selbst habe „für die Freiheit in Iran null Preis bezahlt“ und sei seit 47 Jahren von der Realität im Land abwesend . Die Menschen im Iran wollten keine „Wellenreiter“, sondern echte Kämpfer für Freiheit. Stattdessen, so die Sprecherin, „schwächt Reza Pahlavi die Opposition nur und sorgt für Spaltung .“
Die GDI ist ein politisch aktiver Verein, der sich für einen Regimewechsel im Iran einsetzt und regelmäßig Demonstrationen in deutschen Städten organisiert, oft mit Fokus auf Berlin oder Hamburg.
10.36 Uhr: Polizei schätzt die Teilnehmerzahl Aktuell liegen die Teilnehmerzahlen noch deutlich unter den bei der Polizei angemeldeten: Die Behörde schätzt die Menschenmenge bei den Demonstrationen am Platz der Republik auf derzeit 150 .
Einer von ihnen ist Reza Abdi (50). Er trägt eine Iran-Flagge als Umhang und ist aus Basel angereist: „Es ist ein sehr wichtiger Tag, damit Leute sehen, dass wir unseren König unterstützen .“ In den vergangenen Monaten war er auch auf Iran-Demos in Düsseldorf, Köln und London.
Extra aus der Schweiz angereist, um seinen „König“ zu supporten. © Marie Nadler
Die Demonstrierenden rufen: „Das ist die letzte Schlacht. Der König kommt zurück in den Iran.“
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Exiled politician Reza Pahlavi wants to give voice to his compatriots during his visit to Berlin. Supporters and opponents are demonstrating. The events in the live blog.

By Lionel Kreglinger, Marie Nadler, Lisa Röther. Updated: 12:39 p.m. today
The Iranian exiled politician Reza Pahlavi, son of the Shah overthrown in 1979, has been visiting Berlin as a private citizen since late Wednesday afternoon. Pahlavi plans to meet with members of the Bundestag in the capital. On Thursday morning, he held a press conference at the Federal Press Conference building on the banks of the Spree River.

"While Iranians continue to fight for their liberation, I have come to Berlin to ensure that their voices are heard," he wrote on X on Wednesday.

Several demonstrations are taking place around the government district – by Pahlavi's supporters as well as his opponents: Demonstrations titled "Freedom for Iran" and "Support for Prince Reza Pahlavi from the EU and Germany" began in the government district near the Reichstag building as early as this morning.

Developments in our live blog: 12:30 p.m.: Pahlavi pelted with tomato sauce – arrested. Pahlavi was pelted with tomato sauce following a press conference. A man was subsequently arrested, police said. The incident occurred after the exiled politician had appeared at the Federal Press Conference. Police did not provide further details. The sauce-like liquid was visible on Pahlavi's shoulder and neck.

11:54 a.m.: 800 police officers deployed in government district. Police are deployed with 800 officers at the pro-Pahlavi demonstrations in the government district today, Thursday. A spokesperson also told the Tagesspiegel newspaper that there was no concrete indication "that the situation could turn violent." Approximately 250 demonstrators are currently present.

An IT engineer from The Hague says: "Our goal is for Iran to be free." Farrokh Ajdadi waves an Iranian flag alongside a historical Persian flag in the colors red, purple, and yellow. It stands for freedom, justice, unity, and love, says Ajdadi.

Farrokh Ajdadi, IT engineer from The Hague. © Marie Nadler

11:29 a.m.: A voice for his murdered brother, Erisa Heydari says in English that he is demonstrating to be the voice of his brother, who was killed by the Iranian regime. He carries a sign with a photo of himself and a blue flag, which represents the Pahlavi dynasty. "I am here so that Pahlavi can bring democracy to Iran." Heydari says he has lost four friends in addition to his brother.

Demonstration by Pahlavi supporters in Berlin-Mitte © Marie Nadler
10:57 a.m.: Criticism of Pahlavi from the Society of German-Iranians. The spokesperson for the Society of German-Iranians (GDI), Sahar Sanaie, strongly warns against politically legitimizing Reza Pahlavi. She told the Tagesspiegel that legitimizing such a figure is "a slap in the face to all those fighting for freedom in Iran." This applies especially to the demonstrators who chanted "Death to the oppressor, be it Shah or leader," as well as to the 17 recently executed political prisoners. In their final messages, these prisoners spoke out against both the mullah dictatorship and a return to the monarchy.

Pahlavi himself "paid no price for freedom in Iran" and has been out of touch with the reality in the country for 47 years. The people of Iran don't want "wave riders," but genuine fighters for freedom. Instead, the spokeswoman said, “Reza Pahlavi is only weakening the opposition and sowing division.”

The GDI is a politically active association that advocates for regime change in Iran and regularly organizes demonstrations in German cities, often focusing on Berlin or Hamburg.

10:36 a.m.: Police estimate the number of participants. Currently, the number of participants is still significantly lower than the number registered with the police: The authorities estimate the crowd at the demonstrations in Republic Square at 150 people.

One of them is Reza Abdi (50). He is wearing an Iranian flag as a cape and traveled from Basel: “It’s a very important day so that people can see that we support our king.” In recent months, he has also attended pro-Iranian demonstrations in Düsseldorf, Cologne, and London.

He traveled all the way from Switzerland to support his “king.” © Marie Nadler
The demonstrators chant: “This is the final battle. The king is coming back to Iran.”

MESSAGE_TEXT:
El parón abarcará del 25 al 27 de junio y busca poner fin a meses de lo que consideran «bloqueo» en las negociaciones por un convenio y salario actualizado
La plantilla este viernes durante una asamblea. / Bernabé / Amanda Castro
Nerea Couceiro
A Estrada 30 MAY 2026 6:06 La plantilla de Geseco, empresa concesionaria del servicio municipal de limpieza viaria y recogida de residuos, ha convocado una huelga durante las fiestas de San Paio ante el bloqueo de las negociaciones del convenio colectivo y la falta de avances en sus reivindicaciones salariales . La decisión fue ratificada por los trabajadores en una asamblea celebrada este viernes y llega después de varios meses de contactos tanto con la dirección de la empresa como con la administración municipal, sin que, según denuncia la CIG, se hayan producido progresos significativos .
Según explican desde la agrupación sindical, el principal punto de conflicto es la actualización de las condiciones económicas de la plantilla, integrada por una veintena de trabajadores . En este sentido, indican que los empleados llevan ocho años en una empresa privada sin mejoras salariales relevantes , una situación que consideran insostenible debido al incremento del coste de la vida registrado en los últimos años.
La propuesta trasladada por la representación sindical pasa por la firma de un convenio con una vigencia de dos años , cuya principal demanda es una subida salarial equivalente al IPC de 2025 (4,2 %) , así como un incremento adicional del 2 % para 2026 . La CIG asegura que esta es la única cuestión irrenunciable dentro de la negociación, mientras que el resto de aspectos permanecen abiertos al diálogo.
Además, critican que la empresa vincule cualquier mejora económica a la resolución del nuevo contrato municipal del servicio . Según expusieron durante la rueda de prensa, la falta de información sobre la futura licitación y la ausencia de los pliegos impiden conocer en qué condiciones se prestará el servicio en los próximos años. El sindicato considera que esta incertidumbre no puede justificar el retraso en la actualización de las condiciones laborales y que esperar a la adjudicación del futuro contrato supondría hipotecar la negociación colectiva .
Noticias relacionadas
Ante esta situación, los trabajadores acordaron convocar una huelga que comenzará a las 00.00 horas del 25 de junio y se prolongará hasta las 24.00 horas del 27 de junio . El sindicato no descarta nuevas movilizaciones en las próximas semanas para visibilizar el conflicto y reclamar avances en la negociación.

The strike will run from June 25th to 27th and aims to end months of what they consider a "blockade" in negotiations for an updated collective bargaining agreement and salary.
The workforce met this Friday during an assembly. / Bernabé / Amanda Castro
Nerea Couceiro
A Estrada, May 30, 2026, 6:06 AM. The workforce of Geseco, the company contracted to provide municipal street cleaning and waste collection services, has called a strike during the San Paio festivities due to the deadlock in collective bargaining negotiations and the lack of progress on their salary demands. The decision was ratified by the workers in an assembly held this Friday and comes after several months of contact with both the company management and the municipal administration, without, according to the CIG union, any significant progress.

According to the union, the main point of contention is the updating of the economic conditions of the workforce, which consists of about twenty employees. In this regard, they indicate that the employees have been with a private company for eight years without significant salary increases, a situation they consider unsustainable due to the rising cost of living in recent years.

The proposal put forward by the union representatives involves signing a two-year collective bargaining agreement, whose main demand is a salary increase equivalent to the 2025 Consumer Price Index (CPI) (4.2%), as well as an additional 2% increase for 2026. The CIG union asserts that this is the only non-negotiable issue in the negotiations, while the remaining aspects remain open to discussion.

Furthermore, they criticize the company for linking any salary improvement to the awarding of the new municipal service contract. As they explained during the press conference, the lack of information about the upcoming tender and the absence of the tender documents make it impossible to know the conditions under which the service will be provided in the coming years. The union believes this uncertainty cannot justify the delay in updating working conditions and that waiting for the awarding of the future contract would jeopardize collective bargaining.

Related news
Given this situation, the workers agreed to call a strike that will begin at midnight on June 25 and last until midnight on June 27. The union does not rule out further protests in the coming weeks to raise awareness of the conflict and demand progress in the negotiations.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
NEW DELHI: The police on Wednesday detained CPI(M) general secretary M A Baby and several party workers during a protest in Thiruvananthapuram against the Enforcement Directorate (ED) raids at the residence of former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan.
A scuffle broke out between police and CPI(M) leaders as they staged a demonstration over the searches. Police said the protesters were detained to maintain law and order and later released. CPI(M) leaders and workers also held a protest outside the ED office, condemning the raids in Keralam.
The central agency conducted searches at 10 premises in Keralam, including the residences of the former Chief Minister and current Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan, in connection with the Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) case.
On Wednesday, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) staged a protest at the Enforcement Directorate (ED) headquarters in Delhi against the agency’s raids on the residence of former Keralam Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan. The protest was led by CPI(M) General Secretary M.A. Baby.
As per CPI(M), during the protest, Delhi Police detained the demonstrators. The detained accused included senior leader Brinda Karat, Polit Bureau members Ashok Dhawale, Mariam Dhawale and Vijoo Krishnan, Central Committee members Vikram Singh, and Delhi State secretary Anurag Saxena. More than one hundred protesters were also detained.
CPI(M), in its statement, said that M A Baby strongly condemned the action carried out by the ED under the direction of the central government and stated that the raid on Pinarayi Vijayan’s residence was a politically motivated act of vendetta.
He pointed out that courts have repeatedly observed that Pinarayi Vijayan has absolutely no connection with the Exalogic case, yet the political witch-hunt against him continues unabated. He is now being targeted even for being Veena’s father. He further stated that such an action taking place immediately after Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan’s meeting with the Prime Minister in Delhi raises serious questions and appears to be a politically orchestrated drama.
Several individuals whose names reportedly appeared in the CMRL diary continue to hold important positions in the state government. However, while ignoring all of them, the continuous targeting of Pinarayi Vijayan further exposes the political vendetta behind these actions.
He said that the party has no intention whatsoever of obstructing any investigation process. However, the blatant misuse of central agencies by the central government for political targeting cannot be accepted. The party will mobilise people and organise strong protests across the country against the selective targeting of opposition leaders and the attacks on democratic rights.
The ED conducted searches in 10 places in connection with the alleged fraudulent payments to Veena, Pinarayi Vijayan’s daughter, amid a Rs 182-crore money laundering probe into the Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) case. (ANI)

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Lisbeth Mejía Reyes/Zona Roja.
Oaxaca, Oax., a 28 de abril de 2026.- La Coordinadora Nacional de Trabajadores de la Educación (CNTE) confirmó que estallará en paro indefinido en el marco del Mundial de Futbol, que albergará México a partir de junio.
Sin embargo, la fecha para el inicio del paro se definirá en la próxima asamblea nacional representativa del 16 de mayo, en la que se reunirán las 27 secciones sindicales de los casi 20 estados en los que tiene presencia la coordinadora.
En esta protesta masiva, exigirá nuevamente que el gobierno de la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo abrogue la Ley del ISSSTE del 2007 y la reforma educativa; también, que atienda otras demandas centrales y específicas de la gremial.
Rumbo al paro indefinido, con el que se retomará la huelga de mayo-junio del 2025, la CNTE también ha preparado una serie de movilizaciones junto con organizaciones y otros sindicatos, resultado de la reciente asamblea nacional del 25 de abril.
La primera movilización será el 1 de mayo, Día del Trabajo, con una marcha que partirá a las 09:00 horas del Ángel de la Independencia al zócalo de la Ciudad de México y tras la cual entregará su pliego petitorio al ejecutivo federal.
La marcha también se hará en la ciudad de Oaxaca, en donde la Sección 22 entregará el pliego petitorio correspondiente al gobierno estatal.
El 15 de mayo, en el día de las y los maestros, también realizará su habitual marcha nacional de la Normal Superior al zócalo de la Ciudad de México. Ese día habrá réplicas en los estados.
Este martes, en conferencia de prensa virtual, los secretarios generales de varias secciones del Sindicato Nacional de Trabajadores de la Educación y de la CNTE, reiteraron que las demandas centrales como la abrogación de la ley del ISSSTE del 2007 sigue, por lo que también esperan la suma de otros sindicatos y trabajadores afectados por esta ley.
Yenny Araceli Pérez Martínez, secretaria general de la Sección 22 en Oaxaca, explicó que e algunas secciones ya tienen su propuesta de fecha para el paro o huelga nacional indefinidos, pero que en el caso de otras, como la 22, se someterá a votación en asamblea estatal. La Sección 22 ha previsto retomar su asamblea estatal el 1 de mayo, después de la marcha por el Día del Trabajo.
Los alcances de la nueva huelga nacional dependerán de la respuesta del gobierno federal, apuntó la secretaria de la Sección 22, al recordar que en el paro de mayo-junio de 2025 acordaron un receso, pero en estos meses la respuesta del gobierno solamente ha sido la represión administrativa y económica, así como la persecución política y jurídica.
La representante recordó que las demandas centrales han sido parte de sus exigencias hacia el gobierno del ex presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador y ahora con el de Claudia Sheinbaum, por lo que exigen respuestas favorables.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Lisbeth Mejía Reyes/Zona Roja.

Oaxaca, Oaxaca, April 28, 2026 – The National Coordinator of Education Workers (CNTE) confirmed that it will launch an indefinite strike during the World Cup, which Mexico will host starting in June.

However, the date for the start of the strike will be determined at the next national representative assembly on May 16, where the 27 union sections from the nearly 20 states where the coordinator has a presence will meet.

In this massive protest, they will again demand that the government of President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo repeal the 2007 ISSSTE Law and the education reform; they will also demand that the government address other central and specific demands of the union.

Heading into an indefinite strike, which will resume the May-June 2025 strike, the CNTE has also prepared a series of mobilizations in conjunction with other organizations and unions, a result of the recent national assembly on April 25.

The first mobilization will be on May 1, Labor Day, with a march departing at 9:00 a.m. from the Angel of Independence to the Zócalo in Mexico City, after which they will deliver their list of demands to the federal government.
A march will also take place in the city of Oaxaca, where Section 22 will deliver its corresponding list of demands to the state government.

On May 15, Teachers' Day, they will also hold their traditional national march from the Normal Superior to the Zócalo in Mexico City. Similar marches will take place in other states that day.

This Tuesday, in a virtual press conference, the general secretaries of several sections of the National Union of Education Workers (SNTE) and the CNTE (National Coordinator of Education Workers) reiterated that their central demands, such as the repeal of the 2007 ISSSTE (Institute for Social Security and Services for State Workers) law, remain in place. They also hope for the support of other unions and workers affected by this law.

Yenny Araceli Pérez Martínez, general secretary of Section 22 in Oaxaca, explained that some sections already have proposed dates for an indefinite national strike, but that in the case of others, such as Section 22, the decision will be put to a vote at a state assembly. Section 22 plans to reconvene its state assembly on May 1st, after the Labor Day march.

The scope of the new national strike will depend on the federal government's response, noted the secretary of Section 22, recalling that during the May-June 2025 strike they agreed to a recess, but in recent months the government's response has been nothing but administrative and economic repression, as well as political and legal persecution.

The representative reiterated that the central demands have been part of their demands on the government of former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador and now on that of Claudia Sheinbaum, and therefore they demand favorable responses.

MESSAGE_TEXT:
Estudiantes del TEC se manifiestan por problemas con becas
La institución académica reconoció que hubo un inconveniente con el otorgamiento del dinero.
Un grupo de estudiantes del Instituto Tecnológico de Costa Rica (TEC) se manifiesta en las instalaciones del campus central en protesta por inconvenientes en el depósito de las becas socioeconómicas. Los jóvenes aseguran que la institución incumplió con el adelanto de la ayuda económica y que ahora se plantea una reducción en los montos asignados.
Según un comunicado estudiantil, el problema se originó en la elaboración del presupuesto de becas para 2026.
“A inicios de año se nos comunicó que la beca de julio se adelantaría a junio. Un día antes del pago, se nos informó que no sería posible. Hoy, en reunión, nos confirmaron lo siguiente: El retroactivo se traslada de julio a agosto, por un faltante de ₡800 millones, pretenden rebajar las becas a los montos del I semestre 2025, es decir, antes de los dos últimos aumentos. La única vía que plantean para sostener los aumentos hasta diciembre es que Hacienda gire el 2% que adeuda del FEES del año pasado", detallaron.
Para los afectados, el origen del problema fue que, "al elaborar el presupuesto de becas socioeconómicas 2026, no se consideraron los tres aumentos aplicados durante 2025. De los ₡1.200 millones contemplados, ya se giró un 60% solo en el I semestre 2026, dejando apenas un 40% para el II semestre. Fue un error de los entes técnicos —hoy bajo investigación para sancionar a los responsables—, pero quien termina pagando las consecuencias es la persona estudiante”.
Los estudiantes señalan que esta situación afecta directamente su capacidad para cubrir gastos básicos como alquiler, alimentación y servicios. “Al rebajar la beca en este momento, no podremos sufragar los gastos mínimos necesarios”, expresaron los afectados, quienes exigen soluciones inmediatas para garantizar la continuidad de los apoyos.
Por su parte, las autoridades del TEC también se pronunciaron y confirmaron que, efectivamente, hay un grupo de estudiantes que se está manifestando en la entrada del TEC y reconocieron que hubo un inconveniente con el otorgamiento del dinero.
“Las instancias técnicas responsables depositaron durante el primer semestre un sobremonto en las becas, el cual no se les va a deducir, pero debe ajustarse para el segundo semestre. Situación por la cual se mantiene una manifestación en nuestro Campus Central”, indicó el TEC.
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
TEC Students Protest Scholarship Issues
The academic institution acknowledged a problem with the disbursement of funds.
A group of students from the Costa Rica Institute of Technology (TEC) are protesting at the main campus over issues with the deposit of socioeconomic scholarships. The students claim the institution failed to make the advance payment and is now considering reducing the allocated amounts.

According to a student statement, the problem originated in the preparation of the 2026 scholarship budget.

“At the beginning of the year, we were informed that the July scholarship payment would be moved to June. The day before the payment was due, we were told that this would not be possible. Today, in a meeting, the following was confirmed: The retroactive payment will be moved from July to August, due to a shortfall of ₡800 million. They intend to reduce the scholarship amounts to those of the first semester of 2025, that is, before the last two increases. The only way they propose to maintain the increases until December is for the Ministry of Finance to release the 2% it owes from last year's Higher Education Funding Fund,” they explained.

For those affected, the problem stemmed from the fact that, "when preparing the 2026 socioeconomic scholarship budget, the three increases implemented during 2025 were not taken into account. Of the ₡1.2 billion allocated, 60% was already disbursed in the first half of 2026 alone, leaving only 40% for the second half. It was an error by the technical bodies—currently under investigation to sanction those responsible—but it is the students who ultimately pay the price."

The students point out that this situation directly impacts their ability to cover basic expenses such as rent, food, and utilities. "By reducing the scholarship at this time, we will not be able to cover even the minimum necessary expenses," the affected students stated, demanding immediate solutions to guarantee the continuity of the support.

For their part, TEC authorities also issued a statement confirming that a group of students is indeed protesting at the entrance to the TEC campus and acknowledged a problem with the disbursement of funds.

“The responsible technical departments deposited an overpayment into the scholarships during the first semester, which will not be deducted, but must be adjusted for the second semester. This situation is the reason for the ongoing protest at our Central Campus,” TEC stated.

CAPTION_ENDORSE: Protest ends in Brake, Germany
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Brake - Es war eine friedliche Demonstration, die sich am Samstag durch die Stadt Brake zog. Rund 400 Menschen protestierten für den Erhalt des St.-Bernhard-Hospitals und eine gute Gesundheitsversorgung vor Ort. Doch der Frieden währte nicht lange. Grund: Der Organisator der Demonstration, SPD-Bürgermeisterkandidat Vehbi Sentuerkler, warf in seiner Ansprache dem Braker Stadtrat vor, er habe die Öffentlichkeit in der Krankenhauskrise über die tatsächlichen Vorgänge bewusst belogen und nicht rechtzeitig informiert.
Beschuldigte erhielten kein Rederecht
Eine Anschuldigung, der die Beschuldigten vor Ort jedoch nichts entgegnen durften. Rederecht erhielten sie nicht. Und so äußerten sich CDU, WGB, FDP und Grüne gemeinsam mit Bürgermeister Michael Kurz im Anschluss per Pressemitteilung zu den Anschuldigungen. In ihrem Statement verurteilen sie die „parteipolitische Instrumentalisierung“ der Krankenhaus-Demonstration „aufs Schärfste“ – und forderten den Rückzug des SPD-Bürgermeisterkandidaten. Er habe das Schicksal des Krankenhauses und seiner Beschäftigten für parteipolitische Interessen missbraucht, so ihr Vorwurf. „Was als Informations- und Bürgerveranstaltung angekündigt wurde, entpuppte sich als reine Wahlkampfbühne, bei der dem amtierenden Bürgermeister Michael Kurz das Rederecht verweigert und Falschbehauptungen über den Stadtrat verbreitet wurden.“ Weiter hieß es: „Mit seinen Aussagen offenbarte der Kandidat eklatante Unkenntnis über die Grundlagen der Krankenhausfinanzierung und die politischen Zuständigkeiten – oder er ignorierte diese bewusst für sein Konzept.“
Klinik nicht in öffentlicher Hand
Dazu muss man wissen: Das St.-Bernhard-Hospital ist nicht in kommunaler Hand, wie etwa die Klinik im Landkreis Friesland. Es ist eine gGmbH und muss auch als katholisches Krankenhaus wie ein Wirtschaftsunternehmen arbeiten. Als die Schließung am 7. Juli bekannt gegeben wurde, wurden als Gründe unter anderem dauerhaft unzureichende Refinanzierung, erhebliche Tarifsteigerungen, gestiegene Energiepreise, höhere Kosten für Medizinprodukte und Arzneimittel, allgemeine Inflation, die wirtschaftliche Auswirkungen der Krankenhausreform und fehlende finanzielle Unterstützung durch einen kommunalen Träger angeführt. Letzteres bedeutet, dass ein Defizit nicht durch Städte, Kreise oder – wie beispielsweise bei Universitätskliniken – vom Land ausgeglichen werden. Die Finanzierung der Krankenhäuser erfolgt ansonsten nach gesetzlichen Vorgaben.
Unabhängig davon hieß es in der Mitteilung von CDU, WGB, FDP, Grüne und Bürgermeister Michael Kurz: „Aufgrund der aktuellen Situation war zudem eine große Mehrheit der Ratsmitglieder bereit, im Rahmen eines Wirtschaftsplanes, weiterer Bedingungen und rechtlicher Genehmigung eine Bürgschaft für ein notwendiges Darlehen zur Weiterführung des Krankenhausbetriebs zu übernehmen.“
TRANSLATED_TEXT:
Brake – It was a peaceful demonstration that wound its way through the town of Brake on Saturday. Around 400 people protested for the preservation of St. Bernhard Hospital and for good local healthcare. But the peace didn't last long. The reason: The organizer of the demonstration, SPD mayoral candidate Vehbi Sentuerkler, accused the Brake town council in his speech of deliberately lying to the public about the actual events in the hospital crisis and failing to provide timely information.

Accused were denied the right to speak.
An accusation to which the accused were not allowed to respond. They were denied the right to speak. Consequently, the CDU, WGB, FDP, and Greens, together with Mayor Michael Kurz, issued a press release addressing the accusations. In their statement, they condemned the "partisan instrumentalization" of the hospital demonstration "in the strongest possible terms" – and demanded the withdrawal of the SPD mayoral candidate. He exploited the fate of the hospital and its employees for partisan political gain, they accused. "What was announced as an informational and public event turned out to be a pure election campaign platform, where the incumbent mayor, Michael Kurz, was denied the right to speak and false claims about the city council were spread." The statement continued: "With his remarks, the candidate revealed a blatant lack of knowledge about the fundamentals of hospital financing and political responsibilities – or he deliberately ignored them for his own agenda."

Hospital not publicly owned

It's important to know that St. Bernhard Hospital is not publicly owned, unlike the hospital in the Friesland district. It is a non-profit limited liability company (gGmbH) and, even as a Catholic hospital, must operate like a business. When the closure was announced on July 7, the reasons given included persistently inadequate funding, significant pay increases, rising energy prices, higher costs for medical devices and pharmaceuticals, general inflation, the economic impact of hospital reform, and a lack of financial support from a municipal sponsor. CAPTION_ENDORSE: Community Health Officers resume healthcare services after National Health Mission authorities assure them that their demands would be considered within time bound period of 15 days in Punjab, India
MESSAGE_TEXT:
Community health officers suspend strike, NHM assures action on pending demands
After nearly two weeks of agitation, Community Health Officers (CHOs) across Punjab on Wednesday announced that they would resume healthcare services after the National Health Mission (NHM) authorities assured them that their demands would be considered within a time bound period of 15 days. Following the assurance, the CHOs also postponed their proposed Sangrur rally scheduled for July 2.
The officers, who had been on strike since June 22, said they were returning to work in the larger interest of public healthcare but warned that the agitation would resume from July 16 if the government failed to take concrete action. “Nearly 126 CHOs participated in the strike in Jalandhar. As part of the state-wide agitation, we staged a demonstration outside the Civil Surgeon’s office on Wednesday,” said Dr Richa Chanday, a protesting Community Health Officer.
The development is significant as CHOs form the backbone of primary healthcare in villages and semi-urban areas. Posted at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (formerly Health and Wellness Centres), they are often the first point of contact for patients seeking treatment at government health facilities.
They treat common ailments, screen people for non-communicable diseases such as diabetes, hypertension and cancer, monitor maternal and child health, supervise immunisation drives, coordinate with ASHA workers and ANMs, implement national health programmes and refer serious cases to higher health facilities. Their return is expected to restore these essential services, many of which had been affected during the strike.
Dr Sunil Targotra, president of the Community Health Officers Association, Punjab said, “We have decided to resume our duties after the assurances given by NHM authorities. A meeting with Punjab Ministers Harpal Singh Cheema, Aman Arora and Baljit Kaur, along with senior health department officials, has been scheduled for July 14. If the government fails to address our demands, we will resume the agitation from July 16 and hold a state-wide rally in Sangrur on July 22.”
The association said that despite shouldering a wide range of public health responsibilities, CHOs continue to serve on contractual appointments without job security or the service benefits available to regular government employees.
Their demands include withdrawal of the newly introduced performance based incentive (PBI) system, regularisation of services, equal pay for equal work, release of the pending Rs 5,000 salary hike and preference for experienced CHOs in regular recruitment, filling of vacant posts, adequate funding and clear operational guidelines to ensure responsibilities are shared across the health team instead of being placed solely on CHOs.

Familiares del profesor fallecido Raúl Cisneros Valdivia se manifestaron este miércoles 10 de junio en la Plaza Lerdo de Xalapa para denunciar una red de presuntas irregularidades administrativas que han obstaculizado el trámite de pensión por invalidez del docente, vulnerando sus derechos laborales y sindicales hasta el día de su muerte.
